title: Translate the shell, the palette and the dates, and reconcile the cross-module suites
description:
## What changes for the user
The frame around every screen is Portuguese: the sidebar says `Início` and `Preferências` and its
collapse button is labelled `Expandir barra lateral`, the command palette says `Ir para` and
`Buscar telas, artigos, notas, assuntos…`, the four failure screens say `Servidor indisponível`,
`Módulo desligado`, `Página não encontrada` and `Não foi possível iniciar o aplicativo`, a date
reads `Sábado, 3 de outubro`, and the document itself declares `lang="pt-BR"`. After this change
the whole frame is English, dates included.

## Outcome
Every string in `web/src/shell/`, in the command palette, in the search registry and in the date
formatting is English; `web/index.html` declares `lang="en"`; the search-entry kind `tela` is
`screen`; and the cross-module tests and end-to-end suites every earlier bead left half-translated
are wholly English.

## Context
This is the last UI bead and it has two jobs.

**The shell's own words.** The sidebar, the top bar, the home screen, the palette, the preferences
panel, the subject screen and picker, the new-subject button, the saved-about panel and the four
failure screens. The dates are the one part that is not a string swap: `web/src/lib/clock.ts:74,
102-107` formats with a pt-BR locale and has its own `hoje`/`ontem` words; the English version
formats with an English locale and says `today`/`yesterday`. `web/src/__fixtures__/
viewDueDate.fixture.vue:11`, `web/src/mock/relative.ts:6` and `web/src/mock/data.ts:43` hold the
formatted result and move with it. This is not an internationalisation layer: there is no catalogue
and no switch, so the locale is a constant in one file.

**The reconciliation.** `web/src/shell/AppShell.test.ts`, `web/src/shell/HomeView.test.ts` and
`web/src/shell/sidebar.test.ts` assert the labels *every* module contributes to the sidebar and the
home screen; `web/e2e/*.spec.ts` walk the whole app. Those are the files no module bead can own,
and this bead is their single owner: each earlier bead touches only the assertions naming its own
module, and this bead is where they come out wholly English and where any assertion an earlier bead
left inconsistent is fixed. That is also why it is last: the convention bead's final sweep is only
meaningful once these files are clean.

Two cross-cutting values land here because no single module can own them:

- **`kind: 'tela'` becomes `kind: 'screen'`** in the search registry. The value is declared in
  `web/src/search/index.ts:53`, read in `web/src/shell/ShellOverlay.vue:44`, asserted in
  `web/src/search/index.test.ts:91`, and set by all five modules' `index.ts`. Those five files
  belong to their own module beads, which all run before this one, so the rename is one atomic
  commit here with those five listed as shared edits.
- **`web/index.html:2`'s `lang="pt-BR"`**, which is what a screen reader uses to pick a voice and
  what the browser uses for hyphenation. Nothing else in the repo owns that file.

The strings themselves, with their English, are in §1.2 of the inventory comment on norte-3ab.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every string in `web/src/shell/` is English: the sidebar (including
      `Expandir barra lateral` / `Recolher barra lateral` and the per-section `Expandir <label>`
      aria-labels), the top bar, the home screen, the command palette, the preferences panel, the
      subject screen, the subject picker, the new-subject button, the saved-about panel, the
      placeholder and the four failure screens.
- [ ] The command palette's group labels and kind words are English in both
      `web/src/shell/paletteSearch.ts` and `web/src/search/index.ts`.
- [ ] `web/src/lib/clock.ts` formats dates in English and says `today` and `yesterday`, and the
      three fixtures that hold a formatted date hold the English form.
- [ ] `web/index.html` declares `lang="en"`.
- [ ] The search-entry kind is `screen` everywhere it is written or read, and
      `web/src/shell/ShellOverlay.vue` filters on it.
- [ ] `web/src/shell/AppShell.test.ts`, `web/src/shell/HomeView.test.ts` and
      `web/src/shell/sidebar.test.ts` assert English labels for **every** module, with no
      assertion deleted: an assertion that named a Portuguese label names its English replacement.
- [ ] The four end-to-end suites assert English labels and English addresses.
- [ ] The **shell forbidden-term check** comes back empty:

          rg -n --no-heading \
            -e '[À-ÿ]' -e 'pt-BR' -e "'tela'" \
            -e '(?i)\b(inicio|preferencias|expandir|recolher|barra|lateral|navegacao|buscar|telas|artigos|notas|assuntos|assunto|ir|para|acoes|atalho|abrir|fechar|carregar|nenhum|nenhuma|nada|servidor|indisponivel|modulo|desligado|pagina|encontrada|aplicativo|iniciar|voltar|tentar|hoje|ontem|sabado|domingo|segunda|terca|quarta|quinta|sexta|janeiro|fevereiro|marco|abril|maio|junho|julho|agosto|setembro|outubro|novembro|dezembro|apagar|criar|cancelar|remover|ligacoes|ligacao|foco|salvos|memoria)\b' \
            web/src/shell web/src/search web/src/lib web/src/mock web/src/__fixtures__ web/index.html web/e2e

      with one allowlisted hit, named in the inventory: `web/src/search/index.ts`'s `normalize`
      strips accents with NFD before comparing, because a saved item's title can be in any
      language; the accent-class characters in that regexp stay, and only its
      `toLocaleLowerCase('pt-BR')` becomes `'en'`.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- component: the sidebar renders `Home`, the search and preferences entries, the English
  collapse/expand labels and the `No subject yet` empty state.
- component: the palette renders `Go to`, `Actions` and the English placeholder, and groups results
  under the English group labels.
- component: each of the four failure screens renders its English title and body.
- unit: `clock.ts` formats a known timestamp in English, and answers `today` and `yesterday` for
  the two relative cases.
- unit: `web/src/search/index.test.ts` asserts every entry's kind is `screen`.
- e2e: `web/e2e/shell-boot.spec.ts` asserts `Module switched off` and `Page not found`;
  `web/e2e/phone-walk.spec.ts`, `web/e2e/library-search-sort.spec.ts` and
  `web/e2e/highlight-anchoring.spec.ts` assert their English labels.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** every `.vue` and `.ts` file under `web/src/shell/` (including `AppShell.test.ts`,
`HomeView.test.ts`, `sidebar.test.ts`, `ShellOverlay.test.ts`, `SubjectView.test.ts`,
`SubjectPicker.test.ts`, `SavedAboutPanel.test.ts`, `drawer.test.ts`, `moduleMount.test.ts`,
`NavigationFailed.test.ts`, `retiredCopy.test.ts`, `boot.test.ts` and `data/apiSource.test.ts`),
`web/src/search/index.test.ts`, `web/src/lib/clock.ts`,
`web/src/lib/clock.test.ts`, `web/src/mock/relative.ts`, `web/src/mock/data.ts`,
`web/src/mock/store.ts`, `web/src/__fixtures__/viewDueDate.fixture.vue`,
`web/src/__fixtures__/mockRecordDate.fixture.ts`,
`web/src/__fixtures__/legacyDateSymbols.fixture.ts`, `web/index.html`,
`web/e2e/shell-boot.spec.ts`, `web/e2e/phone-walk.spec.ts`,
`web/e2e/library-search-sort.spec.ts`, `web/e2e/highlight-anchoring.spec.ts`,
`web/e2e/csp.spec.ts`, `web/e2e/reader-reading-position.spec.ts`,
`docs/tools/ci-checks.md`
**Shared edits:** `web/src/search/index.ts` (owner norte-6vs, which renames the subject route and
the home entry in it; this bead changes its group labels, its `kind: 'tela'` declaration and the
`toLocaleLowerCase('pt-BR')` in `normalize`), `web/src/modules/library/index.ts`,
`web/src/modules/notes/index.ts`,
`web/src/modules/projects/index.ts`, `web/src/modules/review/index.ts`,
`web/src/modules/study/index.ts` — the `kind: 'tela'` line only, whose owners are those modules'
own beads, all of which block this one
**Reads only:** `web/src/modules/`, `web/src/components/ds/`

Every file under **Edits** that an earlier bead also touched is listed in that bead's
**Shared edits**, and the dependency edges are what keep two agents off it. This bead depends on
every UI bead for exactly that reason.

`docs/tools/ci-checks.md` quotes `Biblioteca`, `Módulo desligado` and `Página não encontrada` in
the `web-e2e-phone` and `web-e2e-shell-boot` descriptions. It is edited here because this bead is
the one that changes the strings those two checks assert.

## Recovery path
No stored data and no contract: strings, one locale constant, one document language and one search
kind. Reverting the commit restores the previous screens exactly.

title: Decide whether the classifier is ready for subject proposals
description:
## Context
Norte's classifier suggests where a saved link belongs, choosing among existing subjects and focus targets; the person accepts or rejects each suggestion. A follow-up step lets the classifier also propose *new* subjects, guarded against near-duplicate names. That step was planned as a second round of the first delivery, meant to start only after the plain classifier has been in daily use, because whether proposals are needed — and how often the suggestions miss for lack of a subject — is learned from that use, not predicted.

Without this question in the tracker, the proposal work would become ready the moment the classifier lands and an unattended agent would build it before anyone has used the classifier. This bead is the gate: the proposal bead depends on it, and it in turn waits for the first delivery's acceptance walk, because the days of use that decide it only begin once that walk has put Norte into real use.

## Options
- **A · Build proposals now.** What changes: the proposal bead becomes ready; the guard (a 0.70 confidence floor, trigram similarity 0.6, aliases) is built on guesses about how the vocabulary will drift, and may be tuned again after use.
- **B · Wait for more use.** What changes: nothing is built; the classifier keeps suggesting only existing subjects; re-ask after another stretch of use.
- **C · Drop proposals.** What changes: the proposal bead is closed as declined; new subjects stay created by hand only, which is the current behaviour.

## What decides it
How often, over the days of use, a saved link got no good suggestion because the right subject did not exist yet — and whether near-duplicate subjects were being created by hand.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The answer (A, B or C) is recorded as a comment on this bead with the observation that decided it.
- [ ] On A, this bead closes and the proposal bead becomes ready; on C, the proposal bead is closed as declined with the reason; on B, this bead is deferred with a date.
- [ ] Done when: one of the three outcomes above is recorded and applied.

title: Build the Estudo home screen
description:
## What changes for the user
Today there is no study home: curricula and subjects are only reachable one by one. After this lands, Estudo shows your streak and weekly numbers, the curricula in a carousel, and every subject as covers or as a table, with one click to add a curriculum, a question or a link.

## Outcome
The Estudo home at `/estudo`, replacing its placeholder, with topbar, title, streak band, curricula carousel and the Assuntos section with its Capas / Tabela views.

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Open `design/prototypes/Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html` in a browser to see the screen. Read `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html` for markup, inline styles and behaviour. The behaviour is a `class Component extends DCLogic` block with React-style `state`/`setState`. The template uses a design-tool runtime whose `sc-if`, `sc-for` and `{{ }}` bindings map almost one to one onto `v-if`, `v-for` and `{{ }}`. Prototype links point at `Norte - X.dc.html?param=`; translate them into the routes below.
- `design/system/` holds the committed design system. It has tokens in `tokens.css`/`tokens.json` (colour, type, a 4px spacing scale, radius, shadow), one `components/<Name>/README.md` per component, props in `components/index.d.ts`, and screenshots in `screenshots/`. Fonts are in `fonts/`: Schibsted Grotesk for display, Geist for sans and Commit Mono for mono.
- There are two themes, Claro and Escuro, switched by `data-theme` on the root element and stored in `localStorage` under `norte-theme`. The visual rule is quiet: one cobalt accent, no cards, no gradients, no warm colours.

Route table (shared by every screen):
- `/` is Início (Command Home).
- `/biblioteca` is the library, with query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`.
- `/notas` is notes, with query `tab` = `highlights|anotacoes|perguntas`.
- `/revisao` is the flashcard review.
- `/estudo` is the Estudo home (Currículos and Assuntos).
- `/curriculos/:slug` is one curriculum.
- `/material/:kind/:id` is one reading item, where kind is `post|livro|paper`.
- `/projetos` is the project list.
- `/areas/:id` is one area.
- `/projetos/:id` is one project.
- `/decisoes/:id` is one decision.
- `/tarefas/:id` is one task.

The repo is public. Never copy the prototype's mock content (health, money, career, named people) into code; use the neutral invented data in `web/src/mock/`. UI strings stay Portuguese.

The repo is a monorepo: the Vue app lives in `web/` and a Go backend will live in `server/` and later serve the built app from one binary. All frontend paths below are under `web/`; `design/` stays at the repo root. The gate is `npm run build && npm test`, run in `web/`.

Reference: `design/prototypes/Home_A/template.html` and `design/prototypes/Norte - Home A (standalone).html`. Mounted at `/estudo`.

Regions in order:
- A topbar with a search input (placeholder "Buscar cursos, notas, perguntas…") that opens the command palette when one exists, a secondary "Adicionar" button with a dropdown, and a primary link to Revisão.
- PageTitle with the current date as title ("Sexta, 2 de outubro" style, from `Intl.DateTimeFormat('pt-BR')`) and a weekly-focus objective.
- A streak band: StreakGrid of 182 days plus four Stat: "Streak atual" (with record), "Estudadas esta semana" (hours), "Para revisar hoje" (cards), and "Concluídos em <month>" (items).
- "Currículos": a Carousel of curriculum covers, 248px cards, 4 visible, stepping by 2. The prototype builds this by hand; use the design-system Carousel and CoverCard instead.
- "Assuntos": a SegmentedControl "Capas / Tabela", default Capas. Capas is a 3-column cover grid. Tabela has columns Assunto, Currículos, Cursos, Artigos, Vídeos, Notas, Perguntas, Atividade.

The Adicionar menu has three items: new curriculum, new question, and save a link. The prototype's sidebar and Shell overlay are the app shell's job, not this view's.

Mock data: this view needs subjects ("assuntos": 6, each with counts per kind and a last-activity label) and study stats (daily activity for 182 days, current and record streak, hours this week, items completed this month). Add those types and data to `web/src/mock/` with invented, neutral content, as the mock-data bead did for the other entities. The prototype also links a "Home B" grid of curricula that was never exported; ignore that link.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The title shows today's date in pt-BR; the four Stat values and the StreakGrid are computed from `web/src/mock/`.
- [ ] The carousel shows 4 curricula, steps by 2, and disables prev/next at the ends; each card routes to `/curriculos/:slug`.
- [ ] The Capas / Tabela control switches views; both list the same 6 subjects, and each subject routes to `/biblioteca?v=tudo`.
- [ ] Adicionar items route to `/curriculos/nova`, `/notas?tab=perguntas` and `/?save=1`; the Revisão button routes to `/revisao`.
- [ ] Side by side with the prototype at 1440px in both themes, layout, spacing and typography match by eye.
- [ ] Done when: every state and link above works on `/estudo`, and the gate is green.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + @vue/test-utils, mounted with the real router and mock data): the view renders its title and main regions; each interactive state listed in the acceptance criteria flips as described; each outbound link resolves to the route named in the criteria.
- Unit: the stat helpers (streak, weekly hours, monthly completed) over a fixed activity fixture.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/views/StudyHomeView.vue`, `web/src/views/StudyHomeView/`, `web/src/router/index.ts`, `web/src/mock/`

One view plus its route, and additive types and data in `web/src/mock/` for subjects and study stats.

title: Log the cause of every internal error and make validation errors name their field
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, when the server answers a request with an internal error, the request id shown to the person leads to a log line that says only "500", so nobody can find out what went wrong. Validation messages also leave out which input was wrong (`"number must be at least 1"` with no field), a wrong HTTP method is reported as "no such endpoint", and `Content-Type: Application/JSON` is refused. Once this lands, every internal error has its cause in the log under its request id, and every validation error says which field or parameter it is about.

## Outcome
The three modules' handler error paths log the underlying error at ERROR level with the request id, and the shared request-validation mapping fills `field` for parameters and unknown body properties, answers 405 for a known path with the wrong method, accepts media types case-insensitively, and produces a clean message for an empty body.

## Context
Each module maps errors to the contract's envelope `{"error":{"code","message","field?","request_id"}}` (`api/openapi/core.yaml`, ErrorDetail: `field` is "the input the failure is attributable to, when it is attributable to exactly one"; `request_id` exists "so an error a person reports can be matched to the log line that recorded it"). Defects, each verified in code:
1. `writeLibraryHandlerError(w, r, _ error)` in `server/internal/library/handlers.go` and its twins in `server/internal/app/apierror.go` (core) and `server/internal/notes/apimount.go` (notes) discard the error for an internal failure; only panics are logged (`server/internal/core/middleware.go`). The comments next to them say the error "is for the log".
2. The request-validation mapping takes `field` from the SchemaError's JSON pointer, which is empty for a query parameter, and returns before the `requestErr.Parameter != nil` branch (`apierror.go` around 392-401; the same copy in notes and library). An unknown body property (`property "extra" is unsupported`) also carries no `field`.
3. The `/api/` catch-all registered in `server/internal/app/server.go` (around line 59) wins in `http.ServeMux` before the validator runs, so the classifiers' `routers.ErrMethodNotAllowed` branch that answers 405 is unreachable; `DELETE /api/config` answers 404 "no such endpoint".
4. Media-type matching is case-sensitive: `Application/JSON` gets 415, though media types are case-insensitive (RFC 9110 section 8.3.1).
5. An empty JSON body produces the message `": value is required but missing"` (an empty reason concatenated, `apierror.go` around 421).
The three copies of the mapping should become one shared function in `server/internal/core` if that is how the code is already arranged; otherwise fix each copy identically.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. `curl "$B/api/library/items?limit=0"` answers `{"error":{"code":"invalid_request","message":"number must be at least 1",...}}` with no `field`.
3. `curl -XPOST $B/api/core/subjects -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"x","extra":1}'` answers without `field`.
4. `curl -XDELETE $B/api/config` answers 404 `no such endpoint`.
5. `curl -XPOST $B/api/core/subjects -H 'Content-Type: Application/JSON' -d '{"name":"x"}'` answers 415.
6. `curl -XPOST $B/api/core/subjects -H 'content-type: application/json'` (no body) answers the message `": value is required but missing"`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An internal error in any of the three modules writes one ERROR log line carrying the request id and the error text; the response body still carries only the generic message.
- [ ] Step 2 answers `field: "limit"`; the same holds for `view`, `sort`, `tipo`, `kind`, `q` length and `cursor` errors in all three modules.
- [ ] Step 3 answers `field: "extra"`.
- [ ] Step 4 answers 405 `method_not_allowed` with an `Allow` header; an unknown path under `/api/` still answers 404.
- [ ] Step 5 answers 201.
- [ ] Step 6 answers a message without a leading colon, e.g. `request body is required`.
- [ ] Done when: steps 2 to 6 behave as above against a running server, and a forced internal error appears in the log with its cause.

## Tests
- unit: table tests over the shared mapping (or each copy) for each case above, in `server/internal/app/contract_test.go` or a new test next to the mapping.
- integration: one test per module that forces an internal error (e.g. a closed database handle) and asserts the log line carries the request id and the cause.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/app/apierror.go`, `server/internal/app/server.go`, `server/internal/notes/apimount.go`, `server/internal/library/handlers.go`, `server/internal/core/apierror.go`, and their tests
More than two modules, which is why this is `size:L`; every change is in the error-mapping layer, no handler logic changes.

title: Import Karakeep bookmarks into the Archive and the Stash
description:
## What changes for the user
The person has 2,286 bookmarks in Karakeep, a self-hosted bookmark manager, collected over two
years, and wants them in Norte without re-saving them one by one and without flooding the Inbox.
After this change one command imports them: each link is fetched and extracted by Norte itself,
placed in the Archive or the Stash, keeps its original save date, note and highlights, and gets
Norte's own tags.

## Outcome
A `norte import karakeep` subcommand reads a Karakeep SQLite database read-only and saves each
link bookmark of one Karakeep user into Norte, with a limit and a dry run, idempotently.

## Context
Inventory of the person's Karakeep on 2026-10-10: 2,286 bookmarks (2,268 links, 16 assets, 2
texts), 616 of them YouTube, 2,842 distinct tags, 56 lists, 394 favourites, 202 highlights, 64
notes; two Karakeep users, one holding 2,285 of the bookmarks.

Decided on 2026-10-10:
- Content: the importer passes only the URL; Norte fetches and extracts the page itself, so the
  import exercises Norte's own fetch path. Dead links end as failed extractions, which is
  information, not an error of the import.
- Location: everything goes to the Archive or the Stash, never the Inbox. The router decides,
  with the import option under which its Inbox choice becomes Archive.
- Tags, lists and favourites are not imported; Norte's tagger tags the items after extraction.
- The bookmark's `createdAt` becomes the item's save date.
- The Karakeep note becomes the item's note; Karakeep highlights become Norte highlights.
- Videos import as the video kind, link only.
- Assets (16) and text bookmarks (2) are skipped and counted in the report.
- First run: 50 bookmarks into a separate test instance, reviewed by the person before the
  real import.

The Karakeep tables read, as found in its database (`data/db.db`):

    bookmarks(id text pk, createdAt integer seconds, archived, favourited, userId, note text,
              title text, type text 'link'|'asset'|'text', summary, ...)
    bookmarkLinks(id text pk -> bookmarks.id, url text, title, description, imageUrl, favicon,
                  crawledAt, htmlContent, crawlStatus, author, publisher, datePublished, ...)
    highlights(id text pk, bookmarkId, userId, startOffset, endOffset, color, note text,
               createdAt integer, text text)
    user(id text pk, name, email, ...)

Norte's side: the save path is `LibraryService.Save` (`server/internal/library/service.go`),
called by the `save` subcommand (`server/internal/library/savecmd.go`, registered through the
library module's `Commands()` in `server/internal/library/library.go`). The item note is
`PUT /api/notes/items/{item_id}/note`, and a highlight is created with `exact`, `prefix` and
`suffix` (`api/openapi/notes.yaml`, `NewHighlight`); a highlight created before extraction is
re-anchored by the notes module's re-anchor job when the text arrives. Karakeep stores no
prefix or suffix, so imported highlights carry only `exact`: one that occurs once in the
extracted text anchors, the rest end ambiguous or orphaned, which the reader already shows.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `norte import karakeep --db <path> --user <email> [--limit N] [--dry-run]` opens the
      database read-only and imports link bookmarks of that user, newest first, up to N.
- [ ] Each imported item's save date equals the bookmark's `createdAt`, its source is `import`,
      and its location comes from the router's import option (Archive or Stash, never Inbox).
- [ ] A bookmark with a non-empty note sets the item note; each highlight with non-empty `text`
      becomes a highlight with that `exact` and empty prefix and suffix.
- [ ] Running the same command twice creates no second item, note or highlight: a URL already in
      the library is reported as skipped, and its note and highlights are left alone.
- [ ] `--dry-run` writes nothing and prints what would be imported.
- [ ] The command ends with a report: imported, skipped as duplicate, skipped as asset or text,
      failed (with reasons), plus how many went to Archive and to Stash.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green, and the review runs `--limit 50` against a copy of the real
      Karakeep database into a test instance and shows the result to the person.

## Tests
- unit: a fixture SQLite built in the test with the four tables above (links, an asset, a text,
  two users, a note, highlights, a duplicate URL), covering the mapping, `--user`, `--limit`,
  ordering, `--dry-run`, idempotence and the report counts.
- integration, by the review: the 50-bookmark run on a copy of the real database.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/library/importkarakeep.go`, `server/internal/library/importkarakeep_test.go`, `server/internal/library/library.go`, `server/internal/library/service.go`

The destinations this bead imports into are the English `archive` and `stash` values of the
`location` field, which norte-bc7 establishes; `server/internal/library/library.go` and
`server/internal/library/service.go` are also edited by norte-u77 and norte-l57, both of which
block this bead, so the edges that order them are already in place.

title: Decide how Norte reaches a local or subscription LLM without an API key
description:
## Context
Norte talks to a language model in exactly one way today: an HTTP call to an OpenAI-compatible
`/chat/completions` endpoint, configured by `NORTE_LLM_URL`, `NORTE_LLM_MODEL` and
`NORTE_LLM_KEY` and sent as a bearer token (`server/internal/core/llm.go`). The only consumer is
the library classifier, which asks for at most three subject suggestions per saved reading and
requires the answer as JSON matching a schema passed in `response_format: json_schema`.

That shape assumes the person has a paid API key, or a model server that honours structured
output. A single-user, self-hosted app is usually run by someone who already pays for an agent
CLI subscription (`claude -p`, `codex exec` and similar run a prompt non-interactively and print
the answer), or who runs a model locally. Neither is reachable today without standing up a proxy.

Measured on 2026-10-09: the first real provider tried, GLM-5.3 on Ollama Cloud through a litellm
proxy, ignores `response_format` entirely, on the OpenAI-compatible route and on Ollama's native
`format` field alike, and answered in prose. Describing the answer shape in the system prompt made
it comply 6 of 6 times. So "local or alternative LLM" also means "a provider that does not
enforce the schema", and the design has to say how the answer is validated when nothing upstream
enforces it.

This is discovery: no code is written until an option is chosen.

## Options
- **A · Local model server only (Ollama or LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible).** What changes: no new
  code path, only documentation and a tested recipe, because the current HTTP client already
  speaks to `http://localhost:11434/v1`. Costs nothing to build; the person still has to run a
  model server and own hardware able to run a useful model, and quality depends on that model.
- **B · Agent CLI as a second transport (`NORTE_LLM_COMMAND`, e.g. `claude -p --output-format
  json`).** What changes: the server spawns a subprocess per classify call, passes the prompt on
  stdin and parses stdout; uses an existing subscription and needs no key in Norte. Costs a
  subprocess per call (seconds of startup each), a CLI binary and its login inside the runtime
  (impossible in the scratch Docker image as built), and a contract that each CLI vendor can
  change without notice.
- **C · Keep one HTTP transport and document a proxy (litellm or similar) as the way to reach
  CLIs and local models.** What changes: Norte stays one code path; the burden moves to an
  external process the person must run and configure. Costs the person a second service, and the
  proxy may silently drop `response_format`, as measured above.

## What decides it
Whether Norte is expected to run where an agent CLI is installed and logged in (the desktop or
the homelab host directly), or only inside its Docker image. If only the image, B is not
reachable and the choice is between A and C.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One option is chosen and recorded as a comment on this bead, with the reason.
- [ ] If B or C is chosen, an implementation task bead exists with its own acceptance criteria
      and a dependency edge from it to this bead.
- [ ] Done when: the decision comment exists and every follow-up bead it implies is filed.

title: Decide which design observations from the end-to-end run become work
description:
## Outcome
Each design observation below has a destination: a task bead, a decline recorded here with its reason, or a date to look again.

## Context
A full end-to-end run against the built binary, after the ten loop-1 beads merged, produced defect beads (filed separately) and the observations below, which are behaviour working as written but arguably not as wanted. None is a contract violation, which is why each needs a decision rather than a fix.

## Options
- **A · Background worker concurrency.** One worker runs every job kind serially. With a slow LLM each classification holds it for 2 × 30 s (timeout and retry), and new saves waited more than 100 s for extraction in a measurement; expired leases are reclaimed only when the worker is idle. What changes: if taken, a second worker or a separate classification lane; extraction latency no longer depends on the LLM. If declined: a slow or down LLM delays every save's reader view.
- **B · Mock modules on a real server.** Estudo, Revisão and Projetos render demo data on Início and in the sidebar ("Revisar 24 cartões", "Projetos 8") on a real install. What changes: if taken, hide mock-backed modules when the server is real, or label them as previews. If declined: the acceptance walk sees invented content next to real data.
- **C · Library state in the URL.** Sort, the unread filter, the search text and the now/date toggle reset on reload and on back. What changes: if taken, they move into the query string like the shelf and kind already are.
- **D · Server error messages in English inside the Portuguese UI** ("the url must be absolute...", "Failed to fetch"). What changes: if taken, map error codes to Portuguese strings on the client.
- **E · Prefix search.** `reten` finds nothing anywhere; notes search skips highlights and set topics. What changes: if taken, prefix matching on the last word, and two more notes providers.
- **F · Rejected suggestions use a classifier slot.** A rejected pair still counts against the three suggestions on re-classification. What changes: if taken, exclude decided pairs before cutting to three.
- **G · Surpresa draws failed or pending items.** What changes: if taken, draw only `extract_status = done`.
- **H · No way to delete a library item, and notes on a deleted subject stay forever with `source: null`.** What changes: if taken, a delete endpoint with a notes cascade.
- **I · Docker image declares no `HEALTHCHECK` and no `VOLUME /data`.** What changes: if taken, a `norte health` subcommand (the scratch image has no shell) and a volume declaration.
- **J · Phone ergonomics.** 30 px tap targets, no `viewport-fit=cover` (safe-area insets are always 0), `100vh` on the reader, no body scroll lock under the drawer. What changes: if taken, one phone-polish bead after the acceptance walk.
- **K · Dialogs do not close on Escape and set no `aria-modal`; the URL field's browser validation bubble pre-empts the app's Portuguese message.** What changes: if taken, one accessibility bead.

## What decides it
Whether the observation would get in the way of daily use in the first loop. The acceptance walk (`norte-915`) is the natural place to see which of these bite; anything that bites there becomes a task, the rest is declined or dated.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every letter A to K above has exactly one recorded outcome in a comment on this bead: a new bead id, "declined: <reason>", or "look again on <date>".
- [ ] Every outcome that names a bead id names one that exists in this tracker (`br show <id>` succeeds).
- [ ] Every "look again" outcome carries a date no later than 60 days after the comment.
- [ ] Done when: the comment covers all 11 letters and the beads it names are filed.

title: Translate the design system's components to English
description:
## What changes for the user
The shared controls every screen is built from carry Portuguese of their own: a finished module
says `Concluído`, a flashcard's buttons are `De novo` / `Difícil` / `Fácil`, the sync badge says
`Salvo localmente`, the selection toolbar offers `Virar pergunta`, the six-question labels are
`O quê` / `Por quê` / `Quando` / `Onde`, and the cover's tagline is `Uma plataforma de cursos
pessoal, guiada por objetivos.` Those strings appear on every screen that uses the component, so
they are the last Portuguese a person would see after the modules are translated. After this change
the design system speaks English.

## Outcome
Every string in `web/src/components/ds/` outside the gallery is English, and the anchor ids the
margin notes and marks generate are English.

## Context
The design system is used by every module and owned by none, which is why it is a bead of its own
rather than part of any module's: four modules asserting its strings would otherwise all have to
edit it. It depends only on the model bead, for the vocabulary, and it is disjoint from every other
translation bead — no module bead edits `web/src/components/ds/`, and this bead edits nothing
outside it. It can therefore run beside the route and module beads rather than behind them.

The gallery (`web/src/components/ds/gallery/`) is norte-89z, a bead of its own: it is 68 rows of invented sample
content with no component logic, and keeping it out is what holds this bead to the component files.

Three details are not plain string swaps:

- **The anchor pair.** `web/src/components/ds/MarginNote.vue:6` builds the anchor id `nota-<n>` and
  `Mark.vue:6,14` builds the link target `#nota-<note>` and the label `Anotação {note}`. Both sides
  have to move together or a margin note stops being reachable from its mark; that pair is why the
  rename is listed here rather than left alone.
- **The unaccented Portuguese.** `Sem trecho` (`AnnotationItem.vue:25,26`), `Concluído` with its
  unaccented siblings in `MaterialRow.vue:29,32`, `ModuleItem.vue:43` and `TrailPath.vue:14`,
  `Salvo localmente` (`SyncStatus.vue:7`), `Abrir painel` (`SidePanel.vue:37`) and the `Cover.vue:4`
  tagline do not all carry an accent. An accent sweep misses `Cover.vue` entirely, which is why the
  check below is a term list rather than a character class.
- **`TrailPath`'s label.** The component name stays; only the Portuguese status words inside it
  move. The study concept's English name is `Track`, proposed in the inventory and used by
  norte-qst; this bead does not rename the component.

`design/system/components/<Name>/README.md` documents these same components in Portuguese. Those
docs are norte-e7c, not here, because they are documentation rather than code and their diff has no
executable surface to review.

The strings, with their English, are in §1.3 of the inventory comment on norte-3ab.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every string §1.3 lists for `web/src/components/ds/` reads its English replacement:
      `No passage`, `No passage · became a question`, `Highlight only`, `+ Annotate this passage`,
      `Next`, `Again` / `Hard` / `Easy`, `Reading now`, `Done`, `Open the original material`,
      `Now`, `What` / `Why` / `When` / `Where`, `Turn into a question`, `Create a card`,
      `Actions for the selected passage`, `Open the panel`, `Study history`, `more`,
      `Saved locally`, `Offline · saved locally`, `Conflict to review`, and the `Cover.vue`
      tagline.
- [ ] The margin-note anchor id and the mark's link target are both `note-<n>`, the mark's label is
      `Annotation {note}`, and a mark still scrolls to its margin note.
- [ ] The **design-system forbidden-term check** comes back empty:

          rg -n --no-heading -e '[À-ÿ]' \
            -e '(?i)\b(concluido|sem|trecho|virar|pergunta|cartao|cartoes|salvo|localmente|conflito|abrir|painel|proximos|agora|lendo|destaque|anotacao|anotar|nota|historico|mais|dificil|facil|novo|plataforma|cursos|guiada|objetivos|quando|onde)\b' \
            -e 'nota-' \
            web/src/components/ds --glob '!gallery/**'

      with one allowlisted hit, named in the inventory: `QuestionItem.vue`'s `why` key is one of
      the six English question kinds (`what|why|who|when|where|how`) and is not the library's
      renamed field. `Mark`, `Menu` and `Icon` carry no Portuguese.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- component: the existing `web/src/components/ds/*.test.ts` cases, with their assertions on the
  English strings — `Done`, `Again` / `Hard` / `Easy`, `Saved locally`, `Highlight only`,
  `Reading now`. No assertion is deleted to make one pass.
- component: a mark's `href` equals the id its margin note renders, asserted from the rendered
  markup rather than from the prop, so the pair cannot drift.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/components/ds/AnnotationItem.vue`,
`web/src/components/ds/AnnotationItem.test.ts`, `web/src/components/ds/Carousel.vue`,
`web/src/components/ds/Carousel.test.ts`, `web/src/components/ds/Cover.vue`,
`web/src/components/ds/Cover.test.ts`, `web/src/components/ds/Flashcard.vue`,
`web/src/components/ds/Flashcard.test.ts`, `web/src/components/ds/MarginNote.vue`,
`web/src/components/ds/MarginNote.test.ts`, `web/src/components/ds/Mark.vue`,
`web/src/components/ds/Mark.test.ts`, `web/src/components/ds/MaterialRow.vue`,
`web/src/components/ds/MaterialRow.test.ts`, `web/src/components/ds/ModuleItem.vue`,
`web/src/components/ds/ModuleItem.test.ts`, `web/src/components/ds/QuestionItem.vue`,
`web/src/components/ds/QuestionItem.test.ts`, `web/src/components/ds/SelectionToolbar.vue`,
`web/src/components/ds/SelectionToolbar.test.ts`, `web/src/components/ds/SidePanel.vue`,
`web/src/components/ds/StreakGrid.vue`, `web/src/components/ds/SyncStatus.vue`,
`web/src/components/ds/TrailPath.vue`, `web/src/components/ds/TrailPath.test.ts`,
`web/src/components/ds/ExerciseItem.test.ts`,
`web/src/components/ds/Highlight.test.ts`, `web/src/components/ds/Menu.test.ts`
**Shared edits:** `web/src/components/ds/CoverCard.test.ts`,
`web/src/components/ds/CourseRow.test.ts` and
`web/src/components/ds/ds.test.ts`, whose fixtures hard-code `/curriculos/<slug>`, `/estudo` and
`/revisao` as `href` props — those addresses are norte-qst's and norte-v6w's, which own the files.
This bead changes only the Portuguese *strings* in them.
**Reads only:** `design/system/components/`, `web/src/modules/`

## Recovery path
Strings and two anchor ids, no stored data. Reverting the commit restores the previous components.

title: Translate the browser extension's strings to English
description:
## What changes for the user
The browser extension is the only way a page behind a login reaches Norte, and it is entirely
Portuguese: the toolbar button says `Salvar no Norte`, the popup asks `O que vale lembrar?` and
`Vincular a um assunto ou foco`, the settings page says `Conectar ao servidor`, and every failure —
a page that cannot be read, a server that did not answer, a page too large to save — reports in
Portuguese. Both pages even declare `lang="pt-BR"`, which is what a screen reader uses to pick a
voice. After this change the extension is in English, and the note it collects is labelled the way
the app labels it: "Why am I saving this?".

## Outcome
Every string in `extension/` is English — in the manifest, the popup, the settings page, the
service worker and the background script — and both HTML documents declare `lang="en"`.

## Context
The extension is plain ES modules with no bundler and no message catalogue, so each string is a
literal in the file that shows it. Its strings are listed in full in §1.5 of the inventory comment
on norte-3ab, which the rework extended: the first pass missed `lang="pt-BR"` in both documents,
the `O que vale lembrar?` placeholder, the `Salvando…` and `salvo` status words, `Conectar ao
servidor` / `Conectar`, `Servidor conectado.`, `Vincular a um assunto ou foco`, `Buscar assunto`
and `Abrir na biblioteca`. The term check below is what makes that kind of miss visible, because
five of those nine carry no accent.

What is **not** here: the request field and the deep link. `extension/src/service.js:64` builds
`payload.why` and `extension/src/popup.js:21` builds the `/biblioteca/<id>` link, and both are the
model bead's — the contract pins `additionalProperties: false`, so a request still carrying `why`
is refused rather than silently dropped, which means the field and the server have to land
together. By the time this bead runs, the payload says `reason` and the link says `/library/<id>`;
this bead must not change either again. The input element's **id** is still `why`
(`popup.html:10`), and that is this bead's: the id, the label and the placeholder move together.

`extension/manifest.json` carries the extension's own name and description, which are what the
browser shows in its extension list. Changing them is a user-visible rename of an installed
extension; it takes effect on the next load of the unpacked build, and nothing needs reinstalling.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `extension/manifest.json`'s description reads `Save the current page to your Norte library.`
      and its action title `Save to Norte`.
- [ ] `extension/src/popup.html` and `extension/src/settings.html` declare `lang="en"`, and their
      titles read `Save to Norte` and `Configure Norte`.
- [ ] The popup reads `Settings`, `Save the page`, `Why am I saving this?` (the placeholder),
      `Link to a subject or focus (optional)`, `Search for a subject`, `Subject or focus`,
      `No link`, `Save` and `Open in the library`; its status words are `Saving…` and `saved`; and
      the note input's id is `reason`.
- [ ] The settings page reads `Connect to the server`, `Use Norte's address on your computer or
      your network.`, `Server address`, `Connect` and `Server connected.`
- [ ] Every failure message in `extension/src/service.js`, `extension/src/settings.js`,
      `extension/src/background.js` and `extension/src/popup.js` is English, with the wording in
      §1.5.
- [ ] The **extension forbidden-term check** comes back empty:

          rg -n --no-heading \
            -e '[À-ÿ]' -e 'pt-BR' \
            -e '(?i)\b(salvar|salvo|salvando|salve|pagina|biblioteca|configurar|configuracoes|conectar|conectado|servidor|endereco|vincular|vinculos|vinculo|assunto|foco|buscar|abrir|sem|nao|tente|novamente|confira|use|permissao|recusada|senha|caminho|consulta|fragmento|identificacao|lembrar|atual|sua)\b' \
            -e '\bid="why"' -e 'fields\.why' \
            extension/src extension/manifest.json extension/README.md extension/tests

      Nothing in the extension is deliberately Portuguese, so there is no allowlisted hit.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- unit (`bin/ci extension-test`): the extension's own suite, with its assertions on the English
  strings and on the `reason` input id. No assertion is deleted to make one pass.
- unit: the settings page shows `Server connected.` on a successful probe and the English failure
  text on each failure branch.
- e2e (`bin/ci extension-e2e`): the loaded extension against a real temporary Norte server saves a
  cookie-protected fixture page — the same run the model bead uses to prove the `reason` field, now
  reading the popup's English labels.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `extension/manifest.json`, `extension/src/popup.html`, `extension/src/settings.html`,
`extension/src/settings.js`, `extension/src/settings-page.js`, `extension/src/background.js`,
`extension/src/capture.js`, `extension/tests/settings.test.mjs`,
`extension/tests/capture.test.mjs`, `extension/tests/harness.mjs`,
`extension/tests/firefox-smoke.mjs`, `extension/tests/firefox-probe.mjs`
**Shared edits:** `extension/src/popup.js`, `extension/src/service.js`,
`extension/tests/service.test.mjs`, `extension/tests/save.e2e.mjs`, `extension/README.md` (owner
norte-bc7, which blocks this bead — it owns the `reason` field and the `/library/<id>` link in
them; this bead changes only their visible strings and the note input's id)
**Reads only:** `api/openapi/library.yaml`, `extension/build.mjs`, `extension/src/style.css`

## Recovery path
No stored data. If the request field is got wrong the extension fails closed — the contract refuses
the body and the popup shows its error — rather than saving an item with no reason, so a mistake is
visible on the first save rather than discovered later. Reverting the commit restores the previous
build; the installed unpacked extension picks it up on reload.

title: Inventory Norte's Portuguese names and plan its translation to English
description:
## What changes for the user
Norte's screens, addresses and messages are in Portuguese today ("Biblioteca", "Depois", "Salvar
na inbox", `/biblioteca`), and so are many names in its code and data ("depois", "arquivo",
"tudo", "livro"). The person who uses and develops it wants the whole product in English. After
this work every screen, route, message and code identifier is English, and the saved data keeps
working through the change.

## Outcome
A complete inventory of every Portuguese name in Norte, grouped by layer, and the translation,
together with the library's new location model, split into implementation beads with
dependencies, ready to dispatch. This bead writes no
product code.

## Context
Portuguese appears in at least five layers, each with a different cost to change:

- UI strings in the Vue components and the design system (labels, empty states, errors).
- Route paths and route names (`/biblioteca`, `/notas`, the route name `biblioteca`), which are
  also inside saved deep links and the browser extension's "open in Norte" link.
- API contract values in `api/openapi/*.yaml`: enums such as the library views and statuses
  (`inbox`, `depois`, `arquivo`, `tudo`), item kinds (`livro`, `curso`) and query parameters
  (`tipo`, `v`), plus the generated clients and servers (`bin/generate`).
- Stored data: SQLite CHECK constraints and stored values (`status IN ('inbox','depois','arquivo')`
  in `server/internal/library/migrations/00002_library_items.sql`), which need a migration that
  rewrites existing rows.
- Code identifiers, comments and test names in Go and TypeScript.

The English names for the library's concepts were settled on 2026-10-10 and are recorded in the
first comment on this bead (the domain glossary). The inventory uses them; a Portuguese term the
glossary does not cover is listed as "name pending" rather than given an invented name.

The translation also carries the library's new location model, decided on 2026-10-10, because
both touch the same names, contract values and stored values, and doing them apart would
migrate the same rows twice:

- `status` becomes `location`, with five values: `inbox` (arrived, not triaged), `up_next`
  (priority), `later` (someday maybe), `archive` (processed: read or dismissed) and `stash` (kept
  with no intent to consume). Existing rows map `inbox -> inbox`, `depois -> later`,
  `arquivo -> archive`; nothing maps to `up_next` or `stash`.
- The fake "Shortlist" sidebar shortcut (it links to the whole library) is removed; Up Next
  replaces it as a real location.
- The focus-ranked view (`view=now`, "O que ler agora") becomes "Suggestions": it reads every
  location, and lists unread items first and read items after them within the same focus score,
  with the unread-only filter still available. Today it forces `unread=true` server side
  (`server/internal/library/list.go` around line 178, refusal in `now.go` around line 144).
- The queue of item-to-subject links the classifier proposes ("Sugestoes") becomes "Pending
  connections".
- The `why` field becomes `reason`; its form label reads "Why am I saving this?".

The translation is not an internationalisation layer: English replaces Portuguese, with no
message catalogue and no language switch, because there is one user and one language.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A comment on this bead lists every Portuguese user-facing string, route, contract value,
      stored value and code identifier family, grouped by the five layers above, each with its
      file path and its English replacement (or "name pending").
- [ ] Implementation beads exist for the translation, split so that no two share a file, each
      with its own acceptance criteria and blast radius, and wired with `br dep add` so the
      contract and data migration land before the UI that depends on them.
- [ ] The implementation beads include the location model above: the migration from `status` to
      `location` with the value mapping, the two new locations in the contract and UI, the
      Shortlist removal, the Suggestions view reading every location with unread first, the
      Pending connections rename and the `why` to `reason` rename.
- [ ] The tag, routing, domain-rule and Karakeep-import beads filed on 2026-10-10 get a
      dependency edge on the last translation implementation bead, so they are written against
      the English names.
- [ ] The stored-data bead carries a recovery path: the migration's down step, or the backup it
      requires before running.
- [ ] Done when: the inventory comment exists and `br dep cycles` is empty over the new beads.

## Tests
- none owed by this bead (it writes no code); each implementation bead names its own tests.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `.beads/issues.jsonl`
**Reads only:** `web/src/`, `server/internal/`, `api/openapi/`, `extension/src/`

Discovery and planning only: the tracker is the one thing written.

comments.author: gabriel
comments.text:
Domain glossary decided 2026-10-10 (names the translation uses):

Containers: Library (the module); Item (one saved thing); Kind: article, book, paper, video, podcast, newsletter, course.

Locations (field `location`, mutually exclusive; replaces `status`):
- Inbox: arrived, not yet triaged; one of the router's two destinations.
- Up Next: priority, what the person most wants to read soon (replaces the fake "Shortlist").
- Later: someday maybe.
- Archive: processed, read or dismissed.
- Stash: kept with no intent to consume (the Karakeep-style dump); the router's other destination.

Views: All (every location); Suggestions (the focus-ranked list, formerly "O que ler agora", reads every location); Surprise (one random item).
Pending connections: the queue of item-to-subject links the LLM proposed, awaiting accept or reject (formerly "Sugestoes").

Attributes: Read/Unread (independent of location); reason (field and code name; the form label reads "Why am I saving this?"); Note; Highlight, Annotation, Question.

Organizing: Subject (few, curated); Focus; Link (suggested, confirmed, rejected; any location can carry links, Archive and Stash included); Tag (new: 5-8 per item, automatic, English, normalized, editable); Router (new: at save, Inbox or Stash; domain rule, then Laya or an LLM, then Inbox); Domain rule (new).

Pipeline: Snapshot, Extraction, Classifier.

comments.author: gabriel
comments.text:
Inventory of every Portuguese name in Norte, with the English it becomes, grouped by the five
layers, plus the library's new location model. Taken on 2026-10-10 at `3f35f4e`.

## How this was taken, and how to retake it

Every row below was produced from the working tree, not from memory. The sweep is a literal and
text-node extractor rather than a plain grep, because a Portuguese label with no accent and no
stopword (`Tudo`, `Livros`, `Salvar`) does not match an accent class, and an English comment full
of `no`, `as` and `do` matches a stopword class. The extractor reads every quoted literal, every
template text node and every bare template line, and keeps the ones holding an accented character
or a word from the domain list:

    # candidates in one file or directory, as file:line:kind:text
    rg -l '' --glob '*.vue' --glob '*.ts' <dir> | xargs python3 extract.py

It found 4,622 candidate rows over 363 files, of which 1,551 rows over 228 files carry an accented
character and are therefore Portuguese beyond doubt. The remainder are the unaccented labels and
the false positives (`material`, `site`, `post`, `nota` are also English or already-English
identifiers), which is why this inventory names rather than counts wherever a name crosses a file
boundary.

**What is enumerated verbatim, with its English:** every route, route name, query parameter and
query value; every contract value; every stored value; every CLI flag; every label, tab, sort
option, empty state and error message that more than one file names or that a test asserts; every
Portuguese code identifier; and every Portuguese string in the extension, which is small and

## Layer 3 — Contract values in `api/openapi/*.yaml`

The contract is the hinge of the whole translation. `web/src/modules/library/data/source.ts` makes
the web's types *be* the contract's types — deliberately, and the file says why: "Nothing here is
renamed on the way in. A field called `saved_at` on the wire stays `saved_at` in the screens,
because a view that reads `savedAt` is a view that cannot be checked against
`api/openapi/library.yaml` by eye." There is therefore no rename seam between the wire and the
screens, and `web/package.json`'s `build` script runs `vue-tsc` which the gate's `generate` check
runs, so a contract value cannot change in one pull request and reach the screens in another
without a red gate in between. That is what forces the first implementation bead to be

**Applied migrations are never edited** — `00002_library_items.sql` says so in its own header, and
the repo's rule is the same. So none of the rows above is an edit to `00002` or `00003`: they are
the *current* state, and the change is a new `00004_library_location.sql` that rewrites the table.
SQLite cannot alter a `CHECK` constraint, and an FTS5 column cannot be renamed, so `00004` is a
full rebuild: create `library_items_new` with the English columns and the five-value check, copy
every row through the value mapping, drop the old table, rename, recreate the four indexes, drop
and recreate `library_fts` and its three triggers, repopulate the FTS table from the copied rows.

Nothing in `core` or `notes` stores a library location or kind: `core_items` holds a module name, a
type string and a title, and `core_links` has a `status` of its own (`suggested`/`confirmed`/
`rejected`) which this translation does not touch. The one place a library kind reaches core is as
the registry `type` value written by the library (`server/internal/library/service.go:268,291`,
`"post"`), which means the kind rename rewrites `core_items.type` for library rows too — the
migration has to cover that, and it is the only cross-module row rewrite in the whole change.

Three terms have no glossary entry and no obvious literal, so no bead invents one:

   `MaterialView.vue:154,219`, and `TestVirarPerguntaFromAnAnnotation`). The glossary has Question
   and Highlight as attributes but no verb for the conversion. Proposed `Turn into a question` and

## The location model, concretely

What the implementation beads carry, restated as the mechanics each one needs:

1. **The stored mapping.** `inbox -> inbox`, `depois -> later`, `arquivo -> archive`. Nothing maps
   to `up_next` or `stash`, so both arrive empty, and the migration asserts that afterwards no row
   holds a value outside the five.
2. **The kinds.** `post -> article`, `livro -> book`, `curso -> course`, in `library_items.kind`
   and in `core_items.type` for the registry rows the library wrote (`module = 'library'`). The
   library's migration is what rewrites the core rows, because the library is what wrote those
   values and core only stores what a module hands it; the alternative — a core migration that
   knows a library value — puts the knowledge in the wrong module. This is the only cross-owner
   write in the change and the bead says so in a comment.
3. **`why -> reason`,** in the column, in the FTS table, in the three FTS triggers, in the bm25
   weight order documented at `migrations/00002_library_items.sql:72`, in the contract, in the CLI
   flag and in the Telegram capture.
4. **Shortlist goes.** `web/src/modules/library/index.ts:82-89` removes the shortcut whose
   `to` is `v=tudo` and whose count borrows the whole library's; Up Next takes its place as a real
   location with its own count.
5. **Suggestions.** Today `view=now` forces `unread=true` at `server/internal/library/list.go:178`
   and refuses `unread=false` at `server/internal/library/now.go:144-147`. After the change it reads
   every location, lists unread before read **within one focus score**, and keeps the unread-only
   filter as an ordinary `unread=true`. That is a new sort key, so the cursor grows a level: the
   predicate at `server/internal/library/list.go:329-336` is three levels deep (score, saved_at,
   id) and becomes four (score, unread, saved_at, id), and `libraryCursorFor` at
   `server/internal/library/list.go:344-360` has to carry the unread flag it pages on. A cursor
   that pages by score alone across a run of equal scores would restart the unread run.
6. **Pending connections.** The `Sugestões` tab becomes `Pending connections`, and the `v=sugestoes`
   query value becomes `v=pending-connections`. The rename matters more than it looks: without it
   the screen would have a `Suggestions` view and a `Suggestions` tab meaning different things.

---

## The implementation beads, and why the split is shaped this way

Eleven beads, filed on 2026-10-10. The chain is the point: `web/src/shell/AppShell.test.ts`
asserts the sidebar labels that *every* module contributes, so a file-disjoint split is
impossible for the module beads, and what keeps two agents off that file is the dependency edge
rather than a promise.

    norte-bc7  the library's location model and English names, end to end     L / critical
      |-- norte-vz5  Suggestions reads every location, unread first            M / reasoning
      |-- norte-2vx  the design system and its gallery                         M / mechanical
      |-- norte-6vs  every remaining Portuguese route, and its links           M / reasoning
            |-- norte-2vz  the browser extension                               S / mechanical
            |-- norte-bb4  the Notes module and its contract keys              M / mechanical
                  |-- norte-wli  the Projects module                           M / mechanical
                        |-- norte-qst  the Study module                        M / mechanical
                              |-- norte-v6w  the Review module                 S / mechanical
                                    |-- norte-05j  the shell and the palette   M / mechanical
    norte-547  make English the repo's own convention   S / mechanical
               (depends on vz5, 2vx, 2vz and 05j, so it is the last one)

Three decisions behind that shape:

**The first bead is end-to-end rather than per-layer, and that is forced.** Splitting the contract
from the server from the screens would be the obvious shape, and it cannot be green:
`web/src/modules/library/data/source.ts` makes the web's types be the contract's types on purpose,
`web/package.json`'s `build` runs `vue-tsc`, and the gate's `generate` check runs that build. A
contract value renamed without the screens following in the same pull request is a red gate. So
`api/openapi/library.yaml`, the migration, `server/internal/library/` and
`web/src/modules/library/` move in one bead.

**The location model travels with the translation rather than after it.** Both rewrite
`library_items`, and SQLite cannot alter a `CHECK` constraint or rename an FTS5 column, so each
would be a full table rebuild. Doing them apart means migrating the person's whole library twice
for one outcome.

**Routes are their own bead, after the library.** A route path is produced in three places — the
Vue router, the Go search and notification paths, and the extension's deep link — and only the
whole set is consistent. Renaming them inside the module beads would mean each module half-fixing
the server, and a link that still points at `/notas` compiles, passes its own test and is simply
wrong.

**The five beads filed on 2026-10-10** — norte-u77 (tagging), norte-ff8 (tags in the library),
norte-l57 (the router), norte-6ty (domain rules) and norte-23h (the Karakeep import) — now depend
on norte-547 rather than on this bead, so each of them is written against the English names
rather than against a vocabulary that is about to move under it. `br dep cycles` is empty over the
whole graph.

## How this was taken, and how to retake it

Every row below was produced from the working tree, not from memory. The sweep is a literal and
text-node extractor rather than a plain grep, because a Portuguese label with no accent and no
stopword (`Tudo`, `Livros`, `Salvar`) does not match an accent class, and an English comment full
of `no`, `as` and `do` matches a stopword class. The extractor reads every quoted literal, every
template text node and every bare template line, and keeps the ones holding an accented character
or a word from the domain list:

    # candidates in one file or directory, as file:line:kind:text
    rg -l '' --glob '*.vue' --glob '*.ts' <dir> | xargs python3 extract.py

It found 4,622 candidate rows over 363 files, of which 1,551 rows over 228 files carry an accented
character and are therefore Portuguese beyond doubt. The remainder are the unaccented labels and
the false positives (`material`, `site`, `post`, `nota` are also English or already-English
identifiers), which is why this inventory names rather than counts wherever a name crosses a file
boundary.

**What is enumerated verbatim, with its English:** every route, route name, query parameter and
query value; every contract value; every stored value; every CLI flag; every label, tab, sort
option, empty state and error message that more than one file names or that a test asserts; every
Portuguese code identifier; and every Portuguese string in the extension, which is small and
entirely user-facing.

**What is enumerated by file, line count and the command that lists it:** the body copy inside a
single component and the mock content ported from the design prototypes — `MaterialReader.vue`'s
invented book chapter, `study/mock/curricula.ts`, `projects/mock/life.ts`, `review/mock/cards.ts`,
`DsGallery.vue`'s sample data. Those sentences cross no boundary, no test asserts them by text,
and a translation written here would be a second copy of the product's prose that rots the moment
a component changes. The bead that owns the file translates them in place, and the per-file counts
below are what makes that checkable: the file is done when the sweep over it comes back empty.

The English names come from the domain glossary decided on 2026-10-10 (the first comment on this
bead). A Portuguese term the glossary does not cover and that is not an obvious literal is listed
as **name pending** and collected in the last section.

## Layer 3 — Contract values in `api/openapi/*.yaml`

The contract is the hinge of the whole translation. `web/src/modules/library/data/source.ts` makes
the web's types *be* the contract's types — deliberately, and the file says why: "Nothing here is
renamed on the way in. A field called `saved_at` on the wire stays `saved_at` in the screens,
because a view that reads `savedAt` is a view that cannot be checked against
`api/openapi/library.yaml` by eye." There is therefore no rename seam between the wire and the
screens, and `web/package.json`'s `build` script runs `vue-tsc` which the gate's `generate` check
runs, so a contract value cannot change in one pull request and reach the screens in another
without a red gate in between. That is what forces the first implementation bead to be
end-to-end rather than per-layer.

**Applied migrations are never edited** — `00002_library_items.sql` says so in its own header, and
the repo's rule is the same. So none of the rows above is an edit to `00002` or `00003`: they are
the *current* state, and the change is a new `00004_library_location.sql` that rewrites the table.

full rebuild: create `library_items_new` with the English columns and the five-value check, copy
every row through the value mapping, drop the old table, rename, recreate the four indexes, drop
and recreate `library_fts` and its three triggers, repopulate the FTS table from the copied rows.

type string and a title, and `core_links` has a `status` of its own (`suggested`/`confirmed`/

the registry `type` value written by the library (`server/internal/library/service.go:268,291`,
`"post"`), which means the kind rename rewrites `core_items.type` for library rows too — the
migration has to cover that, and it is the only cross-module row rewrite in the whole change.

## The location model, concretely

What the implementation beads carry, restated as the mechanics each one needs:

1. **The stored mapping.** `inbox -> inbox`, `depois -> later`, `arquivo -> archive`. Nothing maps
   to `up_next` or `stash`, so both arrive empty, and the migration asserts that afterwards no row
   holds a value outside the five.
2. **The kinds.** `post -> article`, `livro -> book`, `curso -> course`, in `library_items.kind`
   and in `core_items.type` for the registry rows the library wrote (`module = 'library'`). The
   library's migration is what rewrites the core rows, because the library is what wrote those
   values and core only stores what a module hands it; the alternative — a core migration that
   knows a library value — puts the knowledge in the wrong module. This is the only cross-owner
   write in the change and the bead says so in a comment.
3. **`why -> reason`,** in the column, in the FTS table, in the three FTS triggers, in the bm25
   weight order documented at `migrations/00002_library_items.sql:72`, in the contract, in the CLI
   flag and in the Telegram capture.
4. **Shortlist goes.** `web/src/modules/library/index.ts:82-89` removes the shortcut whose
   `to` is `v=tudo` and whose count borrows the whole library's; Up Next takes its place as a real
   location with its own count.
5. **Suggestions.** Today `view=now` forces `unread=true` at `server/internal/library/list.go:178`
   and refuses `unread=false` at `server/internal/library/now.go:144-147`. After the change it reads
   every location, lists unread before read **within one focus score**, and keeps the unread-only
   filter as an ordinary `unread=true`. That is a new sort key, so the cursor grows a level: the
   predicate at `server/internal/library/list.go:329-336` is three levels deep (score, saved_at,
   id) and becomes four (score, unread, saved_at, id), and `libraryCursorFor` at
   `server/internal/library/list.go:344-360` has to carry the unread flag it pages on. A cursor
   that pages by score alone across a run of equal scores would restart the unread run.
6. **Pending connections.** The `Sugestões` tab becomes `Pending connections`, and the `v=sugestoes`
   query value becomes `v=pending-connections`. The rename matters more than it looks: without it
   the screen would have a `Suggestions` view and a `Suggestions` tab meaning different things.

## 7. Forbidden-term checks, and the allowlist

"Every string in this directory is English" is not a criterion. It cannot be run, two people read
it differently, and the sweep that stood behind it — a class of accented characters — misses
`Tudo`, `Livros`, `Salvar`, `hoje`, `ontem`, `Conectar`, `Sem trecho`, `pt-BR` and the whole of
`Cover.vue`. So each bead now carries a **forbidden-term command** over the paths it owns, built
from the vocabulary this inventory enumerates for those paths, and its criterion is that the
command returns nothing outside a named allowlist. The commands are in the beads; what follows is
the vocabulary they are drawn from and the allowlist they are written against.

### 7.1 The term vocabulary

Four groups. A bead takes the terms that can appear in its paths, never the whole list — a check
that flags `assunto` inside the Review module is a check nobody runs twice.
