  `biblioteca`, `leitor`, `notas`, `projetos`, `projeto`, `decisao`, `tarefa`, `revisao`,
  `estudo`, `curriculo`, `nao-encontrado`, `modulo-desligado`.
- **Unaccented words**, the group the first sweep could not see: `tudo`, `livro`, `livros`,
  `curso`, `cursos`, `salvar`, `salvo`, `salvando`, `conectar`, `conectado`, `hoje`, `ontem`,
  `sem`, `trecho`, `nada`, `nenhum`, `nenhuma`, `abrir`, `fechar`, `buscar`, `carregar`, `tentar`,
  `voltar`, `anotar`, `anotacoes`, `perguntas`, `conjuntos`, `concluido`, `dificil`, `facil`,
  `expandir`, `recolher`, `preferencias`, `inicio`, `galeria`, `trilha`, `tarefa`, `tarefas`,
  `decisoes`, `assunto`, `assuntos`, `nova`, `novo`, `proximo`, `pagina`, `servidor`, `endereco`,
  `vincular`, `vinculo`, `vinculos`, `permissao`, `identificacao`.
- **Locales**: `pt-BR` anywhere — an `Intl` argument, an `html lang` attribute, a
  `toLocaleLowerCase` call.

And the accent class `[À-ÿ]` as a backstop, which catches the prose the term lists cannot
enumerate. It is a backstop, not the check: every bead runs both.

### 7.2 The allowlist — where Portuguese is deliberate

Each entry has a reason, and a sweep that flags one of these has found a feature, not a defect.
norte-547 writes this list into `AGENTS.md` so that the next sweep, by a person or an agent, does
not "fix" it.

| path | what | why it stays |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `server/internal/library/cleanup.go:25-32` | `anterior\|pr[oó]ximo\|pr[oó]xima\|segui[nd]te`, `inscreva-se\|assine\|receba .{0,30}(e-?mail\|caixa de entrada)` | the extractor's cleanup rules match both languages, and the file says so: "Portuguese and English both, because Norte reads both". Dropping the Portuguese arms would stop the previous/next strip and the subscription pitch being removed from Portuguese pages |
| `server/internal/library/testdata/pages/wikipedia-article.html` and its siblings | captured input pages, 22 accented rows in the Wikipedia one | what language a saved page is in is not a property of Norte; these are fixtures of the world, not of the product |
| `server/internal/core/slug.go:18` | the comment "which is how `programacao` finds `Programação`" | a comment that demonstrates accent stripping cannot demonstrate it in English |
| `server/internal/library/extractor.go:288` | the comment "what turns `Instalação` into `instalacao`" | the same |
| `server/internal/notes/list.go:159,186`, `server/internal/notes/search.go:45` | comments quoting `MEMÓRIA`, `memoria`, `memória` | the same |
| `web/src/search/index.ts:22-28` | `normalize`'s NFD decomposition and `[̀-ͯ]` strip | a saved item's title can be in any language, so the comparison has to be accent-insensitive. Only the `toLocaleLowerCase('pt-BR')` argument changes, to `'en'` |
| `web/src/components/ds/QuestionItem.vue:6`, `web/src/modules/notes/data/source.ts:27` | `QuestionKind` includes `'why'` | one of the six English question words (`what\|why\|who\|when\|where\|how`), not the library's renamed field. Every `why` check excludes it |
| `web/src/modules/projects/views/ProjectView/TaskDialog.vue:10,45,67`, `web/src/modules/projects/views/AreaView.vue:388,907` | the task's own `why` prop and the `.task-why` class | Projects' own model, already English. The glossary's `why -> reason` is about the library item's field |
| `server/internal/core/files_test.go:200-216` | `why string` as a test helper's parameter | an English parameter name |

Any other hit is a defect. norte-547's final criterion is that the repo-wide sweep returns the
allowlist and nothing else, **and that anything else is fixed there rather than named in the pull
request** — the previous plan allowed the latter, which turned the one check that proves the
translation finished into a note.

---

## 8. The names that were pending, now proposed

The first pass left three terms open. An open name is a string that never gets translated, so each
is now a **proposal** — chosen here, used by the beads, and cheap to revise later because each is
one or two labels.

1. **`Material`** — *proposed: keep `Material`.* The word is identical in both languages. The
   glossary's containers are Library / Item / Kind, and "material" is a fourth word for the same
   thing, but folding it into Item is a product decision about a screen and a route
   (`/material/:kind/:id`, `MaterialView`, `MaterialReader`, `MaterialRow`, `material-*` CSS
   classes), not a translation. Every bead leaves it as `material`.
2. **`Trilha` / `TrailPath`** — *proposed: the concept is a `Track`; the component keeps its name.*
   `Trilha` appears as the gallery's `Trilha de redes` and as the already-English design-system
   component `TrailPath`. `Track` reads naturally for a named sequence of modules inside a
   curriculum, and it is what norte-qst uses for the visible label. `TrailPath` is **not** renamed:
   it is a shared control, the rename would touch its README, its preview, its test and every
   importer, and nothing behaves differently afterwards. If a later study-module bead decides the
   concept is a path or a trail, changing one label is a one-line change; leaving it Portuguese
   is not, which is why this is settled rather than deferred.
3. **`Virar pergunta` / `Virar cartão`** — *proposed: `Turn into a question` and `Create a card`,
   with `TurnInto` as the Go and TypeScript identifier.* The glossary has Question and Highlight as
   attributes but no verb for the conversion. The visible labels are norte-2vx's
   (`SelectionToolbar.vue:3`) and norte-3em's (`MaterialView.vue:154,219`); the identifier is
   norte-bb4's, which renames `TestVirarHighlightOnASavedSelection` to
   `TestTurnAHighlightIntoAQuestionOnASavedSelection` and `TestVirarPerguntaFromAnAnnotation` to
   `TestTurnAnAnnotationIntoAQuestion`. One verb in the label and in the identifier, or neither.

---

## 9. One owner per file, and the shared files that remain

The rule the first split claimed — "no two beads share a file" — cannot hold for this change, and
pretending otherwise is what produced six beads all editing `web/src/shell/AppShell.test.ts`. The
reason is structural: that file asserts the sidebar labels *every* module contributes, so every
module's translation breaks it, and the gate runs `vitest` over it. A file-disjoint split would
require either one enormous bead or weakening those assertions, and the assertions are there to
catch exactly what the translation changes.

So the convention is explicit instead:

- **`**Edits:**` lists the files the bead changes that no other bead touches.** No file appears
  under `**Edits:**` in two beads. That is checkable, and it holds across all thirteen.
- **`**Shared edits:**` lists the files it changes that another bead also changes**, naming the
  owner and the direction of the edge. A bead's blast radius is `**Edits:** ∪ **Shared edits:**`.
- **Every shared file has a dependency edge ordering its editors.** A shared edit with no edge is
  how two green branches break when they meet, and that is the failure this convention exists to
  prevent.
- **The owner is the first bead to touch the file.** Not the one with the biggest diff: the point
  of ownership is collision avoidance, and the first toucher is the one whose change the others
  build on.

The files that are genuinely shared, with the order of their editors:

| file | editors, in order |
| --- | --- |
| `web/src/shell/AppShell.test.ts` | bc7 → 3em → 6vs → bb4 → wli → qst → v6w → **05j (owner)** |
| `web/src/shell/HomeView.test.ts` | bc7 → 3em → **05j (owner)** |
| `web/src/shell/sidebar.test.ts` | bc7 → 6vs → bb4 → qst → v6w → **05j (owner)** |
| `web/src/shell/ShellOverlay.test.ts`, `SubjectView.test.ts`, `SavedAboutPanel.test.ts`, `drawer.test.ts`, `moduleMount.test.ts`, `data/apiSource.test.ts` | bc7 → 6vs → **05j (owner)** |
| `web/src/search/index.test.ts` | bc7 → **05j (owner)** |
| `web/e2e/phone-walk.spec.ts`, `library-search-sort.spec.ts`, `csp.spec.ts`, `reader-reading-position.spec.ts`, `highlight-anchoring.spec.ts`, `shell-boot.spec.ts` | **bc7** or **6vs** → **05j (owner)** |
| every file under `web/src/modules/library/` that holds both a value and copy | **bc7 (owner)** → 3em |
| `web/src/modules/study/views/StudyHomeView.vue`, `StudyHomeView.test.ts` | **bc7 (owner)** → 6vs → bb4 → v6w → qst |
| `web/src/modules/study/views/CurriculumView/curriculum.ts` | **bc7 (owner)** → qst |
| `web/src/modules/review/views/ReviewView.vue`, `ReviewView.test.ts` | **bc7 (owner)** → 6vs → qst → v6w |
| `web/src/modules/projects/views/DecisionView.vue` | **bc7 (owner)** → wli |
| `web/src/modules/notes/views/NotesView.vue`, `data/testing.ts`, `server/internal/notes/search.go`, `search_test.go`, `testenv_test.go` | **bc7 (owner)** → bb4 |
| `web/src/modules/library/views/MaterialView/MaterialExercises.vue` | **bc7 (owner)** → 3em → bb4 |
| `extension/src/popup.js`, `src/service.js`, `tests/service.test.mjs`, `tests/save.e2e.mjs`, `README.md` | **bc7 (owner)** → 2vz |
| `web/src/components/ds/ds.test.ts`, `CoverCard.test.ts`, `CourseRow.test.ts` | **2vx (owner)** → qst → v6w |
| each module's `index.ts`, for `kind: 'tela'` only | **that module's bead (owner)** → 05j |
| `docs/tools/ci-checks.md` | **05j (owner)** → 547, only if the final sweep finds something |

---

## 10. The implementation beads, rebuilt

Thirteen beads. norte-vz5 is closed as superseded: the Suggestions behaviour could not be separated
from the model slice, because the unread forcing, the `ORDER BY` and the four-level cursor
predicate all live in `server/internal/library/list.go`, which the location filter rewrites anyway,
and `view=now -> view=suggestions` is a contract value of the same bead.

    norte-bc7   the library's model, wire and Suggestions behaviour, end to end    L / critical
      |
      +-- norte-3em   the Library module's copy                                    M / mechanical
      |     +-- norte-6vs   the shell's routes and the subject route               M / reasoning
      |           +-- norte-bb4   Notes: routes, contract keys, copy               M / mechanical
      |                 +-- norte-wli   Projects: routes and copy                  M / mechanical
      |                       +-- norte-qst   Study: routes and copy               M / mechanical
      |                             +-- norte-v6w   Review: route and copy         S / mechanical
      |                                   +-- norte-05j   shell, palette, dates,   L / mechanical
      |                                                   and the reconciliation
      +-- norte-2vx   the design system's components                               M / mechanical
      |     +-- norte-89z   the component gallery                                  S / mechanical
      |     +-- norte-e7c   the design system's documentation                       M / mechanical
      +-- norte-2vz   the browser extension's strings                              M / mechanical

    norte-547   make English the convention, and prove the translation finished    S / mechanical
                (depends on 05j, 2vz, 89z and e7c — the four leaves)

### What is parallel, and what is not

**Four beads run beside the chain:** norte-2vx, norte-89z, norte-e7c and norte-2vz. The design
system is used by every module and owned by none, and the extension is its own tree; none of them
touches a file the chain touches, except the three design-system test fixtures that hard-code a
`/curriculos` or `/revisao` `href`, which is why norte-qst and norte-v6w depend on norte-2vx.

**The UI chain cannot be parallelised, and the reason is one file.**
`web/src/shell/AppShell.test.ts` and `web/src/shell/sidebar.test.ts` assert the sidebar labels and
route names that every module contributes. Any module whose labels change breaks them. Making the
module beads parallel would mean either deleting those assertions, which is the coverage the
translation most needs, or splitting the files per module, which is a change to the repo's test
architecture made for the convenience of a plan. So the module beads are chained, on purpose, and
§9 records the order.

### Routes are folded into each module's bead

The first split had one route bead for everything outside the library, and it was both too large to
review and incomplete — §2.5 lists the nine producers it missed, every one of them a hard-coded
`RouterLink` inside a view. A route path is produced in the module's `routes`, in its
`manifest.routePaths`, in the breadcrumbs and links of its own screens, and in the Go paths its own
server package builds; all of those are that module's files. So each module's bead renames its own
routes and its own copy in one diff, and the only cross-module references — a study screen linking
to Notes, a review screen linking to the home — are the declared shared edits in §9.

The library's routes stay in norte-bc7 rather than getting a bead: the files that produce them
(`web/src/modules/library/index.ts`, three other modules' views, the Go search and Telegram paths,
the extension's deep link, five end-to-end specs) are files norte-bc7 already rewrites for the
values, and a separate bead would share all of them.

### The two beads that exceed the reviewability guideline, and why

Every bead is held to about 25 edited files except two, and in both cases the number is a property
of the gate rather than of the split:

- **norte-bc7, about 70 files.** The gate runs `vue-tsc --build` over `src/**/*` and `e2e/**/*`,
  `vitest run`, `go test ./...` and the extension's real-server end-to-end suite, all in one run.
  Every file in §3.1 holds a value the contract rename invalidates, and a contract value that
  changes without its consumers is a red gate. The only alternative is an expand/contract
  migration — a transitional contract carrying both spellings, so consumers move in small beads —
  and it costs two rebuilds of the table holding the person's whole library, plus a long window in
  which a bead can "pass" by using the Portuguese spelling. For one user and one library, the
  atomic slice is the cheaper risk. It is reviewable layer by layer: the criteria are grouped
  contract, migration, server, wire, behaviour, UI.
- **norte-e7c, about 50 files.** Documentation under `design/system/`: no executable line, no
  contract, no stored value, no test. The guideline bounds how much *risk* one review carries, and
  this diff carries none; the term check in its criteria is mechanical and complete.

### The five beads filed on 2026-10-10

norte-u77 (tagging), norte-ff8 (tags in the library), norte-l57 (the router), norte-6ty (domain
rules) and norte-23h (the Karakeep import) depend on norte-547, so each is written against the
English names rather than a vocabulary about to move under it. Two pairs among them share files and
now carry a direct edge as well, because an edge is the only thing that keeps two agents off a
file: **norte-l57 depends on norte-u77** (both edit `server/internal/library/migrations/`,
`extract.go` and `library.go`), and **norte-6ty depends on norte-ff8** (both edit
`web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue` and `web/src/modules/library/index.ts`). Their
migration numbers are now fixed rather than "the next number free": norte-bc7 takes `00004`,
norte-u77 `00005`, norte-l57 `00006` and norte-6ty `00007` in the library, and norte-6vs takes
`00003` in the core. `br dep cycles` is empty over the whole graph.

**Amendment to the inventory comment immediately above.** Everything there stands; §9's shared-file
table gains four rows and corrects two, after the ownership check below was run over the tracker
rather than over the prose.

The check, which anyone can rerun from the repository root, extracts every backticked path from
each translation bead's `**Edits:**` block and reports a path claimed by two beads:

    python3 - <<'EOF'
    import json, re, collections
    beads = ['norte-bc7','norte-3em','norte-6vs','norte-bb4','norte-wli','norte-qst','norte-v6w',
             'norte-05j','norte-2vx','norte-89z','norte-e7c','norte-2vz','norte-547']
    owners = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for line in open('.beads/issues.jsonl'):
        d = json.loads(line)
        if d.get('id') not in beads: continue
        desc = d['description']
        start = desc.index('**Edits:**')
        end = min(e for e in (desc.find(t, start) for t in
                  ('**Shared edits','**Regenerates','**Reads only')) if e != -1)
        for p in re.findall(r'`([^`]+)`', desc[start:end]):
            if p.startswith(('web/','server/','api/','extension/','design/','docs/')) \
               or p in ('AGENTS.md','CLAUDE.md'):
                owners[p].append(d['id'])
    dups = {k: v for k, v in owners.items() if len(v) > 1}
    print('Edits paths:', len(owners), '| duplicates:', len(dups))
    for k, v in sorted(dups.items()): print('  ', k, '->', v)

| file | correction |

Two further notes on the checks in §7, from running them:

  numbers to drive to the allowlist, and each bead's pull request quotes its own.
- **An allowlist entry only matters to the checks that can reach it.** norte-bc7's pattern set is
  values and fields, so the only allowlist entry it can hit is `payload.why` in
  `web/src/modules/projects/views/ProjectView.vue:201` — the task's own `why`, Projects' model,

title: Add the module registry and GET /api/config
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing visible yet, but this is what makes Norte four apps that can be used one at a time. After this lands, starting the server with only some products switched on gives an install that has only those products: their tables, their routes, their commands, nothing else. A typo in the list of products stops the server at startup with the bad name in the message instead of running with a product silently missing.

## Outcome
A module registry: the `Module` interface, `NORTE_MODULES` parsing, and mounting of each enabled module's migrations (core first, each module in its own goose version table), HTTP routes, CLI commands, job handlers, focus providers and search providers. `GET /api/config` reports what is enabled. A `library` module stub with one migration exercises the whole path.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. `server/` is its Go backend: one static binary, SQLite, goose migrations, sqlc queries, an OpenAPI contract per module under `api/openapi/` from which `bin/generate` produces strict-server Go interfaces into `server/gen/api/<module>/` and TypeScript types into `web/src/api/<module>.d.ts`. The always-on part that is not a module is the "core" (`server/internal/core/`), which already has the database, the item registry, links, subjects, the jobs table and the file store.

Products are modules switched on by configuration. Each module owns tables prefixed with its name, and no foreign key crosses a module boundary; relations between modules go through the core's `core_links` table by global id. Products and modules are not one to one: the products are library, study, review and projects, and `notes` is a fifth module both library and study write into, so highlights survive either being disabled.

The interface, decided (package `app`, `server/internal/app/`):

```go
type Module interface {
    Name() string                                   // "library"
    Migrations() fs.FS                              // embedded from internal/<name>/migrations/
    Register(r *Router, deps Deps)                  // routes under /api/<name>/
    Commands() []*cobra.Command                     // subcommands
    JobHandlers() map[string]core.JobHandler        // job kinds this module runs
    Start(ctx context.Context) error                // long-running adapters; called by serve only
    Text(ctx context.Context, id string) (string, bool, error) // readable text of an item this module owns
    FocusTargets(ctx context.Context) ([]core.FocusTarget, error)
    SearchEntries(ctx context.Context, q string, limit int) ([]core.SearchEntry, error)
}
```

Rules this bead implements:

- `NORTE_MODULES` is comma-separated; names are trimmed, a duplicate keeps its first occurrence, an empty entry inside a non-empty list is an error, and the configured order is the order of migrations and of `/api/config`'s list. Its default is every module compiled into the binary. An empty value (`NORTE_MODULES=`) means no module, core only. A name the binary does not know fails startup with a non-zero exit and the name in the message.
- `main` reads the setting, instantiates the named modules and mounts routes, commands and job handlers. Migrations run only in `norte migrate` and at the start of `norte serve`: core first, then each module in the order listed. Each module has its own goose version table, `goose_<module>`, because one shared table would make two modules' migration numbers collide. A disabled module leaves its tables untouched if they exist from an earlier run and creates none if they do not.
- **Adapter lifecycle.** After migrations and route wiring, `norte serve` runs every enabled module's `Start` concurrently under one child context. The first error that is not a cancellation cancels the others and makes `serve` exit non-zero; SIGTERM cancels the context and waits for the adapters within the shared 15 s drain.
- `GET /api/config` (declared in `api/openapi/core.yaml`, the core's contract) returns `{modules: [...], version, llm: bool, telegram: bool, timezone}`: `llm` is true when `NORTE_LLM_URL` is set, `telegram` when `NORTE_TELEGRAM_TOKEN` is set, `timezone` is the IANA name of `NORTE_TIMEZONE` (default: the system zone). The frontend mounts only what is listed.
- The `Deps` passed to `Register` carry what the core offers at this point — the database handles, `*core.Jobs` (the queue from the worker bead), `core.Files` and `core.Clock` — so a module never reaches for a global. The extraction bead adds the event bus to `Deps` when it creates the bus.
- **Boundary types and provider interfaces live in the core, and the core never imports `app`.** `app.Module` refers to core types, so the reverse import would be a cycle. This bead creates `server/internal/core/providers.go` with the value types `core.FocusTarget{ID, Type, Title}` and `core.SearchEntry{ID, Module, Type, Title, Subtitle, Path, Score}` (`Score` a finite float in [0, 1]) and the narrow interfaces `core.TextProvider`, `core.FocusProvider` and `core.SearchProvider` (each one method, matching the `Module` methods). `app.Router` wraps the server's `*http.ServeMux` with a prefix: `Register` receives one scoped to `/api/<name>/`, and a pattern outside it panics at startup with the pattern in the message. The registry hands the enabled modules to the core at startup as `map[string]core.TextProvider` keyed by module name (so `core.Text` can route by `core_items.module`) and as `[]core.FocusProvider` and `[]core.SearchProvider`; the core's text, focus and search services (built by later beads) receive them by injection. `core.Job` and `core.JobHandler` are the jobs worker bead's types, and this bead depends on it: after instantiating the modules, `main` calls `core.Jobs.Register(kind, handler)` for every entry of every enabled module's `JobHandlers()`, before the worker starts.
- The `library` stub: a `server/internal/library/` package implementing `Module` with one trivial migration (for example a `library_meta` table) and no routes, so the mounting, the separate goose table and the enable/disable behaviour are exercised before the real library lands. The real library bead drops that table in its own, next migration.
- Mounting of `FocusTargets` and `SearchEntries` means: the registry exposes the list of enabled providers; the endpoints that merge them (`/api/core/focus`, `/api/core/search`) are built by later beads.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `NORTE_MODULES=library norte serve` answers `GET /api/config` with `modules: ["library"]`; `NORTE_MODULES= norte serve` answers with `modules: []`; both include `version`, `llm`, `telegram` and `timezone`.
- [ ] After `NORTE_MODULES=library norte migrate`, the tables `goose_core` and `goose_library` both exist and the stub's table exists; after `NORTE_MODULES= norte migrate` on a fresh `NORTE_DATA`, `goose_library` and the stub's table do not exist.
- [ ] Running `NORTE_MODULES= norte migrate` on a database where library was migrated earlier leaves the library tables and `goose_library` unchanged.
- [ ] `NORTE_MODULES=nope norte serve` and `NORTE_MODULES=nope norte migrate` exit non-zero, and stderr contains `nope`.
- [ ] With `NORTE_LLM_URL` set, `/api/config` returns `llm: true`; unset, `llm: false`; the same for `NORTE_TELEGRAM_TOKEN` and `telegram`.
- [ ] `server/internal/core` does not import `server/internal/app` (`go list -deps ./internal/core` does not list it).
- [ ] A job kind returned by an enabled module's `JobHandlers()` is claimed by the worker; the same kind from a disabled module stays `queued`.
- [ ] With two stub modules, a `Start` error cancels the other and `serve` exits non-zero; SIGTERM stops both cleanly.
- [ ] A command returned by a module's `Commands()` appears in `norte --help` only when that module is enabled.
- [ ] Done when: `NORTE_MODULES=library` and `NORTE_MODULES=` produce different `/api/config` answers and different applied migrations, each module in its own goose table, and `NORTE_MODULES=nope` exits non-zero with the name in the message.

## Tests

title: Refuse an unknown NORTE_TIMEZONE at startup and hide credentials in the LLM URL
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, a typo in the timezone setting (say `America/Sao_Pualo`) starts a healthy server, but the app shows "Servidor indisponível" forever and nothing says why. Separately, `norte config` prints the LLM address verbatim, including a password or `?key=` token written into it. Once this lands, a mistyped timezone stops the server at startup with a message naming the setting, and `norte config` never prints a credential.

## Outcome
`NORTE_TIMEZONE` is validated when the configuration is loaded, and the displayed value of `llm_url` has its userinfo and query string redacted.

## Context
Configuration is one table in `server/internal/app/config.go`; each setting has a `parse` and a `show` function. The timezone's `parse` stores any string unvalidated (around line 126). The server never uses the zone itself; it only reports it in `GET /api/config`, and the web client passes it to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, which throws `RangeError` on an unknown zone. That exception lands inside the boot retry loop and is read as a network failure (handled by a separate bead on the client). `time/tzdata` is embedded in the binary (`server/cmd/norte/main.go`), so `time.LoadLocation` answers the same on every machine and inside the scratch Docker image. An unknown module name is already refused at startup the same way (`norte: setting modules: unknown module ...`, exit 1); the timezone should follow that precedent. The `llm_key` setting is already shown as `<hidden>`; the same credential written into the URL (`https://user:pass@host/v1?key=...`) is not.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `NORTE_TIMEZONE=Mars/Olympus NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") ./server/norte serve` starts, and `GET /api/config` reports `"timezone":"Mars/Olympus"`; the UI never leaves "Servidor indisponível".
2. `NORTE_LLM_URL='http://u:pw@127.0.0.1:1/v1?api_key=SECRET' ./server/norte config` prints `llm_url = http://u:pw@127.0.0.1:1/v1?api_key=SECRET (env)`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `NORTE_TIMEZONE=Mars/Olympus norte serve` exits 1 with a message that names `timezone` and the bad value; the same for `--timezone` and the TOML key.
- [ ] `America/Sao_Paulo`, `UTC` and an empty value (system default) still start.
- [ ] `norte config` with the URL above prints `llm_url = http://<hidden>@127.0.0.1:1/v1?<hidden> (env)` or an equivalent form where neither `pw` nor `SECRET` appears; a URL with no userinfo or query prints unchanged.
- [ ] Done when: both reproduction steps above behave as the criteria say.

## Tests
- unit: cases in `server/internal/app/config_test.go` for an invalid zone (env, flag, file), a valid zone, an empty one, and the redacted display of a URL with userinfo and query.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/app/config.go`, `server/internal/app/config_test.go`
Confined to the configuration table and its tests.

title: Match the sidebar to its prototype
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the sidebar on every screen has no way to collapse it, no sign of when data was last synced, and groups its shortcuts under "Fixados" with Inbox, Currículos and Revisão, which is not what the design shows. After this lands the sidebar matches the design: a collapse button beside the "Norte" brand hides it, a "Sincronizado há N min" line with a status dot sits at the bottom, and the shortcut groups are "Biblioteca" (Inbox, Artigos, Shortlist) and "Estudo" (Currículos), each with its count.

## Outcome
The app sidebar (`web/src/components/AppSidebar.vue`, inside the layout `web/src/components/AppShell.vue`) matches the sidebar of the prototype "Norte - Command Home (standalone).html" at 1440px in both themes: collapse toggle next to the brand, the prototype's shortcut groups, and the sync status footer.

## Context
Norte is a Vue 3 frontend (under `web/`) ported from a design-tool prototype; every screen runs on mock data in `web/src/mock/`. The shell was built from a bead that described the sidebar as having a "Fixados" favourites group with star toggles, but the prototype it pointed at (`design/prototypes/Command_Home/template.html`) has no "Fixados" group: that description was wrong, and the prototype is the authority. A visual comparison with headless Chromium at 1440x900, both themes, found three differences in the sidebar:

1. The prototype has a small icon button at the top right of the sidebar, beside "Norte", that collapses the sidebar; the app has none.
2. Below the main navigation (Início, Biblioteca, Estudo, Projetos, Notas) the prototype shows two labelled shortcut groups: "Biblioteca" with Inbox, Artigos and Shortlist, and "Estudo" with Currículos, each entry with a right-aligned count. The app shows one group "Fixados" with Inbox, Currículos and Revisão.
3. At the bottom, under Buscar ⌘K and Preferências, the prototype shows a status line "Sincronizado há 2 min" preceded by a small green dot; the app has none.

Read the prototype's markup, styles and behaviour for these three elements in `/home/gabriel/repositories/norte/design/prototypes/Command_Home/template.html` (git-ignored, exists only in the main checkout; read it there, read-only), including what the collapsed state looks like and where each shortcut links. Translate prototype links into the app's routes: `/biblioteca` takes query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`. Counts come from the mock store. The sync line is static mock data ("Sincronizado há <N> min", N from mock), since there is no backend. UI strings are Portuguese. The repo is public: never copy the prototype's mock text.

Removing the "Fixados" group also removes its star toggles; the existing shell test that covers pinning is updated to the new groups rather than kept.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A button beside "Norte" toggles the sidebar between expanded and the prototype's collapsed state; the state persists across route changes within the session.
- [ ] The sidebar shows a "Biblioteca" group with Inbox, Artigos and Shortlist and an "Estudo" group with Currículos, each with a count from the mock store, each routing to the matching Biblioteca or Currículos route; no "Fixados" group remains.
- [ ] The sidebar footer shows a green dot followed by "Sincronizado há <N> min", N from mock data.
- [ ] Main navigation, Buscar ⌘K, Preferências, active-entry marking, the 900px hide rule and `layout: 'bare'` routes behave as before.
- [ ] A 1440x900 screenshot of any sidebar screen next to the prototype standalone export, light and dark, shows the same sidebar elements and order; run with Playwright headless Chromium from a throwaway script outside the repo, without adding Playwright as a dependency.
- [ ] Done when: the sidebar matches the prototype's three elements above and `cd web && npm run build && npm test` passes.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + @vue/test-utils, real router and mock data): the collapse button toggles the collapsed state; each shortcut entry renders its count and routes to its target; the sync footer renders; the existing navigation and active-marking assertions still pass.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/components/AppSidebar.vue`, `web/src/components/AppShell.vue`, `web/src/components/AppShell.test.ts`, `web/src/mock/store.ts`
**Reads only:** `design/prototypes/Command_Home/template.html`, `web/src/router/index.ts`

Confined to the sidebar and its layout; no screen view, route or design-system component changes.

title: Build the app shell: sidebar, layout and every route
description:
## What changes for the user
Today each prototype screen is a separate file with its own copy of the sidebar. After this lands, the app has one sidebar, and every menu entry opens its screen in place, even before that screen is built.

## Outcome
`AppShell.vue` with the 232px sidebar and a content slot, plus every route in the route table pointing at a view. Views not yet built are placeholders that show their name.

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Open `design/prototypes/Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html` in a browser to see the screen. Read `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html` for markup, inline styles and behaviour. The behaviour is a `class Component extends DCLogic` block with React-style `state`/`setState`. The template uses a design-tool runtime whose `sc-if`, `sc-for` and `{{ }}` bindings map almost one to one onto `v-if`, `v-for` and `{{ }}`. Prototype links point at `Norte - X.dc.html?param=`; translate them into the routes below.
- `design/system/` holds the committed design system. It has tokens in `tokens.css`/`tokens.json` (colour, type, a 4px spacing scale, radius, shadow), one `components/<Name>/README.md` per component, props in `components/index.d.ts`, and screenshots in `screenshots/`. Fonts are in `fonts/`: Schibsted Grotesk for display, Geist for sans and Commit Mono for mono.
- There are two themes, Claro and Escuro, switched by `data-theme` on the root element and stored in `localStorage` under `norte-theme`. The visual rule is quiet: one cobalt accent, no cards, no gradients, no warm colours.

Route table (shared by every screen):
- `/` is Início (Command Home).
- `/biblioteca` is the library, with query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`.
- `/notas` is notes, with query `tab` = `highlights|anotacoes|perguntas`.
- `/revisao` is the flashcard review.
- `/estudo` is the Estudo home (Currículos and Assuntos).
- `/curriculos/:slug` is one curriculum.
- `/material/:kind/:id` is one reading item, where kind is `post|livro|paper`.
- `/projetos` is the project list.
- `/areas/:id` is one area.
- `/projetos/:id` is one project.
- `/decisoes/:id` is one decision.
- `/tarefas/:id` is one task.

The repo is public. Never copy the prototype's mock content into code; use the neutral invented data in `web/src/mock/`. UI strings stay Portuguese.

The repo is a monorepo: the Vue app lives in `web/` and a Go backend will live in `server/` and later serve the built app from one binary. All frontend paths below are under `web/`; `design/` stays at the repo root. The gate is `npm run build && npm test`, run in `web/`.

The sidebar is copy-pasted into every prototype screen. Use `design/prototypes/Command_Home/template.html` as the reference. It has the "Norte" brand; a "Fixados" favourites group with star toggles; and collapsible sections with counts: Início, Biblioteca (Tudo / Inbox / Depois, Tipos, Listas), Estudo (Currículos, Assuntos, Revisão, Perguntas), Projetos (areas, plus "Nova área") and Notas (Anotações, Highlights, Notas). At the bottom are Buscar ⌘K and Preferências; those two only emit events here, because the overlay is a separate bead. The sidebar uses the `sunken` background and hides below 900px. Material screens (`/material/...`) do not use the sidebar; they have their own top bar. Mark that with a route meta flag `layout: 'bare'`. Counts come from `web/src/mock/`.

title: Keep semicolon query pairs and normalise the default port and empty path in canonical URLs
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, two different pages whose addresses differ only after a `;` in the query (common on older sites) are merged into one library item, and saving one overwrites the other's note. Meanwhile the same page written as `https://example.com` and `https://example.com/`, or with `:443`, is kept twice. Once this lands, different pages stay different and the same page is kept once.

## Outcome
`libraryCanonicalURL` keeps query pairs containing `;`, drops the scheme's default port, and turns an empty path into `/`.

## Context
The canonical URL decides dedupe: a save whose canonical URL already exists updates the existing item (`server/internal/library/canonical.go`). It lowercases the host, drops the fragment and tracking parameters (`utm_*`, `fbclid`, `ref`...), and re-encodes the query sorted. It calls `u.Query()`, and since Go 1.17 `url.ParseQuery` silently drops any pair containing `;`, so `?page=1;lang=pt` and `?page=2;lang=en` both canonicalise to `https://example.com/`. The fix is to split the raw query on `&` yourself and keep each pair's raw text, removing only the tracking keys. Default ports (`:80` for http, `:443` for https) and an empty path are not normalised today.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. `POST {"url":"https://example.com/?page=1;lang=pt"}` answers 201; `POST {"url":"https://example.com/?page=2;lang=en"}` answers **200** with the same id.
3. `POST {"url":"https://example.com/"}` and `POST {"url":"HTTPS://Example.COM:443/"}` both answer 201; so do `https://example.com` and `https://example.com/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `https://example.com/?page=1;lang=pt` and `https://example.com/?page=2;lang=en` canonicalise to two different strings, each keeping its pair.
- [ ] `HTTPS://Example.COM:443/`, `https://example.com` and `https://example.com/` canonicalise to `https://example.com/`; `http://example.com:80/x` to `http://example.com/x`; a non-default port is kept.
- [ ] Tracking-parameter removal, fragment removal and query sorting behave exactly as today (existing cases in `canonical_test.go` stay green unchanged).
- [ ] Done when: the reproductions above give two items for step 2 and one item for each pair in step 3.

## Tests
- unit: table cases in `server/internal/library/canonical_test.go` for each criterion.

## Recovery path
Existing rows keep the canonical URL they were saved with; a URL that now canonicalises differently simply stops deduping against an old row whose stored form used the old rule. No migration rewrites stored canonical URLs; that trade-off is accepted because the affected forms (`:443`, empty path, `;`) are rare and a duplicate is visible, while a silent merge is not.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/library/canonical.go`, `server/internal/library/canonical_test.go`

title: Make English the repo's own convention and prove the translation finished
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing on screen. This is the bead that stops the Portuguese coming back: the repo's own rule
still says "UI strings are Portuguese", and every agent that reads `AGENTS.md` before writing a
screen will keep following it. It is also the bead that proves the translation finished, by running
one sweep over the whole repo and accounting for every hit.

## Outcome
`AGENTS.md` states that every string in Norte is English, no document in the repo describes Norte
as a Portuguese-language product, and the repo-wide forbidden-term sweep returns nothing but the
allowlist — which this bead is also where the allowlist gets written down in the repo rather than
only in a bead.

## Context
This is the last bead of the translation, and it has to be: the convention is only true once the
screens are. It depends on every leaf — the shell bead, the design-system beads, the extension bead
and the module beads — so that nothing can flip the rule while a module is still half Portuguese.

What changes:

- `AGENTS.md:1` describes Norte as "a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI", and its
  Conventions section says "UI strings are Portuguese. Code, comments and commits are English."
  Both become one rule: everything is English.
- `CLAUDE.md` and the root `README.md`, wherever they repeat the convention or quote a Portuguese
  string.
- `docs/` prose: any sentence that quotes a Portuguese UI string or calls the product Portuguese.
  `docs/tools/ci-checks.md`'s check descriptions are norte-05j's, because a check description that
  quotes a string the check no longer asserts is wrong the moment the string moves; this bead's job
  in that file is only to confirm nothing Portuguese is left.
- A new short section in `AGENTS.md` recording **the allowlist**: the places where Portuguese is
  deliberate, each with the reason, so the next sweep does not treat them as a regression and
  nobody "fixes" them. The list is the inventory's, and the sweep below is written against it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` describes Norte's UI as English and states one language rule rather than two, and
      nothing in it tells a reader to write Portuguese strings.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` carries the allowlist of deliberate Portuguese, each entry with its reason:
      `server/internal/library/cleanup.go` (the cleanup regexes match both languages because Norte
      reads both); `server/internal/library/testdata/pages/*.html` (captured input pages — what
      language a saved page is in is not a property of Norte);
      `server/internal/core/slug.go:18`, `server/internal/library/extractor.go:288`,
      `server/internal/notes/list.go:159,186` and `server/internal/notes/search.go:45` (comments
      that demonstrate accent stripping, which cannot be demonstrated in English);
      `web/src/search/index.ts` (the NFD accent-stripping comparison, because a saved title can be
      in any language).
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md`, the root `README.md` and every file under `docs/` are English and describe an
      English product.
- [ ] The **repo-wide final sweep** returns nothing outside the allowlist:

          rg -n --no-heading \
            -g '!server/gen' -g '!**/db/**' -g '!web/src/api' \
            -g '!*.png' -g '!*.woff2' -g '!**/node_modules/**' -g '!**/dist/**' \
            -e '[À-ÿ]' -e 'pt-BR' \
            -e "['\"](depois|arquivo|tudo|livro|curso|sugestoes|tela)['\"]" \
            -e '/(biblioteca|notas|projetos|estudo|revisao|curriculos|decisoes|tarefas|assuntos)\b' \
            -e 'tab=(anotacoes|perguntas)' -e 'notas=nota' \
            -e '(?i)\b(hoje|ontem|salvar|salvo|salvando|conectar|anotar|anotacoes|perguntas|conjuntos|concluido|dificil|facil|preferencias|inicio|expandir|recolher|galeria|trilha)\b' \
            .

      Every hit is either an allowlist entry above or a defect this bead fixes. A hit that is
      neither is named in the pull request **and fixed**, not merely reported: the previous plan
      allowed "unexpected matches may be named in the pull request", which turns the one check that
      proves the translation finished into a note.
- [ ] `rg -c` over the sweep returns a count this bead's pull request quotes, so the number is on
      the record rather than a claim.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- none owed beyond the gate: the change is documentation. The sweep in the acceptance criteria is
  the check, and the pull request records its exact output.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the root `README.md`, and any file under `docs/` that quotes a
Portuguese string or calls the product Portuguese
**Shared edits:** `docs/tools/ci-checks.md` (owner norte-05j), only if the final sweep finds
something it missed
**Reads only:** `web/src/`, `server/`, `extension/`, `api/`, `design/system/`, `bin/`, `scripts/`,
`.github/`

## Recovery path
Documentation only; nothing executes and nothing is stored. Reverting the commit restores the
previous text — and the rule it restores is the one that says to write Portuguese, which is why
this bead lands last rather than first.

title: Match subjects word by word in the global search and score the best hit 1
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, searching for `filosofia mente` finds nothing although a subject called "Filosofia da Mente" exists; only the exact contiguous phrase works. Once this lands, a subject is found when every word typed occurs in its name, in any order.

## Outcome
The subject provider of `GET /api/core/search` matches each query word separately, and its scores are normalised so that the best subject hit scores 1, like the other providers.

## Context
The global search merges hits from core (subjects), library and notes, ordered by score. The contract says "Every word must match" (`api/openapi/core.yaml`, the `q` parameter around line 251) and "The best hit of a query scores 1" (around lines 564-566). Notes and library already match per word and normalise their scores (`NormalizeSearchScores`). `server/internal/core/searchsubjects.go` (around line 47) slugifies the whole query into one needle (`filosofia-mente`) and `server/internal/core/subjects.go` (around lines 356-365) matches it as a single substring; its fixed scores 1.0 / 0.8 / 0.6 (exact / prefix / substring, `searchsubjects.go` around lines 21-23) are not normalised, so a lone substring hit scores 0.6.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. `POST $B/api/core/subjects {"name":"Filosofia da Mente"}`.
3. `GET $B/api/core/search?q=filosofia%20mente` and `?q=mente%20filosofia` return `{"entries":[]}`; `?q=filosofia` returns the subject with `score: 0.8`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both queries in step 3 return the subject.
- [ ] `q=filosofia%20quimica` does not return it (every word must match).
- [ ] The best subject hit of any query scores 1, and the relative order among subject hits is unchanged.
- [ ] Accent and case folding behave as today.
- [ ] Done when: step 3 returns the subject for both word orders with `score: 1`.

## Tests
- unit: cases in `server/internal/core/search_test.go` for word order, a missing word, and score normalisation.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/core/searchsubjects.go`, `server/internal/core/subjects.go`, `server/internal/core/search_test.go`

title: Build the Área screen
description:
## What changes for the user
Areas group projects but have no page today. After this lands, an area shows its projects, loose tasks, decisions and sessions, and can be edited or archived.

## Outcome
The area page with its lists and edit mode, including `/areas/nova` for a new area.

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Open `design/prototypes/Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html` in a browser to see the screen. Read `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html` for markup, inline styles and behaviour. The behaviour is a `class Component extends DCLogic` block with React-style `state`/`setState`. The template uses a design-tool runtime whose `sc-if`, `sc-for` and `{{ }}` bindings map almost one to one onto `v-if`, `v-for` and `{{ }}`. Prototype links point at `Norte - X.dc.html?param=`; translate them into the routes below.
- `design/system/` holds the committed design system. It has tokens in `tokens.css`/`tokens.json` (colour, type, a 4px spacing scale, radius, shadow), one `components/<Name>/README.md` per component, props in `components/index.d.ts`, and screenshots in `screenshots/`. Fonts are in `fonts/`: Schibsted Grotesk for display, Geist for sans and Commit Mono for mono.
- There are two themes, Claro and Escuro, switched by `data-theme` on the root element and stored in `localStorage` under `norte-theme`. The visual rule is quiet: one cobalt accent, no cards, no gradients, no warm colours.

Route table (shared by every screen):
- `/` is Início (Command Home).
- `/biblioteca` is the library, with query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`.
- `/notas` is notes, with query `tab` = `highlights|anotacoes|perguntas`.
- `/revisao` is the flashcard review.
- `/estudo` is the Estudo home (Currículos and Assuntos).
- `/curriculos/:slug` is one curriculum.
- `/material/:kind/:id` is one reading item, where kind is `post|livro|paper`.
- `/projetos` is the project list.
- `/areas/:id` is one area.
- `/projetos/:id` is one project.
- `/decisoes/:id` is one decision.
- `/tarefas/:id` is one task.

The repo is public. Never copy the prototype's mock content into code; use the neutral invented data in `web/src/mock/`. UI strings stay Portuguese.

The repo is a monorepo: the Vue app lives in `web/` and a Go backend will live in `server/` and later serve the built app from one binary. All frontend paths below are under `web/`; `design/` stays at the repo root. The gate is `npm run build && npm test`, run in `web/`.

Reference: `design/prototypes/Area/template.html` and its standalone HTML. Mounted at `/areas/:id`.

Pick the area by `:id` from the mock data; `nova` opens an empty edit form. The `editing` mode edits name and intent and archives or unarchives. Regions: projects filtered Todos / Ativos, loose tasks, decisions and sessions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each mock area renders its own projects, tasks, decisions and sessions; the Todos/Ativos filter changes the project list.
- [ ] `/areas/nova` saves a new area, which then appears in the sidebar's Projetos section.
- [ ] Project, task and decision rows route to `/projetos/:id`, `/tarefas/:id` and `/decisoes/:id`.
- [ ] Side by side with the prototype at 1440px in both themes, layout, spacing and typography match by eye.
- [ ] Done when: every state and link above works on `/areas/:id`, and the gate is green.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + @vue/test-utils, mounted with the real router and mock data): the view renders its title and main regions; each interactive state listed in the acceptance criteria flips as described; each outbound link resolves to the route named in the criteria.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/views/AreaView.vue`, `web/src/router/index.ts`

One view, plus its route entry swapped from the placeholder. Small view-local subcomponents go under `web/src/views/AreaView/`.

title: Add library items: save, dedupe, list, counts and search
description:
## What changes for the user
Today a link "saved" in Norte lives only in the mock and is gone on reload; the real links are scattered across other apps and never read again. After this lands, saving a link — from the command line now, from the browser extension and the phone later — puts it in the library at once, with the "why I saved this" note, and saving the same link twice does not create a second copy but keeps whatever new note or selection came with it. The library can then be listed by inbox, later, archive or everything, by kind, by unread, and searched by any word in the title, the note or (once extracted) the text.

## Outcome
The library module's tables, full-text index, service and API: `POST /api/library/items` saves (blob first, then one transaction for item, registry row, file reference, links and the extraction job), list with views, filters, sort, full-text query and cursor pagination, counts, detail, patch, the "opened" call, and `norte save`. Canonical-URL dedupe makes a second save return the first item with the new note applied.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. `server/` is its Go backend: one binary, SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite` (one writer connection, a reader pool), goose migrations per module (`goose_<module>` version tables), sqlc queries, and an OpenAPI contract per module under `api/openapi/` generated into strict-server Go interfaces (`server/gen/api/<module>/`) and TypeScript types (`web/src/api/<module>.d.ts`) by `bin/generate`. The contract is edited first; a handler can only exist for a route it names. Products are modules switched on by `NORTE_MODULES`; each owns tables prefixed with its name and no foreign key crosses a module. A `library` module stub already exists with one throwaway migration (a placeholder table): this bead adds the real tables as the next migration and drops the stub table in that same migration.

What the always-on core offers this bead: `core.NewID()` (UUIDv7 string), `core.Now()` and fixed-width UTC times `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`; `core_items(id, module, type, title, url, created_at)` — the item registry every module writes to with `core.RegisterItem`/`core.UpdateItem` inside its own transaction, so another module can show a title and open the original without the library; `core_links(src_id, dst_id, kind, source, status, confidence, …)` with a unique `(src_id, dst_id, kind)` — the only cross-module relation; `core.Files` (content-addressed blobs, references in `core_file_refs`); the jobs queue `core.Jobs.Enqueue(ctx, tx, kind, payload, dedupeKey)`.

Decided:

- **Schema conventions**, shared by every table in Norte: `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` holding a UUIDv7 string; `created_at`/`updated_at` in the fixed UTC format; the module prefix on every table name; foreign keys only inside the module; a `CHECK` on every enumerated column; per-type variable data in a `meta TEXT` JSON column rather than in sparse columns.
- **Why the snapshot's file reference is marked `snapshot`.** A later delivery adds `GET /api/core/files/{hash}`, which serves only blobs referenced with kind `material_file` or `cover` and never a `snapshot`, because unsanitized HTML served from the app's own origin would be a stored script. Writing the kind correctly now is what keeps that rule enforceable without a data migration.
- **Table** `library_items(id, kind, url, canonical_url UNIQUE, title, title_edited, author, site, published_at, lead_image, why, selection, status, unread, saved_at, read_at, last_opened_at, read_position, source, html_hash, content_html, content_text, content_headings, extract_status, extract_generation INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, extracted_at, extract_error, minutes, meta, created_at, updated_at)` with `CHECK`s: `kind` in `post|livro|paper|video|podcast|newsletter|curso`; `status` in `inbox|depois|arquivo`; `extract_status` in `pending|done|failed`; `source` in `app|extension|cli|telegram|import` (`app` is a save from Norte's own Início dialog; the original plan listed only the other four). `unread` is independent of `status`: "only unread" is a filter over any view, and "read" is an event (`read_at`), not a place. `selection` is JSON `{exact, prefix, suffix}` captured by the extension, or null. `read_position` is JSON `{v: 1, anchor, percent}`. `html_hash` points at the HTML snapshot in the file store. `meta` is a JSON column for per-source data (Telegram messages, an extracted title the person overrode, and `snapshot_source` — `extension|cli|server_fetch|import`, written whenever `html_hash` changes and independent of the item's own `source`). The extraction columns are written by the extraction job, a separate bead; here a save sets `extract_status = pending`.
- **Full-text** `library_fts` FTS5 `(id UNINDEXED, title, author, why, content_headings, content_text)`, a standard (not external-content) table — external content keys on rowid, and a TEXT primary key's rowid can change under `VACUUM` — kept in sync by insert, update and delete triggers on `library_items`. Ranked with `bm25` column weights title > headings > why > author > content_text.
- **Save** is a service function `Save(ctx, tx, input)` so the curriculum import of a later delivery can run it inside its own transaction; the HTTP handler and `norte save` both call it (no logic in an adapter). Input `{url, title?, html?, selection?, why?, link_to?: string[]}` plus an adapter-owned `source` that is not a free request field: the web app's request is recorded as `app`, a request carrying `source: extension` (validated against that one value) as `extension`, `norte save` as `cli`, Telegram as `telegram`. `link_to` defaults to empty; duplicate ids collapse to one link; an id not in `core_items` returns 400 and rolls back the save. Before any blob is stored or transaction opened, the URL must parse as an absolute `http`/`https` URL with a hostname and no embedded credentials; anything else returns 400 and leaves every table and the file store unchanged. A new item starts with `kind = post`; extraction never changes `kind`, only a `PATCH` does. Steps: if `html` is present, store it with `core.Files` **before** the transaction (a crash leaves an orphan blob, never a dangling reference); then one transaction: insert the item, register it in `core_items` with `type = kind`, record the file reference with `core_file_refs.kind = 'snapshot'`, call `core.Links.Confirm(tx, item, target, about)` for each `link_to`, and enqueue an `extract` job with payload `{item_id, generation, refresh}` and `dedupe_key = "extract:<item id>:<generation>"`. `extract_generation` starts at 1 on insert and is incremented by every duplicate save or retry that enqueues a new `extract` job (a duplicate save that does not re-extract leaves it unchanged; the column is not in the original plan's schema and exists so the extraction job can detect that it was superseded), so a request made while an older extraction is still running gets its own job instead of being absorbed by the old one. Until extraction gives a title, `title` is the sent tab title or the URL's path. The save responds 201 with the id without waiting for extraction (the worker may claim the job before or after the response is written; nothing depends on that order).
- **Canonical URL** = the URL with tracking parameters (`utm_*`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, `mc_cid`, `mc_eid`, `ref`) and the fragment removed and the host lowercased. A save whose canonical URL exists returns the existing item with 200: the request's `why` and `selection` are applied, its `link_to` links are created unless they exist, and when the request carries HTML and the existing snapshot did not come from the extension (`meta.snapshot_source != "extension"`) or the extraction failed, the snapshot is replaced and extraction re-enqueued. Replacing a snapshot updates `html_hash`, inserts the new `(new_hash, item, snapshot)` reference and deletes the previous `(old_hash, item, snapshot)` reference in the same transaction, so the old blob becomes eligible for `norte files gc`. Two concurrent saves of one URL resolve by the unique index: one inserts, the other catches the constraint error, reads the winner and returns it.
- **List** `GET /api/library/items` with `view=inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo`, `tipo=<kind>`, `unread=true|false`, `sort` (`saved_desc` default, `saved_asc`, `title`, `last_opened_desc` — which lists only items that have been opened, newest-opened first, and is what the home's "continuar lendo" block uses), `q` (FTS), `cursor`, `limit` (default 50). Lists return summaries, never `content_html` or `content_text`. Every sort is a total order (the id breaks ties), backed by an index for stored columns; the cursor encodes the sort value, the id and a hash of the filters, and a cursor presented with different filters or sort is refused with 400. When `q` is present the order is the `bm25` rank, then id, and the cursor stores the rank; an explicit `sort` together with `q` is refused with 400. These are the filters the current frontend has; the prototype's Feed, favourites and tags are not in this delivery.
- **Counts** `GET /api/library/counts` → `{views: {inbox, depois, arquivo, tudo}, kinds: {post, livro, …}, unread}` in one query, so a list call never recomputes them.
- **Detail and patch.** `GET /api/library/items/{id}` returns the full record; a `GET` never writes. `PATCH` accepts `status`, `unread` (setting `read_at` or clearing it), `why`, `kind` (updating the registry `type` via `core.UpdateItem` in the same transaction), `title` (setting `title_edited = true` and updating the registry title), `read_position`. `POST /api/library/items/{id}/open` sets `last_opened_at` and never touches `unread`.
- **CLI** `norte save <url> [--html file] [--why text] [--link id]...` (`--link` may repeat).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `api/openapi/library.yaml` declares every route above under `/api/library/`; the generated interface is implemented and `bin/ci`'s freshness and prefix checks pass.
- [ ] `norte save https://example.org/a?utm_source=x#top --why "w1"` creates one item; it appears in `view=inbox`, `view=tudo`, `tipo=post` and `unread=true`, and `/api/library/counts` reports `inbox: 1, tudo: 1, unread: 1`.
- [ ] Saving `https://EXAMPLE.org/a` again with `--why "w2"` through `POST /api/library/items` returns HTTP 200 and the same id, and through `norte save` prints the same id and exits 0; the item's `why` is `w2`.
- [ ] A new item has `kind = post`; saves from the Início dialog, the extension, the CLI and Telegram record `source` `app`, `extension`, `cli` and `telegram`.
- [ ] One save with two `link_to` ids creates two confirmed `about` links in the same transaction; a repeated id creates one; an unknown id returns 400 and creates no item.
- [ ] Relative, malformed, `file:`, `javascript:` and credential-bearing URLs return 400 and leave every table and the file store unchanged.
- [ ] A CLI-created item later saved with HTML by the extension records `meta.snapshot_source = "extension"`; a later duplicate without HTML does not replace that snapshot.
- [ ] A duplicate save that replaces the snapshot leaves exactly one `snapshot` reference for the item, and `norte files gc` (fake clock past one hour) removes the old blob.
- [ ] With 60 items matching `q`, two pages of `limit=50` follow the `bm25` order with no duplicates; `q` with `sort=title` returns 400.
- [ ] Two concurrent `POST /api/library/items` for one URL leave exactly one row and both responses carry the same id.
- [ ] After `PATCH why = "zebra"`, `GET /api/library/items?q=zebra` returns the item; after `PATCH why = "other"`, it does not.
- [ ] A save with `html` stores one blob, one `core_file_refs` row with `kind = 'snapshot'` and sets `html_hash`; the item, its registry row, its links and one `extract` job are committed together (a test that forces the job enqueue to fail leaves no item row).
- [ ] `PATCH unread=false` sets `read_at`; `PATCH unread=true` clears it; `POST …/open` changes `last_opened_at` and not `unread`.
- [ ] `PATCH title` sets `title_edited` and updates `core_items.title`; `PATCH kind=livro` updates `core_items.type`.
- [ ] Paginating 120 items with `limit=50` returns 50, 50, 20 with no duplicate or missing id; reusing a cursor with a different `view` returns 400.
- [ ] `sort=last_opened_desc` returns only items with `last_opened_at` set, newest-opened first; a never-opened item never appears.
- [ ] A list response contains no `content_html` or `content_text` field.
- [ ] The migration that creates these tables also drops the stub module's placeholder table.
- [ ] Done when: `norte save` of a fixture URL creates an item visible in every current view filter with correct counts, saving it again with a new `why` returns the same id and the new `why`, two concurrent saves of one URL leave one row, and FTS finds it by a word in `why` after an update to `why`.

## Tests
- Unit (Go, `server/internal/library/`): canonical URL normalisation over a table of inputs; cursor encode/decode and filter-hash mismatch; status and unread transitions.
- Integration (Go, `httptest` + temp `NORTE_DATA`): every acceptance criterion, including the concurrent-save race (two goroutines) and the transactional rollback.
- FTS (Go integration): triggers keep `library_fts` in sync across insert, update of `why` and delete.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `api/openapi/library.yaml` (new), `server/gen/api/library/` and `web/src/api/library.d.ts` (generated), `server/internal/library/` (migration, queries and generated `db/`, service, handlers, `norte save` command; the stub module becomes the real one).
**Reads only:** `server/internal/core/` (registry, links, files, jobs), `server/internal/app/` (module interface), `bin/ci` (run as the gate, not edited).

One module plus its contract. Size L because it is a schema change.

## Recovery path
New tables only; no existing data is rewritten. Dropping the stub table loses nothing (it never held data). If the schema is wrong after real items exist, the fix is a new goose migration in `goose_library`, never an edit of the applied one; `NORTE_DATA` is a plain directory the person can copy before upgrading.
close_reason: Merged in PR #28. bin/ci green locally and in CI. Reviewer fixed bm25 weights landing one column early (UNINDEXED id) with a ranking test that fails on the old weights, and the stage-order test breaking with a second contract (rework:2). Non-blocking: job kind is library.extract (the extraction bead must register that name); extract_generation increments only on snapshot replacement; several criteria lack a dedicated test (unique-violation retry path, repeated --link, depois/arquivo counts); a failed-extraction duplicate without HTML re-enqueues nothing.

comments.author: gabriel
comments.text: rework:2 (found by reviewer): bm25 weights landed one column early (UNINDEXED id counts), ranking a note match above a title match; fixed with a ranking test. Also fixed the stage-order test that broke with a second contract.

title: Clear the model confidence on a manual link and refuse an empty item title
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, confirming one of the classifier's suggestions by linking the item by hand keeps the model's confidence on the link, so it still reads as the model's opinion. Editing an item's title to empty is accepted, after which the item shows a blank title everywhere and later extractions can never restore one. Once this lands, a link the person made carries no model confidence, and a title cannot be emptied.

## Outcome
The manual-confirm upsert clears `confidence`, and `PATCH /api/library/items/{id}` refuses an empty or blank title.

## Context
1. Links between items have a status (`suggested`, `confirmed`, `rejected`) and a source (`llm`, `manual`); `confidence` is "present only on a suggestion it made" (`api/openapi/core.yaml`, around lines 630-632). A manual `POST /api/core/links` over an existing suggested row flips it to `confirmed`/`manual` through the `ConfirmCoreLink` query in `server/internal/core/queries/core.sql`, which keeps `confidence`. The generated code under `server/internal/core/db/` is produced by `cd server && go tool sqlc generate` and is never edited by hand.
2. `PatchItemRequest.title` in `api/openapi/library.yaml` has no `minLength`, while subjects require `minLength: 1`. A PATCH to `""` sets `title_edited: true`, which blocks every later extraction from replacing the title. The contract change regenerates the Go and TypeScript types with `bin/generate api`; generated files are never edited by hand. Blank-only titles (`"   "`) should be refused in the handler too.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. With a `status=suggested` LLM link (confidence 0.85) between an item and a subject, `POST $B/api/core/links` with the same `src_id`/`dst_id`/`kind`: the answer is `{"status":"confirmed","source":"manual","confidence":0.85}`.
3. `curl -XPATCH $B/api/library/items/<id> -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"title":""}'` answers 200 with `title: ""`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Step 2 answers a link with no `confidence` field (or `null`, per the contract's existing representation).

title: Add a link from the Biblioteca through an add menu and the A shortcut
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the only way to add a link from inside Norte is a "Salvar link" button on the Início page;
the Biblioteca itself, where links are read and sorted, has no way to add one. After this change
the Biblioteca header has a "+" button that opens a small menu whose first entry, "URL", opens
the same save dialog, and pressing A anywhere in the Biblioteca opens it directly.

## Outcome
The Biblioteca page carries an add button with a menu, its "URL" entry and the A shortcut open
the existing save-link dialog, and that dialog is one component shared by Início and Biblioteca.

## Context
The save dialog lives in `web/src/modules/library/home/LibrarySaveAction.vue`, which renders
both the "Salvar link" button and the dialog (title "Salvar link", submit "Salvar na inbox"). It
is mounted only in the Início page's `actions` region (`web/src/modules/library/index.ts`,
registration `library-save`; rendered by `web/src/shell/HomeView.vue`). The save itself is
`POST /api/library/items`; a new item always lands in the Inbox.

The reference is the add menu of another read-later app: a "+" at the left of the library
title opening a menu of sources (URL, Upload, Email, RSS ...), each with a keyboard shortcut.
Only "URL" exists in Norte today. Upload has no endpoint and no reader for files yet and is a
separate decision, so this bead ships a menu with one entry, built so the next entries are one
line each.

This bead uses `web/src/components/ds/Menu.vue`, the menu component created by the bead that
reworks the Biblioteca header into one row; that bead also owns the header layout this button
sits in.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The dialog markup and logic move into one component,
      `web/src/modules/library/components/SaveLinkDialog.vue`, used by both the Início "Salvar
      link" action and the Biblioteca; the Início behaviour is unchanged (its existing tests
      pass unmodified apart from imports).
- [ ] The Biblioteca header shows an icon button with `aria-label="Adicionar"` immediately left
      of the page title. It opens a `Menu` with one item, "URL", showing the shortcut hint "A".
- [ ] Choosing "URL" opens the save dialog with focus in the URL field.
- [ ] Pressing `a` or `A` on the Biblioteca page opens the dialog, except while focus is in an
      input, textarea, select or contenteditable element, and except with Ctrl, Meta or Alt held.
- [ ] After a successful save from the Biblioteca the list and the counts are reloaded, so a new
      item appears at the top of Inbox when Inbox is the open tab and sorted by "Mais recentes".

- unit: `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.test.ts` asserts the add button, the menu
  entry, the A shortcut, its suppression inside an input and with a modifier, and the reload

title: Ship Norte as one Docker image
description:
## What changes for the user
To read on the phone, Norte has to run somewhere other than a laptop that sleeps. After this lands, Norte runs as one small container: `docker compose up` starts it with the chosen products, it keeps its data in one volume, it is reachable from the machine it runs on, and a commented example shows how to reach it from the phone over Tailscale — without opening it to the local network.

## Outcome
A two-stage `Dockerfile` producing a `scratch` image with the static binary, CA certificates and embedded time zones, running as a non-root user with `/data` as the data directory; a `docker-compose.example.yml` with a named volume, the port published on `127.0.0.1` and a commented Tailscale variant; a CI job that builds the image and checks `/api/config`.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. `server/` builds one static Go binary with no CGO (SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite`), which embeds the built frontend from `web/`; that is what makes a `scratch` image possible (about 25 MB). Configuration is by environment: `NORTE_MODULES` (comma-separated enabled modules: `library`, `notes`, later `study`, `review`, `projects`), `NORTE_DATA` (the one data directory: database plus content-addressed files, created `0700`), `NORTE_LISTEN` (default `127.0.0.1:8080`), `NORTE_TIMEZONE` (IANA zone for "today"). `GET /api/config` returns `{modules, version, llm, telegram, timezone}`. There is no authentication in this version: the boundary is localhost or the Tailscale network. The gate is `bin/ci`, run by a GitHub Actions workflow; the Go version is pinned by the `toolchain` directive in `server/go.mod`. `bin/generate` builds the frontend and copies it into the embed directory before `go build`.

Where it will run (the desktop or the homelab) is deliberately undecided; the phone-as-reader requirement points to the homelab over Tailscale. This bead makes both possible and decides neither.

Decided:

- **Dockerfile**, two stages: (1) build the frontend and the Go binary (`bin/generate`, then `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build`), with the Go version repeated from `go.mod`'s `toolchain`; the binary imports `time/tzdata` so `NORTE_TIMEZONE` resolves on an image with no zoneinfo; (2) `FROM scratch`, copy the binary and CA certificates, create `/data` owned by a non-root uid (prepared in the build stage, since `scratch` has no shell) and `USER` that uid, `ENV NORTE_LISTEN=0.0.0.0:8080 NORTE_DATA=/data`, `ENTRYPOINT ["/norte", "serve"]`.
- **`docker-compose.example.yml`**: `NORTE_MODULES` set explicitly, one **named volume** on `/data` — a bind mount arrives root-owned and the first start would fail with EACCES, so the example uses a named volume and says why in a comment — and the port published on `127.0.0.1:8080:8080`, so "no authentication" stays true on a shared network; a commented second example binds the Tailscale address for the phone and sets `NORTE_PUBLIC_URL` to the exact origin the phone uses — the server's `Host` allowlist rejects any other host with 421, and inside the container `NORTE_LISTEN` is `0.0.0.0`, so the public URL is the only way the phone's host is allowed — with a health check sent with that `Host` header. No `mem_limit` yet: it is suggested once the study module's PDF ingestion exists and its memory is measured (estimated at about 250 MB per PDF job).
- **CI job** in the GitHub workflow: build the image, start it with `NORTE_MODULES=library,notes` and `NORTE_TIMEZONE=America/Sao_Paulo`, wait for `/api/health`, assert `/api/config` lists exactly those modules and that timezone, save an item with a small `html` snapshot (so no outbound fetch happens), restart the container, read the item back, and check the image's user is non-zero, `/data` is owned by it, and the CA bundle exists in the image.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `docker build .` succeeds and the final image is based on `scratch` and runs as a non-zero uid (`docker inspect` shows `User`).
- [ ] `docker compose -f docker-compose.example.yml up` with `NORTE_MODULES=library,notes` serves the app at `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, and `/api/config` returns `modules: ["library", "notes"]`.
- [ ] With `NORTE_TIMEZONE=America/Sao_Paulo`, `/api/config` returns that zone (proving `time/tzdata` is embedded).
- [ ] After saving an item and restarting the container, the item is still there (data in the named volume), and `norte.db` inside the volume is owned by the container's non-root uid.
- [ ] The compose example's port is bound to `127.0.0.1`, and its comments explain the named volume and the Tailscale variant.
- [ ] The CI job builds the image and asserts the `/api/config` answer above on every PR.
- [ ] Done when: `docker compose up` with those modules serves the app with only those modules, reachable from the host, writing to the `/data` volume as non-root, with `NORTE_TIMEZONE=America/Sao_Paulo` accepted.

## Tests
- CI (GitHub Actions job): build, run, `curl /api/config`, assert modules and timezone.
- Manual: only the real phone-over-Tailscale reachability check, in the first delivery's acceptance walk.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `Dockerfile` (new), `docker-compose.example.yml` (new), `.dockerignore` (new), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the image job), `server/cmd/norte/main.go` (the `time/tzdata` import, if not already present).
**Reads only:** `bin/generate`, `server/go.mod`.

Build and deploy files only: five small files, none of them application logic; size M.

## Recovery path
Before upgrading, stop Norte and archive the named volume (for example `docker run --rm -v <volume>:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine tar czf /backup/norte-data.tgz -C /data .`). If a release misbehaves and it ran no migration, the previous image tag may reuse the volume. If it ran a migration, restore the pre-upgrade archive into the volume before starting the previous tag: an older binary is never assumed to understand a newer schema.
close_reason: Merged into local main (GitHub unreachable). Lane: opencode Muse Spark 1.3 xhigh (wrote lane.done). Gate 15/15 green after merging main; image built from the merged tree and /api/config answered (modules library,notes, America/Sao_Paulo). Review built and ran the image: scratch base, uid 65532, data survives restart and recreate, migrations for core/library/notes, HTTPS fetch works. Fixed before merge: the GitHub CI CA-bundle step died of SIGPIPE on a correct image (red on every PR); compose volume named norte-data so the documented backup command targets it; Node pinned in check-pins, tarball SHA256 verified, TARGETARCH honoured; version stamped via ldflags; /data 0700; env_file block documenting the six settings; extension/ excluded from the build context. Not verified: the GitHub workflow itself (GitHub unreachable tonight), the arm64 build.
