title: Build the Início screen
description:
## What changes for the user
Opening the app today shows nothing. After this lands, the first screen says what to review, what to continue studying and reading, and lets you save a link in two clicks.

## Outcome
The Início screen with review call-to-action, continue-studying, continue-reading carousel, recently saved list and the Salvar link modal.

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Open `design/prototypes/Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html` in a browser to see the screen. Read `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html` for markup, inline styles and behaviour. The behaviour is a `class Component extends DCLogic` block with React-style `state`/`setState`. The template uses a design-tool runtime whose `sc-if`, `sc-for` and `{{ }}` bindings map almost one to one onto `v-if`, `v-for` and `{{ }}`. Prototype links point at `Norte - X.dc.html?param=`; translate them into the routes below.
- `design/system/` holds the committed design system. It has tokens in `tokens.css`/`tokens.json` (colour, type, a 4px spacing scale, radius, shadow), one `components/<Name>/README.md` per component, props in `components/index.d.ts`, and screenshots in `screenshots/`. Fonts are in `fonts/`: Schibsted Grotesk for display, Geist for sans and Commit Mono for mono.
- There are two themes, Claro and Escuro, switched by `data-theme` on the root element and stored in `localStorage` under `norte-theme`. The visual rule is quiet: one cobalt accent, no cards, no gradients, no warm colours.

Route table (shared by every screen):
- `/` is Início (Command Home).
- `/biblioteca` is the library, with query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`.
- `/notas` is notes, with query `tab` = `highlights|anotacoes|perguntas`.
- `/revisao` is the flashcard review.
- `/estudo` is the Estudo home (Currículos and Assuntos).
- `/curriculos/:slug` is one curriculum.
- `/material/:kind/:id` is one reading item, where kind is `post|livro|paper`.
- `/projetos` is the project list.
- `/areas/:id` is one area.
- `/projetos/:id` is one project.
- `/decisoes/:id` is one decision.
- `/tarefas/:id` is one task.

The repo is public. Never copy the prototype's mock content into code; use the neutral invented data in `web/src/mock/`. UI strings stay Portuguese.

The repo is a monorepo: the Vue app lives in `web/` and a Go backend will live in `server/` and later serve the built app from one binary. All frontend paths below are under `web/`; `design/` stays at the repo root. The gate is `npm run build && npm test`, run in `web/`.

Reference: `design/prototypes/Command_Home/template.html` and its standalone HTML. Mounted at `/`.

Regions: a "Revisar N cartões" button with the due count; "Continuar estudando" with the in-progress curricula as CourseRow (item x/y, percent); a "Continuar lendo" Carousel of 6 items; "Salvos recentemente". The "Salvar link" modal takes a URL plus an optional "why" and adds the item to the saved list. It also opens when the URL has `?save=1`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] "Revisar" routes to `/revisao`; a curriculum row routes to `/curriculos/:slug`; a reading item routes to `/material/:kind/:id` by its kind.
- [ ] The Salvar link modal opens from its button and from `/?save=1`, rejects an empty URL, and on save the item appears first in "Salvos recentemente" and in Biblioteca's Inbox.
- [ ] Side by side with the prototype at 1440px in both themes, layout, spacing and typography match by eye.
- [ ] Done when: every state and link above works on `/`, and the gate is green.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + @vue/test-utils, mounted with the real router and mock data): the view renders its title and main regions; each interactive state listed in the acceptance criteria flips as described; each outbound link resolves to the route named in the criteria.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/views/HomeView.vue`, `web/src/router/index.ts`

One view, plus its route entry swapped from the placeholder. Small view-local subcomponents go under `web/src/views/HomeView/`.

title: Let the person manage domain rules and accept suggested ones
description:
## What changes for the user
The router places saved links in the Inbox or the Stash, and some domains always belong in one of
them. Today there is no way to say so. After this change the person can list, add and remove
domain rules, and when they keep moving links from the same domain by hand, Norte offers to make
that a rule, without ever creating one on its own.

## Outcome
The library API exposes domain rules and rule suggestions, and the web client has a screen to
manage rules and a prompt that offers a suggested rule.

## Context
The routing bead adds the rules table (domain, location `inbox` or `stash`), the
`location_source` column on items (`rule`, `decider`, `default`, `user`, `import`) and applies
the rules at save time. This bead only lets the person edit them and offers new ones.

A suggestion comes from the person's own moves: when they have moved at least 3 items of the
same domain into the same one of Inbox or Stash by hand (`location_source = user`), and no rule
for that domain exists and none was dismissed, Norte suggests `<domain> -> <location>`. Accepting
creates the rule; dismissing records that so it is not offered again. Rules never apply
retroactively unless the person asks: creating a rule changes only future saves.

Device-only preferences live in `web/src/shell/ShellOverlay.vue` (theme, in `localStorage`);
rules are server data, so they get their own screen in the library module rather than that
overlay.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `GET /api/library/domain-rules` lists rules; `PUT /api/library/domain-rules/{domain}` with
      `{"location": "inbox"|"stash"}` creates or replaces one; `DELETE` removes it. A domain is
      stored lowercased with no scheme, path or leading `www.`; an invalid one answers 400 with
      `field: domain`.
- [ ] `GET /api/library/domain-rules/suggestions` lists suggestions as described, with the count
      of moves behind each; `POST .../suggestions/{domain}/dismiss` records a dismissal.
- [ ] A library screen at `/biblioteca/regras` (renamed by the translation bead) lists rules with
      add, change and remove, and is linked from the Library's header menu.
- [ ] When a suggestion exists, the Library shows a dismissible notice naming the domain, the
      location and the count, with "Create rule" and "Dismiss"; creating a rule leaves existing
      items where they are.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- unit: handlers for list, put, delete, domain normalization and the 400 case.
- unit: suggestion counting (threshold of 3, only `user` moves, one location, dismissed and
  existing rules excluded).
- unit: the rules screen and the suggestion notice in the web tests.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/library/rules.go`, `server/internal/library/rules_test.go`, `api/openapi/library.yaml`, `web/src/modules/library/views/DomainRulesView.vue`, `web/src/modules/library/views/DomainRulesView.test.ts`, `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue`, `web/src/modules/library/index.ts`
**Reads only:** `bin/ci`, `bin/generate`, `server/internal/library/router.go`

## Recovery path
A dismissals table is added by this bead's migration, whose down step drops it. The number: norte-bc7
adds `00004_library_location.sql`, norte-u77 `00005` and norte-l57 `00006`, so this bead's is
`00007`.

`web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue` and `web/src/modules/library/index.ts` are also
edited by norte-ff8, which adds the tag chips and the tag filter to the same header. That is why
this bead now depends on norte-ff8 directly rather than only through norte-547: a dependency edge
is the only thing that keeps two agents off those two files, and a shared edit with no edge is how
two green branches break when they meet.

title: Rename the shell's own routes and the subject route to English
description:
## What changes for the user
Two addresses that belong to the shell rather than to any product are Portuguese: the subject
screen is at `/assuntos/<slug>`, and the home, not-found and switched-off screens are known
internally as `inicio`, `nao-encontrado` and `modulo-desligado-<module>-<index>`. Those addresses
sit in the browser's history, in bookmarks, in the links the command palette opens and in the
search entries the Go server builds. After this change the subject screen is at
`/subjects/<slug>`, and the shell's route names are English.

## Outcome
Every route path and route name declared in `web/src/router/index.ts` is English, every producer of
a subject path agrees on `/subjects/<slug>` — the Vue router, the shell's sidebar composition, the
palette, the Go search entries and the subject registry URL — and the core contract's description
of the subject address says so.

## Context
The library's own addresses (`/library`, `/library/:id`) are the model bead's, because the files
that produce them are the files it already rewrites. Each product module's addresses are that
module's own bead, so that a module's routes and its screens move in one diff instead of two. What
is left is the shell's: the routes `web/src/router/index.ts` declares itself, and the subject
screen, which belongs to the core rather than to a module.

A subject path is produced in four places and only the whole set is consistent:

- `web/src/router/index.ts:29-32` declares the route, and `web/src/shell/composition.ts:130-147`
  builds the sidebar section id `assuntos`, the row id `assunto-${slug}` and the route name it
  navigates by.
- `server/internal/core/searchsubjects.go:14` and `server/internal/core/subjects.go:589` build
  `/assuntos/<slug>`; the second is also the registry URL a subject is created with, so a stored
  row carries the path.
- `api/openapi/core.yaml:197` and `:561` describe the address in prose, which the generated clients
  carry.
- `web/src/shell/paletteSearch.ts` and `web/src/search/index.ts` name the route when they build
  palette targets.

The renames:

| today | English |
| --- | --- |
| `/` name `inicio`, title `Início` | name `home`, title `Home` |
| `/assuntos/:slug` name `assunto`, title `Assunto` | `/subjects/:slug` name `subject`, title `Subject` |
| dev-only `/_ds` title `Galeria` | title `Gallery` |
| name `modulo-desligado-${module}-${index}` | `module-off-${module}-${index}` |
| name `nao-encontrado` | `not-found` |
| sidebar section id `assuntos`, row id `assunto-${slug}` | `subjects`, `subject-${slug}` |

The `meta.title` of each route it renames moves with it, because a route record is one object and
splitting it between two beads would mean editing the same lines twice. The `RouteMeta.title` doc
comment at `web/src/router/index.ts:12` calls it "Portuguese screen name" and stops being true
here. The four failure screens' *body copy* is not here — that is norte-05j's.

No redirect from the old addresses is added. There is one user and one browser; a bookmark that
breaks is reopened from the sidebar, and a redirect table for every old Portuguese path is
permanent weight for a one-time cost.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `web/src/router/index.ts` declares `/subjects/:slug` with name `subject`, the home route with
      name `home`, the not-found route with name `not-found`, and the switched-off route name
      `module-off-<module>-<index>`.
- [ ] A deep link into a switched-off module still renders the switched-off page, matched through
      each module's `routePaths`, and `disabledModuleRoutes` produces one record per entry with
      the `module-off-` name.
- [ ] `server/internal/core/searchsubjects.go` and `server/internal/core/subjects.go` build
      `/subjects/<slug>`, and the registry URL a subject is created with is the same path.
- [ ] `api/openapi/core.yaml` describes the subject address as `/subjects/<slug>` in both places,
      and `bin/check-contracts` passes.
- [ ] `server/internal/core/migrations/00003_core_subject_paths.sql` rewrites every `core_items.url`
      of the form `/assuntos/<slug>` to `/subjects/<slug>` for rows whose module is the core's
      subject registry, and its down step rewrites them back.
- [ ] The sidebar's subjects section id is `subjects` and each row id is `subject-<slug>`, and the
      tests that select on them select on the English ids.
- [ ] The **shell-route forbidden-term check** comes back empty:

          rg -n --no-heading -g '!server/gen' -g '!web/src/api' \
            -e '/assuntos' -e "'assuntos?'" -e 'assunto-' -e "'inicio'" \
            -e 'nao-encontrado' -e 'modulo-desligado' \
            web/src web/e2e server/internal extension api docs

      No allowlisted exception applies: every hit is a name this bead renames.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- unit: the route table holds `/subjects/:slug` with name `subject`, and `shellDocumentTitle` names
  the tab from the English title.
- unit: `disabledModuleRoutes` produces a record per `routePaths` entry with the `module-off-` name.
- unit (Go): `subjectSearchPath` and the subject registry URL are `/subjects/<slug>`.
- unit (Go): the core migration's up step over a database holding a subject row whose
  `core_items.url` is `/assuntos/<slug>` leaves it at `/subjects/<slug>`, and its down step puts it
  back; a row whose url is not a subject path is untouched by both.
- e2e: `web/e2e/shell-boot.spec.ts` — a deep link into a switched-off module, and an unknown
  address, both against the English route names.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/core/migrations/00003_core_subject_paths.sql`,
`web/src/router/index.ts`, `web/src/router/index.test.ts`,
`web/src/shell/composition.ts`, `web/src/shell/paletteSearch.ts`,
`web/src/shell/NewSubjectButton.vue`, `web/src/shell/SubjectView.vue`,
`web/src/shell/ModuleDisabled.vue`, `web/src/shell/NotFoundView.vue`,
`web/src/shell/AppSidebar.vue`, `web/src/shell/AppTopBar.vue`, `web/src/shell/boot.test.ts`,
`web/src/search/index.ts`, `api/openapi/core.yaml`,
`server/internal/core/searchsubjects.go`, `server/internal/core/subjects.go`,
`server/internal/core/search_test.go`, `server/internal/core/slug_test.go`,
`server/internal/core/subjectpaths_test.go`,
`server/internal/app/subjectsfixes_test.go`
**Shared edits** (the subject path and the shell route names only): `web/src/shell/data/testing.ts`
and `server/internal/app/subjectsapi_test.go` and `server/internal/app/e2e_test.go` (owner
norte-bc7, which blocks this bead); `web/src/shell/sidebar.test.ts`,
`web/src/shell/SubjectView.test.ts`, `web/src/shell/data/apiSource.test.ts`,
`web/e2e/shell-boot.spec.ts` (owner norte-05j, which this bead blocks);
`web/src/modules/study/views/StudyHomeView.vue` and
`web/src/modules/study/views/StudyHomeView.test.ts` (owner norte-qst, which this bead blocks);
`web/src/modules/review/views/ReviewView.vue` and
`web/src/modules/review/views/ReviewView.test.ts` (owner norte-v6w, which this bead blocks)
**Regenerates (by `bin/generate`, never by hand):** `server/gen/api/core/`, `web/src/api/core.d.ts`
**Reads only:** `web/src/modules/*/manifest.ts`, `web/src/modules/mounting.ts`

## Recovery path
No stored data and no migration except one: the subject registry URL is **written into

code: the old addresses stop working the moment the build lands, which is the intended behaviour,

title: Build the Revisão flashcard session
description:
## What changes for the user
There is no way to review cards today. After this lands, you pick a deck, flip cards, rate them by keyboard, and see how much you recalled at the end.

## Outcome
The review screen: deck picker, card session and finish screen.

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Open `design/prototypes/Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html` in a browser to see the screen. Read `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html` for markup, inline styles and behaviour. The behaviour is a `class Component extends DCLogic` block with React-style `state`/`setState`. The template uses a design-tool runtime whose `sc-if`, `sc-for` and `{{ }}` bindings map almost one to one onto `v-if`, `v-for` and `{{ }}`. Prototype links point at `Norte - X.dc.html?param=`; translate them into the routes below.
- `design/system/` holds the committed design system. It has tokens in `tokens.css`/`tokens.json` (colour, type, a 4px spacing scale, radius, shadow), one `components/<Name>/README.md` per component, props in `components/index.d.ts`, and screenshots in `screenshots/`. Fonts are in `fonts/`: Schibsted Grotesk for display, Geist for sans and Commit Mono for mono.
- There are two themes, Claro and Escuro, switched by `data-theme` on the root element and stored in `localStorage` under `norte-theme`. The visual rule is quiet: one cobalt accent, no cards, no gradients, no warm colours.

Route table (shared by every screen):
- `/` is Início (Command Home).
- `/biblioteca` is the library, with query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`.
- `/notas` is notes, with query `tab` = `highlights|anotacoes|perguntas`.
- `/revisao` is the flashcard review.
- `/estudo` is the Estudo home (Currículos and Assuntos).
- `/curriculos/:slug` is one curriculum.
- `/material/:kind/:id` is one reading item, where kind is `post|livro|paper`.
- `/projetos` is the project list.
- `/areas/:id` is one area.
- `/projetos/:id` is one project.
- `/decisoes/:id` is one decision.
- `/tarefas/:id` is one task.

The repo is public. Never copy the prototype's mock content into code; use the neutral invented data in `web/src/mock/`. UI strings stay Portuguese.

The repo is a monorepo: the Vue app lives in `web/` and a Go backend will live in `server/` and later serve the built app from one binary. All frontend paths below are under `web/`; `design/` stays at the repo root. The gate is `npm run build && npm test`, run in `web/`.

Reference: `design/prototypes/Revisao/template.html` and its standalone HTML. Mounted at `/revisao`.

The deck list shows "Tudo de hoje" plus 3 decks, with remaining counts and percent. A session shows one Flashcard at a time; Space reveals the back, and the ratings are De novo / Difícil / Bom / Fácil, with intervals 10 min / 2 d / 6 d / 14 d, by button or keys 1-4. Ratings go to the mock store. When the deck empties, a finish screen shows the percent recalled (good + easy over total) and a restart.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Picking a deck starts a session with exactly its due cards; the remaining count drops by one per rating.
- [ ] Keys Space and 1-4 drive the whole session without the mouse.
- [ ] The finish screen's percent equals (good + easy) / rated × 100, rounded; restart returns to the deck list.
- [ ] Side by side with the prototype at 1440px in both themes, layout, spacing and typography match by eye.
- [ ] Done when: every state and link above works on `/revisao`, and the gate is green.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + @vue/test-utils, mounted with the real router and mock data): the view renders its title and main regions; each interactive state listed in the acceptance criteria flips as described; each outbound link resolves to the route named in the criteria.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/views/ReviewView.vue`, `web/src/router/index.ts`

One view, plus its route entry swapped from the placeholder. Small view-local subcomponents go under `web/src/views/ReviewView/`.

title: Anchor highlights whose context crosses a paragraph or heading boundary
description:
## What changes for the user Today, selecting a passage that starts or ends near the edge of a paragraph or a heading and pressing "Destacar" stores the highlight but no mark appears, and later the passage shows up under "Trechos que não estão mais neste texto". The same happens from the browser extension's "Virar highlight". Roughly every passage within a sentence of a paragraph edge is lost this way. Once this lands, any passage that occurs once in the text is anchored and marked, wherever it sits. ## Outcome The server's highlight anchoring matches the client's prefix and suffix context against the article text without being sensitive to whether a block boundary was spelled with whitespace, so contexts captured from the DOM anchor. ## Context A highlight is stored with `exact` (the selected text) plus up to 32 code points of `prefix` and `suffix` context; the server looks for `exact` in the item's extracted text and keeps the occurrence whose surrounding text matches the context (`server/internal/notes/anchor.go`, `notesAnchor`, `notesTailMatches`, `notesHeadMatches`). The extracted text separates blocks with newlines, which the server's normaliser collapses into one space (`notesNormalizeText`). The reader builds the context with `Range.toString()` (`web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderView.vue` around 363-377) and the extension does the equivalent in `extension/src/capture.js`; neither inserts anything between adjacent block elements, so the context arrives as `brilhante.Terceiro` while the server's text reads `brilhante. Terceiro`, and the match fails. Measured with the API alone on the same passage: prefix `inteiro sem parar.Segundo parágrafo ` stores `orphaned`, prefix `inteiro sem parar. Segundo parágrafo ` stores `anchored`. Fixing it on the server is chosen over fixing each client: there are two clients today (reader, extension) and both read text from a DOM, so any client spelling of a boundary must match. The rule: compare context with all whitespace removed on both sides (the `exact` search itself keeps its current whitespace normalisation). Removing whitespace cannot create a false unique match that the current rule would reject for a different reason, because `exact` must still occur in the text, and the context comparison only chooses among those occurrences. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`. 2. Save a snapshot: `POST $B/api/library/items` with `{"url":"https://example.com/anchor","html":"

Título

Primeiro parágrafo fala do mar inteiro sem parar.

Segundo parágrafo descreve montanhas geladas onde lobos cinzentos caçam renas.

"}` and wait until `extract_status` is `done`. 3. `POST $B/api/notes/highlights` with `{"item_id":"","exact":"Segundo parágrafo descreve","prefix":"inteiro sem parar.","suffix":" montanhas geladas"}`. 4. Observed: `"status":"orphaned"`. With `"prefix":"inteiro sem parar. "` the same request answers `"status":"anchored"`. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] The request in step 3 answers `status: anchored` with the `position_hint` of the passage's code-point offset. - [ ] A passage that occurs twice with identical context still answers `orphaned` with `ambiguous: true`. - [ ] A passage absent from the text still answers `orphaned` without `ambiguous`. - [ ] Re-anchoring after a re-extraction (`notes.reanchor`) uses the same comparison, so a highlight anchored by the new rule stays anchored when the text is unchanged. - [ ] Done when: the reader, against a real server, marks a passage selected within the first ten characters of a paragraph. ## Tests - unit: table cases in `server/internal/notes/anchor_test.go` for a glued prefix, a glued suffix, a context spanning a heading, and the unchanged ambiguous and absent cases. - unit: one case in `server/internal/notes/reanchor_test.go` re-anchoring a highlight created with a glued context. - e2e: a Playwright case in `web/e2e/` that selects a passage at the start of a paragraph in the real reader, presses Destacar, and asserts a mark appears and the stored status is `anchored`. ## Blast radius **Edits:** `server/internal/notes/anchor.go`, `server/internal/notes/anchor_test.go`, `server/internal/notes/reanchor_test.go`, one new spec under `web/e2e/` **Reads only:** `web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderView.vue`, `extension/src/capture.js` The clients are not changed. The stored highlight format and the API contract are not changed.
close_reason: Merged into local main; full gate at 9a8c4e1: 18/20 first run, go-test and web-test red on timeouts under external CPU pressure (77% some), both green on rerun and the jobs test 20/20.

title: Translate the design system's component gallery to English
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing a reader of the product sees. The component gallery at the dev-only `/_ds` address is the
one screen a developer reads to see what a shared control looks like, and it is Portuguese: the
page is `Galeria de componentes`, the sections are `Componentes de leitura e estudo`, and the
sample data behind every variant — course titles, subject names, flashcard questions, annotation
prose — is 68 rows of invented Portuguese. After this change the gallery reads in English, so the
next component written from it arrives in English.

## Outcome
`web/src/components/ds/gallery/` is English: the page and section headings, and the invented sample
data every variant renders.

## Context
This is split from the design-system component bead (norte-2vx) on purpose. That bead is logic
plus labels and its diff is worth reading line by line; the gallery is one large file of sample content and its
diff is worth reading as a whole. Merging them would put 68 rows of prose in front of the reviewer
who is checking that a mark still points at its margin note.

The sample data is invented, not the person's, and is rewritten as neutral invented English rather
than translated sentence by sentence — the repo's rule is that prototype content is never copied.
Rewriting it is also the chance to drop content that only makes sense in Portuguese, such as a
flashcard whose answer is a Portuguese pun.

The gallery renders the same components the design-system bead renames, so it must land after it:
a gallery variant that still passes `kind="why"`-era Portuguese props would render English labels
over Portuguese sample text.

The headings, with their English, are in §1.3 of the inventory comment on norte-3ab.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `Galeria de componentes`, `Variantes documentadas dos controles compartilhados, nos dois
      temas.`, `Componentes de leitura e estudo` and `Blocos compostos usados pelas telas de
      currículo, leitura e revisão.` read `Component gallery`, `Documented variants of the shared
      controls, in both themes.`, `Reading and study components` and `Composed blocks used by the
      curriculum, reading and review screens.`
- [ ] Every sample value the gallery renders is English invented content, and no variant shows a
      Portuguese word.
- [ ] The **gallery forbidden-term check** comes back empty:

          rg -n --no-heading -e '[À-ÿ]' \
            -e '(?i)\b(galeria|componentes|variantes|documentadas|controles|compartilhados|temas|leitura|estudo|curriculo|revisao|telas|blocos|compostos|usados|pergunta|anotacao|assunto|trilha|redes|concluido)\b' \
            web/src/components/ds/gallery

      Nothing in this directory is deliberately Portuguese, so there is no allowlisted hit.
- [ ] Opening `/_ds` in a dev build renders every section with no Portuguese visible.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- component: the gallery mounts without error and its two section headings render their English
  text — the gallery has no behaviour of its own, so the heading assertions plus the term check are
  the whole obligation.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/components/ds/gallery/DsGallery.vue`, and every other file under
`web/src/components/ds/gallery/`
**Reads only:** `web/src/components/ds/`

Disjoint from every other translation bead: no other bead edits anything under `gallery/`.

## Recovery path
Sample content on a dev-only screen; nothing stored, nothing in the product build's user path.
Reverting the commit restores the previous gallery.

title: Walk the first delivery end to end on real data
description:
## What changes for the user
This is the day the first delivery is used for real, not tested. The person saves a real article from the browser, reads it on the phone in Norte, links it to a subject, answers one of the classifier's suggestions and writes a question from it — with no invented data anywhere in the path. Whatever breaks along the way becomes a task, so the next round fixes what real use found instead of what was imagined.

## Outcome
The acceptance walk of the first delivery happened end to end on real data, its result is recorded in this bead, and every defect it found is a bead of its own.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI, being delivered in loops that are each used the day after they ship: first reading, then study, review and projects. The measure of the first loop is not "links are saved" but "a link saved at the wrong moment reappears at the right one, and reading it ends in something that survives the day". Every piece is built and tested by its own bead: the Go server in one binary or container, the library with extraction and full-text search, notes (highlights, annotations, questions), subjects and focus, the LLM classifier with suggestions and subject proposals, "what to read now" and serendipity, the browser extension, the Telegram inbox, the phone-usable reader, home and search, and Docker. Each passed its own automated gate; none of them proves the person can do the whole thing.

Subject proposals are not part of this walk: they are the second round of this loop, decided by a separate question after this walk has put the classifier into daily use. This bead has no code. It is a walk performed by the person (an agent may prepare the environment and take notes, but the walk is the person's), plus the manual checks other beads deferred to it: the Firefox smoke test of the extension when no Firefox binary was available in CI, a real logged-in Substack save, and a real Telegram message from the phone.

The walk:

1. Run Norte where the person will actually use it (desktop or homelab, reachable from the phone), with the library and notes modules, the LLM configured and the Telegram token set.
2. Save a real article from the browser extension, with a "why".
3. On the phone, open it in Norte and read it.
4. Link it to a subject (creating the subject if needed).
5. Accept or reject one classifier suggestion in the "Sugestões" queue.
6. Write a question from it at the end of reading.
7. Confirm no mock data appears anywhere in that path (the library and notes screens, the subject page, the queue).
8. The deferred manual checks above.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Steps 1-8 were performed on real data, and a comment on this bead records the date, the deployment class only (`desktop` or `homelab over Tailscale`), and one line per step: passed, or the defect seen. The tracker is committed to a public repository, so the comment never carries the real address, the article's URL or title, or screenshots; those, if worth keeping, go to the git-ignored `local/` directory.
- [ ] The article saved in step 2 is the one read in step 3: the comment names its item id only; `GET /api/library/items/{id}` shows `source: extension` and `extract_status: done`, `GET /api/core/links?src_id={id}&status=confirmed` contains the manual subject link from step 4 (plus the suggestion accepted in step 5, if one was accepted; a rejected one stays `rejected`), and the notes questions endpoint filtered by that item shows one question.
- [ ] Defect beads filed from the walk describe a sanitized reproduction, never the real article or address.
- [ ] Step 7 is checked by opening the Biblioteca, the reader, Notas, the subject page and the "Sugestões" queue and confirming every entry shown traces to something saved in this walk or before it, never to the invented mock content.
- [ ] Each of the three deferred manual checks (Firefox smoke, logged-in Substack, Telegram from the phone) has its own line: passed, failed with a bead id, or not run with the reason.
- [ ] Every defect found has its own bead (bug or task), linked from that comment by id; "nothing broke" is recorded explicitly when true.
- [ ] Done when: that walk happened and every defect it found has a bead.

## Tests
- Manual (acceptance walk): steps 1-8 above, performed by the person on real data and recorded as a comment on this bead.
- Manual (deferred checks): the Firefox smoke test of the extension, a logged-in Substack save, a Telegram message from the phone.
- The automated tests (unit, integration, the Go vertical end-to-end test, the Playwright phone walk and the extension test) belong to the beads this one depends on; this bead adds none.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** this bead's tracker entry and new defect entries in `.beads/issues.jsonl`, through `br` only. No application source file is edited.

External state: the running Norte instance receives the acceptance article, its link and its question. Defects are filed as new beads, not fixed here.

title: Fix the phone drawer, toolbar overflow and notes sheet in the phone layout
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, on a phone: opening Buscar or Preferências from the side menu leaves the menu on top of them, so search results cannot be tapped; the Biblioteca toolbar is wider than the screen, so the Sugestões tab, the search box, the sort and the unread filter are off-screen; the notes sheet in the reader covers the Inbox/Depois/Arquivo/Lido buttons; tapping the panel icon inside the menu turns it into an empty strip that stays that way; and the home page scrolls sideways by a few pixels. Once this lands, every control on those screens is visible and tappable on a 390-pixel-wide phone.

## Outcome
On viewports under the phone breakpoint, overlays opened from the drawer close it, the library toolbar wraps, the notes sheet sits above the full action bar, the drawer has no collapse control, and no route scrolls horizontally.

## Context
Verified in code with the iPhone 13 (390 px) and Pixel 7 (412 px) profiles:
1. `web/src/shell/ShellOverlay.vue` uses `z-index: 50` (around line 238), the drawer in `web/src/shell/AppShell.vue` uses 60 (around line 192), and `open()` (around lines 46-48) does not close the drawer. `AppShell.vue` (around line 104) already states "arriving somewhere closes it".
2. `.library-tools` in `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue` (around lines 708-712) has no `flex-wrap`, the five-option `web/src/components/ds/SegmentedControl.vue` is `inline-flex` with no wrap (around lines 41-48), and the phone media query (around line 1012) leaves both alone; the document becomes 568 px wide.
3. The reader's notes sheet (`web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderNotesSheet.vue`, `.reader-sheet`) is pinned at `bottom: 62px`, with a comment saying the action bar stays reachable, but `ReaderActionBar.vue` is two rows and 103 px tall, and the sheet sits above it (z 45 against 40).
4. `web/src/shell/AppSidebar.vue` keeps rendering its collapse button inside the drawer; `collapsed` hides the whole nav and nothing resets it on phones.
5. `web/src/components/ds/Carousel.vue` places its arrows at `right: -20px` / `left: -20px` (around lines 150-155) while the phone content padding is 16 px, so `/` is 394 px wide on a 390 px screen.
The library search bead edits the same `LibraryView.vue` (its query builder); this bead only touches its styles, and is ordered after it.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. With Chromium's iPhone 13 profile: open `$B/`, open the menu, tap Buscar, type a word: the drawer covers the left 300 px of the palette.
3. Open `$B/biblioteca`: `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` is 568.
4. Open an item in the reader, tap Anotar: the status chips are covered by the sheet.
5. Open the menu, tap the panel icon at its top right, close and reopen the menu: a 52 px empty strip.
6. On `$B/`, `scrollWidth` is 394.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Opening Buscar or Preferências from the drawer closes the drawer; a result row is tappable (hit test returns the row).
- [ ] On every route, at 390 px and 412 px wide, `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` equals `innerWidth`.
- [ ] All Biblioteca controls (five tabs, Surpresa, search, sort, unread filter) have their bounding box inside the viewport at 390 px.
- [ ] With the notes sheet open, each of Inbox, Depois, Arquivo and Lido passes a hit test.
- [ ] No collapse control is rendered inside the phone drawer, and the drawer always shows the full navigation.
- [ ] Desktop layout at 1440 px is unchanged (existing tests stay green).
- [ ] Done when: steps 2 to 6 all pass under the iPhone 13 and Pixel 7 profiles.

## Tests
- e2e: extend `web/e2e/phone-walk.spec.ts` with a horizontal-overflow assertion over every route, the drawer-then-search tap, the library controls' bounding boxes, and the sheet hit tests, under both device profiles.
- unit: `web/src/shell/drawer.test.ts` gains a case that opening an overlay closes the drawer; `web/src/shell/sidebar.test.ts` a case that the collapse button is absent in drawer mode.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/shell/AppShell.vue`, `web/src/shell/AppSidebar.vue`, `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue` (styles only), `web/src/components/ds/SegmentedControl.vue`, `web/src/components/ds/Carousel.vue`, `web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderNotesSheet.vue`, `web/e2e/phone-walk.spec.ts`, `web/src/shell/drawer.test.ts`, `web/src/shell/sidebar.test.ts`
More than two areas of the web app, which is why this is `size:L`.
close_reason: Merged into local main; full gate 21/21 green at 1c4b9c7, and the end-to-end recheck of the original reproductions passes 16/16 on the final binary.

title: Take the write lock up front so the CLI and the server can save at the same time
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, running `norte save` while the server is running fails now and then with "database is locked", and the server itself can answer a save with an error at the same moment. Once this lands, saving from the command line while the app is open simply waits its turn and succeeds.

## Outcome
Every write transaction opened through the core database handle starts as `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so the 5-second busy timeout covers a contended write across processes.

## Context
The database is SQLite in WAL mode via `modernc.org/sqlite`, opened in `server/internal/core/database.go`, which sets a 5-second `busy_timeout` whose comment says it "covers a checkpoint or another process holding the file briefly". Save transactions are opened with `BeginTx(ctx, nil)` (e.g. `server/internal/library/service.go`, around line 172), which is a deferred transaction: it reads (the canonical-URL lookup) and then upgrades to a write. When another process wrote in between, SQLite returns `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` (517) or a deadlock-avoidance `SQLITE_BUSY` immediately, and the busy handler never runs. Starting writers with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` takes the write lock before the read, so the busy timeout applies. The modernc driver supports this through the `_txlock=immediate` DSN parameter on the write handle. If the core opens one handle for reads and writes, apply it to the handle that writers use; read-only queries outside a transaction are unaffected.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. In one shell, loop 150 saves over HTTP (`curl -XPOST $B/api/library/items` with distinct `url`s and a small `html`), in parallel with a loop of 30 `NORTE_DATA=<same dir> ./server/norte save https://example.com/cli-<n> --html page.html`.
3. Observed: some CLI saves fail with `inserting the library item: database is locked (517)` or `(5) (SQLITE_BUSY)`, and occasionally one HTTP save answers 500.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The DSN (or transaction options) used for write transactions results in `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`; the read path is unchanged.
- [ ] The reproduction above, run three times, gives zero CLI failures and zero HTTP 500s.
- [ ] Done when: a test running two processes (or two independent `*sql.DB` handles on one file) doing interleaved read-then-write transactions completes 200 writes with no busy error.

## Tests
- integration: a test in `server/internal/core/database_test.go` opening two independent handles on one temporary database file and running 100 read-then-write transactions on each concurrently; it must fail (busy error) with the deferred mode and pass with the immediate one. Prove the red by running it once against the old DSN.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/core/database.go`, `server/internal/core/database_test.go`
**Reads only:** `server/internal/library/service.go`
close_reason: Merged into local main (91de441); deep review: all criteria met, 4 mutations caught; e2e 150 HTTP + 30 CLI saves x3 with 0 failures where the old binary had 2-6 CLI failures and 25x500; full gate 17/17 at 54ba546.

title: Build the reading screen for posts, books and papers
description:
## What changes for the user
Reading a material is impossible today. After this lands, you read a post, book or paper with margin notes, highlight a selection, annotate it, switch to exercises and mark it done.

## Outcome
One view that renders the three prototype variants, chosen by `:kind`: a top bar, read mode with marks and a collapsible side panel, and exercises mode.

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. title: Show question kinds and statuses truthfully and land note search hits where the note is
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, the Perguntas list labels every question written on its own as "O quê" and every dropped question as "Aberta". Searching for words in an item's note and opening the result lands on the annotations tab, where that note is not listed. Once this lands, each question shows its real kind (or none) and status, and a note hit opens the item where the note is.

## Outcome
The notes list renders a question's kind only when it has one and maps all three statuses, and a search hit for an item note links to that item's reader with its note panel open.

## Context
1. `web/src/modules/notes/views/NotesView.vue` uses `question.kind ?? 'what'` (around line 251) and maps every non-answered status to `'open'` (around line 253). The contract's `QuestionKind` says "a question written on its own has none", and `QuestionStatus` is `open | answered | dropped` (`api/openapi/notes.yaml`).
2. The notes search provider (`server/internal/notes/search.go`, around lines 14-16) says a hit sends the person to "the tab that lists its kind", and gives item notes the path `/notas?tab=anotacoes`. No notes tab lists item notes; they are visible only in the reader's "Nota" tab of their item. The hit's path should be the item's reader route with a query that opens the note tab (check how the reader selects its tab; if it has no such query, add one).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. `POST $B/api/notes/questions {"text":"Por quê?"}`, then `PATCH` another question to `{"status":"dropped"}`; open `$B/notas?tab=perguntas`: both show the "O quê" badge, the dropped one shows "Aberta".
3. Save an item, `PUT $B/api/notes/items/<id>/note {"text":"Nota do material inteiro."}`; `GET $B/api/core/search?q=inteiro` returns the note with `path: /notas?tab=anotacoes`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A question with no kind shows no kind badge; a question with a kind shows its Portuguese label.
- [ ] A dropped question shows a "Descartada" status; answered and open are unchanged.
- [ ] The note hit's path opens the item's reader with the note visible.
- [ ] Done when: steps 2 and 3 show the corrected badges and the hit lands on the note.

## Tests
- unit: cases in `web/src/modules/notes/views/NotesView.test.ts` for kindless and dropped questions.
- unit: a case in `server/internal/notes/search_test.go` asserting the item-note hit path.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/modules/notes/views/NotesView.vue`, `web/src/modules/notes/views/NotesView.test.ts`, `server/internal/notes/search.go`, `server/internal/notes/search_test.go`, and the reader's tab query in `web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderView.vue` only if one does not exist
**Reads only:** `api/openapi/notes.yaml`

title: Resolve links against the final URL after redirects and decode non-UTF-8 page metadata
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, saving a short link (t.co, bit.ly, a newsletter tracking link) produces an article whose in-text links all point at the short-link service and whose site reads as that service. Saving a page written in an older encoding such as ISO-8859-1 shows a garbled title. Once this lands, links and the site name come from the page actually read, and titles show their accents correctly.

## Outcome
Extraction uses the fetch's final URL (after redirects) as the base for links, images and `site`, and the metadata parser decodes the page with its declared charset.

## Context
The fetcher follows up to five redirects and records `FinalURL` (`server/internal/library/fetch.go`, around lines 69 and 335), but nothing reads it: extraction parses `item.Url` (`server/internal/library/extract.go`, around line 149) and the extractor uses it as the base (`server/internal/library/extractor.go`, around line 96). Measured: saving `https://httpbin.org/redirect-to?url=https%3A%2F%2Fgo.dev%2Fblog%2Fgo1.22` gives `site: httpbin.org` and in-article links such as `https://httpbin.org/blog/pgo`. The final URL must be persisted with the fetched snapshot (e.g. in the item's `meta`, next to `snapshot_source`) so a later re-extraction from the stored snapshot uses it too. Whether the final URL should also dedupe against an existing item is out of scope here.

Separately, `server/internal/library/metadata.go` (around line 74) runs `html.Parse(strings.NewReader(string(source)))` on the raw bytes, while the body text is decoded correctly by the readability library. A latin-1 page's title is stored as invalid UTF-8 (`hex` shows `E7E36F` for `ção`) and copied into the registry and FTS. `golang.org/x/net/html/charset.NewReader` (with the response's Content-Type, when known) decodes by the `<meta charset>` and the header.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. `POST $B/api/library/items` with `{"url":"https://httpbin.org/redirect-to?url=https%3A%2F%2Fgo.dev%2Fblog%2Fgo1.22"}`; after `done`, `site` is `httpbin.org` and `content_html` links point at `https://httpbin.org/...`.
3. `NORTE_DATA=<dir> ./server/norte save https://example.com/latin1 --html page-latin1.html` where the file is ISO-8859-1 bytes with `<meta charset='iso-8859-1'><title>Acentuação</title>`; the stored title is mojibake.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After step 2, `site` is `go.dev` and every relative link in `content_html` resolves under `https://go.dev/`.
- [ ] Re-extracting that item from its stored snapshot (`POST .../extract` with no refresh) keeps `site` and the links on `go.dev`.
- [ ] After step 3, the title is `Acentuação` and is valid UTF-8 in `library_items`, `core_items` and the search results.
- [ ] A UTF-8 page and a page with no declared charset are unchanged.
- [ ] Done when: both reproductions show the expected values.

## Tests
- unit: `server/internal/library/extract_test.go` gains a case extracting a snapshot whose recorded final URL differs from the item URL and asserts the link base and `site`.
- unit: `server/internal/library/fetch_test.go` (or a metadata test) gains a latin-1 fixture asserting the decoded title.
- integration: a fetch test with an `httptest` redirect chain asserting the final URL is recorded with the snapshot.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/library/extract.go`, `server/internal/library/extractor.go`, `server/internal/library/fetch.go`, `server/internal/library/metadata.go`, and their tests
The database schema is not changed (the final URL goes into the existing `meta` JSON).

title: Add the "what to read now" view and the serendipity button
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the library can be filtered by status, kind and unread and sorted by date or title, but nothing ranks it by what the person is focused on, so whatever was saved weeks ago about the subject now in focus is buried. After this lands, the Biblioteca has a "o que ler agora" view that puts first the unread items linked to what the person is focused on, and a "surpresa" button that opens a random unread item — preferably one away from the current focus — for the bored moment.

## Outcome
`GET /api/library/items?view=now` ranks unread items by a focus score; `GET /api/library/items/random` samples unread items weighted away from the focus, with an optional seed for tests; the Biblioteca gets the view selector and the serendipity button.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. The measure of its first delivery is "a link saved at the wrong moment reappears at the right one". The library has three ways to be looked at: the default list by date saved; "what to read now", ranked by relation to the current focus, selectable and not the default; and a serendipity button that opens a random unread item, preferably unrelated to the focus.

`server/` is the Go backend. The library's list endpoint `GET /api/library/items` already supports `view=inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo`, `tipo`, `unread`, `sort`, `q` and cursor pagination (the cursor encodes the sort value, the id as tie-breaker and a hash of the filters; every sort is a total order). The core has `core_links(src_id, dst_id, kind, source, status, confidence)` — `status` `confirmed|suggested|rejected`, `confidence` null or in [0, 1] — and `GET /api/core/focus`, which returns the focus targets: subjects with `focus = true` plus each enabled module's in-progress items. Items are `library_items` with `unread`, `saved_at`.

Decided:

- **Focus score** of an item = the sum over its links whose `dst_id` is a focus target of `1.0` for a `confirmed` link and `confidence` (or `0.5` when null) for a `suggested` one; `rejected` links count 0.
- **`view=now`**: unread items ordered by focus score descending, ties by `saved_at` descending, then id; the score is computed in the query (not stored), and the cursor encodes it. Items with score 0 follow the scored ones in `saved_at` order.
- **Random**: `GET /api/library/items/random?away_from_focus=true` samples one unread item with weight `1 / (1 + focus_score)`; `away_from_focus=false` samples uniformly. Optional `seed` and `n` (draws in one call, with replacement; `n` defaults to 1 and must be within 1..100, anything else returns 400) make it reproducible: the same seed and data return the same ids, and unit tests drive the weighting through an injected random source; without a seed it uses a fresh source. Returns item summaries.
- **Frontend**: a view selector in the Biblioteca ("por data" default, "o que ler agora") and a "surpresa" button that opens the drawn item in the reader.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With two focus targets A and B, and items linked as: x→A confirmed, y→A suggested 0.8, z→B suggested null, w→A rejected, v unlinked — `view=now` returns x (1.0), y (0.8), z (0.5), then w and v by `saved_at` descending, exactly as the test computes by hand.
- [ ] A read item (`unread = false`) never appears in `view=now` or in a random draw.
- [ ] `view=now` paginates with `limit=2` with no duplicates or gaps, and a cursor reused with `view=tudo` is refused with 400.
- [ ] Two calls with `seed=42&n=20` on the same data return the same 20 ids; with an injected random source returning fixed values, the draw picks exactly the items the test computes from the weights.
- [ ] A component test asserts the Biblioteca's first request uses the date order (no `view=now`), that `view=now` is requested only after it is selected, and that "surpresa" calls the random endpoint with `away_from_focus=true`.
- [ ] `n=0`, a negative `n` and `n=101` return the standard 400 envelope; an omitted `n` returns exactly one item.
- [ ] With no unread items, the random endpoint returns 404 with the standard error envelope and the button shows "nada para ler".
- [ ] An unseeded 100-draw check that unfocused items are drawn more often than focused ones is a benchmark run by the review, not a gate.
- [ ] Done when: with two focus targets, `view=now` lists their linked items first in the exact score order a test computes by hand, and the random endpoint is reproducible for a fixed seed and picks the expected items under an injected random source.

## Tests
- Integration (Go, `httptest` + temp `NORTE_DATA`): the score-order fixture; pagination of `view=now`; seeded draws; empty case.
- Unit (Go): the weight function.
- Component (Vitest, fake provider): view selector switches the query; "surpresa" navigates to the drawn item.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/library/` (the `now` view query, the random endpoint), `api/openapi/library.yaml` and generated outputs, `web/src/modules/library/` (selector and button).
**Reads only:** `core_links`, the focus service in `server/internal/core/`.

Library server, its contract and its frontend; size M.
close_reason: Merged into local main 770326a (GitHub unreachable). Gate 12/12 green on the merged tree. Review: 14 mutations; the score-order test could not fail because the fixture's save order equalled its score order (3 mutations survived) - fixture back-dated so newest-first differs from score order, all 3 now red; cursor compares a ROUND(score,9) instead of raw floats. Open, non-blocking: the draw reads every unread (id, score) into memory; the component's 'ranked above' assertion exercises the fake's ordering, not the server's.

title: Save links sent to a private Telegram chat
description:
## What changes for the user
The phone is where links often arrive, but there is no way to save from it into Norte yet. Until a proper share button exists, the person can send a link to a private Telegram chat with Norte's bot: it appears in the library inbox within seconds, any text sent with the link becomes the "why I saved this" note, and the bot replies with the article's title and a link to read it in Norte — or says it was saved but the text could not be extracted.

## Outcome
A Telegram long-polling adapter inside the library module, started by `norte serve` when `NORTE_TELEGRAM_TOKEN` is set: it accepts URLs only from the configured chat, saves them like an extension save without HTML, advances a persisted update cursor in the same transaction as the save, and replies through a `notify_telegram` job with at-least-once delivery: a completed reply suppresses later replays, but every crash between Telegram accepting a send and `replied_at` being written can repeat that reply, because Telegram offers no idempotency key. Tested against a Telegram fake.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. The phone is a reader, not a capture device; a share-sheet entry comes later, and until then a Telegram chat the backend listens to is the temporary phone entry. It is an input adapter of the library, not a module, and is expected to be removed when the share sheet exists.

`server/` is the Go backend. The library's save service `Save(ctx, tx, input)` takes `{url, title?, html?, selection?, why?, link_to?}`, inserts a `library_items` row (with `source` in `app|extension|cli|telegram|import` and a JSON `meta` column), dedupes by canonical URL (a URL already saved returns the existing item and applies the new `why`), and enqueues an `extract` job. The extraction job, on success or final failure, already enqueues one `notify_telegram` job per entry of `meta.telegram_messages` without `replied_at`, keyed by `(chat_id, message_id, item_id)`; this bead registers that job's handler. The core has `core_settings(key, value, updated_at)` for server-side cursors; the jobs queue retries a failing handler at +1 min and +5 min, and a crash after a handler's effect and before its status write replays it. The module interface has `Start(ctx)`, called by `norte serve` only, for long-running adapters. Settings: `NORTE_TELEGRAM_TOKEN` (secret: never a flag, never logged), `NORTE_TELEGRAM_CHAT` (the only chat id accepted), `NORTE_PUBLIC_URL` (the URL the phone reaches; used for the link in replies).

Decided:

- **Location**: `server/internal/library/telegram/`, started by the library module's `Start(ctx)` when the token is set.
- **Startup validation** when the token is set: `NORTE_TELEGRAM_CHAT` must be a number and `NORTE_PUBLIC_URL` an absolute `http(s)` URL; otherwise `serve` exits non-zero naming the setting.
- **Polling**: `getUpdates` long polling with `offset = telegram_update_id + 1` (from `core_settings`), timeout 30 s. For each update: if it comes from the allowed chat and its text contains a URL, save the **first** URL with `source = telegram`, the rest of the message text (URL removed, trimmed) as `why` if non-empty, and append `{chat_id, message_id, replied_at: null}` to `meta.telegram_messages` in the same transaction. The `update_id` is advanced in `core_settings` **in the same transaction** as the save and the enqueue, so a restart neither replays nor skips a message; updates from other chats or without a URL also advance it (in their own small transaction). Delivery is at least once.
- **One reply per message, not per item.** Each accepted message is recorded on the item as an entry of `meta.telegram_messages` (`[{chat_id, message_id, replied_at}]`), appended in the save transaction; a duplicate save of a URL that was first saved from the extension or the CLI appends the entry and does not change the item's `source`. If the item's extraction is already terminal (`done` or `failed`), the save transaction enqueues `notify_telegram` for that message at once; if it is `pending`, the extraction job's terminal step enqueues one for every entry without `replied_at`.
- **Reply job** `notify_telegram`, payload `{chat_id, message_id, item_id}`, dedupe key built from those three: a replayed job is a no-op while queued or running. After it is done, the handler's first step reads that message's entry and exits if `replied_at` is set, and its last step sets it, so a replay after completion sends nothing. Reply text: the title and `NORTE_PUBLIC_URL` + `/biblioteca/<item id>` on success; "salvo, mas não consegui extrair o texto" and the same link on failure. The duplicate that remains is a crash between the send and that write: each such crash can repeat the reply once (Telegram has no idempotency key), and a run that completes its write sends nothing more. The handler's comment documents it.
- **Telegram fake**: an `httptest` server implementing `getUpdates` and `sendMessage` with scripted updates, under `server/internal/library/telegram/telegramtest/`; no test reaches Telegram.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Against the fake, a message from the allowed chat containing a URL creates an inbox item with `source = telegram` within 10 seconds of the fake delivering it; the text around the URL becomes `why`.
- [ ] A message from another chat creates nothing and still advances `telegram_update_id`.
- [ ] Stopping and restarting the poller after a save does not save the message again (the fake re-offers updates from the persisted offset).
- [ ] A message whose URL was already saved from the CLI and already extracted returns the existing item (one row, `source` unchanged) and gets its own reply within one worker cycle.
- [ ] Two messages with the same URL each get one reply.
- [ ] After a successful extraction the fake receives exactly one `sendMessage` with the title and the public link; after a final extraction failure, one with the failure text.
- [ ] Running the `notify_telegram` handler again after it completed sends nothing.
- [ ] A test that simulates two consecutive crashes after `sendMessage` and before `replied_at` is written, then a clean run, shows three sends in total, and later replays send nothing.
- [ ] With the token set and `NORTE_TELEGRAM_CHAT=abc`, `norte serve` exits non-zero naming `NORTE_TELEGRAM_CHAT`; the same for a relative `NORTE_PUBLIC_URL`.
- [ ] The token never appears in any log line.
- [ ] Done when: a URL sent from the phone appears in the inbox within ten seconds, a replayed job sends nothing, a restart after the save does not re-save the message, and the duplicate a crash can cause is documented in the job's comment and covered by a test showing one crash yields exactly one repeat.

## Tests
- Integration (Go, Telegram fake + temp `NORTE_DATA` + worker with a fake clock): every criterion above.
- Unit (Go): URL detection and `why` derivation over a table of message texts (URL at start, middle, end; several URLs; none).
- Manual (recorded in the first delivery's acceptance walk): a real message from the phone.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/library/telegram/` (new: poller, reply handler, fake), `server/internal/library/` (`Start` wiring and the `notify_telegram` handler registration).
**Reads only:** the library save service, `core_settings`, the jobs queue, the config.

One package inside the library module; size M.

title: Create the typed mock data every screen reads
description:
## What changes for the user
Every screen shows lists of articles, courses, projects and tasks, and clicking one must open the matching detail. After this lands, all screens draw from one consistent set of invented data, so links between them land on real items.

## Outcome
`web/src/mock/` with TypeScript types and data for library items, curricula (modules, materials, exercises), review decks and cards, notes (highlights, annotations, questions), areas, projects (features, bugs, priorities), decisions (options), tasks (steps, bucket) and sessions. A small in-memory store lets screens mutate it during a session.

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Open `design/prototypes/Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html` in a browser to see the screen. Read `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html` for markup, inline styles and behaviour. The behaviour is a `class Component extends DCLogic` block with React-style `state`/`setState`. The template uses a design-tool runtime whose `sc-if`, `sc-for` and `{{ }}` bindings map almost one to one onto `v-if`, `v-for` and `{{ }}`. Prototype links point at `Norte - X.dc.html?param=`; translate them into the routes below.
- `design/system/` holds the committed design system. It has tokens in `tokens.css`/`tokens.json` (colour, type, a 4px spacing scale, radius, shadow), one `components/<Name>/README.md` per component, props in `components/index.d.ts`, and screenshots in `screenshots/`. Fonts are in `fonts/`: Schibsted Grotesk for display, Geist for sans and Commit Mono for mono.
- There are two themes, Claro and Escuro, switched by `data-theme` on the root element and stored in `localStorage` under `norte-theme`. The visual rule is quiet: one cobalt accent, no cards, no gradients, no warm colours.

Route table (shared by every screen):
- `/` is Início (Command Home).
- `/biblioteca` is the library, with query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`.
- `/notas` is notes, with query `tab` = `highlights|anotacoes|perguntas`.
- `/revisao` is the flashcard review.
- `/estudo` is the Estudo home (Currículos and Assuntos).
- `/curriculos/:slug` is one curriculum.
- `/material/:kind/:id` is one reading item, where kind is `post|livro|paper`.
- `/projetos` is the project list.
- `/areas/:id` is one area.
- `/projetos/:id` is one project.
- `/decisoes/:id` is one decision.
- `/tarefas/:id` is one task.

The repo is public. Never copy the prototype's mock content into code; use the neutral invented data in `web/src/mock/`. UI strings stay Portuguese.

The repo is a monorepo: the Vue app lives in `web/` and a Go backend will live in `server/` and later serve the built app from one binary. All frontend paths below are under `web/`; `design/` stays at the repo root. The gate is `npm run build && npm test`, run in `web/`.

The shapes come from the prototype's `DCLogic` blocks: read the `state` and data arrays in each `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html`. Ids must be stable strings, because routes use them: curriculum slugs, `a-<name>` for areas, and decision ids. The content must be invented and neutral. Use generic topics such as compilers, typography, gardening or a home-server project. Do not reuse any item, note or person's name from the prototype's mock data. Public authors and public URLs in the library are fine. Mutations needed by screens: change a library item's status (inbox/depois/arquivo/read), add a saved link, add a question, rate a card, decide or postpone a decision, toggle task steps and done, add a project, task or session, add or edit an area (including archive), edit a curriculum, and add a highlight or annotation to a material. Use a `reactive()` store module, not Pinia.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `web/src/mock/types.ts` defines one exported type per entity listed in the outcome.
- [ ] Counts at least: 18 library items across all six `tipo` values, 9 curricula of which 2 are in progress, 3 decks with 24 cards due, 6 areas, 8 projects, 4 decisions, 12 tasks, and 10 notes of each kind.
- [ ] Every cross-reference id (the project of a task, a decision's blocked tasks, a material's curriculum) resolves to an existing entity; a test asserts it.
- [ ] `web/src/mock/store.ts` exposes the mutations listed in the context as functions, and screens update reactively when they are called.
- [ ] No title or note text in `web/src/mock/` is copied verbatim from `design/prototypes/*/template.html`; check it locally by searching each mock string in the templates, which exist only in the main checkout.
- [ ] Done when: the referential-integrity test and the mutation tests pass.

## Tests
- Unit: referential integrity over every cross-reference; each store mutation changes the expected entity and nothing else.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/mock/`

New directory only.

title: Suggest destinations for saved links with the LLM classifier
description:
## What changes for the user
Most links are saved without saying where they belong, because at the moment of saving there is no time to think about it. After this lands, Norte suggests a destination by itself: a few moments after a link is saved and read by the server, a language model proposes up to three subjects or focus targets it belongs to, and a "Sugestões" tab in the Biblioteca shows each suggestion to accept or reject. Nothing is linked without the person's yes, and a rejected suggestion is never proposed again.

## Outcome
The core's LLM client, the `classify` job and its prompt, the rule that merges results into `core_links` without touching decided rows, `GET /api/core/links?status=suggested`, and a "Sugestões" review queue in the Biblioteca with accept and reject. A stub LLM server for tests.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. Its core problem: a link is saved at the wrong moment and never finds its destination. Linking at save time is optional; when the person did not link an item, a background job asks an LLM to classify it against the existing subjects and focus targets, and stores the result as a suggestion. A review queue shows suggestions to accept or reject. Nothing is linked silently.

`server/` is the Go backend. The core has: `core_links(id, src_id, dst_id, kind, source, status, confidence, created_at, decided_at)` with `UNIQUE(src_id, dst_id, kind)`, `source` in `manual|llm`, `status` in `confirmed|suggested|rejected`, `confidence` null or in [0, 1] — the only relation mechanism between modules, where a rejected row stays as the record that the pair was rejected; subjects (`core_subjects`, each registered in `core_items`); `GET /api/core/focus` returning focus subjects plus each enabled module's in-progress targets as `{id, type, title}`; `POST /api/core/links/{id}/decide` (accept/reject); the jobs queue (retries at +1 and +5 min, then `failed`; `core.Permanent` fails at once; handlers must be idempotent). The library's extraction job already enqueues a `classify` job (payload `{item_id}`) after a successful extraction when `NORTE_LLM_URL` is set and the item has no `confirmed` link; this bead registers its handler. The library item has `title`, `why` (the person's "why I saved this") and `content_text`. The "Salvos sobre isso" panel lists the `confirmed` `about` links to a target. Settings: `NORTE_LLM_URL` (an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint; empty disables LLM jobs), `NORTE_LLM_MODEL`, `NORTE_LLM_KEY` (secret, never a flag, never logged).

Decided:

- **LLM client** `core.LLM.Complete(ctx, system, user, jsonSchema)` in `server/internal/core/llm.go`: POSTs a chat completion with `response_format` set to the JSON schema, parses the answer as JSON, 30 s timeout, one retry on a timeout or 5xx. Returns `ErrDisabled` when `NORTE_LLM_URL` is empty (and the extraction job then does not enqueue `classify`). The key is sent as a bearer token and never logged.
- **The prompt** carries: the item's title, its `why`, the first 2,000 characters of `content_text` inside a delimited block that the system prompt marks as untrusted data (instructions inside it are content, not commands — a saved page is attacker-controllable), and the candidate set — every subject plus every `/api/core/focus` target — as `{id, title}`. The answer schema is a ranked list of `{id, confidence}`. The candidate set is deduplicated by id (a focused subject appears once; the subject record wins). The answer is normalised before merging: entries with a non-finite confidence or one outside [0, 1] are dropped, unknown ids are dropped, duplicate ids collapse to their highest confidence, the rest is sorted by confidence descending then id, and at most 3 are kept.
- **Merge rule**: for each kept `(item, target)` call `core.Links.Suggest(tx, item, target, about, confidence)` in one transaction; its state rules (insert a missing pair, update a `suggested` one, never touch decided rows) are the core's. Idempotent by the links' unique index: running the job twice leaves one suggestion per pair. Every run validates and merges its whole answer atomically, so a second run — after a re-extraction, or a replayed extraction that enqueued `classify` again — can update the confidence of existing suggestions and add new candidates, and never touches decided rows. A replay costs one extra LLM call, which is accepted rather than skipping runs that could carry new information.
- **Queue**: `GET /api/core/links?status=suggested` (with the source item's and the target's titles from `core_items`); a "Sugestões" tab in the Biblioteca listing them with accept and reject, each calling the decide endpoint. Accepting makes the item appear on the target's "Salvos sobre isso" panel.
- **Stub LLM server** for tests in `server/internal/core/llmtest/` (an `httptest` server answering chat completions with canned JSON per test), so no test reaches the network.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With the stub LLM answering two candidate ids and one unknown id, a saved item with no link gets exactly two `suggested` links within one worker cycle after extraction, with the stub's confidences; the unknown id produces nothing.
- [ ] With the stub answering five candidates, only the top three are stored.
- [ ] A focused subject appears once in the prompt; a schema-valid stub answer with duplicate, unsorted, out-of-range and unknown entries yields exactly the documented normalised top three; the normaliser is unit-tested directly with `math.NaN()` and infinities; a malformed JSON answer is a job failure (retried), not a normalisation case.
- [ ] Running the `classify` job twice on one item, with the stub's answer changed between runs, updates the confidence of the existing suggestion, adds the new candidate, and leaves one row per pair.
- [ ] A pair already `rejected` or `confirmed` is not changed by a classifier result that names it.
- [ ] The prompt sent to the stub contains the item's title, its `why`, at most 2,000 characters of its text inside the untrusted-data delimiters, and the candidate ids.
- [ ] A registry test proves the classify handler receives the injected client when `NORTE_LLM_URL` is set and `ErrDisabled` behaviour when it is not.
- [ ] With `NORTE_LLM_URL` empty, no `classify` job is enqueued after extraction and `/api/config` reports `llm: false`.
- [ ] Accepting a suggestion in the "Sugestões" tab makes the item appear on the target subject's panel; rejecting removes it from the tab.
- [ ] `NORTE_LLM_KEY` never appears in any log line (a test captures the logs of a full classify run).
- [ ] Done when: against the stub LLM, a saved item with no link gets a suggestion within one worker cycle, running the job twice leaves one suggestion, and accepting it makes the item appear on the target's panel.

## Tests
- Unit (Go): merge rule over the four row states; candidate filtering and top-3 cut; prompt construction (golden file).
- Integration (Go, stub LLM + temp `NORTE_DATA` + worker with a fake clock): save → extract → classify → suggestion; idempotent replay; LLM disabled; log redaction.
- Component (Vitest, fake providers): "Sugestões" tab accept and reject.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/core/llm.go` and `server/internal/core/llmtest/` (new), `server/internal/library/` (the `classify` handler and its registration), `api/openapi/core.yaml` (the `status` filter on links, if not already there) and generated outputs, `web/src/modules/library/` (the "Sugestões" tab), `server/internal/app/` (`Deps` gains the LLM client) and `server/cmd/norte/` (constructing it from `NORTE_LLM_*`).
**Reads only:** `server/internal/core/` links, subjects and focus; the extraction job's enqueue.

Core, library and a frontend tab: more than two modules, so size L, though each part is small.
close_reason: Merged into local main 2a99d86 (GitHub unreachable). Gate 15/15 green after merging main (semantic conflict with norte-agu in LibraryView resolved so the Sugestões tab, the 'O que ler agora' ordering and Surpresa coexist; 3 tests added for the combination). Review: 11/11 criteria MET, 20/20 mutations red. Fixed before merge: transport errors carry host + cause, never the URL (query token); page text cannot close the prompt fence, title and why moved inside it; schema drops maxItems/minimum/maximum (normaliser enforces them) since strict-mode endpoints may reject them; per-attempt timeout injectable and its retry tested; whitespace-only NORTE_LLM_URL counts as unconfigured; chat path appended before the URL's query. Open: real-endpoint call not exercised (no LLM configured here) - first real classify happens in norte-915.
