title: Index heading text, not the headings JSON, in the library full-text search
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, searching the library or the global search for common words such as "text", "level" or "anchor" returns nearly every saved article, because the search reads the machine format of the article's section titles rather than only their words. Once this lands, those words match only articles that actually contain them.

## Outcome
The library's full-text index holds the plain text of the headings (their titles, space-separated), never the JSON they are stored as, for existing items and new ones.

## Context
Extraction stores the article's headings in `library_items.content_headings` as JSON, e.g. `[{"level":1,"text":"Spaced repetition","anchor":"spaced-repetition"}]` (`server/internal/library/extract.go`, around line 290). The FTS5 table `library_fts` and its triggers, defined in `server/internal/library/migrations/00002_library_items.sql`, copy that column verbatim, and `server/internal/library/list.go` weighs it at 7.0 in bm25. So the keys `level`, `text` and `anchor`, and every slug fragment, are indexed for every item with a heading. The contract describes `q` as a query "over the title, the note and the extracted text" (`api/openapi/library.yaml`).

The fix is a new library migration (the next number after `00002`) that recreates the triggers so the indexed value is the heading titles joined by spaces (SQLite's `json_each` over `content_headings`, taking `$.text`), and rebuilds `library_fts` from the table so existing rows are corrected. The Go code and the column format are unchanged. This is the only bead in its batch that adds a migration.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. Save `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spaced_repetition` and wait for `done`.
3. `GET $B/api/library/items?view=tudo&q=anchor` returns the item, although "anchor" appears in none of its title, note or text. `GET $B/api/core/search?q=level` returns it too.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After the migration, `q=anchor`, `q=level` and `q=text` return no item whose title, note and extracted text lack that word.
- [ ] A word that appears only in a heading title still matches its item.
- [ ] Items saved before the migration are corrected by it (the rebuild runs inside the migration).
- [ ] `norte migrate` on a database already at the new version reports nothing to do.
- [ ] Done when: the reproduction above returns no result for `anchor` on a database migrated from the previous version.

## Tests
- integration: a test in `server/internal/library/search_test.go` that saves an item with headings, runs the migration, and asserts the three key words do not match while a heading word does.
- integration: a migration test that creates a database at the previous version with one item, migrates, and asserts the FTS row no longer contains `anchor`.

## Recovery path
The migration's down step restores the previous triggers and rebuilds `library_fts` from the table, which returns the index to its current content. No user data is rewritten: only the derived FTS table changes.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** one new file `server/internal/library/migrations/00003_*.sql`, `server/internal/library/search_test.go`
**Reads only:** `server/internal/library/migrations/00002_library_items.sql`, `server/internal/library/list.go`

title: Translate the Notes module's routes, contract keys and copy to English
description:
## What changes for the user
Notes is where highlights, annotations and questions live, and all of it is Portuguese: the
address is `/notas`, the tabs are addressed as `?tab=anotacoes` and `?tab=perguntas` and read
`Anotações` / `Highlights` / `Perguntas`, the question sets are `Conjuntos de perguntas`, and the
counts the sidebar prints come back from the server under the keys `anotacoes`, `perguntas` and
`conjuntos`. After this change the module answers at `/notes`, its tabs are `?tab=annotations` and
`?tab=questions`, it reads in English, and the API answers in English.

## Outcome
`api/openapi/notes.yaml`, the notes server, the notes routes and the notes screens use English
names: the summary keys are `annotations`, `questions` and `question_sets`, the routes are
`/notes`, `/notes/sets` and `/notes/sets/:id`, and every string the module shows is English.

## Context
Routes and copy are one bead per module here, not two. A route record is one object, the sidebar
row that points at it and the screen it opens are in the same files, and splitting them would mean
two beads editing the same lines — which is how the previous split produced six beads sharing one
file.

The contract keys are why this reaches the server as well: `api/openapi/notes.yaml:769-785`
declares the summary object with the Portuguese keys, the generator turns them into the Go fields
`Anotacoes`, `Perguntas` and `Conjuntos` that `server/internal/notes/handlers.go:386-388` fills,
and the same generator turns them into the TypeScript the sidebar reads. Renaming a key renames
all three at once, and the gate typechecks the web against the regenerated types, so they cannot
land apart.

The renames:

| today | English |
| --- | --- |
| `/notas` name `notas` title `Notas` | `/notes` name `notes` title `Notes` |
| `/notas/conjuntos` name `notas-conjuntos` title `Conjuntos de perguntas` | `/notes/sets` name `notes-question-sets` title `Question sets` |
| `/notas/conjuntos/:id` name `notas-conjunto` title `Conjunto de perguntas` | `/notes/sets/:id` name `notes-question-set` title `Question set` |
| `?tab=anotacoes`, `?tab=perguntas` | `?tab=annotations`, `?tab=questions` |
| sidebar ids `anotacoes`, `perguntas-notas`, `conjuntos`, `estudo-perguntas` | `annotations`, `notes-questions`, `question-sets`, `study-questions` |
| summary keys `anotacoes`, `perguntas`, `conjuntos` | `annotations`, `questions`, `question_sets` |
| `server/internal/notes/search.go:20-21` `/notas?tab=anotacoes`, `/notas?tab=perguntas` | the English paths |

Two Portuguese Go test names sit at `server/internal/notes/api_test.go:198,265`:
`TestVirarHighlightOnASavedSelection` and `TestVirarPerguntaFromAnAnnotation`. The glossary has
Question and Highlight as attributes but no verb for the conversion, and the inventory now proposes
one: **`TurnInto`**, giving `TestTurnAHighlightIntoAQuestionOnASavedSelection` and
`TestTurnAnAnnotationIntoAQuestion`, with `Turn into a question` as the visible label. This bead
uses that verb and does not reopen it; if the implementation finds the verb wrong for a reason the
inventory did not see, it says so in the pull request and still ships one verb everywhere.

Two things in this module are **not** this bead's: the reader's `?notas=nota` deep link and the
`/biblioteca/<id>` path at `web/src/modules/notes/views/NotesView.vue:119` belong to the model
bead, which owns the library's address; and the notes labels asserted inside
`web/src/shell/AppShell.test.ts` are shared with norte-05j, which owns that file.

This module's screens and tests hold 33 accented rows in `api_test.go`, 14 in `NotesView.test.ts`
and 8 in `ReaderNotesPanel.vue` — mostly fixture prose and assertion strings, which move with the
strings they assert. The per-file counts are in §1.4 of the inventory comment on norte-3ab.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `api/openapi/notes.yaml`'s summary object declares `annotations`, `questions` and
      `question_sets`, no description names `Notas` or a Portuguese tab, and `bin/check-contracts`
      passes.
- [ ] `server/internal/notes/` fills the regenerated English fields, builds `/notes?tab=annotations`
      and `/notes?tab=questions`, and no Go identifier in the module is Portuguese.
- [ ] The module declares `/notes`, `/notes/sets` and `/notes/sets/:id` with the English route
      names and titles, and `web/src/modules/notes/manifest.ts` lists exactly those three paths.
- [ ] The notes screen reads the `tab` query values `annotations`, `highlights` and `questions`,
      and selects a tab from the query.
- [ ] Every string the notes screens show is English, including the three tabs, the question-set
      screens and the reader's notes panel, and the four sidebar ids are English.
- [ ] The two Go test names use `TurnInto`, and the same verb appears in the visible label and in
      any identifier the conversion gains.
- [ ] The **notes forbidden-term check** comes back empty:

          rg -n --no-heading -g '!server/gen' -g '!**/db/**' -g '!web/src/api' \
            -e '[À-ÿ]' \
            -e '(?i)\b(notas|nota|anotacoes|anotacao|perguntas|pergunta|conjuntos|conjunto|virar|destaque|trecho|salvar|fechar|abrir|carregar|nenhum|nenhuma|nada|responder|resposta|estudo)\b' \
            -e '/notas' -e 'tab=(anotacoes|perguntas)' -e "name: ?'notas" \
            web/src/modules/notes server/internal/notes api/openapi/notes.yaml

      with one allowlisted exception, named in the inventory: `server/internal/notes/list.go:159,186`
      and `server/internal/notes/search.go:45`, whose comments quote `MEMÓRIA`/`memória` to show
      what the accent-stripping comparison does. Those comments stay; a comment that demonstrates
      accent stripping cannot do so in English.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- unit (Go): the summary endpoint answers the three English keys with the right counts.
- unit (Go): the notes search paths are `/notes?tab=annotations` and `/notes?tab=questions`.
- unit (Go): the two renamed conversion tests, unchanged in what they assert.
- unit: the route table holds the three English paths and names, and `manifest.routePaths` matches.
- component: the notes screen renders the three English tabs and selects one from the `tab` query.
- component: the reader's notes panel renders in English inside the library's reader.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `api/openapi/notes.yaml`, `server/internal/notes/handlers.go`,
`server/internal/notes/list.go`, `server/internal/notes/service.go`,
`server/internal/notes/apimapping.go`, `server/internal/notes/notes.go`,
`server/internal/notes/anchor_test.go`, `server/internal/notes/api_test.go`,
`server/internal/notes/schema_test.go`, `server/internal/notes/reanchor.go`,
`web/src/modules/notes/index.ts`, `web/src/modules/notes/manifest.ts`,
`web/src/modules/notes/views/NotesView.test.ts`,
`web/src/modules/notes/views/QuestionSetsView.vue`,

title: Carry the library's location model, English names and Suggestions behaviour through contract, data, server and wire
description:
## What changes for the user
The library speaks Portuguese today: a saved book is a `livro`, an item put off is `depois`, the
one line written when saving is a `why`, and the address is `/biblioteca`. It also has a shelf that
does not exist — a "Shortlist" shortcut that silently opens the whole library — and a
focus-ranked list that refuses to show anything already read. After this change the library has
five real locations: Inbox, Up Next, Later, Archive and Stash; it answers at `/library`; and
Suggestions reads every location, unread first. Everything already saved keeps working: a row that
was `depois` is in Later, a row that was `arquivo` is in the Archive.

The screens still read in Portuguese when this bead lands. That is deliberate and it is what keeps
this bead finite — see §Why the copy is not here.

## Outcome
`api/openapi/library.yaml`, the library's stored rows, the library's Go service, its CLI, its
Telegram capture, the browser extension's save request and every typed consumer of a library value
use the English names and the five-value `location` field. `why` is `reason`, `livro`/`curso`/`post`
are `book`/`course`/`article`, the `tudo` view is `all`, `now` is `suggestions`, the `tipo`
parameter is `kind`, the Shortlist shortcut is gone, and Suggestions reads every location and lists
unread before read within one focus score.

## Context
This bead is end-to-end on purpose, and the reason is written into the repo.
`web/src/modules/library/data/source.ts` makes the web's types *be* the contract's types, and says
why: "Nothing here is renamed on the way in. A field called `saved_at` on the wire stays
`saved_at` in the screens, because a view that reads `savedAt` is a view that cannot be checked
against `api/openapi/library.yaml` by eye." There is therefore no rename seam between the wire and
the screens. `web/package.json`'s `build` runs `vue-tsc --build`, whose `tsconfig.app.json` covers
`src/**/*` including every `*.test.ts`, and `tsconfig.e2e.json` covers `e2e/**/*.ts`; the gate's
`generate` check runs that build. A contract value renamed in one pull request and followed in the
screens in another leaves a red gate in between. Contract, server, screens and every typed
consumer move together or not at all.

### Why the copy is not here
The visible strings stay Portuguese through this bead. A label is not a value: the sidebar row can
read `Depois` while the value behind it is `later`, and `VIEW_LABELS` can map `up_next` to a
Portuguese word. Keeping the copy out is what separates this bead from the five copy beads it
blocks, and it is what makes each of those a bounded diff instead of a second pass over the same
files. Two consequences the implementation must respect:

- Every `VIEW_LABELS`-style map gains an entry for `up_next` and `stash`, in Portuguese, written to
  be replaced. The empty states for the two new locations are the same.
- A test that asserts a *label* is left alone. A test that asserts a *value* — a fixture `kind`, a
  `v=` query, a patch body — is this bead's.

### What changes, precisely
- **`status` becomes `location`**, schema `ItemStatus` becomes `ItemLocation`, with five values
  `inbox`, `up_next`, `later`, `archive`, `stash`. Existing rows map `inbox -> inbox`,
  `depois -> later`, `arquivo -> archive`; nothing maps to `up_next` or `stash`, so both start
  empty.
- **`LibraryView`** gains the five locations plus `all` (was `tudo`) and `suggestions` (was `now`).
- **The kinds** become `article`, `book`, `paper`, `video`, `podcast`, `newsletter`, `course`. The
  migration rewrites `library_items.kind` and also `core_items.type` for the rows whose `module`
  is `library`: the library wrote those values and core only stores what a module hands it, so the
  library is the owner of the rewrite. That is the one cross-owner write in this change, and it
  gets a comment saying so.
- **`why` becomes `reason`** in the column, in the `library_fts` virtual table, in all three FTS
  triggers, in the bm25 weight order documented at `migrations/00002_library_items.sql:72`, in the
  contract, in `norte library save --why`, in the Telegram capture and in the extension's request
  body.
- **The sidebar** lists six rows — Inbox, Up Next, Later, Archive, Stash, All — and the fake
  Shortlist shortcut at `web/src/modules/library/index.ts:82-89` is removed, because Up Next is
  what it was pretending to be.
- **`sugestoes` becomes `pending-connections`** as the `v=` tab value, so that the screen does not
  end up with a Suggestions view and a Suggestions tab meaning two different things.
- **The library's own routes** become `/library`, `/library/:id`, route names `library` and
  `reader`; `/material/:kind/:id` is already English and keeps its name. They are here rather than
  in a route bead because `v=` query values, the `name:` route references in three other modules'
  views and the extension's deep link all sit in files this bead already owns. Every other
  Portuguese route belongs to its own module's bead.
- **Suggestions reads every location, unread first.** Two things make it unread-only today and
  both are deliberate, so both are undone deliberately:
  - `server/internal/library/list.go:178` sets `unread := true` inside the `view == LibraryViewNow`
    branch; the comment there explains that it normalises the flag at that point so a cursor issued
    with no `unread` parameter continues a list asked for with `unread=true`, because the filter
    hash has to match. The forcing goes; `in.Unread` is already one of the four inputs to
    `libraryFilterHash`, so the hash already distinguishes "unread only" from "everything". What
    must not happen is the flag being normalised at all: the view no longer has an opinion.
  - `server/internal/library/now.go:144-147` refuses `unread=false` with "the now view is what is
    left to read". That refusal goes. The other two refusals in `libraryRefuseNowConflicts` — `q`
    and an explicit `sort` — stay, because the view still carries its own order.
  The ordering change is the substantive part. `libraryNowOrderBy` orders by score, then
  `saved_at`, then `id`, and the cursor predicate at `server/internal/library/list.go:329-336` is
  three levels deep for exactly that reason, with a comment explaining that a page boundary inside
  a run of equal scores has to continue by the saved date rather than restarting the run. Adding
  unread as the second key makes it four levels — score, unread, `saved_at`, `id` — and
  `libraryCursorFor` at `server/internal/library/list.go:344-360` has to carry the unread flag of
  the row it paged on. Getting this wrong is not visible on the first page: it shows up as a
  repeated or skipped item at a page boundary where several items share a score, which is the
  common case when the focus is narrow. `unread` is stored as an integer 0 or 1, so "unread first"
  is `unread DESC` and the cursor comparison is on that integer, not on a boolean. Bump
  `libraryCursorVersion` so a cursor issued by the old build is refused as undecodable rather than
  silently paging from the wrong position, which is what that field already exists for.
- **The reader's location control offers all five destinations.** It offers three today
  (`web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderView.vue:66-69`). Without this, an implementation could
  satisfy every other criterion and leave Up Next permanently unreachable.

Applied migrations are never edited — `migrations/00002_library_items.sql` says so itself — so this
is a new `00004_library_location.sql`. SQLite cannot alter a `CHECK` constraint and an FTS5 column
cannot be renamed, so the up step is a rebuild: create the new table with the English columns and
the five-value check, copy every row through the value mapping, drop the old table, rename the new
one, recreate the four indexes (`library_items_by_status_saved` becomes
`library_items_by_location_saved`), drop and recreate `library_fts` and its three triggers, and
repopulate the FTS table from the copied rows.

The full name-by-name inventory, with every file and line, is the inventory comment on norte-3ab.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `api/openapi/library.yaml` names `location` with the five values, `all` and `suggestions`,
      the English kinds, the `kind` query parameter and `reason`; `LibraryCounts.views` has the
      five locations and `all`, and `LibraryCounts.kinds` the English kinds. The forbidden-term
      check below finds nothing in that file, and `bin/check-contracts` passes.
- [ ] `server/internal/library/migrations/00004_library_location.sql` rewrites `library_items` as
      described, maps `depois -> later` and `arquivo -> archive`, maps `post -> article`,
      `livro -> book` and `curso -> course` in `library_items.kind`, rewrites `core_items.type` for
      `module = 'library'` with the same three mappings, and leaves no row with a value outside the
      five locations or the seven kinds.
- [ ] The migration's `-- +goose Down` restores the three-value `status` column, the `why` column
      and all three Portuguese kinds in **both** `library_items.kind` and `core_items.type` for
      `module = 'library'`, and writes every row whose location is `up_next` or `stash` into a
      preservation table `library_location_preserved (item_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, location TEXT NOT
      NULL)` before collapsing it. The up step reads that table back, restores those locations for
      the ids still present, and drops it.
- [ ] The library's Go service accepts and stores the five locations and refuses a sixth with
      `unknown location %q` on field `location`; `libraryValidStatuses` is `libraryValidLocations`.
- [ ] `norte library save --reason` is the flag, and `--why` no longer exists.
- [ ] The extension's save request sends `reason`, not `why`, and
      `extension/tests/save.e2e.mjs` asserts the saved item carries it. The contract pins
      `additionalProperties: false`, so a request still carrying `why` is refused rather than
      silently dropped: the extension and the contract land together or the extension stops saving.
- [ ] `view=suggestions` returns items from every location, including `archive` and `stash`;
      within one focus score every unread item comes before every read one; across scores the
      higher score comes first regardless of unread state.
- [ ] `view=suggestions&unread=false` answers 200 and returns only read items; `q` and an explicit
      `sort` under `view=suggestions` are still refused with the messages those refusals carry.
- [ ] Paging through a list where at least four items share one focus score and straddle the unread
      boundary returns each item exactly once, over at least three pages.
- [ ] The library answers at `/library` and `/library/:id`, route names `library` and `reader`; the
      palette entry the server builds for a library item, the Telegram item link and the
      extension's "open in Norte" link all point at `/library/<id>`.
- [ ] The reader's location control offers all five destinations, and selecting `up_next` or
      `stash` sends `{ location: 'up_next' }` / `{ location: 'stash' }`.
- [ ] No Shortlist shortcut is rendered, and the sidebar lists six rows in the order Inbox, Up
      Next, Later, Archive, Stash, All.
- [ ] The **model forbidden-term check** comes back empty over the whole tree:

          rg -n --no-heading -g '!server/gen' -g '!**/db/**' -g '!web/src/api' \
            -e "['\"](depois|arquivo|tudo|livro|curso|sugestoes)['\"]" \
            -e '\b(ItemStatus|LibraryStatus|LibraryShelf|LibraryViewNow|librarySortNow|libraryValidStatuses|libraryRefuseNowConflicts|libraryNowOrderBy)\b' \
            -e '/biblioteca' -e 'v=(depois|tudo|arquivo|sugestoes)' -e "\\bname: ?'(biblioteca|leitor)'" \
            -e '\.why\b' -e '\bwhy = \?' -e '--why' -e "\\bWhy:" \
            web/src web/e2e server/internal server/cmd extension api docs

      Run against the tree as it stands today the command returns 384 lines; after this bead it
      must return only hits the inventory's allowlist (§7.2) names. For this pattern set that is a
      single file: `web/src/modules/projects/views/ProjectView.vue:201`, where `payload.why` is the
      *task's* own `why` — Projects' model, already English, and not the library item's renamed
      field. Every other allowlist entry (the bilingual regexes in
      `server/internal/library/cleanup.go`, the captured pages under
      `server/internal/library/testdata/pages/`, `why` as an English parameter name in
      `server/internal/core/files_test.go`, and `QuestionKind`'s `why` in the design system and the
      notes module) is matched by the broader sweeps the later beads run, not by this one; they are
      listed here so a reviewer reading one bead sees the whole allowlist.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- unit (Go, new `server/internal/library/migrations_test.go`): the up step against a database
  holding `inbox`, `depois` and `arquivo` rows and `post`/`livro`/`curso` kinds, with matching
  `core_items` rows — every row lands on the mapped value in both tables, the FTS table still finds
  a row by its `reason` text, and a row inserted afterwards with `up_next` and with `stash` is
  accepted while a sixth value is refused by the CHECK.
- unit (Go, same file): the down step on that database returns the three-value `status` column, the
  `why` column and `post`/`livro`/`curso` in both `library_items.kind` and `core_items.type`.
- unit (Go, same file): **up, then write `up_next` and `stash` rows, then down, then up** — the two
  rows come back at `up_next` and `stash`, and `library_location_preserved` is gone afterwards.
- unit (Go): `List` accepts each of the five locations and `all`, refuses an unknown view, and
  filters by `location` for a single location but not for `all`.
- unit (Go): a patch to each of the five locations is stored; a patch to `depois` is refused with
  `unknown location "depois"` on field `location`.
- unit (Go): the counts endpoint answers all five locations plus `all`.
- unit (Go): a fixture with two focus scores and read and unread items at each — assert the exact
  returned order under `view=suggestions`, not just membership.
- unit (Go): pagination over a run of equal scores crossing the unread boundary, with a limit of 2,
  collecting every id across pages and asserting the set and the order.
- unit (Go): a cursor issued under `view=suggestions&unread=true` presented with `unread=false` is
  refused, because the filter hash differs.
- unit (Go): the item path the search entry, the Telegram link and the palette use is
  `/library/<id>`.
- component: the reader's location control renders five destinations, and clicking Up Next and
  Stash each sends the matching `{ location: … }` patch body.
- component: the save dialog sends `reason` in the request body.
- unit (extension, `bin/ci extension-test`): the save payload carries `reason` and no `why`.
- e2e (`bin/ci extension-e2e`): the loaded extension against a real temporary Norte server saves a
  cookie-protected fixture page and the saved item carries the typed reason — which is what proves
  the field is accepted rather than refused by the closed schema.
- e2e: `web/e2e/library-search-sort.spec.ts`, `web/e2e/phone-walk.spec.ts`, `web/e2e/csp.spec.ts`,
  `web/e2e/reader-reading-position.spec.ts` and `web/e2e/highlight-anchoring.spec.ts` against the

  addresses and values move.

## Blast radius
This bead edits about 70 files, which is over the reviewability guideline the other beads keep to.
That is a property of the gate, not of the plan, and it is argued in the pull request: every file

Every file under **Shared edits** has exactly one `**Edits:**` owner elsewhere; this bead touches

edges keep two agents off it.

## Recovery path
**The backup is the recovery; the down step is the fallback.** The up step drops and recreates the
table holding the person's whole library, and `norte serve` migrates automatically before opening
the listener (`server/internal/app/cli.go:130-139`), so there is no "start it and decide later".

The data directory is **not** necessarily `$NORTE_DATA`: it resolves from a flag, the environment
or a TOML file (`server/internal/app/config.go:90`). Read the resolved path from the binary rather
than assuming it:

    data="$(norte config | sed -n 's/^data *= *\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p')"
    # with the server stopped:
    sqlite3 "$data/norte.db" ".backup '$data/norte.db.pre-location'"

That backup is a **deployment prerequisite, not advice**: the bead ships a check that refuses to
proceed when `$data/norte.db.pre-location` is absent or older than `$data/norte.db`, so running the
migration without a backup is an error rather than a decision.

Rolling back is `goose down` against the embedded library migrations; the binary exposes no `down`
subcommand today, which is why the preservation table exists. A down step that merely collapsed
`up_next` and `stash` into `inbox` and `arquivo` would lose every post-cutover triage, and the
pre-cutover backup cannot give it back because it predates those writes. The preservation table is
what makes down-then-up lossless, and the `up -> write -> down -> up` test is what proves it.

title: Create the core database, ids, clock and file store
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing visible yet: the app still shows mock data. What changes is that Norte now has a place to keep things. Running `norte migrate` on a fresh machine creates one private database file and a private folder for saved files, so everything saved from the next steps on lives in one directory the person owns and can back up by copying it.

## Outcome
`norte migrate` on an empty data directory creates the core schema in one SQLite file, with the directory and files private to the user. The core package offers the id, clock and time-format helpers every later bead uses, a content-addressed file store with reference tracking, and `norte files gc` that removes only blobs nothing references.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. The repo is a monorepo: `web/` is a Vue 3 frontend that today runs on mock data, and `server/` is the Go backend being built — one static binary with no CGO, SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite`, `sqlc` for typed queries, `goose` for SQL migrations, no ORM. Products are modules switched on by the `NORTE_MODULES` setting; each module owns tables prefixed with its name and no foreign key crosses a module boundary. The "core" is the always-on part that is not a module; its tables carry the `core_` prefix. This bead builds on the server skeleton (Go module under `server/`, cobra CLI with `serve`, `migrate`, `version`, `config`, a config loader that resolves `NORTE_DATA`).

What this bead builds, and why each piece is shaped this way:

- **Database open.** One file, `NORTE_DATA/norte.db`. Pragmas are per connection in `modernc.org/sqlite`, so they go in the DSN: `_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)`, `_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)`, `_pragma=foreign_keys(1)`, `_pragma=synchronous(NORMAL)`. Two `*sql.DB` handles open the same file: a writer with `SetMaxOpenConns(1)`, used for every write and by the jobs worker, and a reader pool for queries. A save or an import is one transaction on the writer. On shutdown (`norte serve` receiving SIGTERM, after in-flight requests drain and the current job finishes or releases its lease) the core runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` on the writer and then closes both handles, so the data directory is one self-contained `norte.db` that can be copied as a backup. One writer avoids `SQLITE_BUSY` storms; the reader pool keeps list queries off the writer.
- **Migrations.** goose with one version table per owner: `goose_core` for the core, and later `goose_<module>` for each module, because one shared version table would make two modules' migration numbers collide. Migrations are SQL files embedded from `server/internal/core/migrations/`. They run only in `norte migrate` and at the start of `norte serve`; `config` and `version` never open the database, so a read-only question never writes.
- **sqlc.** Configured (`sqlc.yaml`) to read queries from `internal/<owner>/queries/` and generate into `internal/<owner>/db/`. Generated code is committed and never edited by hand.
- **Ids and time.** `core.NewID()` returns a UUIDv7 as a 36-character lowercase string; time-ordered, so primary-key inserts stay append-only in SQLite's B-tree. No table uses integer ids. `core.Clock` is the one clock: `Now() time.Time` and `NewTimer(d time.Duration) core.Timer` (a channel plus `Stop`). Production wraps `time.Now` and `time.NewTimer`; `server/internal/core/clocktest` ships a manual clock whose `Advance(d)` moves `Now` and fires every due timer synchronously, used by this bead's gc tests and by every later bead that schedules work. Every timestamp is stored as a fixed-width UTC string `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`, written and parsed only through `core.FormatTime` and `core.ParseTime`, so lexical order equals time order.
- **Schema conventions**, for these tables and every module's: `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` holding a UUIDv7 string; `created_at`/`updated_at` in the fixed UTC format; the owner's prefix on every table name; foreign keys only inside the owner; a `CHECK` on every enumerated column; per-type variable data in a `meta TEXT` JSON column rather than in sparse columns.
- **The core tables**, with every enumerated column under a `CHECK`:
  - `core_items(id, module, type, title, url, created_at)` — the item registry. Every module inserts a row when it creates something that can be the end of a link, so a link can be rendered (type, title, url to open) even when the module owning the other end is disabled. It holds what is needed to *open* an item, never what is needed to read it (no author, image or date).
  - `core_links(id, src_id NOT NULL REFERENCES core_items ON DELETE CASCADE, dst_id NOT NULL REFERENCES core_items ON DELETE CASCADE, kind, source, status, confidence, created_at, decided_at)`, `UNIQUE(src_id, dst_id, kind)`, indexes on `(dst_id, status)` and `(src_id, status)`. `kind` in `about|material_of|derived_from|blocks`; `source` in `manual|llm`; `status` in `confirmed|suggested|rejected`; `confidence` `NULL` or between 0 and 1 by `CHECK`. This is the only relation mechanism between modules; the foreign key stays inside the core, so it breaks no module rule.
  - `core_subjects(id, name, slug UNIQUE, focus, created_at)` and `core_subject_aliases(alias_slug PRIMARY KEY, subject_id REFERENCES core_subjects ON DELETE CASCADE)`. Subjects are the stable vocabulary the library groups by; `focus` is a boolean. (The proposals table arrives with the subject-proposal work and is not created here.)
  - `core_jobs(id, kind, payload, dedupe_key, status, attempts, available_at, lease_until, lease_owner, last_error, created_at, started_at, finished_at)`, status in `queued|running|done|failed`, index on `(status, available_at)`, and a partial unique index on `dedupe_key` where `status IN ('queued','running')`. The worker that uses it is a separate bead; this bead only creates the table.
  - `core_files(hash PRIMARY KEY, media_type, size, created_at)` and `core_file_refs(hash REFERENCES core_files, owner_id REFERENCES core_items ON DELETE CASCADE, kind, PRIMARY KEY(hash, owner_id, kind))`. `kind` says what the blob is to its owner: `snapshot` (a page's raw HTML, written by the library), and in a later delivery `material_file` and `cover`; a later file-serving endpoint serves only the last two, never a `snapshot`.
  - `core_settings(key PRIMARY KEY, value, updated_at)` — preferences and cursors the server must know (`stats_hidden`, `telegram_update_id` later).
  - `core.RegisterItem`, `core.UpdateItem(id, title, type)` and `core.UnregisterItem` take a transaction so modules call them inside their own.
  - `core.Links.Confirm(tx, src, dst, kind)` inserts a `manual`/`confirmed` row, or flips an existing `suggested` or `rejected` row of that triple to `confirmed` with `source = manual` and `decided_at` set, and is a no-op on a `confirmed` one; `core.Links.Suggest(tx, src, dst, kind, confidence)` inserts an `llm`/`suggested` row, updates `confidence` on an existing `suggested` row, and leaves `confirmed` and `rejected` rows untouched. These are the only writers of `core_links` outside the decide endpoint, so the triple's state rules live in one place.
- **Files.** `core.Files` stores a blob under `NORTE_DATA/files/<sha256[0:2]>/<sha256>` and returns the hash; callers record the reference in `core_file_refs` inside the same transaction as their own row. Deduplicated by construction. The blob is written *before* the transaction that references it, so a crash between the two leaves an orphan blob, never a dangling reference. `norte files gc` removes blobs, and their `core_files` rows, that have no `core_file_refs` row and are older than one hour; it never looks into module tables. The hour protects a blob written by a save whose transaction has not committed yet.
- **Permissions.** `NORTE_DATA` and every directory under it are created `0700`, files `0600`: the database will hold everything the person reads and writes, on a machine that may be shared.

Rejected before this bead: a document store (the data is relational, and a graph is an edge table — `core_links` traversed with `WITH RECURSIVE` if ever needed); integer ids (would make cross-module references and a later graph impossible without a rewrite); a graph table beyond `core_links`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `norte migrate` with `NORTE_DATA` pointing at a non-existent directory creates it `0700`, creates `norte.db` `0600`, and applies the core migrations; a test asserts the mode bits and the presence of every table listed in Context via `sqlite_master`.
- [ ] Running `norte migrate` twice is a no-op the second time (goose reports nothing pending; exit 0).
- [ ] `norte version` and `norte config` do not create or open `norte.db`: a test runs both against an empty `NORTE_DATA` and asserts the file does not exist afterwards.
- [ ] Closing the database through the core's shutdown path leaves `norte.db-wal` absent or zero bytes.
- [ ] The writer handle has `MaxOpenConns == 1`; a test asserts, on a writer and on a reader connection, `journal_mode = wal`, `foreign_keys = 1`, `busy_timeout = 5000` and `synchronous = 1` (NORMAL).
- [ ] Starting `norte serve` against a fresh `NORTE_DATA` applies the core migrations before `/api/health` answers.
- [ ] Inserting an invalid `core_links.kind`, `source` or `status`, or an invalid `core_jobs.status`, fails on its `CHECK`.
- [ ] A stored blob's shard directory is `0700` and the blob `0600`; unregistering a `core_items` owner removes its `core_file_refs` rows by cascade.
- [ ] `core.NewID()` returns a 36-character lowercase UUID whose version nibble is 7; 1,000 ids generated in sequence sort lexically in generation order.
- [ ] `core.FormatTime`/`core.ParseTime` round-trip a time with millisecond precision to the exact string `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`, and two formatted times compare lexically in the same order as the times.
- [ ] Inserting a second `core_links` row with the same `(src_id, dst_id, kind)` fails on the unique index; inserting `confidence = 1.5` fails on the `CHECK`; deleting a `core_items` row removes every link whose `src_id` or `dst_id` is that id.
- [ ] The manual clock fires a 2-minute timer on `Advance(2m)` and not on `Advance(119s)`.
- [ ] `Confirm` on a `rejected` triple leaves one row, `confirmed`, `source = manual`, `decided_at` set; `Suggest` on a `confirmed` triple changes nothing.
- [ ] A blob stored twice through `core.Files` yields one file on disk and one `core_files` row.
- [ ] With a fake clock: an unreferenced blob older than one hour is removed by `norte files gc` (file and `core_files` row), an unreferenced blob 59 minutes old is kept, and a referenced blob older than one hour is kept.
- [ ] Done when: `norte migrate` on an empty `NORTE_DATA` creates the core tables with 0700/0600 permissions, the unique index and cascade on links are proved by a test, and a file round-trips through the store with gc removing only the old unreferenced blob.

## Tests
- Unit (`server/internal/core/*_test.go`): id format and ordering; time format round-trip and lexical order; `core_links` unique index, `CHECK` and cascade; file store dedupe; gc with a fake clock over the three cases above.
- Integration (Go test invoking the CLI entry point against a `t.TempDir()` `NORTE_DATA`): `migrate` twice, permissions, `version`/`config` not touching the database.
- All tests run under `go test ./...` from `server/` with a temporary `NORTE_DATA`; none reaches the network.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/core/` (new files: database open, migrations runner, ids, clock and time format, item registry helpers, file store, gc), `server/internal/core/migrations/` (the core SQL migration), `server/internal/core/queries/` and the generated `server/internal/core/db/`, `server/sqlc.yaml`, `server/cmd/norte/` (wiring `migrate` and the `files gc` subcommand), `server/go.mod`/`go.sum` (goose, modernc sqlite, uuid, sqlc tool dependency).
**Reads only:** the server skeleton's config loader and CLI root.

One new package plus the CLI wiring and a schema; no frontend file is touched. Size L because it is a schema change and more than five new files.

## Recovery path
The schema is new and holds no data before this bead, so nothing is migrated. If a migration is wrong after landing and before any real data exists, delete `NORTE_DATA/norte.db` and fix the migration in place. Once real data exists, a fix is a new goose migration, never an edit of an applied one.

title: Let the classifier propose new subjects, guarded against near-duplicates
description:
## What changes for the user
Once suggestions are in daily use, some saved links will belong to a subject that does not exist yet. After this lands, the classifier may propose a new subject — showing the closest existing one and why it is not the same — and the person chooses "criar" or "é o mesmo que X". Choosing "the same as X" teaches Norte that name for good: the next time it comes up it quietly becomes a suggestion for X instead of another proposal, so the vocabulary does not fill up with near-duplicates like "ML", "Machine learning" and "Aprendizado de máquina".

## Outcome
The classifier may return a new-subject proposal when no existing subject or alias scores above 0.70; the server normalises it and, when it equals or closely resembles an existing subject or alias, turns it into a plain link suggestion instead. Surviving proposals are stored in `core_subject_proposals` and shown in the review queue next to their closest subject with "criar" and "é o mesmo que X", the latter recording an alias.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. Subjects are the stable vocabulary saved items are grouped by: `core_subjects(id, name, slug UNIQUE, focus, created_at)`, created by the person from the UI or CLI, never by an LLM on its own. `core_subject_aliases(alias_slug PRIMARY KEY, subject_id REFERENCES core_subjects ON DELETE CASCADE)` maps alternative names to a subject. A `classify` background job already asks an LLM (OpenAI-compatible, through `core.LLM.Complete` with a JSON schema) to rank existing subjects and focus targets for a saved item, keeps at most three, and stores them as `suggested` rows in `core_links` for the person to accept or reject in a "Sugestões" tab of the Biblioteca. A stub LLM server exists for tests.

This is the second round of the first delivery: it is meant to land **after the classifier has been in daily use**, because whether proposals are needed, and how often near-duplicates appear, is learned from that use. The person asked for it with an explicit guard against near-duplicate names.

Decided:

- **When the classifier may propose.** The answer schema gains an optional `proposal {name, closest_subject_id, reason}`. A proposal is accepted from the model only when no existing subject or alias in its ranking scores **above 0.70** (a best score of exactly 0.70 still allows a proposal). The prompt receives the alias list, so a short form like "ML" can be matched to its subject by the model itself.
- **Normalisation** before any comparison: lowercase, accents stripped, punctuation removed, whitespace collapsed; the slug is the normalised name with spaces as hyphens.
- **`closest_subject_id` is checked too.** It is accepted only when it names a subject in the prompt's candidate set; an unknown id is stored as null, so a hallucinated id never reaches the foreign key and never fails or retries the job.
- **Server-side guard**, before anything reaches the queue: if the proposal's normalised slug equals an existing subject slug or alias slug, or its trigram similarity to an existing normalised slug is **0.6 or above**, it becomes a plain `suggested` link to that subject instead of a proposal; when several qualify, the order is exact subject slug, then exact alias slug (resolved to its canonical subject), then highest trigram similarity, ties by canonical slug then id. Trigram similarity is Jaccard over the 3-grams of the slug padded with two spaces each side, computed in Go.
- **Table** `core_subject_proposals(id, name, slug, closest_subject_id NULL REFERENCES core_subjects ON DELETE SET NULL, item_id REFERENCES core_items ON DELETE CASCADE, reason, status, created_at, decided_at)`, `status` in `pending|created|merged` by `CHECK` (there is no discard action in this version, so no `dropped`), a new core migration. `item_id` is the saved item the proposal came from, so accepting it can link that item; it is not in the original plan's table and was added so "criar" and "é o mesmo que X" have an item to link.
- **Queue.** The review queue shows each proposal next to its closest existing subject with two actions: "criar" (creates the subject, registers it, links the source item `confirmed`, marks the proposal `created`) and "é o mesmo que X" (records the proposal's slug as an alias of X, links the item to X `confirmed`, marks `merged`). Both actions also resolve every other `pending` proposal with the same normalised slug in the same transaction (linking each one's item to the resulting subject and marking it `created` or `merged` like the first), so a duplicate left in the queue can never fail later on the subject's unique slug. From then on, a proposal with that name resolves to X by the slug-equals-alias rule without reaching the queue.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Trigram similarity is unit-tested on fixture pairs with the expected values written in the test: `machine-learning` vs `machine-learnings` ≥ 0.6, `machine-learning` vs `aprendizado-de-maquina` < 0.6, and at least four more pairs.
- [ ] With "Machine learning" existing and `ml` as its alias, a stub answer proposing "ML" yields a `suggested` link to Machine learning and no proposal row.
- [ ] Proposing "Aprendizado de máquina" (no subject or alias above 0.70, similarity below 0.6) yields one `pending` proposal naming Machine learning as closest.
- [ ] Choosing "é o mesmo que Machine learning" records `aprendizado-de-maquina` as its alias and links the item; a second proposal of "Aprendizado de Máquina" then yields a link suggestion and no proposal.
- [ ] With two `pending` proposals of "Aprendizado de máquina" from two items, deciding one resolves both and links both items.
- [ ] A proposal with an unknown `closest_subject_id` is stored with null; "criar" stays available and "é o mesmo que…" opens a subject picker and stays disabled until a target is chosen; the `classify` job does not fail.
- [ ] With two qualifying subjects inserted in either order, the proposal resolves to the same one.
- [ ] Choosing "criar" creates the subject (with a `core_items` row) and a `confirmed` link from the item.
- [ ] A proposal returned while an existing subject scores 0.71 is ignored; one returned while the best existing score is exactly 0.70 is kept.
- [ ] Done when: with "Machine learning" existing and "ml" as its alias, proposing "ML" yields a link suggestion, not a proposal; proposing "Aprendizado de máquina" yields a proposal; rejecting it as the same makes a second proposal of that name resolve silently.

## Tests
- Unit (Go): normalisation and slug over a table (accents, punctuation, case, whitespace); trigram Jaccard over fixture pairs.
- Integration (Go, stub LLM + temp `NORTE_DATA`): every acceptance criterion through the `classify` job and the queue endpoints.
- Component (Vitest, fake provider): the proposal row with "criar" and "é o mesmo que X".

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/core/` (proposals migration, normalisation and trigram helpers, proposal decide endpoints), `server/internal/library/` (the `classify` handler's schema and guard), `api/openapi/core.yaml` and generated outputs, `web/src/modules/library/` (the proposal rows in the review queue).
**Reads only:** `core_subjects`, `core_subject_aliases`, the stub LLM.

Core, library and a frontend component plus a schema change; size L.

## Recovery path
The migration adds one table and no existing row changes. A wrong alias recorded by "é o mesmo que" is undone by deleting the alias row (`norte subjects` gains no command for it in this bead; a direct `DELETE` on `core_subject_aliases` is the documented fix).

title: Make every frontend store asynchronous and drop hard-coded dates
description:
## What changes for the user
Today every screen assumes its data is already there, and the app thinks today is 3 October 2026 forever because the date is written into the code. After this lands, every list and every item page shows a loading state while it waits, an empty state when there is nothing, a readable error when something fails, and a "not found" page for an item that does not exist; a failed change leaves the screen as it was and says so instead of pretending it worked. "Today", "yesterday" and due dates follow the real calendar in the server's time zone.

## Outcome
Each module's store is a set of injected composables (`useLibraryItems`, `useLibraryItem(id)`, and their equivalents in every module) exposing `data`, `loading`, `error` and `refresh`, with cancellation of superseded requests and the API's final list and detail shapes — still reading the mock data. Every list and detail view renders loading, empty, error and not-found states. `read` is removed from the library status. No production code derives "today" from a literal.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. `web/` is its Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript frontend. It has just been reorganised into one folder per module under `web/src/modules/<name>/` (library, notes, study, review, projects) plus `web/src/shell/`; each module's `index.ts` declares a `manifest` with `backing: 'api' | 'mock'`, and the app fetches `GET /api/config` (which returns `{modules, version, llm, telegram, timezone}`) before mounting. Every view still calls a synchronous mock store: `addSavedLink` returns the new item, `setLibraryItemStatus` mutates in place.

An HTTP store is not that shape: every call is asynchronous, can fail, and the view has to show loading, empty and error states. This bead is the second of three steps that replace the mock seam: views migrate to the async shape now, with no backend involved, so that the next step swaps only the data source and never the views again.

Decided:

- **Composables.** Per module, composables expose `data`, `loading`, `error`, `refresh`. Reads expose the API's final shapes from the start: `{items, next_cursor, counts}` for lists, the detail record for one item. A superseded request (a new search while the old is in flight, a route change) is cancelled with an `AbortController`. Mutations (`save`, `setStatus`, `addHighlight`, …) await the source and update local state **only from the response**; on error the view keeps its previous state and shows the error — no optimistic write. Providers are injected with `provide/inject`, so a view test mounts with a fake provider.
- **Library status model.** `LibraryStatus` (today `'inbox' | 'depois' | 'arquivo' | 'read'` in `mock/types.ts:3`, now under the library module) loses `read`. Read is an event, not a place: an item has `status` in `inbox|depois|arquivo`, plus `unread: boolean` and `read_at`. Marking read sets `unread = false` and `read_at = now`; marking unread sets `unread = true` and clears `read_at`. The four seed items with `status: 'read'` become `arquivo` with `unread: false` and a `read_at`. Code that uses `'read'` today: `LibraryView.vue:166-187`, `MaterialView.vue:141` and `:213`, `CurriculumView/curriculum.ts:81`, `store.ts:60`. Tests that assert or rely on it and must migrate to `unread`/`read_at`: `LibraryView.test.ts:158` (and its counts at line 67: Inbox 6, Depois 4, Arquivo 4, Tudo 18), `MaterialView.test.ts:120`, `CurriculumView.test.ts:60-63`, `CurriculumView/curriculum.test.ts:23-25`.
- **"Today" comes from the clock and the config's time zone.** Remove from production code: `TODAY` in `HomeView.vue:13`, `StudyHomeView.vue:23`, `ReviewView.vue:12`; `MOCK_TODAY` and `DEFAULT_DUE_DATE` in `DecisionView.vue:26-27`; `STUDY_TODAY` in `mock/study.ts:3` (and its seed `20261003` at line 94); `AGE_BY_DATE` in `NotesView.vue:34-45`; the hard-coded title "Sábado, 3 de outubro" in `HomeView.vue:194`; `savedAt: '2026-10-03'` in `MaterialView.vue:72`; the literals in `mock/store.ts` (lines 70, 77, 85, 195, 203), `mock/learning.ts:431`, `mock/life.ts` (40, 46, 47). (File paths are as before the module move; they now live under `web/src/modules/`.) A small date helper computes "today" in the `timezone` from `/api/config`. Mock record dates become relative to that clock (for example "saved 3 days ago" is `today - 3`), so the mock keeps looking alive. Fixtures in test files may keep literals; tests fix the clock with `vi.setSystemTime`. Tests that pin dates today: `mock/store.test.ts:15,96,104,128`, `mock/study.test.ts:18-25,67-68`, `StudyHomeView.test.ts:46`, `HomeView.test.ts:48-50`, `AppShell.test.ts:42`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every module exposes its reads through composables returning `data`, `loading`, `error`, `refresh`; no view imports a mock store directly: a test scans every production `.vue`/`.ts` file under `web/src/modules/**` and `web/src/shell/**` for direct imports of any mock store, and a planted violating import in a fixture proves the scan fails.
- [ ] Every list view and every detail view has a test rendering its loading, empty (lists) or not-found (details), and error states with a fake provider.
- [ ] A mutation test with a provider that rejects asserts the view's data is unchanged and the error is shown; with a provider that resolves, the view shows the response's value, not the request's.
- [ ] Starting a second search while the first is pending aborts the first (the fake provider observes the abort signal).
- [ ] `LibraryStatus` has exactly `inbox`, `depois`, `arquivo`; items carry `unread` and `read_at`; the library counts test asserts Inbox 6, Depois 4, Arquivo 8, Tudo 18, and that "only unread" over Tudo shows 18 minus the seed items with `unread: false` (14 if the four converted items are the only ones).
- [ ] A test rejects, in production files under `web/src` (excluding tests and fixtures), every legacy date symbol (`TODAY`, `MOCK_TODAY`, `STUDY_TODAY`, `DEFAULT_DUE_DATE`, `AGE_BY_DATE`), and in the mock-data modules and the views that used them any ISO (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or compact (`YYYYMMDD`) date literal used as a runtime "today", a due-date default, an age table or a record timestamp; format strings and parsers are allowed. Planting a fixed-date constant in each targeted area makes the test fail.
- [ ] With one instant fixed and two configured time zones on which that instant falls on different dates, the rendered "today" follows the configured zone, not the browser's.
- [ ] A route change aborts the composable's in-flight request (the fake provider observes the abort).
- [ ] With `vi.setSystemTime` set to two different days, the home's "today" title and the review's due list change accordingly.
- [ ] Done when: every view renders its loading, error and not-found states in a test, mutations update only from the response, no view or store derives "today" from a literal (mock record dates are relative to the config's clock), and every frontend test passes.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + `@vue/test-utils`, jsdom, fake injected providers): loading, empty, error and not-found per view; mutation success and failure; cancellation.
- Unit (Vitest): the date helper over a time zone where UTC and local dates differ (for example 23:30 in `America/Sao_Paulo` is the next day in UTC); the library status transitions.
- Regression: every existing test, migrated where it asserted `read` or a fixed date.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/modules/*/` stores, composables and views (every module), `web/src/shell/` (home), the mock slices' data files, the library types, a new date helper under `web/src/shell/` or `web/src/lib/`, and the tests listed in Context.
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/core.d.ts` (the config type), `web/src/components/ds/`.

Frontend only. Size L: more than two modules and well over six files of one kind (views).

Resumed once on claude/primary after the gmail account hit its five-hour limit. No criterion-by-criterion review before the merge: do one when convenient.

title: Make the shell and the reader usable on a phone
description:
## What changes for the user
The phone is where reading happens, and today Norte is not usable there: below 900 pixels the sidebar disappears with no way to open it, the reader's main actions are hidden, the library's row buttons only appear on mouse hover, and highlighting needs a mouse. After this lands, the whole first delivery works with a thumb on a phone: a menu button opens the navigation, the reader's actions sit in a bar at the bottom, notes open in a sheet from below, a passage can be highlighted from a touch selection, and every row action opens from a tap.

## Outcome
A mobile shell and reader: a navigation drawer below 900px, a bottom action bar in the reader (mark read, status, highlight, note, question), annotations in a bottom sheet, highlighting from a touch selection, tap menus for the Biblioteca row actions, no hover-only control anywhere. Two Playwright suites join the gate: the content-security-policy browser test and a 390x844 phone walk.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI, used from a desktop browser and a phone; the phone being a reader is a requirement, not a nice-to-have. `web/` is the Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript frontend, organised by module under `web/src/modules/<name>/` with the shell in `web/src/shell/`; the library and notes modules read the Go server's API. The server serves the built app from one binary under a content security policy: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' https: data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`.

What is broken on a phone today (paths as of before the module move): the sidebar is `display: none` below 900px (`AppSidebar.vue:609-613`) with nothing replacing it; the reader route renders without the sidebar (`layout: 'bare'`) and its top actions — the next link and "Marcar como concluído" — are hidden below 900px (`MaterialView.vue:448-461`), with more rules at 860px and 1180px hiding the margin column, the work title and the citation copy (`MaterialReader.vue:745-809`); text selection for highlights is read on `@mouseup` with `window.getSelection()` (`MaterialReader.vue:124`); the Biblioteca row actions are invisible until hover or focus (`.actions` with `opacity: 0; pointer-events: none`, revealed by `.item:hover`/`.item:focus-within` in `LibraryView.vue:430-434, 524-538`). The reader's highlight, margin-note, note-tab and "virar pergunta" actions exist on desktop (from the notes work); Playwright is not yet a dependency.

Decided:

- **Drawer**: below 900px the sidebar collapses into a drawer opened by a menu button in a top bar, closed by a tap outside, by Escape or by navigating.
- **Reader bottom bar** below 900px: mark read, status (inbox/depois/arquivo), highlight, note, question. Margin notes become the annotations tab of a bottom sheet.
- **Touch selection**: highlighting reads the selection on `selectionchange` (debounced) as well as `mouseup`, so a touch selection followed by the bar's highlight button works.
- **Tap menus**: the Biblioteca row actions (later, archive, read) open from a tap on a "more" button on touch-sized viewports; the desktop hover reveal stays, but every control is also reachable without hover.
- **No hover-only control** in the shell, Biblioteca, reader and Notas surfaces this bead touches: a control that is only reachable by hover is a defect of this bead.
- **Playwright** added to `web/` (Chromium), with two suites run by `bin/ci`:
  1. **The CSP test**: loads the app served by `norte serve` under its policy, renders an article whose image is served by a second local TLS server (self-signed, Playwright launched with `ignoreHTTPSErrors`), so the `https:` allowance is exercised without the network, and a dynamic progress style, asserts no CSP violation is reported, and asserts that an injected inline script is blocked.
  2. **The phone walk** at a 390x844 viewport against a real `norte serve` on a temp data directory seeded with one extracted fixture article.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At 390x844, the Playwright walk: opens the drawer and navigates from it to the Biblioteca; uses a row's tap menu to move an item to "depois"; opens an item in the reader; selects a sentence by touch and highlights it from the bottom bar; opens the annotations sheet; writes a question; marks the item read — and each step's effect is asserted through the API.
- [ ] The CSP suite passes: no violation on the article with an external image and a dynamic style, and the injected inline script does not execute (a `securitypolicyviolation` event is observed for it).
- [ ] In the 390x844 Playwright suite, every named action of the shell, Biblioteca, reader and Notas is reached by tap without any hover (jsdom cannot prove layout or hover, so this lives in Playwright).
- [ ] Touch selection is proved with a programmatic `Selection` plus a `selectionchange` event; native touch-handle selection on a real phone is a manual check of the first delivery's acceptance walk.
- [ ] Desktop layouts are unchanged above 900px: the existing component tests pass, and a 1440x900 Playwright run reaches the same actions as before.
- [ ] Both Playwright suites run inside `bin/ci`.
- [ ] Done when: the browser test of the content security policy (the app under its CSP, an article with an external image and a dynamic style, an injected inline script blocked) passes, and a Playwright run at a 390x844 viewport opens the drawer and navigates from it, uses a row's tap menu, reads an item, highlights a sentence from the bottom bar, opens the annotations sheet, writes a question, and marks the item read.

## Tests
- E2E (Playwright, Chromium, real `norte serve` + temp `NORTE_DATA` seeded with a fixture article): the phone walk; the CSP suite.
- Component (Vitest): drawer open/close; bottom bar actions; tap menu.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/shell/` (drawer, top bar), `web/src/modules/library/` (reader bottom bar, annotations sheet, touch selection, Biblioteca tap menu), `web/src/modules/notes/` (sheet content where the reader embeds notes UI), `web/package.json` and lockfile (Playwright), `web/e2e/` (new: the two suites and the seeding helper), `bin/ci` (runs them).
**Reads only:** the server (run, not edited), `web/src/components/ds/`.

Several frontend modules plus a new test harness and the gate; size L.

Fixed before merge: Destacar bar sticky in the reader column on desktop (bare routes lost their outer padding so the 100vh reader fits); each Playwright test seeds its own state and passes alone; the walk asserts computed opacity/pointer-events after dropping hover and focus (catches a hover-only reveal); phone cell frame removed; Playwright browsers cached in CI. title: Add the notes module: highlights, annotations and questions
description:
## What changes for the user
Reading leaves a trace. After this lands, the person can highlight a passage in the reader, write a note in the margin or a note for the whole text, and turn what they read into a question — a single one, or a set opened from a topic using the six "what, why, who, when, where, how" prompts. All of it is kept by the server, survives a reload, and survives the article's text being re-extracted later; a highlight whose passage no longer exists is listed as lost instead of disappearing. The Notas screen shows everything with the title of where it came from, and its filters keep working.

## Outcome
The `notes` module: migrations, API under `/api/notes/` for highlights anchored by text, annotations, the per-item note, questions and question sets; re-anchoring after a re-extraction through a core event and a job; `core.Text` so notes reads an item's text without reading the library's table. On the frontend: the Notas view on the API, the reader's highlight, margin-note and note-tab actions, "virar highlight" on a saved selection, "virar pergunta" at the end of reading, and the question-set screen.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. `server/` is the Go backend (one binary, SQLite, goose per module with a `goose_<module>` table, sqlc, an OpenAPI contract per module under `api/openapi/` generated into Go and TypeScript by `bin/generate`). Products are modules switched on by `NORTE_MODULES`; each owns tables prefixed with its name and **no foreign key crosses a module**. `notes` is its own module, written into by the library's reader now and by study later, owned by neither, so highlights survive either being disabled. `web/` is the Vue 3 frontend, organised by module under `web/src/modules/<name>/` with injected async composables; the library module already reads the API (Biblioteca, reader on an `ArticleContent` component, a read-only "trecho selecionado ao salvar" box).

What the core offers: the item registry `core_items(id, module, type, title, url)` (any module's item can be shown by title without its module), `core.RegisterItem`, `core_links` for cross-module relations, the jobs queue, and the in-process event bus `core.Events` (ids-only payloads, published after commit). The library publishes `library.item_extracted {item_id}` when an extraction succeeds, and stores `selection` `{exact, prefix, suffix}` on an item when the browser extension captured one at save time. The module interface has a `Text(ctx, id) (string, bool, error)` method each module may implement for items it owns.

Decided:

- **`core.Text(ctx, id)`**, built here in `server/internal/core/`: looks up `core_items.module` for the id and asks that module's `core.TextProvider` — the providers are injected into the core by the module registry at startup (the registry already defines `core.TextProvider`, and the core never imports the registry, which would be an import cycle); returns `ErrNoText` when the module is disabled or has no text yet. The library implements `Text` by returning `content_text` when `extract_status = done`. This is how notes reads text without reading `library_items`.
- **Tables** (migration in `goose_notes`), following Norte's schema conventions: `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` holding a UUIDv7 string, `created_at`/`updated_at` in the fixed UTC format, a `CHECK` on every enumerated column (`status`, `kind`), foreign keys only between `notes_*` tables:
  - `notes_highlights(id, item_id, section_ref NULL, location_label NULL, exact, prefix, suffix, position_hint, status, created_at)`, `status` in `anchored|orphaned`. `section_ref`/`location_label` are for PDF/EPUB pages in a later delivery (null for articles).
  - `notes_annotations(id, item_id, highlight_id NULL REFERENCES notes_highlights ON DELETE CASCADE, text, created_at, updated_at)` — margin notes, attached to a highlight or free.
  - `notes_notes(id, item_id UNIQUE, text, created_at, updated_at)` — the one freeform note per item (the reader's "Nota" tab).
  - `notes_questions(id, item_id NULL, annotation_id NULL REFERENCES notes_annotations ON DELETE SET NULL, set_id NULL REFERENCES notes_question_sets ON DELETE SET NULL, kind NULL, text, answer, status, created_at, updated_at)`, `kind` NULL or in `what|why|who|when|where|how` by `CHECK` (set only for questions written from a question set's prompts; a single question and a "virar pergunta" question have none), `status` in `open|answered|dropped`.
  - `notes_question_sets(id, topic, created_at)`, each registered in `core_items` as type `question_set` so it can be linked to a subject through `core_links`. A set is one evening's curiosity; a subject is stable vocabulary; they are not merged.
  - `item_id` is a global id with **no** foreign key (it points at another module's item). With the library disabled, a highlight still shows its own `exact` text and the item's title from `core_items`.
- **Anchoring by text, not offset**, because extracted text changes when extraction is redone and an offset would silently point at the wrong words. `exact` is the selected text with whitespace normalised; `prefix` and `suffix` are the 32 code points around it; `position_hint` is the character offset into `core.Text`'s result at creation, used only to choose between several matches. The server computes `position_hint`; the client sends `{item_id, exact, prefix, suffix}` (an offset from the browser's DOM has no relation to the extracted text's offsets).
- **Re-anchoring.** The notes module subscribes to `library.item_extracted` and enqueues a `notes.reanchor` job for the item (dedupe key `reanchor:<item_id>`), so the reaction is as durable as the queue. The job reads `core.Text` again and searches each highlight's `exact` together with its `prefix` and `suffix`, trying occurrences nearest to the hint first: exactly one occurrence whose context also matches keeps `anchored` (updating `position_hint`); none, or several indistinguishable ones, sets `orphaned` — the hint orders the search but never silently chooses between identical passages. At creation the same rule applies: `exact`, `prefix` and `suffix` are normalised with the same function used for `content_text`; a unique context match is anchored, and zero or several indistinguishable matches store the highlight as `orphaned` with the ambiguity reported to the reader, never silently attached to the first occurrence. When the owning module is off, highlights keep their stored text and are not re-anchored. Idempotent: re-running computes the same result.
- **Known gap, accepted on purpose.** The re-anchor reaction comes only from the `library.item_extracted` event, and the event bus keeps nothing for a subscriber that is not registered. So if an item is re-extracted while the notes module is disabled, its highlights are never re-anchored against the new text when notes is enabled again; they keep their stored `exact`/`prefix`/`suffix` and status. A startup pass that re-enqueues `notes.reanchor` for every item with highlights would close it and was declined: Norte runs with notes enabled, so the case needs a deliberate disable plus a re-extraction. Revisit if notes is ever routinely switched off.
- **API** under `/api/notes/` (contract `api/openapi/notes.yaml`): highlights (create, list by item, delete), annotations (create, update, delete, list by item), the per-item note (get, put), questions (create, update text/answer/status, list with filters), question sets (create with topic, list, get with its questions). List endpoints return the source item's title from `core_items` so Notas needs no library call. Every notes list is cursor-paginated like every list in Norte: `cursor` and `limit` (default 50), a documented total order with the id as tie-breaker, the filters hashed into the cursor (a cursor reused with other filters is refused with 400), and a `{items, next_cursor}` envelope, and Notas loads further pages with "carregar mais".
- **Frontend.** The notes module's manifest becomes `backing: 'api'` and its mock slice is deleted. The reader's highlight, margin-note, "Nota" tab, "virar highlight" and "virar pergunta" actions are notes UI rendered inside the library's reader through a slot the library exposes and the notes module fills from its `index.ts`, so with `notes` absent from `/api/config` none of them renders and the saved selection shows without "virar highlight". The Notas view (today three tabs `highlights`, `anotacoes`, `perguntas` synced to `?tab=`, a text filter over the note, question or highlight text and the source title from the registry (author filtering is dropped: notes cannot read the library's author and must keep working with the library disabled), and single-question creation that requires a trailing "?" and hard-codes a material id) keeps its tabs, filter and single-question creation, now on the API, with the source item chosen instead of hard-coded. The reader gets: highlight from a mouse selection, a margin note on a highlight, the "Nota" tab, orphaned highlights listed below the text, "virar highlight" on the saved selection (posting its `exact/prefix/suffix`), and a "virar pergunta" action at the end of reading that may point at an annotation. A question-set screen takes a topic, shows the six kinds as prompts, and stores only the questions the person actually writes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A highlight made in the reader is listed after a page reload.
- [ ] After `POST /api/library/items/{id}/extract` re-runs on unchanged text, the highlight stays `anchored`; after a re-extraction on a fixture whose text no longer contains the passage, it becomes `orphaned` and the reader lists it below the text.
- [ ] Selecting the second of two occurrences with identical context stores an `orphaned` highlight, not one anchored to the first; whitespace differences and non-BMP characters in the context still anchor.
- [ ] A passage whose exact text appears twice with different context re-anchors to the right occurrence; one whose two occurrences share identical context becomes `orphaned` after a re-extraction.
- [ ] Highlights, annotations and questions appear in Notas with their source item's title; with `NORTE_MODULES=notes` only (library off), Notas still lists them with titles from the registry.
- [ ] The Notas text filter and the tab-in-URL behaviour still work (their existing tests pass, migrated to a fake API).
- [ ] "virar highlight" on an item with a saved selection creates a highlight with that `exact` text.
- [ ] A question set created with topic "Kubernetes" where the person fills two of the six prompts stores exactly two questions with those kinds, and the set is a `core_items` row of type `question_set`.
- [ ] "virar pergunta" from an annotation stores a question whose `annotation_id` is that annotation.
- [ ] Each notes list (highlights, annotations, questions, question sets) pages 120 fixtures as 50/50/20 with no duplicates, and the UI can load every page.
- [ ] A single question from Notas stores `kind = NULL`; a question from a set's "why" prompt stores `kind = why`; `kind = 'other'` fails on the `CHECK`.
- [ ] With `/api/config` listing only `library`, the reader renders none of the five notes actions and the selection box has no "virar highlight".
- [ ] No notes table has a foreign key to a table outside `notes_*`, checked by a test over `PRAGMA foreign_key_list`.
- [ ] Done when: a highlight made in the reader survives a reload and a re-extraction, appears in Notas with its source title, an orphaned one is listed as such, the existing Notas filters still work, and a set yields only the questions the person wrote.

## Tests
- Unit (Go): anchoring search over a table of texts (unique, missing, duplicated, whitespace-different); `core.Text` with the owner disabled.
- Integration (Go, `httptest` + temp `NORTE_DATA`): the API; the event-to-job-to-reanchor path; the foreign-key test; notes-only mode.
- Component (Vitest, fake providers): Notas tabs and filter; reader highlight and margin-note actions; "virar highlight"; question-set screen.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `api/openapi/notes.yaml` (new) and its generated outputs, `server/internal/notes/` (new module: migrations, queries, service, handlers, re-anchor job, event subscription), `server/internal/core/text.go` (new), `server/internal/app/` and `server/cmd/norte/` (registering the notes module and injecting the text providers), `server/internal/library/` (its `Text` method only), `web/src/modules/notes/` (views, composables, question-set screen, mock slice deleted), `web/src/modules/library/` (reader actions only).
**Reads only:** `server/internal/core/` registry, events and jobs; `library_items` columns through the library's own `Text`.

More than two modules (notes server, core, library reader, notes frontend) and a schema; size L. Not split: the reader actions and the Notas view share the notes composables, and the server API is meaningless without one of them.

## Recovery path
New tables only. A wrong schema after real notes exist is fixed by a new migration in `goose_notes`, never by editing the applied one.

Fixed before merge: reader marks highlights by exact+prefix+suffix over whitespace-collapsed DOM text and across inline elements; suffix-only anchor test; 'trecho repetido' notice on ambiguous create; itemNotes follows next_cursor; a question citing another item's annotation is 400. Deferred to norte-cfp: touch selection (selectionchange) and a highlight bar near the selection.
