title: Scaffold the Vue 3 app with design tokens, fonts and themes
description:
## What changes for the user
Today there is no app to open, only static prototype files. After this lands, `npm run dev` opens an empty Norte page in the right fonts and colours, and the theme follows the saved preference.

## Outcome
A Vite + Vue 3 + TypeScript project in `web/`, with Vue Router, Vitest and @vue/test-utils, the design tokens and fonts loaded globally, and a theme helper that applies `data-theme`.

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Open `design/prototypes/Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html` in a browser to see the screen. Read `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html` for markup, inline styles and behaviour. The behaviour is a `class Component extends DCLogic` block with React-style `state`/`setState`. The template uses a design-tool runtime whose `sc-if`, `sc-for` and `{{ }}` bindings map almost one to one onto `v-if`, `v-for` and `{{ }}`. Prototype links point at `Norte - X.dc.html?param=`; translate them into the routes below.
- `design/system/` holds the committed design system. It has tokens in `tokens.css`/`tokens.json` (colour, type, a 4px spacing scale, radius, shadow), one `components/<Name>/README.md` per component, props in `components/index.d.ts`, and screenshots in `screenshots/`. Fonts are in `fonts/`: Schibsted Grotesk for display, Geist for sans and Commit Mono for mono.
- There are two themes, Claro and Escuro, switched by `data-theme` on the root element and stored in `localStorage` under `norte-theme`. The visual rule is quiet: one cobalt accent, no cards, no gradients, no warm colours.

Route table (shared by every screen):
- `/` is Início (Command Home).
- `/biblioteca` is the library, with query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`.
- `/notas` is notes, with query `tab` = `highlights|anotacoes|perguntas`.
- `/revisao` is the flashcard review.
- `/estudo` is the Estudo home (Currículos and Assuntos).
- `/curriculos/:slug` is one curriculum.
- `/material/:kind/:id` is one reading item, where kind is `post|livro|paper`.
- `/projetos` is the project list.
- `/areas/:id` is one area.
- `/projetos/:id` is one project.
- `/decisoes/:id` is one decision.
- `/tarefas/:id` is one task.

The repo is public. Never copy the prototype's mock content into code; use the neutral invented data in `web/src/mock/`. UI strings stay Portuguese.

The repo is a monorepo: the Vue app lives in `web/` and a Go backend will live in `server/` and later serve the built app from one binary. All frontend paths below are under `web/`; `design/` stays at the repo root. The gate is `npm run build && npm test`, run in `web/`.

Scaffold into `web/` with `npm create vue@latest` choices TypeScript, Router and Vitest, with no Pinia, no JSX and no e2e. Plain Vite was chosen over Vite+ for now: same engine, and Oxlint has no Vue template linting yet. Copy `design/system/tokens.css` and the woff2 files into `web/src/styles/` and `web/src/assets/fonts/`, with `@font-face` rules for the three families and the CSS variables `--font-display`, `--font-sans` and `--font-mono`. Remove the scaffold's demo components.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cd web && npm install && npm run build && npm test` exits 0 on a clean clone.
- [ ] `npm run dev` serves a page whose body background is the `ground` token and whose text uses Geist.
- [ ] `web/src/theme.ts` exports `getTheme()` and `setTheme('light'|'dark')`. These read and write `localStorage['norte-theme']` and set `document.documentElement.dataset.theme`; at boot the stored value is applied, defaulting to `light`.
- [ ] No scaffold demo component (HelloWorld, TheWelcome, icons) remains in `web/src/`.
- [ ] Done when: a fresh clone builds, tests and serves a blank page styled by the Norte tokens in both themes.

## Tests
- Unit: `web/src/theme.ts` round-trips both themes through localStorage and sets the dataset attribute, and defaults to light with empty storage.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/package.json`, `web/vite.config.ts`, `web/tsconfig*.json`, `web/index.html`, `web/src/main.ts`, `web/src/App.vue`, `web/src/theme.ts`, `web/src/styles/`, `web/src/assets/fonts/`, `web/src/router/index.ts`

New project files under `web/` only; nothing at the repo root changes.

title: Translate the design system's documentation and previews to English
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing on screen. The design system's documentation is what the next component is written from,
and it is Portuguese: `design/system/README.md` describes the system in Portuguese, each of the
twenty-four `design/system/components/<Name>/README.md` files documents its props and variants in
Portuguese with Portuguese examples, each `<Name>/preview.html` renders those examples,
`design/system/components/bundle.js` carries the sample copy they share, and every `usage` string
in `design/system/tokens.json` explains what a colour is for in Portuguese. After this change the
documentation reads the way the product does.

## Outcome
`design/system/` is English: the system README, every component README and preview, the shared
bundle and every `usage` note in `tokens.json` and `index.d.ts`.

## Context
This is documentation only. Nothing here is imported by `web/`, nothing here is executed by the
gate, and no test asserts a word of it — `web/src/components/ds/` is the implementation and it has
its own bead. That is why it is a bead of its own rather than part of either the component bead or
the convention bead: it is a large, flat, zero-risk diff, and putting it in front of the reviewer
who is checking that a mark still points at its margin note would bury the one change that can
break something.

It lands after the component bead (norte-2vx) so that a README documents the English labels the component
actually renders. A README that says a module shows `Concluído` while the component says `Done` is
worse than one that is wholly Portuguese, because it reads as current.

The file count is about fifty, which is over the reviewability guideline the other beads keep to.
That guideline exists to bound how much *risk* one review carries; this diff carries none — no
executable line, no contract, no stored value, no test. The honest bound here is the term check in
the acceptance criteria, which is mechanical and complete.

`tokens.json`'s `usage` strings are the one part worth care: they are the reason a colour exists,
not a description of it, and several carry a judgement ("Branco frio, nunca creme") that a literal
translation flattens. They are rewritten to keep the judgement, not the sentence.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `design/system/README.md` is English.
- [ ] Every `design/system/components/<Name>/README.md` is English, for all twenty-four components.
- [ ] Every `design/system/components/<Name>/preview.html` renders English sample content.
- [ ] `design/system/components/bundle.js` and `design/system/components/bundle.css` carry no
      Portuguese sample copy, and `design/system/components/index.d.ts`'s prop documentation is
      English.
- [ ] Every `usage` string in `design/system/tokens.json` is English and keeps the judgement the
      Portuguese one carried, rather than being dropped or flattened to a colour name.
- [ ] Each component README's examples match what that component now renders: a README that quotes
      a label quotes the English one the component shows.
- [ ] The **design-system documentation forbidden-term check** comes back empty:

          rg -n --no-heading \
            -e '[À-ÿ]' \
            -e '(?i)\b(pagina|titulos|texto|fundo|branco|creme|paineis|linhas|lista|verso|menus|pocos|trilho|progresso|celulas|vazias|divisores|separadores|decorativo|pista|controle|bordas|botao|secundario|acento|unico|acao|primaria|item|atual|exemplo|exemplos|variantes|usado|usada|quando|concluido|salvo|trecho|pergunta|cartao|nota|anotacao|assunto|curso|cursos|leitura|estudo|revisao)\b' \
            design/system --glob '!*.png' --glob '!*.woff2'

      Nothing under `design/system/` is deliberately Portuguese, so there is no allowlisted hit.
      The `--glob` exclusions are for binaries, whose bytes match a character class by accident.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- none owed: the change is documentation, nothing here is imported or executed, and the term check
  in the acceptance criteria is the verification. The pull request records its output.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `design/system/README.md`, every `design/system/components/<Name>/README.md`, every
`design/system/components/<Name>/preview.html`, `design/system/components/bundle.js`,
`design/system/components/bundle.css`, `design/system/components/index.d.ts`,
`design/system/tokens.json`

`design/system/`.

Documentation only; nothing executes, nothing is stored, nothing is imported. Reverting the commit
restores the previous text.

title: Wire the Biblioteca and the reader to the library API
description:
## What changes for the user
This is the first moment Norte shows real saved links. After it lands, the Biblioteca lists what was actually saved, with the real counts in the sidebar, page by page; opening an item shows the article's extracted text in the reader, an "extraindo" state while that is still happening, and the reason plus a retry button when it failed. Marking read, moving to later or archive, and the place where reading stopped are kept by the server, and the Início save dialog saves for real.

## Outcome
The library module's frontend reads and writes the API instead of the mock: the Biblioteca view with its filters and cursor pagination, sidebar counts from the counts endpoint, the Material view rendering extracted HTML through a new `ArticleContent` component with pending polling and failed-retry states, read/status/position mutations, the open call on entry, the saved selection shown read-only, and the Início save dialog posting to the API. The library's mock slice is deleted.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. `web/` is the Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript frontend; the Go server in `server/` serves it and the API from one binary, and `npm run dev` proxies `/api` to a running `norte serve`. Generated TypeScript types live in `web/src/api/<module>.d.ts`, and `web/src/api/client.ts` (openapi-fetch) is the one HTTP client.

Two earlier steps prepared this one. The frontend is organised into modules under `web/src/modules/<name>/`, each with a `manifest` declaring `backing: 'api' | 'mock'`; a module is mounted when it is `mock`, or `api` and listed by `GET /api/config`. Every store is a set of injected composables (`useLibraryItems`, `useLibraryItem(id)`) exposing `data`, `loading`, `error`, `refresh`, already returning the API's final shapes (`{items, next_cursor, counts}`, the detail record) from the mock, with mutations that update state only from the response. This bead is step three for the library: swap the composables' source to the API. The async data shape and the generic loading and error states should not need another migration; the view changes listed here (API wiring, pagination, reader states, the save dialog, `ArticleContent`) are this bead's own work, and only a further data-shape rewrite is reported as a defect of the previous step.

The library API this bead consumes: `GET /api/library/items` (`view=inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo`, `tipo`, `unread`, `sort`, `q`, `cursor`, `limit`; summaries only), `GET /api/library/counts` (`{views: {inbox, depois, arquivo, tudo}, kinds, unread}`), `GET /api/library/items/{id}` (full record including `content_html`, `extract_status` `pending|done|failed`, `extract_error`, `selection` `{exact, prefix, suffix}` or null, `read_position` `{v: 1, anchor, percent}`), `PATCH /api/library/items/{id}` (`status`, `unread`, `why`, `kind`, `title`, `read_position`), `POST /api/library/items/{id}/open`, `POST /api/library/items/{id}/extract`, `POST /api/library/items`. Library status is `inbox|depois|arquivo` plus a separate `unread` flag and `read_at`.

Decided:

- **Swap the source.** The library composables call the API through `client.ts`; the library manifest becomes `backing: 'api'`; the library's mock slice is deleted, not kept as a fallback (the other modules' mock slices are self-contained and do not depend on it).
- **Biblioteca** (`LibraryView`): the existing filters (view, tipo, unread, sort) map to query parameters, and pagination is "carregar mais" over `next_cursor`. Sidebar counts come from `/api/library/counts`, refreshed after a mutation.
- **`ArticleContent`**, a new component, inserts the server's already-sanitized `content_html` with `v-html` (correct here because the server sanitized it with an allowlist; the component adds no sanitizer of its own) and, after every change of `content_html` (pending to final, or a re-extraction), waits for Vue's DOM update, removes the listeners it installed for the previous value, and walks the current anchors and images once to add what plain insertion cannot; unmount performs the same cleanup with one stylesheet covering every element the allowlist admits: headings, paragraphs, lists, blockquote, pre/code, em/strong, links, images, figure/figcaption, tables, hr. External links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Images load lazily (`loading="lazy"`) and an image that fails to load is replaced by its `alt` text (an `error` listener added in that walk). Images are fetched from their source host by the browser; that is accepted and documented in a comment (a proxy only if privacy or availability makes it necessary). It replaces `MaterialReader`'s hand-written Vue nodes for articles.
- **Reader states.** While `extract_status = pending`, the reader shows "extraindo" and polls the detail with backoff (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, then every 10 s, stopping on leave). When `failed`, it shows `extract_error` and a retry button calling `POST …/extract`.
- **Reader route.** The API-backed reader is `/biblioteca/:id` (the item's UUID); the old `/material/:kind/:id` stays for mock-backed study materials. This is the path the server puts in Telegram replies and in search entries.
- **Reading actions.** Mark read/unread (`PATCH unread`), status changes, `read_position` saved on scroll (debounced, 2 s) as `{v: 1, anchor, percent}`, where `anchor` is the `anchor` of the `content_headings` entry nearest above the viewport (the element with that `id` in the rendered article) and `percent` the scroll fraction; on opening, after the final HTML is mounted, the reader restores a saved anchor that still exists, otherwise the saved percent clamped to [0, 1], and writes no position while restoring; `POST …/open` on entry. The selection captured at save time, when present, is shown read-only as "trecho selecionado ao salvar"; turning it into a highlight arrives with the notes work.
- **Início save dialog** (`HomeView`'s dialog, `saveLink`) posts `{url, why?}` to `POST /api/library/items` and shows the new item; today it calls a mock `addSavedLink` that always sets `kind: 'post'`, `status: 'inbox'` and a fixed date.
- **Cross-module actions** from a library item toward study or projects stay hidden while those are mock-backed (the gating rule: target mounted and same `backing`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With `norte serve` running and an item saved by `norte save <fixture>`, the Biblioteca shows it, the sidebar counts match `/api/library/counts`, and the reader shows its extracted text — with the library's mock slice deleted from the tree.
- [ ] A component test with a fake API returning `extract_status: pending` then `done` shows "extraindo" and then the article, and stops polling on unmount.
- [ ] With `extract_status: failed`, the reader shows `extract_error` and the retry button issues `POST /api/library/items/{id}/extract`.
- [ ] An `ArticleContent` fixture test renders each allowlisted element and asserts external links carry `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and images carry `loading="lazy"`; dispatching an `error` event on an image makes its `alt` text visible in its place.
- [ ] A component that changes from pending to final HTML decorates the final links and images; replacing the HTML again leaves one error listener per current image and none on removed nodes.
- [ ] Reopening an item scrolls to its saved heading anchor; after a re-extraction that removed that heading, it falls back to the saved percent; restoring issues no `PATCH`.
- [ ] Scrolling the reader issues at most one `PATCH read_position` per 2 s; opening an item issues one `POST …/open`.
- [ ] A saved selection is shown under "trecho selecionado ao salvar"; an item without one shows nothing there.
- [ ] Loading 120 items shows 50, then 100, then 120 via "carregar mais", with no duplicates.
- [ ] The Início save dialog creates an item through the API and it appears in the Biblioteca without a reload.
- [ ] `npm test` and `bin/ci` pass.
- [ ] Done when: a link saved by `norte save` is readable in the browser with no mock data involved, and a failed extraction shows its error and can be retried from the UI.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + `@vue/test-utils`, jsdom, a fake API provider): Biblioteca filters and pagination; reader pending/done/failed; retry; debounced position; open call; save dialog.
- Fixture (Vitest): `ArticleContent` over a fixture HTML containing every allowlisted element.
- Manual check recorded in the PR: one real saved article read in the browser against `norte serve`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/modules/library/` (composables' source, Biblioteca and Material views, new `ArticleContent` component, deletion of the mock slice), `web/src/shell/` (Início save dialog, sidebar counts).
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/client.ts`, `web/src/api/library.d.ts`, `bin/ci` (run as the gate, not edited), the server (run, not edited).

Frontend only, the library module and the shell. Size L: the source swap, the views, the new component, their tests and the mock-slice deletion exceed five edited files.
close_reason: Merged into local main 188cd06 (GitHub unreachable). Gate 12/12 green. Review: 18 mutations; every tested criterion MET; folded in three norte-c7z defects (API shape, server counts, stale detail on id change) and three smaller c7z gaps (date scan over modules/**, boot->clock tz assertion). Fixed before merge: apiSource.ts tests over a stubbed fetch, reader offsets relative to the scroll container, restore guard cleared after two animation frames, rows leaving the shelf after a write, kind links v=tudo, open/navigation race, failed loadMore keeps the rows. Open, non-blocking: the 'Artigos' shortcut count spans every shelf while its link opens inbox (pinned by AppShell.test as the prototype); search has no debounce; a pending position is dropped when leaving the reader; minutesFor shows 8 min when unknown. Manual check against a real norte serve deferred to norte-915.

title: Fix the reader's highlight feedback and reading-position restore
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, in the reader, a highlight the server could not place shows no mark and no message; "Virar highlight" shows nothing until a page reload and then offers itself again, creating duplicates; passages that were never found are explained as "o texto foi extraído de novo" even when nothing was re-extracted; reopening an article jumps back to the last section heading instead of where the person stopped; and leaving the reader right after scrolling forgets the new position. Once this lands, the reader says when a passage could not be placed, marks a new highlight immediately, explains the orphan list truthfully, and reopens the article where reading stopped.

## Outcome
The reader refreshes its highlights after any highlight is created, shows a notice when a created highlight is `orphaned`, uses accurate wording for the orphan list, restores the position from `percent` (using the heading anchor only to correct small offsets), and flushes a pending position when it unmounts.

## Context
The reader is `web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderView.vue`; the notes panel and actions are `web/src/modules/notes/components/ReaderNotesPanel.vue`, `ReaderHighlightAction.vue` and `web/src/modules/notes/components/ReaderSelectionAction.vue`; highlights are loaded by `useItemNotes` in `web/src/modules/notes/data/composables.ts`. Defects, verified in code:
1. `ReaderHighlightAction.vue` (around lines 62 and 106) shows a notice only when the create response has `ambiguous: true`; an `orphaned` answer without `ambiguous` shows nothing.
2. `ReaderSelectionAction.vue` tracks "stored" in a local ref (around line 24); `notesGainedNote()` bumps a revision counter, but `useItemNotes` (`composables.ts` around line 190) watches only the item id, so the highlight layer never refreshes.
3. `ReaderNotesPanel.vue` (around lines 59 and 250-252) always says "O texto foi extraído de novo e estes trechos não foram encontrados". The server does not store `ambiguous` (only the create response carries it), so after a reload the reader cannot tell the reasons apart; the honest wording covers both, e.g. "Trechos que não foram encontrados neste texto".
4. `restorePosition` (`ReaderView.vue` around lines 262-270) scrolls to `read_position.anchor` whenever that heading exists and uses `percent` only without an anchor. The anchor is "the last heading above the viewport", so a long section restores far above the stopping point (measured: 30% and 45% restored at 0.7%; 90% at 50%).
5. `onBeforeUnmount(clearPositionTimer)` (`ReaderView.vue` around line 303) drops a debounced position write instead of flushing it.
The server-side anchoring of contexts that cross block boundaries is fixed in a separate bead; this one is about what the reader shows.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. Save an article with several paragraphs and two headings; open it at `$B/biblioteca/<id>`.
3. Create a highlight through the API with a passage that does not exist (`"exact":"xyz inexistente"`), then select a real passage in the reader and press Destacar while the server answers `orphaned` (e.g. a passage repeated twice with identical context): no mark and, in the non-ambiguous case, no message.
4. Save the item through the API with a `selection`, open it, press "Virar highlight": no mark until reload; after reload the button is back.
5. Scroll to 45% of a long section, wait 3 seconds, reload: the view starts at the section heading. Scroll again and navigate away within 300 ms: the stored `read_position.percent` is the previous value.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A Destacar whose response is `orphaned` shows a visible notice within the reader, with distinct wording for `ambiguous: true` (passage repeats) and otherwise (passage not found).
- [ ] After Destacar or "Virar highlight", the new mark appears without a reload, and "Virar highlight" is not offered again for a selection already stored.
- [ ] The orphan list's explanation no longer claims a re-extraction.
- [ ] After reloading, the scroll position is within 2% of the stored `percent` for positions saved at 30%, 45% and 90% of a two-section article.
- [ ] Leaving the reader within 300 ms of a scroll writes the latest position (one PATCH carrying it).
- [ ] Done when: steps 3 to 5 behave as the criteria say in a real browser against a real server.

## Tests
- unit: `web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderView.test.ts` gains cases for restore-by-percent and flush-on-unmount.
- unit: `web/src/modules/notes/components/readerActions.test.ts` gains cases for the orphaned notice and for the highlight layer refreshing after creation.
- e2e: a Playwright case in `web/e2e/` that scrolls a real article to a fraction, reloads, and asserts the restored fraction.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderView.vue`, `web/src/modules/notes/components/ReaderSelectionAction.vue`, `web/src/modules/notes/components/ReaderHighlightAction.vue`, `web/src/modules/notes/components/ReaderNotesPanel.vue`, `web/src/modules/notes/data/composables.ts`, their tests, one new spec under `web/e2e/`
Two web modules (library and notes), which is why this is `size:L`. The server and the API are not changed.
close_reason: Merged into local main; full gate 20/20 green at db627bc.

title: Show, filter by, edit and manage tags in the Library
description:
## What changes for the user
Once the server tags every item, the person needs to see the tags, filter by one, fix a wrong
one, and tidy the vocabulary. After this change each library row shows its first tags, the
filter menu lets the person pick a tag, the reader lets them add and remove tags on the item
they are reading, and a tag list lets them rename or merge tags.

## Outcome
The web client shows, filters by, edits and manages tags through the endpoints the server bead
adds.

## Context
The server side (tag storage, automatic tagging, the `tag` list filter, add/remove/rename/merge
endpoints, `tags` on item summaries) is the bead this one depends on; its contract in
`api/openapi/library.yaml` is the source of truth for names and shapes.

The library header's filter menu is built on `web/src/components/ds/Menu.vue` and lives in
`web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue`; the kind filter there writes the `kind` query
parameter (renamed from `tipo` by norte-bc7) so a filtered view survives a reload, and the tag
filter follows the same rule with a `tag` parameter. The reader is `web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderView.vue`. The design
system has `Tag.vue` for chips.

Tags are for finding, so they appear small and secondary on a row, never louder than the title.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A library row shows up to 3 of its tags as chips after the meta line, then "+N" when it has
      more; a row with no tags shows none.
- [ ] Clicking a chip filters the list to that tag (sets the `tag` query parameter).
- [ ] The filter menu has a "Tag" section with a text box that narrows the tag list from
      `GET /api/library/tags`, showing each tag's count; choosing one sets `tag`, and the filter
      icon shows its active colour while a tag is set.
- [ ] The reader shows the item's tags with a remove control on each and an input to add one;
      both call the item tag endpoints and update the chips without a reload.
- [ ] A "Manage tags" entry at the bottom of the filter menu opens a list of every tag with its
      count, where a tag can be renamed; renaming onto an existing name asks for confirmation
      that the two will merge, then calls the rename endpoint.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- unit: `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.test.ts` for chips, "+N", chip click, the tag
  section of the filter menu and the `tag` query parameter.
- unit: `web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderView.test.ts` for add and remove.
- unit: the manage-tags list for rename and the merge confirmation.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue`, `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.test.ts`, `web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderView.vue`, `web/src/modules/library/views/ReaderView.test.ts`, `web/src/modules/library/components/ManageTags.vue`, `web/src/modules/library/components/ManageTags.test.ts`, `web/src/modules/library/data/source.ts`
**Reads only:** `bin/ci`, `api/openapi/library.yaml`, `web/src/components/ds/Menu.vue`, `web/src/components/ds/Tag.vue`

Web only.

title: Correct the library and home counts, labels and the read-now row actions
description:
## What changes for the user
Today several small things in the library and the home page say something untrue: the sidebar's "Artigos" count includes archived items while the link opens only the inbox; in "O que ler agora", pressing Depois or Arquivo removes the item from a list that is supposed to show every unread item; the save dialog says "Salvo na inbox" for a link that is still in Arquivo; rows with no author repeat the site name; "Continuar lendo" shows the whole reading time as time remaining, and an article whose length is unknown shows an invented "8 min". Once this lands, every count, label and duration on those screens matches what is stored.

## Outcome
The listed library and home labels and behaviours match the data they describe.

## Context
Defects, verified in code:
1. `web/src/modules/library/index.ts` (around lines 71-74): the "Artigos" sidebar entry links without a view (so the library opens on the inbox) but counts with `kindCount('post')`, which covers every view. Link to `v=tudo&tipo=post`, or count the inbox only; linking to `tudo` is chosen because the label is a kind, not a shelf.
2. `web/src/modules/library/data/composables.ts` (around line 22, `matchesFilters`) compares `item.status !== 'now'`; `now` is a view, not a status, so the comparison is always true and any patch drops the row from the focus-ranked list. In `view=now`, a row stays while it is unread.
3. `web/src/modules/library/home/LibrarySaveAction.vue` (around line 125) prints a fixed "Salvo na inbox" whatever the response; a 200 (existing item) should say "Já estava salvo" plus the item's current shelf.
4. `web/src/modules/library/home/items.ts` (`sourceOf` falls back to `siteOf`, around line 26) makes the row print the site twice when there is no author; print the site once.
5. `minutesFor` returns `item.minutes ?? 8` (`home/items.ts` around lines 40-42), and `LibraryReadingBlock.vue` (around line 26) uses it as the remaining time. Remaining minutes are `ceil(minutes * (1 - read_position.percent))`; with no `minutes`, show no duration.
6. `QuestionSetsView.vue` and `QuestionSetView.vue` print "1 perguntas"; use the singular for one. (Notes screen, but the same one-line class of fix.)

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. Save three items, archive one: the sidebar shows "Artigos 3", the link opens a list of 2.
3. In Biblioteca, choose "O que ler agora" and press Depois on a row: it disappears.
4. Archive an item, then save its URL again from "Salvar link": the dialog says "Salvo na inbox".
5. On Início, an item read to 50% with `minutes: 20` shows "20 min restantes".

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The "Artigos" count equals the number of rows its link shows.
- [ ] In `view=now`, Depois and Arquivo keep the row (with its new status chip) while it is unread; "Marcar lido" removes it.
- [ ] A duplicate save shows a message naming the existing item's current shelf.
- [ ] A row with no author shows the site once.
- [ ] "Continuar lendo" shows `ceil(minutes × (1 − percent))` remaining, and nothing when `minutes` is null.
- [ ] A set with one question reads "1 pergunta".
- [ ] Done when: steps 2 to 5 show the corrected values.

## Tests
- unit: cases in `web/src/modules/library/index.test.ts`, `web/src/modules/library/data/composables.test.ts`, `web/src/shell/HomeView.test.ts` and `web/src/modules/notes/views/QuestionSets.test.ts` for each criterion.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/modules/library/index.ts`, `web/src/modules/library/data/composables.ts`, `web/src/modules/library/home/LibrarySaveAction.vue`, `web/src/modules/library/home/items.ts`, `web/src/modules/library/home/LibraryReadingBlock.vue`, `web/src/modules/notes/views/QuestionSetsView.vue`, `web/src/modules/notes/views/QuestionSetView.vue`, and the tests named above
Many small files of one kind (labels), which is why this is `size:M` rather than larger; no logic beyond the six items changes.

title: State the classifier's answer shape in its system prompt
description:
## What changes for the user
The person configures Norte with a model provider and saves an article. Today, if the provider
does not enforce the JSON schema Norte sends, the model answers in prose, the suggestion job
fails after its retries and nothing ever appears in the suggestions queue, with no hint why.
After this change the same provider returns usable suggestions.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run Norte with `NORTE_LLM_URL` pointing at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that ignores
   `response_format` (Ollama Cloud, directly or through a litellm proxy), model `glm-5.3`.
2. Create a subject and save an article whose text matches it.
3. Observe the classify job: the model answers in prose, the answer fails to parse, the job
   retries and ends failed; the suggestions queue stays empty.

## Context
The library classifier asks the model for at most three subject suggestions per saved reading.
It sends the expected answer shape only as `response_format: {type: json_schema, strict: true}`
(`server/internal/core/llm.go`); the system prompt (`libraryClassifySystemPrompt` in
`server/internal/library/classify.go`) never describes that shape. Providers that do not enforce
structured output therefore never learn what to answer.

Measured on 2026-10-09 with the real prompt: GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-flash, Kimi K3 and MiniMax M3 on
Ollama Cloud, through a litellm proxy and directly, all answered in prose ("**Proposta:**
subj_stats ..."). Ollama Cloud ignores both the OpenAI-compatible `response_format` and the native
`format` field. Adding one paragraph to the system prompt that gives the exact JSON shape made
GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-flash answer valid JSON in 6 of 6 calls. The schema stays in the request,
because providers that do enforce it should keep doing so.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `libraryClassifySystemPrompt` ends with a paragraph stating that the answer is one JSON
      object and nothing else, shaped `{"suggestions": [{"id": "<candidate id>", "confidence":
      <number from 0 to 1>}]}`, with `{"suggestions": []}` as the empty answer.
- [ ] The request still carries `response_format` with `type: json_schema` and `strict: true`.
- [ ] A unit test asserts the system prompt sent to the test LLM server contains the literal
      `{"suggestions": []}`, and fails when the paragraph is removed.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green and a classify job against GLM-5.3 through litellm produces a
      pending suggestion in the queue.

## Tests
- unit: `server/internal/library/classify_test.go` gains the prompt-content assertion above.
- e2e (manual, by the review): one save against GLM-5.3 through the local litellm proxy produces a
  suggestion.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/library/classify.go`, `server/internal/library/classify_test.go`

Confined to the classifier's system prompt and its test. The LLM client, the schema and the
normaliser are untouched.
close_reason: Fixed in e3e579e (merged locally): the system prompt now spells out the JSON answer shape; unit assertion proven by mutation; bin/ci 21/21 green. Live check against GLM-5.3 follows at deploy.

title: Match the Início screen to its prototype
description:
## What changes for the user
On the Início screen today there is no search field in the top bar, the curricula under "Continuar estudando" show a dash where a "Continuar" button should be and no percentage, the reading cards under "Continuar lendo" give no sense of how far each item has been read or where it comes from, and the saved items show raw dates like `2026-10-01`. After this lands the screen looks and reads like the prototype: search sits next to "Salvar link", each curriculum shows its progress and a "Continuar" button, each reading card shows its progress bar and source site, and saved items say "hoje", "ontem" or "29 set".

## Outcome
The `/` route matches the prototype "Norte - Command Home (standalone).html" at 1440px in both themes, region by region, apart from the invented mock text: top-bar search field, curriculum rows with percent and "Continuar" button, reading cards with progress bar and domain line, saved rows with relative dates and full meta line.

## Context
Norte is a Vue 3 frontend (under `web/`) ported from a design-tool prototype; every screen runs on mock data in `web/src/mock/`. The Início screen (`web/src/views/HomeView.vue`) was built from a bead whose acceptance included a 1440px side-by-side check that was never run, because no headless browser was reachable for that worker. A visual comparison run afterwards with headless Chromium at 1440x900, both themes, found these differences against the prototype (text content differs on purpose and is not a defect):

1. Top bar: the prototype has a search input with placeholder "Buscar artigos, notas, cursos…" to the left of "Salvar link"; the app has none.
2. "Continuar estudando" rows: the prototype shows, per row, the title; a subtitle line "<module> · <lesson>" followed by a mono `item x/y`; on the right a progress bar with the percent in mono underneath (e.g. `38%`), and an outlined "Continuar" button that routes to the curriculum. title: Extract the snapshot a duplicate save sends instead of re-downloading the page
description:
## What changes for the user Today, saving a page that is already in the library again from the browser extension throws away what the browser captured: the server downloads the URL itself instead. For a page behind a login or a paywall the item then ends as "falhou", and for a public page the captured version is silently replaced by whatever the server sees. Once this lands, a re-save from the extension shows exactly what the browser had on screen. ## Outcome A duplicate save that carries HTML replaces the stored snapshot and extracts that snapshot, never a fresh download. ## Context A save whose canonical URL already exists answers 200 and applies the new note, selection, links and snapshot to the existing item (`api/openapi/library.yaml`, `saveLibraryItem`). In `server/internal/library/service.go`, `replaceLibrarySnapshot` stores the new snapshot and then calls `s.enqueueLibraryExtract(ctx, tx, existing.ID, generation, true)` (around line 410). The last argument is the job's `refresh` flag, which the contract documents as "download the page again instead of re-reading the stored snapshot" (an explicit retry option on `POST /api/library/items/{id}/extract`), and the extraction worker reads the stored snapshot only when `!payload.Refresh` (`server/internal/library/extract.go`, around line 211). The existing test of this path (`server/internal/library/extracthandler_test.go`, around line 525) runs the worker by hand with `refresh=false`, so it never executes the payload the save actually enqueued; that is why the gate stayed green. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`. 2. `POST $B/api/library/items` with `{"url":"https://example.com/resave","html":"Primeira

Primeira versão ... (30 sentences)

"}`; wait for `extract_status: done`. 3. `POST` the same URL again with `"source":"extension"` and HTML titled `Segunda` with different text; it answers 200. 4. Observed: the log shows `stored a fetched snapshot`, the item's text is example.com's live page, and `meta.snapshot_source` is `server_fetch`. With an unresolvable host (`https://fixtures.invalid/x`) the item ends `extract_status: failed` after three attempts, still carrying the first title. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] After step 3, the job enqueued by the save carries `refresh: false` in its payload. - [ ] After step 3 and the worker's run, the item's title is `Segunda`, its text is the second snapshot's, its `extract_generation` is 2, and no network fetch was made (the log has no `stored a fetched snapshot` line for that generation). - [ ] A duplicate save **without** HTML behaves as today. - [ ] `POST /api/library/items/{id}/extract` with `{"refresh":true}` still downloads the page. - [ ] Done when: re-saving an item from the extension with a host the server cannot resolve ends `extract_status: done` with the extension's text. ## Tests - integration: a test in `server/internal/library/extracthandler_test.go` that performs the duplicate save through the service, then runs the worker on the job **as enqueued** (read back from the jobs table, not constructed by hand), against an unresolvable host, and asserts `done` with the second snapshot's text. Break it on purpose by restoring `true` and confirm it goes red. ## Blast radius **Edits:** `server/internal/library/service.go`, `server/internal/library/extracthandler_test.go` **Reads only:** `server/internal/library/extract.go` The contract and the worker are not changed.

title: Separate adjacent blocks in the extracted text when the HTML has no whitespace between them
description:
## What changes for the user Today, when a saved page's HTML has no line break between its paragraphs and headings (common on minified pages and on what the browser extension captures), the extracted text runs the blocks together: the last word of one paragraph is glued to the first word of the next ("parar.Segundo", "TítuloPrimeiro"). Search then misses words at those joins, the reading-time estimate counts glued words as one, and a highlight that spans the join can never be found. Once this lands, every paragraph, heading and list item is separated in the extracted text whatever the markup looked like. ## Outcome The extracted `content_text` separates adjacent block-level elements with a newline even when the source HTML has no whitespace between them. ## Context Extraction turns a saved page into `content_html` (sanitised article HTML) and `content_text` (plain text used for search, reading minutes and highlight anchoring), in `server/internal/library/extract.go` and `server/internal/library/extractor.go`. For a snapshot like `

Título

Primeiro parágrafo ... parar.

Segundo parágrafo ...

` with no whitespace between tags, the stored `content_text` reads "TítuloPrimeiro parágrafo ... parar.Segundo parágrafo". Pages that do carry newlines between blocks are extracted correctly, which is why most real articles look fine. Highlights are anchored by searching their selected text in `content_text` (`server/internal/notes/anchor.go`), so a selection spanning such a join ("parar. Segundo") is reported as not found. Where the text is produced from the HTML tree, a block-level element (p, h1-h6, li, blockquote, pre, div, section, article, tr, br) must contribute a newline boundary. Re-extraction of existing items picks the fix up through the normal `POST /api/library/items/{id}/extract`; nothing is migrated. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Build and start a server: `bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`, then `NORTE_DATA= NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`. 2. `POST http://127.0.0.1:18080/api/library/items` with `{"url":"https://example.com/glued","html":"

Título

Primeiro parágrafo fala do mar inteiro sem parar.

Segundo parágrafo descreve montanhas geladas onde lobos cinzentos caçam renas.

"}` (repeat each paragraph's sentence enough times for extraction to accept the page). 3. When `extract_status` is `done`, `GET /api/library/items/` shows `content_text` containing `parar.Segundo` and `TítuloPrimeiro`. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] After step 3, `content_text` contains `parar.\n\nSegundo` (or `parar.` and `Segundo` separated by at least one newline) and `Título` and `Primeiro` separated by a newline. - [ ] A page whose HTML already has newlines between blocks produces the same `content_text` as today (an existing extraction test fixture is unchanged). - [ ] `POST /api/notes/highlights` with `exact` "parar. Segundo" on that item answers `anchored`. - [ ] Done when: the reproduction shows separated blocks and the spanning highlight anchors. ## Tests - unit: a case in `server/internal/library/extract_test.go` extracting the glued fixture above and asserting the separators, plus the unchanged case for a fixture with newlines. - integration: a case in `server/internal/notes/api_test.go` (or the existing extraction-plus-notes test) anchoring a highlight that spans the join. ## Blast radius **Edits:** `server/internal/library/extractor.go`, `server/internal/library/extract_test.go`, `server/internal/notes/api_test.go` **Reads only:** `server/internal/library/extract.go`, `server/internal/notes/anchor.go`

title: Stop the Biblioteca search from sending a sort with the text query
description:
## What changes for the user Today, typing anything into "Buscar na biblioteca" empties the list and shows "Não foi possível carregar a biblioteca: sort and q cannot be combined". Search inside the library does not work at all. Once this lands, typing a word lists the saved items that contain it, ranked by relevance. ## Outcome The library screen never sends `sort` together with `q`, so every search request is accepted by the server and the list shows the ranked matches. ## Context The list endpoint `GET /api/library/items` refuses an explicit `sort` combined with a text query `q`, because a text query orders by full-text rank (`api/openapi/library.yaml`, the `listLibraryItems` description; enforced in `server/internal/library/list.go`). The screen's query builder in `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue` (the `query` computed, around line 166-180) always includes `sort: sort.value`, whose default is `'saved_desc'`, and `web/src/modules/library/data/apiSource.ts:78` serialises it whenever it is set. The unit test of the API source checks the serialised query string, never what the server accepts, which is why the gate stayed green. The same request without `sort` returns the right items. While a query is active the sort control has nothing to do, so it should be hidden the same way it already is for the focus-ranked view. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`. 2. Save two items, e.g. `curl -s -XPOST $B/api/library/items -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"url":"https://example.com/a","html":"Aprendizado

aprendizado espaçado ...(repeat the sentence 30 times)

"}'`. 3. Open `$B/biblioteca` and type `aprendizado` in the search box. 4. Observed: the request is `GET /api/library/items?view=inbox&sort=saved_desc&q=aprendizado`, it answers 400, and the error message replaces the list. `curl "$B/api/library/items?q=aprendizado&sort=saved_desc"` answers 400 with `field: sort`. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] With a non-blank search text, the query object built by `LibraryView.vue` carries no `sort` key, and the URL sent to `/api/library/items` has no `sort` parameter. - [ ] With a blank search text, the chosen sort (`saved_desc` or `title`) is still sent exactly as today. - [ ] While a non-blank search text is active, the sort toggle button is not rendered. - [ ] Done when: typing a word that occurs in a saved item, against a running `norte serve`, lists that item and shows no error. ## Tests - unit: `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.test.ts` gains a case that types a query and asserts the request URL has `q` and no `sort`, and one that clears it and asserts `sort` is back. - e2e: a Playwright case in `web/e2e/` that saves an item through the API of a real `norte serve`, types a word into the search box, and asserts the row appears and no error text is shown. This is the test that closes the gap the unit test left: it goes through the real server's validation. ## Blast radius **Edits:** `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue`, `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.test.ts`, one new spec under `web/e2e/` Confined to the library screen's query builder and its tests. The API contract and the server are not touched.

title: Plan file uploads to the Library: PDF, EPUB and images
description:
## What changes for the user
Everything in the Library today comes from a URL. The person also keeps PDFs (papers, books),
EPUBs (books) and images, and has nowhere in Norte to put them. After this work a file can be
uploaded from the Library's add menu, next to "URL", and each format behaves as its kind
should: EPUBs and text-friendly PDFs read in the reader, images kept and shown.

## Context
Parked on 2026-10-10: the formats are decided (PDF, EPUB, images) and nothing else is. No
discovery has been done and none is wanted until this is picked up.

What exists to build on, as of that date: the Library's add menu has one entry, "URL", built so
further entries are one line each; there is no upload endpoint in `api/openapi/library.yaml`; the
core schema already allows file references of kind `material_file` and `cover`
(`server/internal/core/migrations/00001_core_schema.sql`) with no endpoint writing them; and
`norte files gc` removes stored blobs nothing references.

The open questions, each costed differently: a PDF can be shown as-is in an embedded viewer
(highlighting is hard there) or have its text extracted into the existing reader (papers with
columns and formulas come out broken); an EPUB is HTML inside and maps to the existing reader
chapter by chapter; an image has no reading at all and belongs with kept items.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Before any code: a planning pass records, as a comment here, which PDF approach is taken
      and why, how a file is stored and served, and the size limit per upload.
- [ ] Implementation beads exist for the chosen approach, one per format at most, wired with

- [ ] Done when: the planning comment exists and the implementation beads are filed.

- none owed by this bead; each implementation bead names its own.

Other read-later apps show a small picture per link. After this change each row shows the page's preview image when it has one, the first image of the article when it does not, and the icon only when there is no image at all. ## Outcome Extraction records a lead image for pages that declare none in their metadata by falling back to the first usable image in the extracted article, and the library list row renders the lead image as its thumbnail with the icon as fallback. ## Context Extraction already stores a lead image per item: column `lead_image` in `server/internal/library/migrations/00002_library_items.sql`, returned as `lead_image` by both the list summary and the item detail (`api/openapi/library.yaml`). It is chosen in `server/internal/library/metadata.go` (around lines 174-180): the first declared meta tag among `og:image`, `twitter:image` and `citation_image`, else trafilatura's own metadata image, made absolute against the page URL. It never looks at the article body, so a page without preview metadata gets no image. Measured on the running instance on 2026-10-10: of two saved posts, one (a Substack-style blog) has `lead_image` and one (a personal blog) does not. The thumbnail another read-later app shows for the first one is its `og:image`. The list row in `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue` (around lines 539-542) always draws `` inside `.item-thumb`, ignoring `lead_image`. The page's CSP already allows `img-src 'self' https: data:` (`server/internal/core/middleware.go`), so remote https images load without a server change. Rejected for now: downloading and storing thumbnails on the server. It would survive link rot and hotlink blocking, but it needs a blob pipeline and a new endpoint; hotlinking with an icon fallback on error is enough until rot is observed. Items already saved keep their current `lead_image` until they are extracted again; no backfill migration is part of this bead. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] When a page declares no `og:image`, `twitter:image` or `citation_image` and trafilatura reports none, `lead_image` is the absolute URL of the first `` in the extracted article HTML whose `src` is `http`/`https` (after resolving relative URLs), skipping `data:` URIs and images whose `width` or `height` attribute is 1 or less. - [ ] A declared `og:image` still wins over the first article image (existing order unchanged). - [ ] A page with no usable image still stores no `lead_image`. - [ ] In the Biblioteca list, a row whose summary has `lead_image` renders an `` with that `src` inside the 64 x 64 px thumbnail box, `object-fit: cover`, `loading="lazy"`, `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` and an empty `alt`. - [ ] A row without `lead_image`, or whose image fails to load (`error` event), shows the existing document icon instead. - [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green and re-extracting the saved personal-blog post on a real server gives it a thumbnail (checked by the review, not the lane). ## Tests - unit: `server/internal/library/metadata_test.go` (or the extraction test that already covers lead images) gains cases for: fallback to the first article image, relative `src` made absolute, a `data:` image skipped, a 1 x 1 tracking pixel skipped, `og:image` still winning, and no image at all. - unit: `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.test.ts` asserts the `` attributes when `lead_image` is present, the icon when absent, and the icon after an `error` event. ## Blast radius **Edits:** `server/internal/library/metadata.go`, `server/internal/library/metadata_test.go`, `server/internal/library/extract.go`, `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue`, `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.test.ts` **Reads only:** `bin/ci`, `server/internal/core/middleware.go`, `api/openapi/library.yaml` `extract.go` is edited only if the article HTML has to be passed into the metadata resolution; the schema, the contract and the migrations are not touched.

title: Route each new item to the Inbox or the Stash and set its kind
description:
## What changes for the user
Today every saved link lands in the Inbox and is a "post", so a Pinterest image, a GitHub repo
and a long essay all compete for the same attention, and the person sorts them by hand. After
this change Norte decides on its own: links the person always keeps without reading go straight
to the Stash, the rest go to the Inbox, each gets a sensible kind, and nothing the person moved
by hand is ever moved back.

## Outcome
At save time and after extraction, a router places each new item in the Inbox or the Stash and
sets its kind, from the person's domain rules first, then the Laya decider, then the Inbox as
the default; the item records which of those decided, and a move by the person always wins.

## Context
Decided on 2026-10-10. The library's locations are Inbox (arrived, not triaged), Up Next
(priority), Later (someday maybe), Archive (processed: read or dismissed) and Stash (kept with no
intent to consume, the dump the person used to keep in Karakeep). The router chooses between
only two of them, Inbox and Stash; everything else is the person's move. Asking at save time
was rejected because it adds a click and a decision at the moment the person least wants one.

Order of decision for a new item:
1. A domain rule the person set (`pinterest.com -> stash`). A rule for a domain also matches its
   subdomains (`br.pinterest.com`); the most specific rule wins.
2. The Laya decider (`NORTE_DECIDER_URL`, a sidecar answering `POST /decide`, built by the
   decider bead): a `choice` between `inbox` and `stash` over a state of URL, host, title, `reason`
   and the first 1500 characters of extracted text. Stash only when P(stash) >= 0.8, because a
   wrong Stash hides an item and a wrong Inbox only costs a glance.
3. Otherwise, including no decider configured or the decider failing, the Inbox.

A domain rule is known at save time; Laya needs the extracted text. So the item is placed at
save by its rule or in the Inbox, and the decider runs inside the extraction pipeline afterwards,
moving the item only if it is still where the router put it and the person has not touched it.

Kind uses the same decider: a `choice` over the kinds, applied when its top probability is at
least 0.6, otherwise the kind stays the default. Kind names follow the translation bead.

Today a new item's location is set twice, by the DB default and explicitly in the service
(`server/internal/library/service.go` around line 275), and its kind is set around line 268 — the
field is `location` and the kind is `article` once norte-bc7 has landed, which it has by the time
this bead is dispatched. Library migrations: norte-bc7 adds `00004_library_location.sql` and
norte-u77 adds `00005`, so this bead's is `00006`. Jobs are registered through `Module.JobHandlers` (`server/internal/library/library.go`)
and the extraction transaction already enqueues follow-up work (`extract.go`, the classify
enqueue around line 587).

The Karakeep import (a separate bead) uses this router with one difference: where the router
would choose the Inbox, the import puts the item in the Archive. Expose that as an option on the
save path the importer calls, not as a second router.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A library migration adds a domain rules table (domain, location in `inbox`/`stash`) and a
      `location_source` column on items with values `rule`, `decider`, `default`, `user`, `import`.
- [ ] Saving a new item whose host matches a rule places it at the rule's location with
      `location_source = rule`; a subdomain matches its parent's rule; the longest matching
      domain wins.
- [ ] Saving a new item with no matching rule places it in the Inbox with
      `location_source = default`, then after extraction the decider is asked; with
      P(stash) >= 0.8 the item moves to the Stash with `location_source = decider`.
- [ ] The decider never moves an item whose `location_source` is `user` or `rule`, nor one whose
      location changed since save; a PATCH that changes location sets `location_source = user`.
- [ ] With no `NORTE_DECIDER_URL`, a decider error, a timeout of 5 s, or a non-2xx answer, the
      item stays in the Inbox, the failure is logged with the item id, and extraction still
      succeeds.
- [ ] The decider's kind answer is applied when its top probability is >= 0.6 and the person has
      not edited the kind; otherwise the kind is unchanged.
- [ ] The save path accepts an import option under which a destination of Inbox becomes Archive
      with `location_source = import`.
- [ ] A duplicate save never changes an existing item's location or kind.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- unit: rule matching (exact, subdomain, most specific wins, no match).
- unit: the decider client against an `httptest` server (stash above and below threshold,
  error, timeout, non-2xx, no URL configured).
- unit: the extraction-time move, including the cases where the person moved the item first.
- unit: kind threshold and a hand-edited kind kept.
- unit: the import option.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/library/migrations/`, `server/internal/library/router.go`, `server/internal/library/router_test.go`, `server/internal/library/decider.go`, `server/internal/library/decider_test.go`, `server/internal/library/service.go`, `server/internal/library/extract.go`, `server/internal/library/library.go`, `server/internal/library/items.go`
**Reads only:** `bin/ci`, `server/internal/app/config.go`, `decider/server.mjs`

The rule editing API and screen are a separate bead; this one reads rules, it does not expose
them.

## Recovery path
The migration's down step drops the rules table and the `location_source` column; locations
already chosen stay where they are.

With no extracted text the 0.8 Stash threshold sends the pin to the Inbox, so domain rules carry the obvious cases; re-measure with text in the state before tuning the threshold.

title: Reorganise the frontend into modules mounted by /api/config
description:
## What changes for the user
Today every part of the app is always there, the app promises offline use and sync it does not have, and nothing reacts to whether the server is running. After this lands, the app asks the server which products are switched on before it opens: a product that is off disappears from the sidebar and the home, its address shows a plain "módulo desligado" page instead of a broken screen, and when the server is not answering the app says "servidor indisponível" and retries by itself. The sidebar line "Sincronizado há 2 min" and the preferences text about sync, which describe something that does not exist, are gone.

## Outcome
`web/src` is reorganised into one folder per module plus a shell. Each module exports its routes, sidebar entries, home blocks, search entries and a static manifest declaring whether it is backed by the mock or by the API. The app fetches `GET /api/config` before mounting and mounts each module by one rule. Cross-module actions are gated by one rule. The retired offline and sync copy is rewritten and a test keeps it out.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. `web/` is its Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript frontend; today every data-backed product view reads one `reactive` singleton, `store`, from `web/src/mock/store.ts` (created at line 236, seeded from `web/src/mock/data.ts`), and the views that change data call its methods synchronously; the placeholder view and the design-system gallery do not use it. The backend is a Go server that already answers `GET /api/config` with `{modules: [...], version, llm, telegram, timezone}` — the list of modules switched on by its `NORTE_MODULES` setting — and generates TypeScript types into `web/src/api/`, with `web/src/api/client.ts` as the one HTTP client.

The server-side products are modules: `library` (reading), `notes` (highlights, annotations, questions — written into by both reading and study), `study`, `review` and `projects`. Only library and notes get a backend in this first delivery; study, review and projects stay on mock data for weeks. This bead is the first of three steps that replace the mock seam without breaking the app at any point: (1) reorganise into modules — this bead; (2) make every store asynchronous over the mock; (3) swap each module's data source to the API, slice by slice.

Today's layout: views in `web/src/views/` (14 files: Area, Curriculum, Decision, DsGallery, Home, Library, Material, Notes, Placeholder, Project, Projects, Review, StudyHome, Task, plus sub-components under `CurriculumView/`, `MaterialView/`, `ProjectView/`, `TaskView/`), mock data in `web/src/mock/` (`data.ts`, `learning.ts`, `library.ts`, `life.ts`, `notes.ts`, `study.ts`, `types.ts`, `store.ts`), the router in `web/src/router/index.ts` (routes at lines 28-73), the shell in `web/src/components/AppShell.vue`, `AppSidebar.vue`, `ShellOverlay.vue` (the command palette and the preferences dialog), the search index in `web/src/search/index.ts`, the design system in `web/src/components/ds/` (stays where it is). 37 Vitest files sit next to their sources.

What this bead does, decided:

- **Move into modules.** `web/src/modules/<name>/` for `library`, `notes`, `study`, `review`, `projects`, each holding its views, components, mock slice and an `index.ts`; `web/src/shell/` for the sidebar, home, command palette and preferences; the design-system gallery `DsGallery.vue` moves to `web/src/components/ds/gallery/` and `Placeholder.vue` to `web/src/shell/`, so `web/src/views/` is deleted. Each `index.ts` exports `routes`, `sidebar`, `homeBlocks`, `searchEntries` and a static `manifest` (`name`, `backing: 'api' | 'mock'`, route paths) the shell can read without mounting the module. Routes are lazy (`() => import(...)`).
- **Config before mount.** `main.ts` fetches `GET /api/config` before mounting the app; while it fails, it shows a "servidor indisponível" screen that retries (every 2 s, then backing off to 10 s).
- **The mount rule.** A module is mounted when its `backing` is `mock`, or when it is `api` and `/api/config` lists it. So in this delivery the mock-backed study, review and projects screens keep working while the library follows the server. For a path in a module's manifest that is not mounted, the router shows a "módulo desligado" page. The sidebar and the home show only mounted modules. One cross-module presentation rule carries over from today's app: when both `study` and `review` are mounted, Revisão is nested under Estudo; when `review` is mounted without `study`, Revisão is its own top-level entry.
- **The gating rule for cross-module actions** (link to a curriculum, make a task, add as material): offered only when the target module is mounted **and** its `backing` equals the source item's. Real ids are UUIDs, mock ids are strings like `saved-link-3`, and nothing may join the two: an `api` item never points at `mock` data and a `mock` item never points at the server. Core entities (subjects, links, focus, search) are not a module; each one becomes API-backed when its endpoint lands (subjects and focus with the subjects bead, search with the home-and-search bead). At the end of this bead only `/api/config` and `/api/health` exist, so the existing mock subject and search data stay behind mock providers until then. The gating rule above is about module-owned entities only.
- **Self-contained mock slices.** The mock study, review and notes data that reference library items today (`libraryItemId`, `sourceLibraryItemId`, `materialId`) get their own small set of mock items inside their slice, so deleting the library's mock slice later breaks nothing.
- **Mock data still backs everything** at the end of this bead; every module's manifest says `mock` except where a test sets `api`.
- **Retired copy.** The app is a client-server app: without the server nothing loads. The copy that makes unsupported sync claims is rewritten: the sidebar line "Sincronizado há {{ store.syncMinutesAgo }} min" (`AppSidebar.vue:365-368`, value from `mock/data.ts:23`), "Sem sincronização configurada" (`ShellOverlay.vue:228`), "O resto sincroniza com a conta." (`ShellOverlay.vue:213`) and the "Tema, dados e sync" subtitle (`ShellOverlay.vue:92`). The `SyncStatus` design-system component (`components/ds/SyncStatus.vue`) is not used by the app shell and stays in the gallery; do not add it anywhere. `design/system/README.md` is the design export kept verbatim and is not touched.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `web/src/modules/{library,notes,study,review,projects}/index.ts` and `web/src/shell/` exist; each `index.ts` exports `routes`, `sidebar`, `homeBlocks`, `searchEntries` and `manifest`, and `web/src/views/` no longer exists.
- [ ] With the library manifest set to `backing: 'api'` and `/api/config` returning `modules: []`, a test asserts: the sidebar and the home show no library entry, navigating to `/biblioteca` renders the "módulo desligado" page, and the study, review and projects screens still render.
- [ ] With `/api/config` failing, the app renders "servidor indisponível" and calls the endpoint again; when it starts answering, the app mounts.
- [ ] Sidebar tests cover study+review, study only, review only and neither, and show Revisão nested under Estudo only when both are mounted.
- [ ] A test asserts an `api`-backed library item shows no "link to curriculum" or "make a task" action while study and projects are `mock`-backed.
- [ ] A static import-boundary test proves no file under the study, review or notes modules imports the library's mock slice (the build after the slice is actually deleted is proved by the bead that deletes it).
- [ ] A test renders the shell and the preferences dialog and asserts that none of "Sincronizado há", "Sem sincronização configurada", "sincroniza com a conta", "Tema, dados e sync" appears.
- [ ] `npm run build` and `npm test` pass; every existing behaviour test passes; tests whose only contract is the retired sync copy (for example the sidebar's "Sincronizado há" assertion in `AppShell.test.ts`) are rewritten to assert its absence; every other moved test changes only its imports.
- [ ] Done when: with the library manifest set to `api` and `library` absent from config, the sidebar, the home and the router show no library entry, `/biblioteca` shows the disabled-module page, the mock-backed study, review and projects screens still render, and every existing frontend test passes.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + `@vue/test-utils`, jsdom): mount rule over the four combinations of `backing` and listed/unlisted; disabled-module page; server-unavailable screen with a fake fetch; cross-module action gating.
- Copy (Vitest): the retired-strings test above, over the rendered shell and preferences.
- Regression: the 37 existing test files, moved with their sources.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/` broadly: moves of `views/*`, `mock/*`, `components/AppShell.vue`, `AppSidebar.vue`, `ShellOverlay.vue`, `search/index.ts` and their tests into `modules/<name>/` and `shell/`; `web/src/router/index.ts`; `web/src/main.ts`; new `index.ts` per module; the new disabled-module and server-unavailable pages.
**Reads only:** `web/src/api/client.ts` and `web/src/api/core.d.ts` (the generated config type), `web/src/components/ds/` (not moved).

Frontend only; no file under `server/` is touched. Size L: it moves well over six files of one kind. It cannot be split along a seam that shares no file — the router, `main.ts` and the shell are touched by every part of the move.
close_reason: Merged in PR #29. bin/ci green locally (after merging main with the jobs-test race fix, PR #30) and in CI; all criteria met per review, 37 test files became 45 with none lost. Non-blocking: the app mounts before /api/config resolves and prunes the router afterwards (equivalent to the criterion, not its wording); the production boot path (readConfig, bootApplication) is untested; the import-boundary test is textual and matches only single-quoted specifiers; ShellOverlay.test polling raised from 20 to 200 attempts.

title: Give the sidebar footer buttons the navigation link typography
description:
## What changes for the user
At the bottom of the sidebar, "Buscar" and "Preferências" are drawn in a visibly larger font than every other sidebar entry, so they look like they belong to a different menu. After this lands they use the same type as the navigation entries above them, as in the design.

## Outcome
The "Buscar ⌘K" and "Preferências" buttons in the sidebar footer render with the same typography as the sidebar navigation links: `var(--font-display)`, 14px, line-height 20px, weight 550, colour `var(--ink-2)`.

## Context
Norte is a Vue 3 frontend under `web/`, ported from a design-tool prototype. In the prototype (`design/prototypes/Command_Home/template.html`, git-ignored, only in the main checkout at `/home/gabriel/repositories/norte/design/prototypes/`), both footer buttons carry the same `nav-item` class as the navigation links, whose rule is `font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 14px; line-height: 20px; font-weight: 550; color: var(--ink-2)`, plus `nav-btn` which only resets the button chrome (`width: 100%; border: 0; background: transparent; cursor: pointer; text-align: left`).

In the app, `web/src/components/AppSidebar.vue` renders them as `.app-item.app-button`, and the `.app-button` rule sets `font: inherit`. That shorthand resets the family, size, line-height and weight that `.app-item` set, so the buttons take the inherited body font at its default size, which a 1440px screenshot shows as larger than the links above. The fix is to keep the button reset without overriding the `.app-item` typography (for example by dropping `font: inherit` or restating the four values after it).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In `web/src/components/AppSidebar.vue`, the computed font of the "Buscar" and "Preferências" buttons equals that of a sidebar navigation link: family from `--font-display`, 14px size, 20px line-height, weight 550.
- [ ] The buttons keep no border, transparent background, full width and left-aligned text.
- [ ] Done when: a 1440x900 screenshot of the sidebar footer shows "Buscar" and "Preferências" at the same size as "Inbox" or "Currículos", and `cd web && npm run build && npm test` passes.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + @vue/test-utils): mounting the sidebar, the footer buttons carry the same typography class or styles as a navigation link (assert on the class set or the scoped style rule, since jsdom does not compute fonts).

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/components/AppSidebar.vue`, `web/src/components/AppShell.test.ts`
**Reads only:** `design/prototypes/Command_Home/template.html`

One style rule in the sidebar component and one test; nothing else changes.
