title: Add the durable background jobs worker
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing visible yet. This is what lets saving be instant later: slow work (extracting an article's text, asking the classifier where it belongs, replying on Telegram) runs in the background after the save has already returned, retries by itself when a site is briefly down, and survives the server being restarted halfway through. When something fails for good, it shows up as a failed job the person can retry with one command instead of vanishing.

## Outcome
A durable job queue inside `norte serve`: jobs are rows in `core_jobs`, one in-process worker claims them with a lease, renews it while running, retries with a fixed backoff, fails permanently after three attempts or at once on a permanent error, and reclaims jobs whose lease expired after a crash. `norte jobs list` and `norte jobs retry <id>` inspect and requeue them.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app. `server/` is its Go backend: one binary, SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite` with one writer connection and a reader pool, goose migrations, sqlc queries. Products are modules switched on by `NORTE_MODULES`; each module registers the job kinds it handles. The "core" (always on, not a module) already has the `core_jobs` table:

`core_jobs(id, kind, payload, dedupe_key, status, attempts, available_at, lease_until, lease_owner, last_error, created_at, started_at, finished_at)`, `status` in `queued|running|done|failed`, index `(status, available_at)`, partial unique index on `dedupe_key` where `status IN ('queued','running')`. Times are fixed-width UTC strings `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ` written through `core.FormatTime`; the clock is `core.Clock`, injectable in tests.

The design, decided:

- **Enqueue.** `core.Jobs.Enqueue(ctx, tx, kind, payload, dedupeKey)` takes the caller's transaction, so a save and its job commit together. `dedupe_key` is nullable; when set and a non-finished job with the same key exists, the call returns that job's id and inserts nothing (enqueueing `extract` for one item twice yields one job).
- **Claim.** One worker goroutine started by `norte serve`. Every 1 s of the injected clock while idle (a "worker cycle"), and again immediately after a job finishes, it claims the oldest `queued` job with `available_at <= now` **whose `kind` has a registered handler** — a job of an unregistered kind (from a module since disabled) stays `queued`, untouched — by setting `status = running`, `lease_until = now + 2 min`, `lease_owner`, `started_at` in the same statement that selects it (`UPDATE ... WHERE id = (SELECT ...) RETURNING ...`) on the single writer, so two claims cannot take one job.
- **Clock and scheduling.** The worker schedules only through the core's `core.Clock` (`Now`, `NewTimer`) and tests use the `core/clocktest` manual clock, both from the database bead. Worker polling, lease renewal, backoff and reclaim use only this clock and never call `time.Sleep`, `time.After` or `time.NewTicker`, so a test can walk minutes of schedule without waiting.
- **Lease renewal.** Every 30 s of the injected clock while the handler runs, the worker extends `lease_until` by two minutes.
- **Attempts are counted at claim.** The claiming statement increments `attempts`, so a job that succeeds on its third run records `attempts = 3`. The handler receives an immutable `core.Job{ID, Kind, Payload, Attempt, MaxAttempts}` (`MaxAttempts = 3`), so a handler can tell its last attempt from an earlier one and perform terminal effects (marking its own row failed, enqueueing a notification) only then.
- **Failure and backoff.** On a handler error (attempts are not incremented again): `last_error` set (redacted: URLs stripped of their query string, never a token), and `available_at = now + 1 min` after the first failure, `+ 5 min` after the second; the third failure sets `failed` and `finished_at`. A handler returning `core.Permanent(err)` (a refused address, a body over a cap, a malformed input) sets `failed` at once with no retry.
- **Reclaim.** At startup and every minute the worker returns `running` jobs whose `lease_until` has passed to `queued`, so a crash mid-job strands nothing. Handlers must therefore be idempotent: a crash after the effect and before the status write replays them. Each handler's bead says what makes it idempotent.
- **In-process on purpose.** A second worker process would be a second deployable for a one-user app and would break "one binary, one container". Heavy runtimes (PDFium later) are created inside the handler and closed when it returns, so their memory is paid only while a job runs.
- **Handler registration.** This bead defines `core.Job{ID, Kind, Payload, Attempt, MaxAttempts}` and `core.JobHandler` (`func(ctx context.Context, job core.Job) error`) in `server/internal/core/jobs.go`, and `core.Jobs.Register(kind, handler)`; the module registry bead, which depends on this one, calls `Register` for each enabled module's `JobHandlers()`. `JobHandlers() map[string]core.JobHandler` on each module (the registry bead mounts them); for this bead, a `core.Jobs.Register(kind, handler)` the registry will call.
- **CLI.** `norte jobs list` (opens the database without migrating; columns id, kind, status, attempts, available_at, last_error) and `norte jobs retry <id>`, which first checks for a `queued` or `running` row with the same non-null `dedupe_key` — if one exists it exits non-zero naming that job and changes neither row, since the partial unique index would otherwise be violated — and otherwise moves the `failed` job back to `queued` with `attempts = 0` and refuses any other status with a non-zero exit.
- **Logging.** Every job logs kind, id, duration and outcome as `slog` JSON; payloads are never logged.
- **Shutdown.** On SIGTERM the worker cancels the handler's context and waits up to the server's 15 s drain. It releases the lease (`status = queued`, `lease_until = NULL`, `attempts = attempts - 1`, so a restart costs no attempt; a reclaim after a crash keeps the count, which bounds a crash loop) only after the handler has returned. If the deadline passes with the handler still running, shutdown logs a non-clean exit and leaves the lease to expire on its own, so the job never becomes claimable while the old handler might still commit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With a fake clock, a job whose handler fails twice and succeeds on the third attempt ends `done` with `attempts = 3`, and the test asserts `available_at` was `failure_1 + 1 min` and then `failure_2 + 5 min`.
- [ ] The handler sees `Attempt` = 1, 2, 3 on successive runs and `MaxAttempts` = 3.
- [ ] A handler that fails three times leaves the job `failed` with `attempts = 3`, `finished_at` set and `last_error` holding the last error.
- [ ] A handler returning `core.Permanent(err)` leaves the job `failed` after exactly one attempt.
- [ ] A job set to `running` with `lease_until` in the past (a "dead" worker) is reclaimed by the reclaim pass and then completed by the worker.
- [ ] While a handler blocks for more than 30 s of fake time, `lease_until` is extended at least once and the job is not reclaimed.
- [ ] Two enqueues with the same `dedupe_key` while the first is `queued` yield one row and return the same id; after the first is `done`, a third enqueue with that key inserts a new row.
- [ ] A job of a kind with no registered handler stays `queued` with `attempts = 0` after ten worker cycles.
- [ ] `norte jobs retry <id>` on a `failed` job sets `queued` and `attempts = 0`; on a `done` job it exits non-zero and changes nothing.
- [ ] Advancing the manual clock fires polling, renewal, backoff and reclaim deterministically, and a static test rejects `time.Sleep`, `time.After` and `time.NewTicker` in the worker's source.
- [ ] A handler that ignores cancellation past the drain deadline never has its lease released early, and a second worker cannot claim the job until the lease expires.
- [ ] Retrying a failed job whose `dedupe_key` is held by a queued or running job is refused with a non-zero exit and changes neither row.
- [ ] `(cd server && go test -race ./internal/core -run TestWorkersDoNotDoubleClaim)` passes and `bin/ci` runs it.
- [ ] A job enqueued while the worker is idle is claimed within 1 s of fake time.
- [ ] A job released by a clean shutdown is claimed again with the same `Attempt`; a job reclaimed after a lease expiry is claimed with `Attempt + 1`.
- [ ] `norte jobs list` does not run migrations (a test against a database at an older core version leaves `goose_core` unchanged).
- [ ] Done when: the fake-clock retry, permanent-failure, reclaim, dedupe and unregistered-kind tests above all pass under `go test ./...`.

## Tests
- Unit (Go, `server/internal/core/jobs_test.go`): every criterion above with a fake `core.Clock` and handlers that record their calls; no `time.Sleep` in tests.
- Concurrency (Go unit, run with `-race`): two worker loops against one database claim 50 jobs with no job run twice.
- Integration (Go test invoking the CLI entry point): `jobs list` and `jobs retry` against a temp `NORTE_DATA`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/core/jobs.go` (new), `server/internal/core/jobs_test.go` (new), `server/internal/core/queries/jobs.sql` (new) and its generated `server/internal/core/db/` output, `server/cmd/norte/` (the `jobs` subcommand and starting the worker in `serve`), `bin/ci` (running the claim race test with `-race`).
**Reads only:** `server/internal/core/migrations/` (the `core_jobs` table already exists; this bead adds no migration), the clock and time helpers.

One package, CLI wiring and one gate line: six edited files, so size L.
close_reason: Merged in PR #26. bin/ci green locally (12 checks) and in CI; disabling reclaim makes the jobs suite fail (by a 600 s timeout: the reclaim test hangs instead of failing fast). Review, non-blocking: a job finishing at the instant of SIGTERM can be released and re-run instead of marked done; terminal and renew write errors are ignored and a lost lease does not cancel the handler; reclaim is serviced only when idle; redaction strips query strings but not userinfo; tests for 'not reclaimed while renewing', 'ten cycles', re-claim right after a job, and jobs list on an older schema are weaker than their criteria.

title: Run Laya as a decider sidecar Norte can call over HTTP
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing visible on its own: this is the piece that lets Norte decide, without asking, where a
newly saved link goes and what kind of thing it is. It runs Laya, a local decision model, next
to the Norte server so those decisions cost no API key and no network call to anyone else.

## Outcome
A small HTTP service in the Norte repository wraps Laya and answers typed questions about a
state, with a health endpoint, a Docker image, and an entry in the example compose file; Norte
can reach it through a new `NORTE_DECIDER_URL` setting.

## Context
Laya (Hugging Face `convaiinnovations/laya`, Apache 2.0 weights) is a decision model, not a text
generator: given a state (here: a saved link's URL, host, title, `why` and the start of its
text) and typed questions, it returns every answer with calibrated probabilities in one forward
pass. Question types: `choice` (one option, a probability per option), `score` (an expected level
on an ordered rubric) and `noul` (P(true) of a statement). The Node package `@receptron/laya`
(source cloned at `/home/gabriel/repositories/_cloned/laya`, see its README) runs the ONNX bundle
through `onnxruntime-node`; the weights (about 1.7 GB fp32) download from Hugging Face on first
use into `LAYA_CACHE` (default `~/.cache/receptron-laya`); it needs about 2 GB of RAM and takes
about 140 ms for a three-question call once warm. Limits: under about 20 options per `choice`,
192 tokens per question header, 512 tokens of state.

Decided on 2026-10-10: Norte is a single static Go binary (`CGO_ENABLED=0`, `FROM scratch`
image), so embedding ONNX Runtime is rejected; Laya runs as a sidecar that Norte calls over HTTP,
the same way it calls its LLM. A native Go or Rust port is a separate side project and not a
dependency.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `decider/` holds a Node service (package.json, one entry file, its tests) depending on
      `@receptron/laya`, listening on `DECIDER_LISTEN` (default `127.0.0.1:8091`).
- [ ] `POST /decide` takes `{"state": <object>, "questions": <Laya questions object>}` and answers
      Laya's `answers` object unchanged plus `usage`; a malformed body answers 400 with a JSON
      error naming the problem; a Laya failure answers 500 with the message.
- [ ] `GET /health` answers 200 with `{"ready": true}` once the model is loaded and 503 with
      `{"ready": false}` while it is still loading; the model loads once at startup, not per
      request.
- [ ] `decider/Dockerfile` builds an image running the service as a non-root user with the model
      cache on a volume; `docker-compose.example.yml` gains a `decider` service, its cache volume,
      and `NORTE_DECIDER_URL` on the Norte service.
- [ ] `server/internal/app/config.go` gains `decider_url` (`NORTE_DECIDER_URL`, flag
      `--decider-url`, empty by default), and `norte config` shows it.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green and the service's own tests pass with Laya stubbed.

## Tests
- unit: the HTTP layer with Laya stubbed (decide, 400 cases, 500 path, health before and after
  load), run by `npm test` in `decider/` and registered in `bin/ci`.
- unit: the new config setting in `server/internal/app/config_test.go`.
- manual, by the review: one real `/decide` call with the downloaded model answering a
  two-option `choice`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `decider/package.json`, `decider/server.mjs`, `decider/server.test.mjs`, `decider/Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.example.yml`, `server/internal/app/config.go`, `server/internal/app/config_test.go`, `bin/ci`
**Reads only:** `/home/gabriel/repositories/_cloned/laya/README.md`

The Norte server does not call the decider yet; the routing bead does.
close_reason: Merged in PR #34 (gate and docker green at 4f44f8f). Review: 33 service tests, config tests, and a real /decide against the downloaded Laya model (pin 0.60 stash, essay 0.81 inbox, ~0.1 s warm). rework:0.

title: Wire home and search to the API and add the vertical test
description:
## What changes for the user
The home screen and the search box still show invented content. After this lands, Início shows what was really saved — "continuar lendo" from what was opened last and "salvos recentemente" — and the command palette (Ctrl+K) finds a saved item by any word in its text, a subject by name, and the app's screens, all with the keyboard. A single automated test then walks the whole first delivery — save, extract, classify, accept, highlight, question — so it cannot quietly break.

## Outcome
Início's library blocks read the API; `GET /api/core/search` merges each enabled module's search provider plus subjects; the command palette merges it with the static screen index in an accessible combobox; the Estudo home's dead search box is wired or removed. A Go end-to-end test proves the loop and runs in `bin/ci`.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. Its first delivery is "read": save a link, have it reappear at the right moment, read it, and end the reading in something that survives the day. `server/` is the Go backend; the library (items, full-text search over title, author, why, headings and text with `bm25` weights, extraction and classification jobs), notes (highlights, annotations, questions) and the core (subjects, links, focus, a stub LLM server for tests) are in place. Each module implements `SearchEntries(ctx, q, limit)` returning `core.SearchEntry{id, module, type, title, subtitle, path}` where `path` is the frontend route that opens it (`/biblioteca/<id>` for a library item, `/assuntos/<slug>` for a subject); the library's provider is its FTS query. The extraction job refuses loopback and private addresses on purpose (SSRF protection), so a test cannot make the server fetch an `httptest` page — it must send the page as an HTML snapshot, the way the browser extension does.

`web/` is the Vue 3 frontend. The command palette lives in `ShellOverlay` (mode `busca`; opened by ⌘K/Ctrl+K in `AppShell`), indexed by `web/src/search/index.ts` (`createSearchIndex`, `filterSearchIndex`, `groupSearchResults`) — now under `web/src/shell/`. The Início view has mock blocks and a `#home-search` box bound to a value nothing uses; the Estudo home has a `#study-search` input with no binding at all. Library items carry `last_opened_at` and `saved_at`.

Decided:

- **Início**: the blocks the library module provides — "continuar lendo" (opened items by `last_opened_at` descending, through the list endpoint's `sort=last_opened_desc`) and "salvos recentemente" (by `saved_at` desc) — read the API. Blocks from mock-backed modules stay on their mock.
- **Search API**: `GET /api/core/search?q=` (contract in `core.yaml`) calls each enabled module's `SearchEntries` with a limit of 10, adds matching subjects from the core, and merges them deterministically: every provider returns `SearchEntry.Score` in [0, 1]: the library maps its FTS5 `bm25` values (lower is better) linearly so the best hit of the query scores 1 and the worst 0, and a single hit or all-equal hits score 1; subjects score 1 for an exact normalised name or alias match, 0.8 for a prefix match and 0.6 for a substring match; entries are deduplicated by id and ordered by score descending, then title, then id, and the total is capped at 30. Nothing is merged twice: the library's provider is its FTS query and no other source indexes library text.
- **Palette**: merges the API's results with its static index of screens; an accessible combobox — arrow keys move, Enter opens, Escape closes, `role="combobox"`/`listbox`/`option`, `aria-activedescendant` on the input; requests superseded by typing are cancelled. The Início `#home-search` box opens the palette with its text.
- **Estudo home search**: wire it to the same endpoint through the palette, or remove it; it must not remain an input that does nothing.
- **Vertical test** in Go (`server/e2e/` or `server/internal/app/e2e_test.go`): boots the full server on a temp `NORTE_DATA` with the stub LLM and the worker on a fake clock; creates a focus subject; saves a fixture page through `POST /api/library/items` with its HTML as a snapshot; waits for extraction and classification; accepts the suggestion; writes a highlight and a question; asserts the item is on the subject's panel (`GET /api/core/links?dst_id=…&status=confirmed`) and first in `GET /api/library/items?view=now`. It runs in `bin/ci`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With items saved through `norte save`, Início's "salvos recentemente" lists them newest first and "continuar lendo" lists an item after it is opened in the reader.
- [ ] `GET /api/core/search?q=<a word only in an item's extracted text>` returns that item with `path` to its reader; a subject name returns the subject; at most 10 entries per provider and 30 in total.
- [ ] Fixed fixtures prove each provider's raw-to-score mapping, including the single-hit and all-equal cases.
- [ ] Two providers plus subjects with tied and unequal scores merge in exactly the documented order whatever the providers' registration order.
- [ ] In the palette, typing that word shows the item; ArrowDown moves `aria-activedescendant`; Enter opens the reader; Escape closes; a component test asserts the roles and attributes.
- [ ] The Estudo home search box either queries the endpoint or no longer exists.
- [ ] The vertical test passes in `bin/ci`, and a negative-control subtest with classification disabled asserts no suggestion and no confirmed link appear and the walk stops at the accept step (proving the main test exercises the classifier).
- [ ] "continuar lendo" never shows an item that was never opened.
- [ ] Typing two palette queries whose first response is delayed aborts the first request (its `AbortSignal` fires) and its results never render.
- [ ] Done when: the home shows items saved from the CLI, the palette finds an item by a word of its content, and the vertical test is green in `bin/ci`.

## Tests
- E2E (Go, full server + stub LLM + fake clock + temp `NORTE_DATA`): the vertical test.
- Integration (Go): search merging and caps with two providers.
- Component (Vitest, fake providers): Início blocks; palette combobox keyboard behaviour and ARIA.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `api/openapi/core.yaml` (search) and generated outputs, `server/internal/core/` (search merge handler), `server/internal/app/` (injecting the enabled `[]core.SearchProvider` into the core search handler; the core never imports the registry), `server/internal/library/` (its `SearchEntries` provider, if not already present), the vertical test file, `bin/ci` (if the test needs its own invocation), `web/src/shell/` (Início blocks, palette, search index), `web/src/modules/library/` (its home blocks), `web/src/modules/study/` (the Estudo home search box only).
**Reads only:** the stub LLM, the fixture corpus under `server/internal/library/testdata/`.

Server core, library, the shell and one study view; size L.
close_reason: Merged into local main 4f0c4f2 (GitHub unreachable). Gate 17/17 green after merging main (one import conflict in AppShell, union). Review: 9/10 criteria MET, 1 PARTLY; 19 mutations, 17 caught; FTS5/LIKE query safety probed with 13 hostile inputs, all 200. Fixed before merge: per-provider cap test now able to fail; vertical walk asserts an absent passage is orphaned (proves extract->highlight); serve wiring extracted to BuildNorteRuntime shared by cli.go and the vertical test; search q limited to 200 characters (400 above). Open: a notes hit opens its tab, not the note (no per-note route yet); the phone top bar has no search button (search via drawer, Ctrl+K, Inicio).

title: Add subjects, focus, links and the subject page
description:
## What changes for the user
A saved link finally has somewhere to go. After this lands, the person can create subjects ("Kubernetes", "Escrita"), link a link to one when saving or later, and open a subject's page to see everything saved about it, counted by kind. A subject can be marked as a current focus with one switch. Subjects get their own entry in the sidebar, and the subjects on the Estudo home open their page instead of the whole library.

## Outcome
The core's subjects API (CRUD, focus toggle, lookup by slug, per-kind counts), `GET /api/core/focus`, the links API (create manual, list by end, decide a suggestion), and the frontend: the subject screen `/assuntos/:slug`, a reusable "Salvos sobre isso" panel, a link picker in the save dialog and on an item, the Estudo home's subjects linking to their pages, "novo assunto" controls, a top-level "Assuntos" sidebar section, and the "Listas" group hidden while study is mock-backed.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. Its core problem, measured on the person: a link saved is almost always the right thing found at the wrong moment — a subject of real interest that is not the current focus — and nothing brings it back when the subject becomes the focus. Subjects and links are how a saved item gets a destination.

`server/` is the Go backend; the always-on "core" (not a module) already has the tables `core_subjects(id, name, slug UNIQUE, focus, created_at)`, `core_subject_aliases(alias_slug, subject_id)`, the item registry `core_items(id, module, type, title, url)` and `core_links(id, src_id, dst_id, kind, source, status, confidence, created_at, decided_at)` with `UNIQUE(src_id, dst_id, kind)`, `kind` in `about|material_of|derived_from|blocks`, `source` in `manual|llm`, `status` in `confirmed|suggested|rejected`. `core_links` is the only relation between modules. A subject is registered in `core_items` like any other link target. The core's contract is `api/openapi/core.yaml`, routes under `/api/core/`. Each module may implement `FocusTargets(ctx)` (title, id, type of what it considers "in progress"); the library implements none; study and projects (later deliveries) will. The library already saves items with an optional `link_to` list that creates `about` links.

`web/` is the Vue 3 frontend, organised by module, with the library and notes reading the API. The sidebar is `AppSidebar` (now under `web/src/shell/`): today the Estudo group has an "Assuntos" child (route `estudo` with hash `#assuntos`, a count summed from module counts, commented as "no subject entity"), and the Biblioteca children end with a "Listas" sub-heading listing library items by curriculum. The Estudo home (`StudyHomeView`, a mock-backed study screen) has a subjects grid (heading `#study-subjects`) whose every entry links to `/biblioteca?v=tudo`.

Decided:

- **Subjects API**: `GET /api/core/subjects?q=&cursor=&limit=` and `POST /api/core/subjects`, where `q` matches accent-insensitively over the normalised name and the aliases (exact, then prefix, then substring, ties by slug then id) and returns each canonical subject once, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/core/subjects/{id}` (`PATCH` renames and toggles `focus`; the slug is derived from the name — lowercase, accents stripped, punctuation removed, spaces to hyphens — and a collision is 409), `GET /api/core/subjects/by-slug/{slug}`. `GET /api/core/subjects/{id}` returns per-kind counts of the library items linked to it (`confirmed` links only). Creating or renaming a subject registers or updates its `core_items` row. Deleting a subject runs, in one writer transaction, the delete and `core.UnregisterItem` for its registry row; the registry row's cascade removes every link to and from it, and the alias cascade removes its aliases. Subjects are created from the UI or the CLI (`norte subjects add|list|focus <name>`), never by an LLM on its own.
- **Focus**: `GET /api/core/focus` returns the subjects with `focus = true` plus every enabled module's `FocusTargets` (the registry injects the enabled modules into the core focus service as `[]core.FocusProvider`; the core never imports the registry), each `{id, type, title}`. "In progress" is defined by each module. Focus is derived, not declared; the subject `focus` flag is the smallest version of an explicit focus, and it is what makes "what to read now" and the classifier testable before curricula and projects exist.
- **Links API**: `POST /api/core/links` (calls `core.Links.Confirm`; an end not in `core_items` is 400; manual, created `confirmed`; on an existing `suggested` or `rejected` pair for the same `(src, dst, kind)` it flips that row to `confirmed` with `source = manual` and `decided_at` set, rather than failing on the unique index), `GET /api/core/links?dst_id=&src_id=&status=&cursor=&limit=` (every filter optional; `status` alone lists the suggestion queue, ordered by `created_at` descending then id and served by a new core index on `(status, created_at)`; each item is `{id, kind, source, status, confidence, created_at, decided_at, src: {id, module, type, title, url}, dst: {...}}` with both ends read from `core_items`), `POST /api/core/links/{id}/decide` (`accept` → `confirmed`, `reject` → `rejected`, setting `decided_at`). A rejected row stays as the record that the pair was rejected.
- **Lists** (subjects, links) are cursor-paginated like every list in Norte: `cursor` and `limit` (default 50), a documented total order with the id as tie-breaker, the filters hashed into the cursor (a cursor reused with other filters is refused with 400), and a `{items, next_cursor}` envelope; the sidebar, the picker, the panel and the suggestion queue load all pages or offer "carregar mais".
- **Deleting a subject** from its screen: the delete action first fetches the number of links to and from it, names that count in a confirmation dialog, and calls `DELETE` only after explicit confirmation; cancelling sends nothing.
- **Subject screen** `/assuntos/:slug`: name, focus switch, per-kind counts, and the "Salvos sobre isso" panel. Counts and lists come only from enabled, `api`-backed modules.
- **"Salvos sobre isso"**: a panel component listing the library items linked (`confirmed`, `about`) to a given target id. Placed on the subject page now; built to be reused by the curriculum and project pages in later deliveries, so it takes the target id as its only input.
- **Link picker** in the Início save dialog and on an item: fed by `GET /api/core/focus` first, then a subject search; selecting creates the link (on save via `link_to`, on an item via `POST /api/core/links`).
- **Sidebar**: a top-level "Assuntos" section listing subjects (links to `/assuntos/:slug`); the old "Assuntos" child under Estudo is removed, since the top-level entry replaces it. The "Listas" group is hidden while `study` is mock-backed — an `api` library item cannot point at mock curricula — and returns in the study delivery fed by `material_of` links.
- **Estudo home**: the subjects grid lists real subjects and each opens its subject page; a "novo assunto" control on the grid and on the subject page.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `POST /api/core/subjects {name: "Machine Learning"}` returns slug `machine-learning` and a `core_items` row of type `subject`; a second subject with the same name returns 409.
- [ ] An item linked to a subject (on save via `link_to`, or later via `POST /api/core/links`) appears on `/assuntos/<slug>` with the right per-kind count, and the subject appears in the sidebar's Assuntos section.
- [ ] Toggling focus on a subject adds it to and removes it from `GET /api/core/focus`.
- [ ] Deleting a subject removes its subject, alias, registry and link rows; the dialog names the link count; cancelling sends no request.
- [ ] Subject search finds a subject by its name typed without accents and by an alias, returns it once, in a stable order.
- [ ] 120 subjects page as 50/50/20; a links cursor reused with changed filters is refused with 400.
- [ ] `POST /api/core/links` on a pair previously `rejected`, and on a pair currently `suggested`, sets it to `confirmed` and leaves one row; `decide reject` on a `suggested` link sets `rejected` and `decided_at`.
- [ ] The "Salvos sobre isso" panel, given a target id, lists exactly the `confirmed` `about` links to it (a suggested or rejected link is not listed).
- [ ] The Estudo home's subjects open `/assuntos/:slug`; the old Estudo "Assuntos" child is gone; the "Listas" group is not rendered while study is mock-backed.
- [ ] `norte subjects add "Escrita"`, `norte subjects list` and `norte subjects focus "Escrita"` work against a temp `NORTE_DATA`.
- [ ] Done when: an item linked to a subject appears on that subject's page with the right per-kind count and in the sidebar's Assuntos section, and toggling focus on a subject changes `/api/core/focus`.

## Tests
- Unit (Go): slug derivation over a table (accents, punctuation, case).
- Integration (Go, `httptest` + temp `NORTE_DATA`): subjects CRUD and counts; focus; links create/flip/decide; CLI.
- Component (Vitest, fake providers): subject screen, panel, link picker, sidebar section, Listas hidden under a mock-backed study.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `api/openapi/core.yaml` (subjects, focus, links) and its generated outputs, `server/internal/core/` (a migration adding the `(status, created_at)` index on `core_links`, subjects, focus, links services and handlers, `subjects` CLI), `web/src/shell/` (sidebar, subject screen, link picker, the panel component), `web/src/modules/study/` (the Estudo home subjects grid only), `web/src/modules/library/` (link picker on an item), `server/internal/app/` (injecting `[]core.FocusProvider`), `server/cmd/norte/` (mounting the `subjects` CLI), the frontend router (the `/assuntos/:slug` route).
**Reads only:** `core_subjects`/`core_links` schema (already migrated).

Server core and three frontend areas; size L.

## Recovery path
No migration: the subject and link tables already exist. The one destructive operation added is deleting a subject, which cascades to its links and its registry row; the UI asks for confirmation and names the number of linked items before deleting. A wrongly deleted subject is recreated by hand and its items relinked; there is no undo in this version.
close_reason: Merged into local main f87c163 (GitHub unreachable). Gate 12/12 green. Review: 18 mutations (11 red, 7 survived, all 7 closed by the fix pass). Fixed before merge: stubbed-fetch tests for shell/data/apiSource.ts and library link_to; carregar mais in the sidebar subjects and the saved-about panel; delete dialog re-reads the link count; rename tests (registry url, 409 on a taken slug); focus provider loop test; counts limited to enabled modules; Decide only accepts suggested links (409 not_suggested otherwise); link resolution as one JOIN. Open, non-blocking: nothing writes subject aliases yet and a new slug can equal another subject's alias; the picker ignores focus targets; Listas criterion vacuous (the string does not exist in source).

title: Translate the Study module's routes and copy to English
description:
## What changes for the user
Study holds the curricula — the modules, materials and exercises of something being learned. Its
addresses are `/estudo` and `/curriculos/<slug>`, its screens read `Currículos`, `Trilha` and
`Próximos estudos`, and it carries the single largest Portuguese file in the repo:
`web/src/modules/study/mock/curricula.ts`, 102 accented rows of invented curriculum content. After
this change the module answers at `/study` and `/curricula/<slug>` and reads in English.

## Outcome
Every route path, route name, route title, DOM id and string in `web/src/modules/study/` is
English, including the invented curriculum content, and the module's sidebar rows, shortcut and
palette entry read in English.

## Context
Routes and copy are one bead per module here. A route record is one object; the breadcrumbs, the
"see all" links and the `router.replace` after creating a curriculum all name the route, and they
sit in the same files as the strings.

The renames:

| today | English |
| --- | --- |
| `/estudo` name `estudo` title `Estudo` | `/study` name `study` title `Study` |

title: Port the base design-system components to Vue
description:
## What changes for the user
Screens cannot be built until the buttons, tabs, titles and panels they share exist. After this lands, every screen can use the same controls the prototype shows, in both themes.

## Outcome
Vue SFCs in `web/src/components/ds/` for Button, Tag, SyncStatus, Stat, ProgressBar, StreakGrid, PageTitle, NavItem, SectionHeader, SegmentedControl, Tabs, SidePanel, TextField and Icon. Each matches its README, its props in `index.d.ts` and its screenshot.

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Open `design/prototypes/Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html` in a browser to see the screen. Read `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html` for markup, inline styles and behaviour. The behaviour is a `class Component extends DCLogic` block with React-style `state`/`setState`. The template uses a design-tool runtime whose `sc-if`, `sc-for` and `{{ }}` bindings map almost one to one onto `v-if`, `v-for` and `{{ }}`. Prototype links point at `Norte - X.dc.html?param=`; translate them into the routes below.
- `design/system/` holds the committed design system. It has tokens in `tokens.css`/`tokens.json` (colour, type, a 4px spacing scale, radius, shadow), one `components/<Name>/README.md` per component, props in `components/index.d.ts`, and screenshots in `screenshots/`. Fonts are in `fonts/`: Schibsted Grotesk for display, Geist for sans and Commit Mono for mono.
- There are two themes, Claro and Escuro, switched by `data-theme` on the root element and stored in `localStorage` under `norte-theme`. The visual rule is quiet: one cobalt accent, no cards, no gradients, no warm colours.

Route table (shared by every screen):
- `/` is Início (Command Home).
- `/biblioteca` is the library, with query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`.
- `/notas` is notes, with query `tab` = `highlights|anotacoes|perguntas`.
- `/revisao` is the flashcard review.
- `/estudo` is the Estudo home (Currículos and Assuntos).
- `/curriculos/:slug` is one curriculum.
- `/material/:kind/:id` is one reading item, where kind is `post|livro|paper`.
- `/projetos` is the project list.
- `/areas/:id` is one area.
- `/projetos/:id` is one project.
- `/decisoes/:id` is one decision.
- `/tarefas/:id` is one task.

The repo is public. Never copy the prototype's mock content into code; use the neutral invented data in `web/src/mock/`. UI strings stay Portuguese.

The repo is a monorepo: the Vue app lives in `web/` and a Go backend will live in `server/` and later serve the built app from one binary. All frontend paths below are under `web/`; `design/` stays at the repo root. The gate is `npm run build && npm test`, run in `web/`.

Each component's spec is `design/system/components/<Name>/README.md`, its typed props are in `design/system/components/index.d.ts`, and its look is `design/system/screenshots/<Name>.png`. The React reference implementation is `design/system/components/bundle.js`, with its CSS in `bundle.css`. Port behaviour and styling, not React idioms: controlled inputs become `v-model` (`modelValue` + `update:modelValue`) for SegmentedControl, Tabs, TextField and SidePanel's `collapsed`. The Icon names are check, play, plus, lock, arrow, arrowLeft, chevronDown, collapse, expand, external, note, comment and image.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All 14 components exist in `web/src/components/ds/` with props typed as in `index.d.ts`.
- [ ] SegmentedControl, Tabs and TextField support `v-model`; SidePanel supports `v-model:collapsed`.
- [ ] Styling uses only token CSS variables; no hex colour literal appears in these files.
- [ ] A dev-only route `/_ds` renders every component in each of its documented variants, and in both themes it matches the screenshots by eye.
- [ ] Done when: `/_ds` shows all 14 components matching their screenshots, and the gate is green.

## Tests
- Component: one test per component covering its props and emitted events (for example, SegmentedControl emits `update:modelValue` on click, and Button renders each variant class).

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/components/ds/`, `web/src/views/DsGallery.vue`, `web/src/router/index.ts`

The gallery route is the only router change.

title: Compare every screen with its prototype, close to pixel level
description:
## Outcome
A report that compares every screen of the app with its prototype export, close to pixel level, at 1440x900 in both themes, and lists every difference with a screenshot crop, so each one can be judged as a valid deviation (invented mock text, intended behaviour) or an implementation error. No code changes.

## Context
Norte is a Vue 3 frontend under `web/` ported from a design-tool prototype. The prototype is one standalone HTML export per screen in `/home/gabriel/repositories/norte/design/prototypes/` (git-ignored, exists only in the main checkout; read it there, read-only): Area, Biblioteca, Command Home, Curriculo, Decisao, Home A, Material Livro, Material Paper, Material Post, Notas, Projeto, Projetos, Revisao, Shell, Tarefa, each as `Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html`, with its source markup in `<Screen>/template.html`.

The app routes are: `/` Início (Command Home), `/biblioteca` (query `v` = inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo, `tipo`), `/notas` (query `tab` = highlights|anotacoes|perguntas), `/revisao`, `/estudo` (the Estudo home, prototype "Home A"), `/curriculos/:slug`, `/material/:kind/:id` with kind post|livro|paper, `/projetos`, `/areas/:id`, `/projetos/:id`, `/decisoes/:id`, `/tarefas/:id`. Pick ids and slugs that exist in `web/src/mock/`. Confirm the "Home A" and "Shell" mappings from their templates and say what you concluded.

The app text differs from the prototype on purpose: the repo is public, so the app uses invented mock data instead of the prototype's content. Differences that come only from different text (different words, different counts, a wrapped line because a title is longer) are expected and must be labelled as such, not reported as errors. Everything else (missing or extra elements, order, spacing, alignment, sizes, typography, colours, borders, icons, states, theme colours) is a candidate implementation error.

A visual check run earlier on the Início screen found real errors that a quick look had missed (a missing search input, missing progress bars, a wrong sidebar group, footer buttons in the wrong font size), so this comparison has to be systematic, not by eye alone.

title: Move the frontend into web/
description:
## Outcome
The Vue 3 frontend lives under `web/` instead of the repository root, so the repository can hold the Go backend in `server/` next to it. `cd web && npm install && npm run build && npm test` passes, and nothing of the frontend remains at the root.

## Context
The repository is becoming a monorepo: `web/` for the Vue frontend and `server/` for a future Go backend that will serve the built frontend and the API from one binary. The project's `AGENTS.md` on the main branch is being updated to describe that layout (frontend in `web/`, gate run inside `web/`), but every frontend file was built at the repository root, so the documented layout and the tree disagree. This bead moves the files; it does not start the backend.

Files that belong to the frontend and move: `src/`, `public/` (if present), `index.html`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`, `tsconfig*.json`, `env.d.ts`, and any other frontend config at the root (for example `.prettierrc`, `eslint` config). Files that stay at the root: `.beads/`, `design/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` if present, `README.md` if present, `.gitignore`, `.github/` if present.

Use `git mv` so history follows the files. Fix every path that the move breaks: relative imports that reach outside `src/` (for example into `design/system/`), Vite and Vitest config paths, `tsconfig` `include`/`paths`, and `.gitignore` entries such as `node_modules` and `dist` (they must match under `web/`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `git ls-files` lists no `src/`, `package.json`, `index.html`, `vite.config.ts` or `tsconfig*.json` at the repository root; all of them exist under `web/`.
- [ ] `cd web && npm install && npm run build && npm test` exits 0 with the same number of passing tests as before the move.
- [ ] `git log --follow web/src/main.ts` shows the history from before the move.
- [ ] `.gitignore` ignores `web/node_modules` and `web/dist`, and `git status` is clean after a build.
- [ ] No `server/` directory is created and no backend code is added.
- [ ] Done when: the frontend builds and tests from `web/` and the root holds only shared repository files.

## Tests
- Existing unit tests: the whole Vitest suite, run from `web/`, passes unchanged in count.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/` (moved frontend files), `.gitignore`

Moves files and fixes the paths the move breaks; no behaviour, component or test logic changes.

title: Tag every library item automatically and expose tags through the library API
description:
## What changes for the user
Finding something saved weeks ago means remembering its title or a word in it. The person's
previous bookmark tool tagged every saved link automatically, and filtering by a tag ("everything
about llm") was how things were found. After this change every saved item gets 5 to 8 English
tags on its own, the list can be filtered by a tag, and tags can be added, removed, renamed and
merged, with a tag removed by hand never coming back on its own.

## Outcome
The server stores tags per item, generates them with the configured LLM after extraction, and
exposes them through the library API: on item summaries, as a list filter, and through endpoints
to add and remove an item's tag and to rename or merge a tag across the library.

## Context
Decided on 2026-10-10: tags are a concept separate from subjects. Subjects are few, curated by
the person, and drive focus and study; tags are many, automatic, and only for finding things.
Tags are English, lowercase, singular, one to three words, 5 to 8 per item, normalized against
the tags that already exist so that the vocabulary does not fork ("llm" and "large language
model" end up as one tag).

The reference is the person's n8n workflow that tagged bookmarks in Karakeep: it gave the model
the list of existing tags and asked it to prefer them, to singularize, to map synonyms to the
existing form, and to create a new concise tag only when nothing existing fits. Reuse that
reasoning, at 5 to 8 tags instead of its 8 to 15.

The tagger's input is the item's title, its `reason` (the one line the person wrote when saving,
labelled "Why am I saving this?") and the start of its extracted text, all inside the same
untrusted-content fence the classifier uses. The `reason` goes
in because it often says what the person cares about in the piece, which the text alone does
not.

How the existing classifier works, to mirror it: after extraction, `writeExtraction` enqueues a
`classify` job inside the extraction transaction (`server/internal/library/extract.go`, around
lines 372 and 573-587, dedupe key `classify:<item>`), skipped when no LLM is configured. A module
registers job handlers through `Module.JobHandlers(deps)` (`server/internal/library/library.go`,
around line 67). The LLM client is `core.LLM` (`server/internal/core/llm.go`), asked for JSON
matching a schema; some providers ignore the schema, so the system prompt must also spell out
the answer shape (the fix that made the classifier work on Ollama Cloud). Tagging is a separate
job from classification so that one failing does not stop the other.

Library migrations live in `server/internal/library/migrations/` (goose, embedded). The translation
bead norte-bc7, which this one depends on through norte-547, adds
`00004_library_location.sql`, so this bead's is `00005`; norte-l57's router migration follows it,
which is why norte-l57 now depends on this bead. The contract is `api/openapi/library.yaml`, with
generated code from `bin/generate`.

"Removed by hand never comes back": the same rule the library already applies to an edited title
and the classifier applies to a rejected suggestion. Store the removal, and drop that tag from
every later automatic answer for that item.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The next library migration adds a tag table (unique normalized name), an item-tag table recording
      whether each tag was added automatically or by hand, and a per-item record of tags removed
      by hand.
- [ ] After a successful extraction, with an LLM configured, a `library.tag` job is enqueued in
      the extraction transaction with dedupe key `tag:<item>`; with no LLM configured none is.
- [ ] The tag job's prompt carries the item's title, its `reason`, the first 2000 characters of its
      extracted text inside the untrusted-content fence, and up to the 200 most-used existing tag
      names; the system prompt states the answer shape `{"tags": ["..."]}` in words as well as in
      the request's JSON schema.
- [ ] The job normalizes each answer tag (lowercase, trimmed, inner whitespace collapsed,
      surrounding punctuation removed), drops empty ones, ones longer than 40 characters and
      ones the person removed from this item by hand, deduplicates, keeps at most 8, and stores
      them as automatic; tags added by hand are never removed by the job.
- [ ] `LibraryItemSummary` and `LibraryItem` carry `tags` (array of names, sorted); the list and
      counts endpoints accept a `tag` filter that keeps only items carrying that tag.
- [ ] `POST /api/library/items/{id}/tags` with `{"name": ...}` adds a tag by hand (normalized the
      same way); `DELETE /api/library/items/{id}/tags/{name}` removes it and records the removal.
- [ ] `GET /api/library/tags` lists every tag with its item count, most used first.
- [ ] `PATCH /api/library/tags/{name}` with `{"name": ...}` renames a tag across the library; when
      the new name already exists, the two merge into one with no duplicate item-tag rows.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- unit: normalizer cases (case, whitespace, punctuation, length cap, dedupe, cap at 8, removed
  tags dropped).
- unit: the job against the `llmtest` server: prompt contents (title, `reason`, fenced text,
  existing tags), stored tags, a removed tag not re-added, a hand tag kept, a prose answer
  retried rather than stored as no tags.
- unit: handlers for add, remove, rename and merge, and the `tag` list filter and counts.
- unit: migration up on a database holding items from `00003`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/library/migrations/`, `server/internal/library/tag.go`, `server/internal/library/tag_test.go`, `server/internal/library/tags.go`, `server/internal/library/tags_test.go`, `server/internal/library/extract.go`, `server/internal/library/library.go`, `server/internal/library/list.go`, `api/openapi/library.yaml`
**Reads only:** `bin/ci`, `bin/generate`, `server/internal/library/classify.go`, `server/internal/core/llm.go`, `server/internal/core/llmtest/llmtest.go`

Server and contract only; the web UI for tags is a separate bead. Generated files under
`server/gen/` and `web/src/api/` change by running `bin/generate`, not by hand.

## Recovery path
The migration's down step drops the three tag tables; no existing table is altered.

title: Add the command palette and preferences overlay
description:
## What changes for the user
Today there is no way to jump between screens by typing, or to switch to the dark theme. After this lands, Ctrl/⌘+K opens a search that jumps to any screen or item, and Preferências switches the theme.

## Outcome
`ShellOverlay.vue` with two modes, `busca` and `prefs`, opened from the sidebar and from Ctrl/⌘+K, wired to the router and the theme helper.

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Open `design/prototypes/Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html` in a browser to see the screen. Read `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html` for markup, inline styles and behaviour. The behaviour is a `class Component extends DCLogic` block with React-style `state`/`setState`. The template uses a design-tool runtime whose `sc-if`, `sc-for` and `{{ }}` bindings map almost one to one onto `v-if`, `v-for` and `{{ }}`. Prototype links point at `Norte - X.dc.html?param=`; translate them into the routes below.
- `design/system/` holds the committed design system. It has tokens in `tokens.css`/`tokens.json` (colour, type, a 4px spacing scale, radius, shadow), one `components/<Name>/README.md` per component, props in `components/index.d.ts`, and screenshots in `screenshots/`. Fonts are in `fonts/`: Schibsted Grotesk for display, Geist for sans and Commit Mono for mono.
- There are two themes, Claro and Escuro, switched by `data-theme` on the root element and stored in `localStorage` under `norte-theme`. The visual rule is quiet: one cobalt accent, no cards, no gradients, no warm colours.

Route table (shared by every screen):
- `/` is Início (Command Home).
- `/biblioteca` is the library, with query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`.
- `/notas` is notes, with query `tab` = `highlights|anotacoes|perguntas`.
- `/revisao` is the flashcard review.
- `/estudo` is the Estudo home (Currículos and Assuntos).
- `/curriculos/:slug` is one curriculum.
- `/material/:kind/:id` is one reading item, where kind is `post|livro|paper`.
- `/projetos` is the project list.
- `/areas/:id` is one area.
- `/projetos/:id` is one project.
- `/decisoes/:id` is one decision.
- `/tarefas/:id` is one task.

The repo is public. Never copy the prototype's mock content into code; use the neutral invented data in `web/src/mock/`. UI strings stay Portuguese.

The repo is a monorepo: the Vue app lives in `web/` and a Go backend will live in `server/` and later serve the built app from one binary. All frontend paths below are under `web/`; `design/` stays at the repo root. The gate is `npm run build && npm test`, run in `web/`.

The reference is `design/prototypes/Shell/template.html`. Its props are `open: 'busca'|'prefs'|null`, `onClose`, `onTheme` and `theme`. In Busca, the input placeholder is "Buscar telas, artigos, projetos, tarefas…". With an empty query it shows the groups "Ir para" and "Ações" ("Alternar tema" and "Preferências"). With a query it filters an index of screens plus mock items by title, sub-label, kind and keywords, shows at most 9 results grouped as Biblioteca / Estudo / Projetos, moves with ↑↓, and opens with ↵; Esc closes. Build the index from the route table plus `web/src/mock/`. Preferências has Tema (Claro/Escuro) and read-only rows for data, sync and the shortcut. The theme helper is `setTheme` in `web/src/theme.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Ctrl+K and ⌘+K open Busca from any route; Esc closes it.
- [ ] Typing filters to at most 9 results in the three groups; ↑↓ moves the highlight and ↵ navigates to the item's route and closes the overlay.
- [ ] "Alternar tema" and the Tema control both flip `data-theme` and persist it.
- [ ] The sidebar's Buscar and Preferências entries open the matching mode.
- [ ] Done when: the full keyboard flow works (open, type, arrow, Enter), and the gate is green.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + @vue/test-utils, mounted with the real router and mock data): the view renders its title and main regions; each interactive state listed in the acceptance criteria flips as described; each outbound link resolves to the route named in the criteria.
- Unit: the search filter ranks and caps results as described, over a fixed index.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/components/ShellOverlay.vue`, `web/src/search/`, `web/src/components/AppShell.vue`

Only the shell's open/close wiring changes in `AppShell.vue`.

title: Translate the Review module's route and copy to English
description:
## What changes for the user
Review is the flashcard queue: one screen at `/revisao`, its sidebar row, its home-screen action
and the cards it runs on. All of it is Portuguese — `Revisão`, `Cartões para revisar`, and 41
accented rows of invented cards. After this change the module answers at `/review` and reads in
English.

## Outcome
The route is `/review` with name `review` and title `Review`, and every string in
`web/src/modules/review/` is English, including the invented cards, the module's sidebar row, its
home action and its palette entry.

## Context
Routes and copy are one bead per module here; this module has one route, one screen and one mock
file, so the whole module is one small diff.

The renames:

| today | English |
| --- | --- |
| `/revisao` name `revisao` title `Revisão` | `/review` name `review` title `Review` |
| sidebar row `Revisão` | `Review` |
| palette `Revisão` / `Cartões para revisar`, keywords `flashcards cartões anki` | `Review` / `Cards to review`, keywords `flashcards cards anki` |

`web/src/shell/sidebar.test.ts:87,97,107` has three Portuguese test titles about this module —
`describe('Revisão in the sidebar')` and two `it` titles naming `Revisão` and `Estudo`. The
`Revisão` half is this bead's; the `Estudo` half is norte-qst's, and `sidebar.test.ts`'s owner is
norte-05j, so this bead touches only the lines naming Review.

The module is still on mock data, so `web/src/modules/review/mock/cards.ts` is what the screen
shows; the cards are invented and are rewritten in English rather than translated literally, under
the repo's rule about never copying prototype content.

The flashcard buttons themselves (`De novo` / `Difícil` / `Fácil`) live in the design system's
`Flashcard.vue` and belong to norte-2vx, not here.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The module declares `/review` with name `review` and title `Review`, and
      `web/src/modules/review/manifest.ts` lists exactly that path.
- [ ] Every string in `web/src/modules/review/` is English, including the invented cards, and the
      screen shows no Portuguese word sourced from them.
- [ ] The sidebar row, the home-screen action and the palette entry with its keywords are English.
- [ ] The three test titles in `web/src/shell/sidebar.test.ts` that name this module are English,
      and the ones naming other modules are left as they are.
- [ ] The **review forbidden-term check** comes back empty:

          rg -n --no-heading -e '[À-ÿ]' \
            -e '(?i)\b(revisao|revisar|cartoes|cartao|baralho|baralhos|dificil|facil|novo|hoje|pendentes|acertos|sessao|nenhum|nada|estudo)\b' \
            -e '/revisao' \
            web/src/modules/review

      Nothing in this directory is deliberately Portuguese, so there is no allowlisted hit.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests

`web/src/modules/review/home/ReviewDueAction.vue`
**Shared edits:** `web/src/components/ds/ds.test.ts` (owner norte-qst, which blocks this bead — its
fixture at lines 104 and 106 hard-codes `/revisao` as an `href` prop, and norte-2vx edits the
Portuguese strings in the same file before either of them);

title: Put the library shelves in one order and the Biblioteca header on one row
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the Biblioteca page lists its shelves as Inbox, Depois, Arquivo, Tudo while the sidebar
lists them as Tudo, Inbox, Depois, Arquivo, so the same four places move around depending on
where the person looks. Under the title sits a second, crowded row: a "Por data / O que ler
agora" toggle, a "Surpresa" button, a search box, a "Data salva" dropdown and a filter icon
that only means "unread only". After this change both places list Inbox, Depois, Tudo, Arquivo,
and the page header is one row: the title, the shelf tabs with their counts, Sugestões,
Surpresa, then on the right the search box, a sort icon and a filter icon, each icon opening a
small menu. Choosing "O que ler agora" becomes one of the sort options.

## Outcome
The shelf order is Inbox, Depois, Tudo, Arquivo in the sidebar and in the Biblioteca tabs; the
Biblioteca header follows the reference prototype's single row with the search box added; sort
and filter are icon buttons that open menus built on a new design-system menu component.

## Context
The library has three stored statuses (`inbox`, `depois`, `arquivo`); `tudo` is a view over all
three, not a status (`api/openapi/library.yaml`, `LibraryView` schema). The tab order is set in
`web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue` (`VIEWS` near line 29 and `segOptions` near
line 222); the sidebar rows under Biblioteca come from `web/src/modules/library/index.ts`
(around lines 48-51). Sugestões is a fifth tab after the shelves and stays there.

The current toolbar is in `LibraryView.vue` inside `.library-tools` (around lines 443-495).
"O que ler agora" requests `GET /api/library/items?view=now`: unread items from every shelf,
ranked by how strongly each links to the subjects in focus. The contract refuses `q`, an
explicit `sort` and `unread=false` together with `view=now`, and refuses `sort` together with
`q` (`library.yaml`, listLibraryItems description). The sort values the contract accepts are
`saved_desc`, `saved_asc`, `title` and `last_opened_desc` (`LibrarySort`); kinds are `post`,
`livro`, `paper`, `video`, `podcast`, `newsletter` (`ItemKind`). Counts per view come from
`GET /api/library/counts`.

The reference is `design/prototypes/Biblioteca/template.html` (header around lines 529-539):
title, then the segmented control with counts, and on the right a sort control and a filter
icon. The person asked for three changes to it: the sort label becomes an icon that opens the
sort options, the filter icon opens filter options too, and a search box sits to the left of
those two icons, everything on one row, with Surpresa to the right of Sugestões.

The design system (`web/src/components/ds/`) has no menu or popover component; `Tag.vue`,
`SegmentedControl.vue` and `Button.vue` are the closest. A menu is needed here and again by the
"add" menu that follows this bead, so it is built once as `ds/Menu.vue`.

Rejected: keeping "Por data / O que ler agora" as its own toggle. It is an ordering (by focus),
so it belongs with the other orderings, and removing it is what makes one row fit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The sidebar rows under Biblioteca read Inbox, Depois, Tudo, Arquivo, in that order,
      followed by the existing Tipos group unchanged.
- [ ] The Biblioteca segmented control reads Inbox, Depois, Tudo, Arquivo, Sugestões, each shelf
      showing its count from `/api/library/counts`; the default tab stays Inbox.
- [ ] At a viewport width of 1280 px the header renders as a single row: title, segmented
      control, Surpresa button immediately right of it, then right-aligned the search box, the
      sort icon button and the filter icon button. No element wraps to a second line.
- [ ] At 390 px wide the header wraps without horizontal page overflow (`scrollWidth` of the
      document equals the viewport width).
- [ ] The "Por data / O que ler agora" segmented control no longer exists.
- [ ] The sort icon button opens a menu with exactly five options, labelled "Mais recentes"
      (`saved_desc`), "Mais antigos" (`saved_asc`), "Título" (`title`), "Abertos recentemente"
      (`last_opened_desc`) and "O que ler agora" (requests `view=now`). The current choice is
      marked, and the button's `aria-label` names it ("Ordenar: Mais recentes").
- [ ] Choosing "O que ler agora" requests `view=now` with no `sort`, `q` or `unread`; while it is
      active the search box is disabled and no shelf tab is selected. Choosing any shelf tab
      returns the order to "Mais recentes".
- [ ] While the search box holds text, the request carries `q` and no `sort`, and the sort icon
      button is disabled (the server refuses the pair).
- [ ] The filter icon button opens a menu with a "Só não lidos" toggle (`unread=true`) and a kind
      choice: "Todos os tipos" plus one entry per `ItemKind`, using the Portuguese labels the
      sidebar's Tipos group already uses. The icon shows its active colour whenever any filter
      is set.
- [ ] `web/src/components/ds/Menu.vue` opens on click, closes on Escape, on an outside click and after a choice,
      moves between items with the arrow keys, and renders `aria-haspopup="menu"` on its trigger
      and `role="menu"` / `role="menuitemradio"` or `menuitemcheckbox` on its contents.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green, including the updated Playwright spec below.

## Tests
- unit: `web/src/components/ds/Menu.test.ts` covers open, Escape, outside click, arrow keys and
  the aria roles.
- unit: `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.test.ts` asserts the tab order, the query each
  sort option and each filter sends, the disabled states, and that "O que ler agora" deselects
  the shelf tabs.
- e2e: `web/e2e/library-search-sort.spec.ts` is updated to drive search and sort through the new
  controls against a real server, and asserts the 1280 px single row by comparing the top offset
  of the title, the segmented control and the filter button.
- e2e: the existing `web/e2e/phone-walk.spec.ts` overflow check keeps passing at 390 px.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue`, `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.test.ts`, `web/src/modules/library/index.ts`, `web/src/components/ds/Menu.vue`, `web/src/components/ds/Menu.test.ts`, `web/e2e/library-search-sort.spec.ts`
**Reads only:** `bin/ci`, `design/prototypes/Biblioteca/template.html`, `api/openapi/library.yaml`, `web/e2e/phone-walk.spec.ts`

Frontend only. The API contract and the server are not touched; every query this bead sends is
one the contract already accepts.
