title: Make the library's Suggestions view read every location and list unread before read
description:
## What changes for the user
Suggestions is the list that answers "what should I read now", ranked by how closely each item
relates to what the person is focused on. Today it only ever shows unread items, and asking it for
read ones is refused outright — so an item already read can never be found through the one view
built around the current focus, and the Stash, which is full of things kept with no intent to
read, is invisible to it. After this change Suggestions reads every location and shows unread
items first and read items after them within the same focus score, with "unread only" still one
click away.

## Outcome
`view=suggestions` reads every location, orders by focus score and then by unread before read,
and accepts `unread=false` instead of refusing it. Its cursor pages correctly across a run of
items sharing one focus score.

## Context
The focus-ranked view is `view=now` today, renamed to `suggestions` by the location-model bead
this one depends on. Two things in the server make it unread-only, and both are deliberate, so
both have to be undone deliberately:

- `server/internal/library/list.go:178` sets `unread := true` inside the `view == LibraryViewNow`
  branch, and the comment there explains why it normalises the flag at that point rather than in
  the `WHERE`: a cursor issued with no `unread` parameter has to continue a list asked for with
  `unread=true`, because the filter hash has to match. Removing the forcing means the filter hash
  now has to distinguish "unread only" from "everything", which it already does — `in.Unread` is
  one of the four inputs to `libraryFilterHash`. What must not happen is the flag being normalised
  to anything at all: the view no longer has an opinion about it.
- `server/internal/library/now.go:144-147` refuses `unread=false` with "the now view is what is
  left to read". That refusal goes. The other two refusals in
  `libraryRefuseNowConflicts` — `q` and an explicit `sort` — stay, because the view still carries
  its own order.

The ordering change is the substantive part. `libraryNowOrderBy` orders by score, then `saved_at`,
then `id`, and the cursor predicate at `server/internal/library/list.go:329-336` is three levels
deep for exactly that reason, with a comment explaining that a page boundary inside a run of equal
scores has to continue by the saved date rather than restarting the run. Adding unread as the
second key makes it four levels — score, unread, `saved_at`, `id` — and `libraryCursorFor` at
`server/internal/library/list.go:344-360` has to carry the unread flag of the row it paged on.
Getting this wrong is not a visible bug on the first page: it shows up as a repeated or skipped
item at a page boundary where several items share a score, which is the common case when the focus
is narrow.

`unread` is stored as an integer 0 or 1, so "unread first" is `unread DESC` and the cursor
comparison is on that integer, not on a boolean.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `view=suggestions` returns items from every location, including `archive` and `stash`.
- [ ] Within one focus score, every unread item comes before every read one; across scores, the
      higher score comes first regardless of unread state.
- [ ] `view=suggestions&unread=true` returns only unread items and is no longer a special case;
      `view=suggestions&unread=false` returns only read items and is not refused.
- [ ] `view=suggestions` with `q`, and with an explicit `sort`, are still refused with the
      messages those two refusals already carry.
- [ ] Paging through a list where at least four items share one focus score and straddle the
      unread boundary returns each item exactly once, over at least three pages.
- [ ] `api/openapi/library.yaml`'s description of the view no longer says it keeps only unread
      items or refuses `unread=false`.
- [ ] The library screen's Suggestions option keeps an "unread only" toggle that sends
      `unread=true`.
- [ ] Done when: `bin/ci` is green.

## Tests
- unit: a fixture with two focus scores and read and unread items at each — assert the exact
  returned order, not just membership.
- unit: `unread=false` under `view=suggestions` answers 200 and returns only read items.
- unit: `q` and an explicit `sort` under `view=suggestions` are still refused, by code and field.
- unit: pagination over a run of equal scores crossing the unread boundary, with a limit of 2,
  collecting every id across pages and asserting the set and the order.
- unit: a cursor issued under `view=suggestions&unread=true` presented with `unread=false` is
  refused, because the filter hash differs.
- component: the Suggestions option renders the unread-only toggle and sends `unread=true` when it
  is on and no `unread` parameter when it is off.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/library/suggestions.go` (the file the location-model bead renames
`now.go` to), `server/internal/library/suggestions_test.go`,
`server/internal/library/list.go`, `api/openapi/library.yaml`, `web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.vue`,
`web/src/modules/library/views/LibraryView.test.ts`
**Regenerates (by `bin/generate`, never by hand):** `server/gen/api/library/`,
`web/src/api/library.d.ts`
**Reads only:** `server/internal/library/items.go`, `server/internal/library/handlers.go`

Four of these files are also edited by the location-model bead. That bead blocks this one, so the
two never run at the same time; this one starts from the English names it left behind.

## Recovery path
No migration and no stored data: the change is a query's ORDER BY, a cursor encoding and a
refusal that goes away. A cursor issued by the old build decodes into the old three-field shape;
bump `libraryCursorVersion` so such a cursor is refused as undecodable rather than silently paging
from the wrong position, which is the same thing the field already exists for.
close_reason: Superseded by norte-bc7, which now carries the Suggestions behaviour. The two were inseparable in files: the unread forcing, the ORDER BY and the four-level cursor predicate all live in server/internal/library/list.go, which norte-bc7 rewrites for the location filter, and the view's rename from now to suggestions is a norte-bc7 contract value. Keeping them apart put list.go, library.yaml, LibraryView.vue and LibraryView.test.ts under two beads at once.

title: Build the server skeleton, the build pipeline and the gate
description:
## What changes for the user
Today Norte only runs as a development server over mock data, and there is no single thing to install. After this lands, one command builds one program, `norte`, and running `norte serve` opens the current app in the browser from that program alone. Nothing the person sees in the app changes yet; what changes is that Norte becomes something that can be installed, started and kept running, and that every later change is checked by the same gate on every machine.

## Outcome
A Go module under `server/` builds the `norte` binary: a cobra CLI with `serve`, `migrate`, `version` and `config`; a config loader; `slog` JSON logging with a request id; an HTTP server with timeouts, a body cap, a `Host` allowlist, a content security policy and graceful shutdown; a plain `GET /api/health`; the built frontend embedded and served with history fallback. `bin/generate` builds the frontend and copies it into the embed directory atomically, the Vite dev server proxies `/api` to the binary, `bin/ci` is the one gate, a GitHub Actions workflow runs it, and `AGENTS.md` describes the monorepo as it now is.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI, used from a desktop browser and a phone. Today the application is only `web/` (Vue 3, Vite, TypeScript, Vue Router, Vitest under jsdom; scripts `dev`, `build` = `vue-tsc --build --force && vite build`, `test` = `vitest run`), plus design assets under `design/` and the tracker in `.beads/` (git-ignored planning notes under `docs/` and `local/` may exist locally and are not part of the build). There is no `server/`, no `bin/`, no `.github/`, no `Dockerfile`, no Node version pin. Everything runs on mock data. The current gate, stated in `AGENTS.md`, is `npm run build && npm test` in `web/`.

The backend decided for it: Go, one static binary, no CGO; SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite`; `sqlc` and `goose` (later beads); an OpenAPI contract per module (later bead); no authentication in v1 — the server listens on localhost or the Tailscale network. The binary embeds the built frontend and serves UI and API together. This bead is the skeleton every other backend bead builds on, and its gate is the gate they all run under — which is why it goes first.

What it contains, decided:

- **Layout.** `server/go.mod` (Go 1.26 via the `toolchain` directive; Go tools pinned as tool dependencies), `server/cmd/norte/main.go`, `server/internal/app/` (config, server wiring), `server/internal/core/` (logging, HTTP helpers), `server/internal/webassets/` (the embed). Every `go` command runs from `server/`; `bin/ci` and `bin/generate` `cd` there.
- **CLI (cobra).** `norte serve` starts the HTTP server; `norte migrate` exists as a command (it applies nothing until the database bead); `norte version` prints the version; `norte config` prints the effective configuration and the source of each value (flag, env, file, default), with secrets redacted. `config` and `version` never open a database.
- **Config.** Every setting is accepted as `NORTE_<NAME>` and in an optional TOML file at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/norte/config.toml` (or `--config <path>`); non-secret settings also as a flag; precedence flag over env over file over default. Secrets (`NORTE_LLM_KEY`, `NORTE_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`) are never flags, because a flag is visible to every process through the process list. A config file holding a secret that is readable by group or others makes `serve` print a warning naming the file. The loader expands `~` itself (Go does not). Settings and defaults: `NORTE_DATA` (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/norte` or `~/.local/share/norte`), `NORTE_MODULES` (every compiled module), `NORTE_LISTEN` (`127.0.0.1:8080`), `NORTE_PUBLIC_URL` (empty), `NORTE_TIMEZONE` (system zone), `NORTE_LLM_URL`, `NORTE_LLM_MODEL`, `NORTE_LLM_KEY` (empty), `NORTE_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`, `NORTE_TELEGRAM_CHAT` (empty), `NORTE_FETCH_MAX_BYTES` (`20971520`), `NORTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES` (`67108864`), `NORTE_LOG_LEVEL` (`info`). The loader knows them all now so later beads only read them.
- **Logging.** `log/slog` JSON on stderr. Every request logs method, path, status, duration and request id. Request bodies, HTML payloads and tokens are never logged; URLs are logged with the query string stripped.
- **HTTP.** `net/http` with the Go 1.22 pattern router, no framework (a framework would be a second way to do what `net/http` does). Middleware: request id (`X-Request-Id`, generated when absent, echoed in every error body); `Host` allowlist (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, the host of `NORTE_LISTEN`, the host of `NORTE_PUBLIC_URL`; anything else gets 421 — with no authentication, a DNS-rebinding page in the browser could otherwise read the server); panic recovery; body cap `NORTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES` (413 above it); JSON error shape `{"error": {"code", "message", "field"?, "request_id"}}`. Server timeouts: read header 10 s, read 60 s, write 60 s, idle 120 s. Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM: stop accepting, drain in-flight requests up to 15 s, close.
- **Content security policy**, sent on every response: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' https: data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. Inline styles are allowed because the design system and extracted articles use them (tightening was considered and deferred); scripts get no exception. So the inline theme-bootstrap script in `web/index.html` (lines 8-15: it sets `<html data-theme>` from `localStorage['norte-theme']`, falling back to light) moves to `web/public/theme-bootstrap.js`, loaded from `<head>` with a classic `<script src="/theme-bootstrap.js">` (not `type="module"`, which Vite would defer past first paint, bringing back the theme flash the inline script exists to prevent),, keeping its behaviour, so the served frontend works under the policy from day one.
- **Health.** A plain hand-written `GET /api/health` returning 200 and a small JSON body. The contract bead later replaces it with a generated handler.
- **Embedding.** Go's `embed` cannot reach outside the package directory, so `bin/generate` copies the built frontend into `server/internal/webassets/dist/`. Directive `//go:embed all:dist`. `.gitignore` gets `server/internal/webassets/dist/*` with `!server/internal/webassets/dist/placeholder.html`, so a committed placeholder keeps the package compiling before the first build. The handler serves files from the embed and falls back to `index.html` for any non-`/api/` path that is not a file (Vue Router uses HTML5 history), and returns 404 JSON for unknown `/api/` paths.
- **`bin/generate`.** For now: `npm ci` if needed, `npm run build` in `web/`, then an atomic swap: build into `dist.new` (copying the placeholder into it), rename `dist` to `dist.old`, rename `dist.new` to `dist`, remove `dist.old`. A failed build never leaves a half-written directory. The contract bead later adds the generators in front.
- **Vite proxy.** `web/vite.config.ts` has no `server` block today (it is 14 lines: the Vue plugin and the `@` alias). Add `server.proxy['/api']` to `http://127.0.0.1:8080` so `npm run dev` talks to a locally running `norte serve`.
- **`bin/ci`.** The one gate, and exactly what CI runs: `gofmt -l` failing on any output, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` with a temporary `NORTE_DATA`, `bin/generate`, `npm run build` and `npm test` in `web/`. Before building it compares the Go version in `server/go.mod`'s `toolchain` directive with the one in the workflow (and, once it exists, the Dockerfile), and `web/.node-version` with the workflow's Node setup, failing with both files and versions on a mismatch. Later beads add their checks to it.
- **GitHub workflow.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `bin/ci` on push and pull request, with the Go version repeated from the `toolchain` directive and Node pinned (add a `.node-version` in `web/` and use it from the workflow).
- **`AGENTS.md`.** Rewrite it to describe the monorepo as it now is: `web/` and `server/`; one OpenAPI file per module under `api/openapi/` (not a single `openapi.yaml`, which is what it says today); generated code under `server/gen/api/`, `server/internal/*/db/` and `web/src/api/` is never edited; `bin/ci` is the gate (replacing `npm run build && npm test`); every `go` command runs from `server/`. Preserve every existing rule that is still true — the design-system location under `design/system/` with its tokens, components and fonts, the git-ignored prototype workflow under `design/prototypes/`, the public-repo rule (neutral invented mock content only), UI strings in Portuguese with code, comments and commits in English, work tracked in `br` — and replace only what this bead makes false: the backend's absence, the single `openapi.yaml`, and the old gate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)` produces one binary at `server/norte`; `(cd server && ./norte serve)` on a free port serves the current frontend at `/`, and a deep link such as `/biblioteca` returns the app's `index.html` (history fallback).
- [ ] `GET /api/health` returns 200; `GET /api/nope` returns 404 with the JSON error shape and a `request_id`.
- [ ] A request with `Host: evil.example` gets 421; `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, the host of `NORTE_LISTEN` and the host of `NORTE_PUBLIC_URL` (each with the port) succeed.
- [ ] A middleware unit test mounts a test-only handler that reads its body and proves that a body over `NORTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES`, sent both with `Content-Length` and chunked, gets 413 with the JSON error shape (no public route reads a body yet).
- [ ] A captured access-log line has method, path without its query string, status, duration and request id, and contains neither the request body nor a token passed in the query.
- [ ] Every response carries the `Content-Security-Policy` header with the exact policy in Context, and `web/index.html` contains no inline `<script>` body; switching theme to dark and reloading still opens dark.
- [ ] `norte config` prints each setting with its source; with `NORTE_LLM_KEY=secret` set, the output contains no `secret`; no flag named `--llm-key` or `--telegram-token` exists.
- [ ] A config file containing `llm_key` with mode `0644` makes `serve` log a warning naming the file; with mode `0600` it does not.
- [ ] `NORTE_DATA=~/x norte config` shows the expanded home path.
- [ ] SIGTERM during a slow request lets it complete (up to 15 s) and the process exits 0.
- [ ] With `norte serve` running, `npm run dev` in `web/` answers `/api/health` through the proxy.
- [ ] `bin/ci` exits 0 on a fresh clone, and the GitHub workflow runs it green on the PR.
- [ ] A workflow fixture with a mismatched Go or Node version makes the pin check fail naming both values.
- [ ] After the rewrite, `AGENTS.md` still names `design/system/` (tokens, components, fonts) and the git-ignored prototype workflow.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` names `bin/ci` as the gate and `api/openapi/<module>.yaml` as the contract layout, and no longer mentions a single `openapi.yaml`.
- [ ] Done when: `norte serve` serves the current frontend from one binary built by `bin/generate && go build`, `npm run dev` reaches it through the proxy, and `bin/ci` is green on a clean clone.

## Tests
- Unit (Go): config precedence (flag over env over file over default), `~` expansion, secret redaction in `config` output, permission warning; `Host` allowlist; body cap (test-only body-reading handler, `Content-Length` and chunked); access-log fields and redaction; error shape; CSP header present; history fallback versus `/api/` 404.
- Integration (Go, `httptest` against the real handler with a placeholder `dist`): health, fallback.
- Subprocess integration (Go test that builds and starts the binary): block an in-flight request, send SIGTERM, release it, assert the request completes and the process exits 0.
- Frontend (Vitest, existing suite): still green after the theme script moves; one test asserts the theme module applies the stored theme.
- Gate: the workflow run on the PR is the proof that `bin/ci` is green outside the author's machine.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/` (new: `go.mod`, `cmd/norte/main.go`, `internal/app/`, `internal/core/` logging and HTTP helpers, `internal/webassets/` with `dist/placeholder.html`), `bin/generate` (new), `bin/ci` (new), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new), `.gitignore`, `web/index.html`, `web/public/theme-bootstrap.js` (new), `web/vite.config.ts`, `web/.node-version` (new), `AGENTS.md`.
**Reads only:** `web/src/theme.ts` (the storage key `norte-theme`), `web/package.json`.

Spans the new server module, the frontend's entry and build config, the gate scripts and the CI workflow. Size L. It is not split because its parts share the gate: the skeleton is only "done" when `bin/ci` and the workflow prove it, and the workflow has nothing to run without the skeleton.
close_reason: Merged in PR #23 (merge of 4def1eb). bin/ci green locally (8 checks) and in the PR's first CI run; host-allowlist mutation caught by two tests; built binary serves /, falls back on /biblioteca and answers /api/health. Reviewer fixed the timezone default and a non-hermetic config test (rework:2).

title: Translate the Projects module's routes and copy to English
description:
## What changes for the user
Projects is the life side of Norte — areas, projects, decisions and tasks — and it is the largest
block of Portuguese left: its addresses are `/projetos`, `/decisoes/<id>` and `/tarefas/<id>`, its
four screens carry about 170 Portuguese strings between them, and the mock content behind them
another 49. After this change the module answers at `/projects`, `/decisions/<id>` and
`/tasks/<id>`, and every one of its screens reads in English.

## Outcome
Every route path, route name, route title, DOM id and string in `web/src/modules/projects/` is
English, including the mock life content the screens still run on, and the module's sidebar row and
palette entry read in English.

## Context
Routes and copy are one bead per module here. A route record is one object; the sidebar row that
points at it, the breadcrumb that names it and the screen it opens are in the same files, and
splitting them would mean two beads editing the same lines.

The renames:

| today | English |
| --- | --- |
| `/projetos` name `projetos` title `Projetos` | `/projects` name `projects` title `Projects` |
| `/projetos/:id` name `projeto` title `Projeto` | `/projects/:id` name `project` title `Project` |
| `/decisoes/:id` name `decisao` title `Decisão` | `/decisions/:id` name `decision` title `Decision` |
| `/tarefas/:id` name `tarefa` title `Tarefa` | `/tasks/:id` name `task` title `Task` |
| `/areas/:id` name `area` title `Área` | path and name unchanged, title `Area` |
| sidebar row `Nova área` id `nova-area` | `New area`, id `new-area` |
| palette `Projetos` / `Áreas, decisões e tarefas`, keywords `areas decisoes tarefas` | `Projects` / `Areas, decisions and tasks`, keywords `areas decisions tasks` |

The route names are referenced from inside the module's own views as `{ name: 'projetos' }`,
`{ name: 'projeto' }`, `{ name: 'decisao' }` and `{ name: 'tarefa' }` — `AreaView.vue`,
`ProjectView.vue`, `TaskView.vue`, `ProjectsView.vue` and `DecisionView.vue` between them hold
about forty of those references, and `ProjectView.vue:109` also carries `kind: 'tarefa'` as a
display kind. Every one of them moves here.

The module is still on mock data: `web/src/modules/projects/mock/life.ts` and

title: Add the per-module OpenAPI contract and the generators
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing visible: this is the agreement between screen and server. What it buys is that every later change to what the server accepts or returns is written once, in one contract file, and both the server and the frontend are regenerated from it, so the screen can never silently send a field the server rejects or read one the server stopped sending. A malformed request gets the same readable error everywhere instead of a crash or a blank screen.

## Outcome
The API contract is a set of OpenAPI files, one per module, from which `bin/generate` produces the Go server interfaces, the TypeScript types and the sqlc query code, in that order, before the frontend build. `bin/ci` fails when a contract or query was edited without regenerating, and when a path sits outside its module's prefix. Every request is validated against the contract before a handler runs, and every error — validation or domain — comes back in one envelope.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. The repo is a monorepo: `web/` is a Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript frontend running on mock data, and `server/` is the Go backend (one static binary that embeds the built frontend). Products are modules switched on by `NORTE_MODULES`; the always-on part that is not a module is the "core". Before this bead the server skeleton exists (cobra CLI, `norte serve` with a plain hand-written `GET /api/health`, `bin/generate` doing only the frontend build and the atomic copy into `server/internal/webassets/dist/`, `bin/ci` as the gate) and the core database exists (SQLite open, goose migrations, sqlc configured).

The decisions this bead implements:

- **One contract file per module** under `api/openapi/`: `core.yaml` now, `library.yaml`, `notes.yaml` and others as their modules land. Each file may only declare paths under `/api/<module>/`; the core file holds `/api/core/...` plus the two paths a client calls before it knows anything, `/api/config` and `/api/health`. `bin/ci` fails on a path whose prefix does not match its file. One file per module means a module implements only its own interface and a disabled module is simply not mounted.
- **Generators.** `oapi-codegen` runs once per file in strict-server mode, standard `net/http`, generating into `server/gen/api/<module>/` (committed, never edited). `openapi-typescript` runs once per file into `web/src/api/<module>.d.ts`. `sqlc generate` runs after both. Then the frontend build, then the atomic swap of `webassets/dist/` the skeleton already does. Generator versions are locked by `go.mod` (tool dependencies) and `web/package-lock.json`, and `bin/generate` invokes them only through those pins — the Go generators through the module's tool dependencies (`go tool`), the npm one through the project-local lockfile (`npm exec --no`) — never a global binary on `PATH`. The person's stated position: hand-written development would never use an OpenAPI generator, but for agents it makes sense — so the generated code must be invisible: the module's handler file is the only hand-written HTTP code and reads as plain Go functions taking typed requests and returning typed responses.
- **Validation.** `oapi-codegen/nethttp-middleware` loaded with the module's spec validates every request, so a handler never sees a body that does not match the contract. Schemas set `additionalProperties: false`. The middleware's errors go through the same error handler as everything else.
- **Error envelope.** `{"error": {"code", "message", "field"?, "request_id"}}`, the request id being the `X-Request-Id` the skeleton's middleware sets. Statuses: 400 for malformed JSON, an unknown field or an invalid enum value; 413 for a body over `NORTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES`; 415 for a wrong content type.
- **Health moves under the contract.** `core.yaml` declares the error schema and `GET /api/health`, which replaces the skeleton's plain handler with a strict-server implementation.
- **A test-only spec.** The core has no `POST` route yet, so `server/internal/app/testdata/` holds a small spec with one `POST` route and a body schema, used only by tests, so the validation cases have a body to reject before the first real `POST` exists.
- **Freshness check.** Over exactly three generated paths — `server/gen/api/`, `server/internal/*/db/` and `web/src/api/*.d.ts` — `bin/ci` takes a content snapshot (a hash of every file, tracked or not), runs `bin/generate`, and fails if generation changed the snapshot, naming the paths that changed. That works on a developer's uncommitted tree as well as in CI; (this replaces the original plan's `git status --porcelain` check, which would fail on a developer's legitimately uncommitted regeneration; the snapshot also catches a new untracked file). `webassets/dist/` is not one of them (it is git-ignored).
- **Frontend client.** `web/src/api/client.ts` wraps `openapi-fetch` on the generated types and is the one place that knows the base URL (relative `/api`, which the Vite dev proxy forwards to `127.0.0.1:8080`).

Order within a task that adds an endpoint, from here on: edit the YAML first; the generated interface then makes a missing handler a compile error, and a handler can only exist for a route the contract names.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `api/openapi/core.yaml` declares the error schema and `GET /api/health`; the running server answers `/api/health` from the strict-server implementation and the skeleton's plain handler is deleted.
- [ ] `bin/generate` runs, in order, oapi-codegen per file, openapi-typescript per file, sqlc, the frontend build and the dist swap; with a deliberately substituted generator executable on `PATH` it still runs the pinned one (the fixture's binary is never invoked).
- [ ] Editing `api/openapi/core.yaml` (adding a field) without running `bin/generate` makes `bin/ci` fail, and the failure names the dirty generated path.
- [ ] A path `/api/library/x` placed in `core.yaml` makes `bin/ci` fail with the file and path in the message; `/api/health` and `/api/config` pass in `core.yaml` and fail in any other module's file (prefix-check tests with both fixtures).
- [ ] `bin/ci` fails when any object schema in `api/openapi/*.yaml` lacks `additionalProperties: false`, naming the schema.
- [ ] A contract that adds a new module file without its generated outputs makes `bin/ci` fail naming the new path.
- [ ] After a correct `bin/generate`, with the regenerated files still uncommitted, `bin/ci` passes locally.
- [ ] Against the test-only `POST` route, each of these gets the standard error envelope with a non-empty `request_id`: an unknown field (400), malformed JSON (400), an invalid enum value (400, `field` set), a body over `NORTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES` (413), `Content-Type: text/plain` (415).
- [ ] `web/src/api/client.ts` exists, imports the generated `core.d.ts` types, and `npm run build` in `web/` succeeds.
- [ ] Done when: an unregenerated YAML change fails `bin/ci`, a mis-prefixed path fails `bin/ci`, the five malformed requests above get the standard envelope with the right status, and the frontend compiles against the generated types.

## Tests
- Unit/integration (Go, `server/internal/app/*_test.go`): the five validation cases through `httptest` against the test-only spec, asserting status and envelope shape; `/api/health` through the strict server.
- Gate check (shell, run inside `bin/ci`): the freshness check and the prefix check; tests invoke both validators against deliberately bad temporary fixtures (an edit without regeneration; a mis-prefixed path) and assert the diagnostics name the changed path and file.
- Build (frontend): `npm run build` compiles against `web/src/api/core.d.ts`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `api/openapi/core.yaml`, `bin/generate`, `bin/ci`, `server/gen/api/core/` (generated), `server/internal/app/` (error handler, validation middleware wiring, health handler, `testdata/` spec), `server/cmd/norte/` (mount), `server/go.mod`/`go.sum` (oapi-codegen tool dependency and middleware), `web/src/api/client.ts`, `web/src/api/core.d.ts` (generated), `web/package.json`/`package-lock.json` (openapi-typescript, openapi-fetch).
**Reads only:** `server/internal/core/` (the database and sqlc setup), the skeleton's HTTP middleware.

Two modules (server app wiring and the web API client) plus the gate scripts; size L.
close_reason: Merged in PR #25 (head afb84df). bin/ci green locally (11 checks) and in CI. Review proved by mutation that the freshness gate was defeated by check order (an unregenerated contract edit passed); reviewer reordered the gate and fixed a stage-order test that failed every CI run (rework:3). Open, non-blocking: additionalProperties check misses untyped and allOf schemas; client.ts has no test.

comments.author: gabriel
comments.text: rework:3 (found by reviewer): The freshness gate was defeated by check order: contracts-test regenerated the tree before the snapshot, so a contract edited without regeneration passed bin/ci (proved by mutation). The stage-order test also failed every CI run by counting npm ci. Both fixed by the reviewer in afb84df.

title: Build the browser extension that saves the current tab
description:
## What changes for the user
Most links are found on the desktop, in the browser. After this lands, a toolbar button saves the current tab: one click opens a small window with Save focused, Enter saves, and it says "salvo" almost at once. Optionally the person types why they saved it and picks a subject or focus to link it to. Because the extension sends the page as the browser rendered it, pages behind a login (a paid newsletter, a logged-in post) are saved with their real text, which the server could never fetch on its own.

## Outcome
A Manifest V3 WebExtension under `extension/` (Chromium target, Firefox smoke-tested): popup, background service worker, injected content script, settings page for the server URL with an optional host permission and a health check, the last result kept in `storage.local`, readable errors, a build script, a Playwright test with the extension loaded, and a Firefox smoke test.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. Its measured problem: links are saved in several apps and never read, and the right thing is usually found at the wrong moment. The entry point for saving on the desktop is a browser extension; saving must feel instant and nothing may wait for extraction.

`server/` is the Go backend, running on the person's machine or homelab (no authentication; it listens on localhost or the Tailscale network). `POST /api/library/items` takes `{url, title?, html?, selection?, why?, link_to?}`, stores the HTML as the item's snapshot, and returns the id (201, or 200 with the existing id for a URL already saved) before extraction runs. The request body cap is 64 MB (`NORTE_BODY_MAX_BYTES`); above it the save fails visibly with 413 — the person chose no silent URL-only fallback, because the fallback fails exactly on the heavy logged-in page where the rendered HTML matters. `GET /api/core/focus` returns the focus targets `{id, type, title}`; `GET /api/core/subjects` lists subjects for search; `GET /api/health` answers 200. Extraction then runs as a background job and the reader in the web app shows the text.

Decided:

- **Manifest V3**, one manifest for Chromium and Firefox (a second manifest only if the Firefox smoke test needs it). Permissions: `activeTab`, `scripting`, `storage`; **no host permissions** at install; optional host permissions declared as the match patterns `http://*/*` and `https://*/*` (granted to nothing at install), so that at runtime the extension can request exactly the configured origin — a browser only allows requesting a subset of what the manifest declares, so declaring only the default origin would make a homelab or Tailscale address impossible.
- **Flow.** A popup cannot read the active tab's DOM, so: the popup messages the background service worker; the background injects a content script into the active tab (`activeTab` is granted by the click); the script returns `document.documentElement.outerHTML` and the current selection; the background posts `{url, title, html, selection?, why?, link_to?, source: "extension"}` to `POST /api/library/items` (the contract allows only the literal `extension` in `source`; the web app omits it and is recorded as `app`). A selection is sent as `{exact, prefix, suffix}` with 32 code points of context on each side. `outerHTML` does not include iframes or shadow roots; that is accepted and documented in the extension's README.
- **Popup.** The page title, a "por que salvei" text field, a link picker fed by `GET /api/core/focus` plus a subject search, and a Save button with focus on open; Enter saves. Save is disabled while a request is in flight. The background owns the request and writes its result to `storage.local` keyed by the page URL, so closing the popup mid-save does not cancel it, the result is shown when the popup reopens on that page, and a popup opened on another tab never shows it. "salvo" as soon as the server returns the id.
- **Settings page.** The server URL (default `http://127.0.0.1:8080`) must parse as an `http` or `https` origin with no credentials, query or fragment, and no path other than `/`; it is normalised to its `URL.origin`, API paths are appended to that origin, and the requested match pattern is derived from it by the WebExtension match-pattern rules. Saving it requests the optional host permission for exactly that origin, checks `GET /api/health`, and persists the URL only after both succeed. With that host permission the background's request is not subject to CORS, so the server needs no extension-specific CORS rule — do not add an origins allowlist to the server.
- **Errors in the popup**: a page that cannot be read (`chrome://` pages, the extension store, an injection failure), a server that does not answer, and a 413 ("página grande demais para salvar").
- **Build** script producing a loadable directory (and a zip). Its tests join `bin/ci`.
- **Tests.** Chromium under Playwright, which can load an extension only in Chromium: a fixture page served locally behind a cookie check, so a server-side fetch of the same URL would fail and only the rendered HTML can produce the text. Firefox: `web-ext lint` plus a load-and-start smoke in CI when a Firefox binary is present; the interactive popup-and-POST check on Firefox is a manual step of the first delivery's acceptance walk.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `extension/manifest.json` is Manifest V3 with exactly `activeTab`, `scripting` and `storage` as permissions, no `host_permissions`, and `optional_host_permissions` of `http://*/*` and `https://*/*`; a unit test proves the settings page derives the match pattern `http://host:8080/*` from `http://host:8080/` and calls `permissions.request` with exactly that pattern (the browser API stubbed, since Chromium's grant prompt cannot be accepted by automation).
- [ ] The Playwright run loads a test build whose manifest adds `host_permissions` for the fixture server's origin only (the build script emits it with `--test-origin <origin>`); the shipped build has none.
- [ ] With no origin granted yet, the popup shows "configure o servidor" with a link to the settings page instead of the server error.
- [ ] The popup opens with Save focused and Enter sends exactly one POST; the loaded-extension test fills "por que salvei", picks a focus target, and asserts `why`, `link_to` and `source: "extension"` in the payload, and the stored item's `source` is `extension`.
- [ ] `prefix` and `suffix` are exactly 32 Unicode code points when the page has them, shorter only at text boundaries.
- [ ] A fake 413 renders "página grande demais para salvar" and no second, URL-only request is sent.
- [ ] The Playwright test loads the built extension in Chromium, opens a fixture page that requires a cookie, triggers save, and asserts: the test server received exactly one `POST /api/library/items` whose `html` contains the fixture's article text and whose `url` is the fixture URL; and after the extraction job runs, `GET /api/library/items/{id}` returns that text in `content_text`.
- [ ] With a text selection on the fixture page, the posted `selection` has `exact` equal to the selected text and `prefix`/`suffix` of at most 32 code points.
- [ ] Closing the popup immediately after Save still completes the request, reopening the popup on that page shows "salvo", and opening it on another tab does not.
- [ ] On a `chrome://` page the popup shows the cannot-read error and sends nothing; with the server down it shows the server error.
- [ ] The settings page refuses a URL whose `/api/health` does not answer 200, and refuses before any permission request a URL with credentials, a non-root path, a query or a fragment; `http://host:8080` and `http://host:8080/` store the same origin.
- [ ] CI runs `web-ext lint` and a Firefox load-and-start smoke when a Firefox binary is present (skipped with a printed reason otherwise); the popup-and-POST check on Firefox is a manual step of the first delivery's acceptance walk, because launching Firefox gives the test no channel to assert the POST.
- [ ] By hand (recorded in the PR): a real logged-in Substack post saved from Chromium shows its text in the reader.
- [ ] Done when: the automated test, against a fixture page served behind a cookie check so the server-side fetch would fail, saves it with its rendered HTML, observes exactly one POST, and the reader shows the article text; by hand, the same on a real Substack post behind login.

## Tests
- E2E (Playwright, Chromium with the extension loaded, a local fixture server and a real `norte serve` on a temp `NORTE_DATA`): the save flow, selection, popup-closed save, error states.
- Unit (the extension's own test runner): selection context extraction (32 code points, at text boundaries), settings validation.
- Smoke (`web-ext lint` and load-and-start, Firefox, conditional).
- Manual: the Substack check above.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `extension/` (new: manifest, popup, background, content script, settings page, build script, tests, README), `bin/ci` (adds the extension's tests and the conditional Firefox smoke).
**Reads only:** `api/openapi/library.yaml` and `core.yaml` (the request shapes; the extension may import the generated TypeScript types), the server (run in tests, not edited).

A new self-contained package of more than six files plus the gate; size L.
close_reason: Merged into local main fb0a786 (GitHub unreachable). Started on codex gpt-6-astra (cut off by its 5h usage limit after ~15 min), resumed in the same worktree on Claude Opus 5. Gate 15/15 green (3 extension checks added). Review: 18 mutations, 16 killed, 2 benign survivors (redundant guards). Fixed before merge: a save stuck in 'saving' after a worker death now expires and is cleared on startup; timeout scales with body size; NORTE_REQUIRE_FIREFOX=1 in CI turns a missing Firefox into a failure; test build output in the OS temp dir; script/style/noscript/template text excluded from selection context; storage.local asserted. Deferred to norte-915: the manual logged-in Substack save and the real Firefox smoke on the person's browser. Open: saved-result entries are never pruned; the Firefox probe patches a web-ext internal (pinned version).

comments.author: gabriel
comments.text:
Found while verifying the extension, out of this bead's blast radius: a cold navigation to /biblioteca/<id> lands on Home instead of the item. The popup's "Abrir na biblioteca" link is exactly such a cold navigation, so the extension's success link currently opens Home.

Cause: web/src/shell/boot.ts:98 runs router.replace(router.currentRoute.value.fullPath) after the config arrives, but the initial navigation has not resolved yet, so currentRoute is still START_LOCATION ("/") and the deep link is replaced by it. It affects every deep link into the app, not only the extension's.

Reproduced in Chromium against a real norte serve: saved item valid, extract_status done, content_text correct, and the browser still ended on "/". The Playwright assertion reaches the reader through Home's saved-item link, so the suite is honest about what it proves. Wants its own bead with a web test; the extension keeps the specified item URL.

title: Fold accented capitals in notes filters and enforce the question and highlight target rules
description:
## What changes for the user
Today, filtering notes by a word with an accented capital (`MEMÓRIA`, `RETENÇÃO`) finds nothing, although the lowercase spelling finds the notes. A question set can end up with two questions of the same kind, a loose question can carry a set's kind, and a highlight can be attached to something that has no text, like a subject, and reports itself as anchored. Once this lands, filters ignore case for every letter and the stored notes always respect their own rules.

## Outcome
The notes `q` filters compare case- and accent-folded text, `POST /api/notes/questions` enforces the kind rules, and `POST /api/notes/highlights` refuses a target that has no text provider.

## Context
1. `server/internal/notes/list.go` (around line 138) filters with SQLite `LIKE`, which folds only ASCII; the contract says "the match is case-insensitive" (`api/openapi/notes.yaml`, the `q` parameter around lines 373-375). The core already has a folding function used for subjects and search (`Slugify`-style NFD plus strip, or the search normaliser in `server/internal/core`); apply the same folding on both sides, either by storing a folded column or by registering a SQLite function. A stored folded column needs a migration; prefer a registered function or folding in Go over a small candidate set only if the lists stay paginated correctly.
2. `prepareQuestion` in `server/internal/notes/service.go` (around lines 352-383) checks neither rule of `notes.yaml`: "a single question carries no kind; a kind is set only for a question written from one of a set's six prompts" (around lines 210-212) and "at most one per kind" in a set (around line 715; enforced only when the set is created, around lines 510-513).
3. `server/internal/notes/service.go` (around lines 118-124) treats `core.ErrNoText` as "anchored at no offset". That is the documented answer when the owning module is switched off (`server/internal/core/text.go`, lines 13-21), but the same branch accepts a subject or a question set id, whose module (core) has no text provider at all, and stores the highlight as anchored.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. `POST $B/api/notes/question-sets {"topic":"Memória","questions":[{"kind":"what","text":"O que é?"}]}`; `GET $B/api/notes/question-sets?q=MEM%C3%93RIA` returns `[]` while `q=mem%C3%B3ria` returns the set.
3. `POST $B/api/notes/questions {"text":"de novo","set_id":"<set>","kind":"what"}` answers 201 and the set now has kinds `["what","what"]`; `POST $B/api/notes/questions {"text":"solta","kind":"why"}` answers 201 with `kind: why` and no set.
4. `POST $B/api/core/subjects {"name":"Teste"}`, then `POST $B/api/notes/highlights {"item_id":"<subject id>","exact":"palavras"}` answers 201 `status: anchored`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `q=MEMÓRIA`, `q=memoria` and `q=Memória` return the same results on highlights, annotations, questions and question sets.
- [ ] A question with a `kind` and no `set_id` answers 400 with `field: kind`.
- [ ] A question with a `kind` already present in its set answers 409 (or 400, per the contract's existing code for the set-creation case) with `field: kind`.
- [ ] A highlight on an item whose type has no text provider (a subject, a question set) answers 400 with `field: item_id`; a highlight on an item of a switched-off module still stores `anchored` as documented.
- [ ] Notes list pagination with `q` still returns every match exactly once across pages.
- [ ] Done when: steps 2 to 4 behave as the criteria say.

## Tests
- unit: cases in `server/internal/notes/api_test.go` for each criterion, including a paginated `q` walk with limit 1.

## Recovery path
If folding is done with a stored column, its migration's down step drops the column; existing rows are never rewritten otherwise. If the rules for questions reject rows already stored, nothing is deleted: the rules apply to new writes only.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/notes/list.go`, `server/internal/notes/service.go`, `server/internal/notes/api_test.go`
**Reads only:** `server/internal/core/text.go`, `api/openapi/notes.yaml`

title: Make the app shell honest about boot failures, switched-off modules and unknown routes
description:
## What changes for the user
Today four things in the app's frame mislead the person. A configuration error in the client shows "Servidor indisponível" for a server that is up. Opening a link to a switched-off module briefly runs that module's screen, which fires requests that fail (and, in the reader, a write), before "Módulo desligado" appears. With the server down, clicking a screen not visited yet does nothing at all. An unknown address shows an empty page, and the browser tab always reads "Norte". Once this lands, each of those cases shows a clear page or message, and the tab title names the screen.

## Outcome
The boot distinguishes an unreachable server from a client-side failure, re-resolves the route before rendering, reports failed lazy navigations, has a not-found page, and sets `document.title` from each route's `meta.title`.

## Context
`web/src/shell/boot.ts` reads `GET /api/config`, sets the clock's time zone (`setClockTimeZone`), prunes the routes of modules that are off, and renders. Four defects:
1. Any exception inside the `try` at roughly lines 66-77, including the `RangeError` that `Intl.DateTimeFormat` throws for an unknown time zone, sets the phase to `unavailable` and retries forever with nothing in the console. The fix: only a failed fetch of `/api/config` means unavailable; any other exception is shown as a boot error with its message, and an invalid zone falls back to the browser's own zone with a console warning.
2. `bootState.phase = 'ready'` (around line 72) renders the app against the route already resolved to the module's real component, before `router.replace` re-resolves it (around line 106). The re-resolve must happen before the phase becomes `ready`.
3. There is no `router.onError` and no `vite:preloadError` listener anywhere in `web/src`, so a lazy chunk that fails to load (server down) is silent. A failed navigation should show the existing server-unavailable state or a toast offering to retry.
4. `web/src/router/index.ts` documents `meta.title` as the document title (around line 10), but nothing assigns `document.title`, and there is no catch-all route, so `/nao-existe` renders an empty main area.
The server-side refusal of an invalid zone is a separate bead; this one makes the client robust to it and to anything similar.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Setup used by every reproduction below: build the binary (`bin/generate && (cd server && go build -o norte ./cmd/norte)`), then `NORTE_DATA=$(mktemp -d -p "$TMPDIR") NORTE_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18080 ./server/norte serve`; `B=http://127.0.0.1:18080`.
2. With `NORTE_TIMEZONE=Mars/Olympus` (before the server refuses it): open `$B/` and observe "Servidor indisponível" with a growing attempt count.
3. With `NORTE_MODULES=library`: open `$B/notas` and observe in the network panel `GET /api/notes/highlights` and others answering 404, plus a vue-router error in the console, before "Módulo desligado" shows. With `NORTE_MODULES=` open `$B/biblioteca/<any id>` and observe `POST /api/library/items/<id>/open` (404).
4. On `$B/biblioteca`, stop the server, click "Início" in the sidebar: nothing changes and nothing is shown.
5. Open `$B/nao-existe`: empty main area. On any route `document.title` is `Norte`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A config whose `timezone` is not a valid IANA zone boots the app using the browser's zone and logs one console warning naming the bad value; the server-unavailable page is not shown.
- [ ] An exception during boot other than a failed `/api/config` request shows an error page carrying the exception message, not "Servidor indisponível".
- [ ] Deep-linking to a switched-off module issues zero requests under `/api/<that module>/` and logs no router error; only "Módulo desligado" renders.
- [ ] A navigation whose lazy chunk fails to load shows a visible message with a retry action within 1 second of the click.
- [ ] An unknown path renders a Portuguese "Página não encontrada" view with a link to Início.
- [ ] After each navigation, `document.title` is `<meta.title> · Norte` when the route has a title, and `Norte` otherwise.
- [ ] Done when: steps 2 to 5 each show the behaviour above in a real browser against a real server.

## Tests
- unit: `web/src/shell/boot.test.ts` gains cases for an invalid zone, a non-network boot exception, and the ordering of route re-resolution before `ready` (assert no module API call is made).
- unit: `web/src/router/index.test.ts` gains cases for the catch-all route and the title update.
- e2e: a Playwright case in `web/e2e/` against a real `norte serve` with `NORTE_MODULES=library` that opens `/notas` and asserts no request to `/api/notes/` was made.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/shell/boot.ts`, `web/src/shell/boot.test.ts`, `web/src/router/index.ts`, `web/src/router/index.test.ts`, one new not-found view under `web/src/shell/`, one new spec under `web/e2e/`
**Reads only:** `web/src/lib/clock.ts`, `web/src/shell/AppRoot.vue`
Confined to the shell's boot and the router.

title: Build the Currículo screen
description:
## What changes for the user
A curriculum is only a static mockup today. After this lands, you can open any curriculum, see its objective and modules, expand them, and jump to the next material.

## Outcome
The curriculum page with objective, module ruler, module accordion of materials, the instrument table, exercises and evaluation, plus edit mode and "Novo currículo".

## Context
Norte is a learning and life-projects app with a Portuguese UI: a reading library, goal-first curricula, spaced-review flashcards, notes, and areas, projects, decisions and tasks. This repo ports a design-tool prototype to Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + Vue Router. It is frontend only: every screen runs on mock data, and there is no backend yet.

Where the design lives:
- `design/prototypes/` holds the prototype, one export per screen. It is git-ignored, so it exists only in the main checkout. Open `design/prototypes/Norte - <Screen> (standalone).html` in a browser to see the screen. Read `design/prototypes/<Screen>/template.html` for markup, inline styles and behaviour. The behaviour is a `class Component extends DCLogic` block with React-style `state`/`setState`. The template uses a design-tool runtime whose `sc-if`, `sc-for` and `{{ }}` bindings map almost one to one onto `v-if`, `v-for` and `{{ }}`. Prototype links point at `Norte - X.dc.html?param=`; translate them into the routes below.
- `design/system/` holds the committed design system. It has tokens in `tokens.css`/`tokens.json` (colour, type, a 4px spacing scale, radius, shadow), one `components/<Name>/README.md` per component, props in `components/index.d.ts`, and screenshots in `screenshots/`. Fonts are in `fonts/`: Schibsted Grotesk for display, Geist for sans and Commit Mono for mono.
- There are two themes, Claro and Escuro, switched by `data-theme` on the root element and stored in `localStorage` under `norte-theme`. The visual rule is quiet: one cobalt accent, no cards, no gradients, no warm colours.

Route table (shared by every screen):
- `/` is Início (Command Home).
- `/biblioteca` is the library, with query `v` = `inbox|depois|arquivo|tudo` and `tipo`.
- `/notas` is notes, with query `tab` = `highlights|anotacoes|perguntas`.
- `/revisao` is the flashcard review.
- `/estudo` is the Estudo home (Currículos and Assuntos).
- `/curriculos/:slug` is one curriculum.
- `/material/:kind/:id` is one reading item, where kind is `post|livro|paper`.
- `/projetos` is the project list.
- `/areas/:id` is one area.
- `/projetos/:id` is one project.
- `/decisoes/:id` is one decision.
- `/tarefas/:id` is one task.

The repo is public. Never copy the prototype's mock content into code; use the neutral invented data in `web/src/mock/`. UI strings stay Portuguese.

The repo is a monorepo: the Vue app lives in `web/` and a Go backend will live in `server/` and later serve the built app from one binary. All frontend paths below are under `web/`; `design/` stays at the repo root. The gate is `npm run build && npm test`, run in `web/`.

Reference: `design/prototypes/Curriculo/template.html` and its standalone HTML. Mounted at `/curriculos/:slug`.

Pick the curriculum by `:slug` from the mock data. Regions: PageTitle with the objective; a module ruler; a ModuleItem accordion of MaterialRows, each with status done / current / next / skipped and O/P for required/optional; an "Instrumento" table; exercises; evaluation. Edit mode and "Novo currículo" live in the same screen; for now they edit the mock store in memory. The slug `nova` opens "Novo currículo" as an empty edit form; any other unknown slug shows a not-found state.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every mock slug renders its own title and modules; `/curriculos/nova` opens an empty edit form that saves a new curriculum; any other unknown slug shows a not-found message.
- [ ] Modules expand and collapse; a MaterialRow routes to `/material/:kind/:id`.
- [ ] Edit mode toggles inputs for title, objective and module titles, and saving updates the page.
- [ ] Side by side with the prototype at 1440px in both themes, layout, spacing and typography match by eye.
- [ ] Done when: every state and link above works on `/curriculos/:slug`, and the gate is green.

## Tests
- Component (Vitest + @vue/test-utils, mounted with the real router and mock data): the view renders its title and main regions; each interactive state listed in the acceptance criteria flips as described; each outbound link resolves to the route named in the criteria.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `web/src/views/CurriculumView.vue`, `web/src/router/index.ts`

One view, plus its route entry swapped from the placeholder. Small view-local subcomponents go under `web/src/views/CurriculumView/`.

title: Extract article text in a background job, safely
description:
## What changes for the user
After a link is saved, its article text appears in Norte by itself a moment later, cleaned of menus, ads and "next post" links, with code blocks intact, so it can be read inside the app on desktop or phone. Saving never waits for this. If a page cannot be fetched or read, the item stays in the library with the reason visible and a retry button, instead of the save failing. Nothing a page contains can run code inside Norte or make the server reach into the person's own network.

## Outcome
The `extract` job: it fetches the page (unless an HTML snapshot was sent) through an SSRF-safe client, stores the fetched HTML as the item's snapshot, extracts metadata and content with go-trafilatura (plus a go-readability pass for code), cleans known leaks, resolves relative URLs, sanitizes with an allowlist, and writes the result in one transaction. It enqueues the follow-up jobs (Telegram reply, classification) and is idempotent. A retry endpoint and `norte extract <id>` re-enqueue it. A committed fixture corpus proves it.

## Context
Norte is a single-user reading, study and projects app with a Portuguese UI. `server/` is its Go backend: one static binary with no CGO, SQLite, goose, sqlc, an OpenAPI contract per module. The library module already saves items: `POST /api/library/items` (and `norte save`) inserts a `library_items` row with `extract_status = pending`, optionally stores the extension's rendered HTML as a content-addressed blob (`html_hash`), increments the item's `extract_generation`, and enqueues an `extract` job with payload `{item_id, generation, refresh}` and `dedupe_key = "extract:<item id>:<generation>"`, so a request made while an older run is still working gets its own job. The jobs worker (in-process, in `norte serve`) runs registered handlers with a lease, retries a failing handler at +1 min and +5 min and marks it `failed` after the third attempt; a handler that returns `core.Permanent(err)` fails at once with no retry. A crash after the effect and before the status write replays the handler, so it must be idempotent.

Relevant `library_items` columns: `url`, `title`, `title_edited`, `author`, `site`, `published_at`, `lead_image`, `source` (`app|extension|cli|telegram|import`), `html_hash`, `extract_generation`, `content_html`, `content_text`, `content_headings`, `extract_status` (`pending|done|failed`; `failed` only once the job has exhausted its attempts — while it retries, it stays `pending` with `extract_error` holding the last error), `extracted_at`, `extract_error`, `minutes`, `meta`. The item is registered in the core registry `core_items(id, module, type, title, url)`, updated with `core.UpdateItem` inside the module's transaction.

Why extraction is a job: the person wants the text shown, and also named "it takes long to save" as the way capture fails. Both hold if the save returns the id at once and the reader shows an "extraindo" state while the job runs. A failed extraction is then a visible, retryable row, not a failed save.

Decided:

- **Fetch** only when the item has no snapshot, or when re-extraction is asked with `refresh=true`. `http`/`https` only. The hostname is resolved exactly once per connection and the connection is dialed to that validated IP through a custom `DialContext` — never to the hostname — so there is no second lookup a changed DNS answer could slip into. Loopback, private (RFC 1918, `fc00::/7`), link-local and unspecified addresses are refused before the first request and after every redirect. At most 5 redirects; 10 s connect timeout, 60 s total; response headers capped at 64 KB; the body capped at `NORTE_FETCH_MAX_BYTES` (default 20 MB) while streaming. A refused address, a body over the cap or a non-HTML content type returns `core.Permanent`. The fetched HTML is stored in the file store and becomes the item's snapshot (`html_hash`, with a `core_file_refs` row of kind `snapshot` — a later file-serving endpoint refuses that kind, because unsanitized HTML served from the app's origin would be a stored script), so a re-extraction reads the same bytes; `refresh=true` refetches, stores the new blob before the writer transaction, and then in one transaction sets `html_hash`, records `meta.snapshot_source = "server_fetch"`, inserts the new `snapshot` reference and deletes the old one. The snapshot size is logged (the person chose "no fallback, measure first": a smaller limit, if ever wanted, comes from these numbers).
- **Extract** with `github.com/markusmobius/go-trafilatura/v2` for metadata (title, author, date, site, image) and content. When the source contains `<pre>`, take the content from a second pass through `codeberg.org/readeck/go-readability/v2`, because trafilatura flattens code blocks into nested `<code>` and go-readability keeps `<pre><code>`. A proof of concept measured go-trafilatura's metadata as identical to Python trafilatura's on seven pages, at 12-46 ms per page warm.
- **Cleanup rules** for the known leaks: previous/next post links and newsletter subscription promos at the end of the content. Each rule is a small function with a fixture.
- **Relative URLs** in links and images are resolved against the page URL. Every `http:` image URL is rewritten to `https:` without probing the host; the content security policy blocks plain `http:` images, and the reader shows the `alt` of any image that fails to load.
- **Sanitize on the server, once**, with `bluemonday` and an element and attribute allowlist (headings, paragraphs, lists, `blockquote`, `pre`, `code`, `em`, `strong`, `a[href]`, `img[src,alt]`, `figure`, `figcaption`, tables, `hr`, `br`, and `style` attributes — the reader and the design system use inline styles, and the policy allows inline styles but never inline scripts). No `script`, no event handler attributes, no `javascript:` URLs, no `iframe`, `object` or `embed`. Stored HTML is already safe, so every consumer reads it without its own sanitizer; a sanitizer change needs a re-extraction, which the snapshot makes cheap.
- **Stale runs write nothing.** Before committing, the handler checks in the same transaction that the item's `extract_generation` still equals its job's `generation`; if a newer request has superseded it, it writes no item column, publishes no event and enqueues no follow-up, and returns success.
- **Write** `content_html`, `content_text`, `content_headings` (JSON list of `{level, text, anchor}`, where `anchor` is a slug of the heading text — lowercase, accents stripped, non-alphanumerics to hyphens — made unique with `-2`, `-3` suffixes in document order; after sanitization every heading in `content_html` gets `id="<anchor>"`, and the sanitizer allows `id` only on `h1`-`h6` and only matching `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, so a page-supplied id never survives), metadata, `minutes` (word count / 230, rounded up), `extract_status = done` and `extracted_at` in one transaction; update `title` and the registry row unless `title_edited`, in which case the extracted title goes to `meta.extracted_title`. On a failure the handler uses the worker's `job.Attempt` and `job.MaxAttempts`: below the maximum it records `extract_error`, keeps `pending` and returns the error so the worker retries; on the last attempt, or on a `core.Permanent` error, it writes `extract_status = failed` and enqueues the terminal follow-up jobs in one transaction before returning the error.
- **Reading position after a re-extraction.** The item's `read_position` (`{v: 1, anchor, percent}`) is validated against the new text in the same transaction: if `anchor` no longer occurs, only the anchor is cleared and `v` and `percent` are kept as the fallback. Every stored error is redacted: URLs lose their query string, no token is ever written.
- **Follow-up jobs**, enqueued in the same transaction: on success or final failure, `notify_telegram` for every Telegram message recorded on the item (`meta.telegram_messages` entries without `replied_at`, each keyed by `(chat_id, message_id, item_id)`; the handler and the recording belong to the Telegram bead); on success, `classify` with payload `{item_id}` and `dedupe_key = "classify:<item id>"` when `NORTE_LLM_URL` is set and the item has no `confirmed` link (its handler belongs to the classifier bead). On success, publish the in-process core event `library.item_extracted` with payload `{item_id}` after the commit; the notes module subscribes to it to re-anchor highlights.
- **The event bus is built here**, because this is its first publisher: `core.Events` in `server/internal/core/events.go`, an in-process, synchronous publish-subscribe with ids-only payloads, published only after a transaction commits. Subscribers are `func(context.Context, core.Event) error`; `Publish` calls a snapshot of the subscribers in registration order, turns a subscriber panic into an error, and returns the aggregate error. The extraction handler returns that error after its own commit, so the worker retries and republishes until every durable reaction has been enqueued; subscribers' job dedupe keys make the replay safe. It exists so the library never writes a notes table and notes never reads a library table. No persistence and no retry: a subscriber that needs durability enqueues its own job from the callback, so a reaction is as durable as the queue. A subscriber whose module is disabled is simply not registered. This bead also adds the bus to the `Deps` the module registry hands each module.
- **Why publishing after the commit loses nothing.** The `extract` handler publishes after its transaction commits but *before it returns*, and the worker marks the job `done` only after the handler returns. A crash between the commit and the publish therefore leaves the job `running`; its lease expires, the worker reclaims it, and the idempotent handler runs again and publishes again. Publishing inside the transaction was considered and rejected: it would let a subscriber's failure roll back an extraction it has nothing to do with, and couple every subscriber to the publisher's transaction.
- **Idempotent**: re-running overwrites the same columns from the same snapshot; the follow-up jobs carry dedupe keys.
- **Retry entry points.** `POST /api/library/items/{id}/extract` (body `{refresh?: bool}`) re-enqueues the job and resets `extract_status` to `pending`; `norte extract <id> [--refresh]` calls the same service.
- **The acceptance corpus** is committed under `server/internal/library/testdata/` and no test reaches the network. The proof of concept used seven page shapes — a Paul Graham essay, a gwern.net page, a Substack post, a Guardian article, a Go blog post, a Wikipedia article and a Martin Fowler article — but its files are lost, and its numbers survive only as "metadata identical to Python trafilatura on all seven". The repo is public, so only pages whose licence allows redistribution are committed: gwern.net (CC0), the Go blog (CC BY 4.0) and Wikipedia (CC BY-SA, with attribution in a `testdata/README.md`) may be captured as real pages; the essay, Substack, Guardian and Fowler shapes are replaced by locally authored fixtures of the same structure (byline placement, metadata tags, footer promos, prev/next links) with invented text. The expected metadata for each fixture is written by hand in a golden file from what the page itself declares, never generated by running the extractor. A hostile fixture (inline `<script>`, `onerror`/`onclick` attributes, a `javascript:` href, an `<iframe>`, an `<object>`, an `<embed>`) and a fixture with code blocks are added.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The corpus has seven page-shape fixtures plus the hostile and code-block fixtures, each with a hand-written golden file of expected `title`, `author`, `published_at`, `site` and `lead_image`, and `testdata/README.md` states the source and licence of each real page.
- [ ] Each page-shape fixture extracts with the golden metadata exactly.
- [ ] The code-block fixture keeps `<pre><code>` in `content_html`.
- [ ] The hostile fixture's `content_html` contains no `<script`, no attribute starting with `on`, no `javascript:`, and no `<iframe`, `<object` or `<embed`.
- [ ] A relative link and a relative image in a fixture come out absolute against the page URL.
- [ ] A fetch of `http://127.0.0.1/`, of a hostname a test resolver maps to `10.0.0.5`, of a redirect chain that ends at a private address, and of a 30 MB body streamed by the test server (generated in the test, never committed) with `NORTE_FETCH_MAX_BYTES` at its default each end with `extract_status = failed` after one attempt and a redacted `extract_error`.
- [ ] With an injected resolver, a fetch calls it exactly once per connection and the dialer receives exactly the validated public IP; a single lookup returning a private address is refused before any dial.
- [ ] With the extract handler blocked on a channel, the save's HTTP response completes with 201 while the handler is still blocked (proves the save does not wait for extraction; no ordering between commit, worker start and response write is required; the sub-100 ms latency is a benchmark, not a gate).
- [ ] Re-extracting an item whose saved `read_position.anchor` still occurs keeps it; one whose anchor is gone clears only the anchor and keeps `percent`.
- [ ] With generation 1 blocked after reading its snapshot while a duplicate save installs a new snapshot as generation 2, only generation 2's content, event and follow-up jobs land.
- [ ] Running the handler twice on one item leaves identical columns and one `classify` job.
- [ ] An item with `title_edited = true` keeps its title after extraction and gets `meta.extracted_title`.
- [ ] With two unreplied entries in `meta.telegram_messages`, success and final failure each enqueue one `notify_telegram` job per entry; with `NORTE_LLM_URL` set and no confirmed link, success enqueues one `classify` job; with a confirmed link, none.
- [ ] A successful extraction publishes `library.item_extracted` once, after commit, to a test subscriber; a failed one publishes nothing.
- [ ] A subprocess integration test starts a worker with a test-only failpoint that calls `os.Exit` after the extraction transaction commits and before publishing; the parent then opens the same database, advances the clock past the lease, starts a new worker, and proves the job is reclaimed and the subscriber's reaction is enqueued.
- [ ] A test subscriber whose enqueue (of a job with a fixed dedupe key) fails once makes the extraction job retry; after the replay exactly one job with that key exists and the extraction columns are unchanged.
- [ ] Every heading in a fixture's `content_html` carries an `id` equal to its `anchor` in `content_headings`; two headings with the same text get `-2`; a page-supplied `id` on a paragraph is removed.
- [ ] After a `refresh=true` re-extraction exactly one `snapshot` reference remains for the item, `meta.snapshot_source` is `server_fetch`, and `norte files gc` removes the old blob after one fake-clock hour.
- [ ] `POST /api/library/items/{id}/extract` on a failed item sets it back to `pending` and enqueues one job; `refresh=true` refetches.
- [ ] Done when: the fixture pages extract with their golden metadata, a page with code blocks keeps `<pre>`, the hostile fixture comes out clean, a fetch to `127.0.0.1`, to a name resolving to a private address, and to a 30 MB fixture are refused with a `failed` row on the first attempt, and a test with the extractor blocked proves the save does not wait for extraction.

## Tests
- Golden (Go, `server/internal/library/extract_test.go`): every fixture against its hand-written golden metadata; sanitized output of the hostile fixture; code-block fixture.
- Unit (Go): the SSRF dialer and redirect policy with an injected resolver; cleanup rules, one fixture each; URL resolution; `minutes`.
- Integration (Go, `httptest` server for fetches — note `httptest` listens on `127.0.0.1`, which the client refuses on purpose, so fetch tests inject a dialer that maps a public test hostname to the `httptest` listener): retries through the worker with a fake clock, permanent errors, idempotent replay, follow-up job enqueueing, the retry endpoint.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `server/internal/library/` (extract handler, fetch client, cleanup rules, sanitizer policy, retry endpoint, `norte extract` command, `testdata/` corpus), `api/openapi/library.yaml` (the extract endpoint) and its generated outputs, `server/go.mod`/`go.sum` (go-trafilatura, go-readability, bluemonday), `server/internal/core/events.go` and its test (new; the event bus), `server/internal/app/` (adding the bus to `Deps`).
**Reads only:** `server/internal/core/` jobs, files, registry and clock; the `library_items` schema.

One module. Size L: well over six edited files in one module, and it is security-critical (SSRF and sanitization), which is why it is labelled critical rather than reasoning.
close_reason: Merged into local main as 34cf63c (not pushed: GitHub auth unavailable on this machine). Security review found six defects, all fixed with failing-first tests (superseded run writing on failure; CGNAT/Tailscale and reserved ranges reachable; lead_image schemes; empty-heading id and anchor collisions; redirect cap; userinfo in redacted errors). bin/ci green on the branch and on merged main (12 checks).

comments.author: gabriel
comments.text:
Implementation complete and committed on feature/extraction (5 commits, all naming norte-zwu, rebased onto origin/main at 6235761). Every acceptance criterion was mutation-checked; the library, core and app suites are green. The full gate was deliberately not run, per the brief.

The branch could NOT be pushed and no pull request was opened. Pushing needs a GitHub credential, and in this lane both git push and gh block indefinitely on the keyring: gh auth token exits 124 on a 90s timeout, gh api answers HTTP 401, and ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml carries no oauth_token. Read access works anonymously, so git fetch and git ls-remote are fine. Unlocking that keyring is a change to the machine rather than to the worktree, so it was left alone.

The dispatching session needs to run: git push -u origin feature/extraction, then open the pull request. A prepared body is in the lane scratchpad as PR-BODY.md.

One departure from the bead is worth the reviewer reading first: metadata is now read from the page own declarations, with go-trafilatura behind them rather than in front, because on the three committed real pages trafilatura disagreed with the pages declarations in six fields (an author read as the declared name plus a fragment of the domain, a site name scraped out of a footer link, an author assembled by splitting a body byline on its comma, and a site suffix left on two titles). The reasoning is in the comment at the top of server/internal/library/metadata.go and at more length in PR-BODY.md.

comments.author: gabriel
comments.text: rework:2 (found by reviewer): Security review: a superseded run still wrote failed/extract_error and enqueued replies on failure; CGNAT (Tailscale) and other reserved ranges reachable; lead_image kept javascript:/data:; a page id survived on an empty heading and anchors could collide; redirect cap one short; userinfo kept in redacted errors. All six fixed with failing-first tests; CGNAT guard mutation-checked.
